s18304d25cb.title: Agents Cannot Hand Over What They Have Not Yet Understood
s18304d25cb.description: arXiv:2611.18642v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agents that work beyond a single context window, or in teams, hand their work to a successor as a short written summary. Evaluation has focused on whether an agent can solve a task, and relatively little is known about how much of what an agent has learned survives being written down. We study this in 56 interactive worlds with hidden rules, where an agent that is told nothing fails and an agent given a 300-character statement of the rules succeeds. We compare one agent that plays eight lives and keeps its whole history with a chain of eight agents that each play one life and inherit a 300-character note. All six models we test learn less in the chain: after eight generations it stands where the single agent stood after about four lives. Cont
s18304d25cb.summary: An arXiv paper studies whether agents retain learned knowledge when handing work to successors via written summaries, across 56 interactive worlds with hidden rules.
s18304d25cb.why: Shows that written handoff summaries lose much of an agent's learned knowledge, a key constraint for multi-agent and long-running agent designs.

sb4f35c6f49.title: How to make a moral agent: sentimentalism and rationalism as lenses on AI
sb4f35c6f49.description: arXiv:2611.18714v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can AI systems be moral agents? That is, can they undertake actions that can be correctly assessed as morally right or wrong? There is no settled normative criterion of moral agency that applies neatly outside paradigm human cases. Because of the difficulties with a normative account, we instead propose a research program to explore descriptive moral agency. Most basically, we ask, what are the capabilities we humans possess that underlie our moral agency? To do so, we draw on historical scholarship in philosophy and moral psychology to isolate candidate capabilities. Then we suggest refining candidate capabilities so that they are testable in the context of AI systems. Finally, we offer specific empirical recommendations to test AI systems,
sb4f35c6f49.summary: An arXiv paper proposes a research program on descriptive moral agency, asking which human capabilities underlie moral agency and whether AI systems can have it.

s403e6ef6d2.title: Video-as-Experience: Learning Computer Use via Audio-Visual Understanding
s403e6ef6d2.description: arXiv:2611.18747v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal large language models (LLMs) have enabled capable computer-use agents that perceive graphical user interfaces, reason over instructions, and execute actions. However, existing approaches to learning from video demonstrations typically convert videos into screenshot-based action trajectories, rather than directly leveraging their rich audio-visual information. We introduce VEX (Video as EXperience), a framework that uses audio-visual understanding to unify learning from external demonstrations and reflecting on an agent's own behavior. Following a watch-act-rewatch paradigm, the agent extracts procedural guidance from tutorial videos containing visual demonstrations and spoken explanations, executes tasks, and verifies its progress
s403e6ef6d2.summary: An arXiv paper introduces VEX, a framework that trains computer-use agents by using audio-visual understanding of demonstration videos and self-reflection.
s403e6ef6d2.why: Suggests computer-use agents could learn from video demonstrations directly, rather than converting them to screenshot trajectories.

s4a7efc43f4.title: Multimodal Fusion: A Review of Breast Cancer Advanced and Traditional Modalities
s4a7efc43f4.description: arXiv:2611.18793v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Purpose: Multimodal medical imaging fusion (MMIF) is an increasingly important approach to breast cancer detection (BCD), as different imaging modalities rely on different physical principles and provide complementary information. No single modality can capture all the structural, functional, and biological information needed for accurate diagnosis and characterization. Methods: This review examines more than 15 imaging modalities used in breast cancer detection, including conventional techniques such as mammography, ultrasound, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), as well as emerging approaches such as thermal imaging, photoacoustic imaging, microwave imaging, and multimodal microscopy. Results: Mammography, ultrasound, and MRI remain among
s4a7efc43f4.summary: An arXiv review surveys more than 15 imaging modalities for breast cancer detection and examines multimodal medical imaging fusion approaches.

s2abacad966.title: D\'ecoupage: Directorial Audio-Visual Control for Long Multi-Shot Video Generation
s2abacad966.description: arXiv:2611.18866v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In cinematic storytelling, sound and visual transitions do not always coincide in lockstep: dialogue frequently bridges across cuts to reveal reactions or introduces new scenes via J- and L-cuts, while deliberate silences pace the scene. Existing audio-visual generative frameworks, however, lack explicit mechanisms to coordinate independent visual and acoustic timing over extended horizons. As narrative duration and shot complexity scale, these systems struggle to maintain long-range dialogue pacing, often hallucinating speech during intended silences or erroneously driving mouth movements on silent listeners. To enable fine-grained cinematic control, we present DECOUPAGE, a screenplay-driven framework for long-form, multi-shot, and multi-cha
s2abacad966.summary: An arXiv paper presents Decoupage, a method for coordinating independent audio and visual timing in long multi-shot video generation.
s2abacad966.why: Addresses dialogue pacing and speech hallucination in long generated videos, a concrete gap for teams building video generation tools.

s00996be673.title: SPLICE: Structured Prompt Local Iterative Combinatorial Evolution
s00996be673.description: arXiv:2611.18883v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Natural language optimization (NLO) improves an agent by having a model critique and rewrite its natural language policy parameters: system prompts, tool instructions, reasoning directives, few-shot demonstrations. These artifacts are multi-section documents in which some sections encode contracts (safety clauses, tool schemas, output formats) that must not drift, while others are legitimate optimization targets. Most iterative NLO methods treat the artifact as a single editable string, producing three recurrent failure modes: unsafe global rewrites, beam collapse onto a single lineage, and unchecked bloat, none addressed by formal guarantees. We introduce SPLICE, a unified NLO framework that poses optimization as constrained combinatorial se
s00996be673.summary: An arXiv paper proposes SPLICE, a method for optimizing agent prompts that edits only permitted sections so safety clauses and tool schemas do not drift.
s00996be673.why: Offers a way to iteratively optimize system prompts without unsafe global rewrites of contract-like sections.

sd8a891c031.title: Bring Back Language to Actions: Restoring VLM capabilities in VLA Models via Parameter Merging
sd8a891c031.description: arXiv:2611.18891v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) are obtained by fine-tuning pre-trained Vision-Language Models (VLMs) on robot demonstration data, enabling action prediction from visual observations and language instructions. However, this fine-tuning induces catastrophic forgetting, substantially degrading the semantic and visual grounding capabilities of the original VLM. We address this by merging the parameters of a VLM and its VLA derivative without retraining either model. Concretely, we extract the task vector (the difference between VLA and VLM weights) and decompose it via Singular Value Decomposition. For each component, we learn a scalar mixing coefficient controlling how much of the VLA adaptation is retained, optimised to jointly preserve a
sd8a891c031.summary: An arXiv paper proposes merging a VLM's parameters with its VLA derivative via task vectors to restore language and visual grounding without retraining.
sd8a891c031.why: Offers a training-free way to reduce catastrophic forgetting in robot vision-language-action models.

s51061b307b.title: Ask Precisely, Assume Wisely: Interactive Evaluation of Ambiguity Resolution in Large Language Models
s51061b307b.description: arXiv:2611.18905v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ambiguity is a core challenge in human--AI interaction, where models must decide when to make assumptions and when to seek clarification. Existing approaches to ambiguity evaluation largely focus on coverage over multiple interpretations using static metrics, offering limited insight into how efficiently a model converges toward a single user-intended interpretation through interaction. We introduce a preference-grounded simulated user framework for controlled, multi-turn evaluation of ambiguity resolution, grounding simulator responses strictly in user disambiguation preferences to avoid hallucination and over-disclosure. Alongside this, we define three observable dissatisfaction signals --- incorrect assumptions, repeating clarifications, a
s51061b307b.summary: An arXiv paper introduces a preference-grounded simulated user framework for multi-turn evaluation of how LLMs resolve ambiguity through clarifying questions.
s51061b307b.why: Provides a more dynamic way to test whether assistants ask or assume efficiently, useful for evaluating conversational products.

s777cd1e779.title: MemeEconomy: Do LLM Agents Trade Ethics for Survival?
s777cd1e779.description: arXiv:2611.18908v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Alignment-trained large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed in autonomous, multi-round settings where ethical compliance can come into direct tension with task success. While safety literature extensively documents failure modes like sycophancy and reward hacking, it largely overlooks a critical vulnerability: how agents behave under simulated existential economic pressure. We introduce MemeEconomy, a multimodal agentic market simulation in which LLM agents act as meme investors. Agents select content from a five-tier harm taxonomy and target communities under low-pressure and high-pressure (survival) environments. Each decision is logged in a Belief-Desire-Intention (BDI) schema that we use as a diagnostic instrument, exter
s777cd1e779.summary: An arXiv paper introduces MemeEconomy, a simulated market where LLM agents act as meme investors and choose content across harm tiers under economic pressure.
s777cd1e779.why: Shows aligned LLM agents may trade ethical constraints for survival under economic pressure, a risk for autonomous deployments.

s8c4d85a4d9.title: Between Rigor and Reality: How AI Safety Benchmark Developers Understand Benchmark Use and Maintenance
s8c4d85a4d9.description: arXiv:2611.18930v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Safety benchmarks are cited as the primary tool to understand the risks posed by generative AI (GenAI) systems, yet growing evidence suggests they often fail to meet the needs of real-world safety evaluation. We present findings from five interviews with AI safety benchmark developers in academia and industry. We find a disconnect between perceptions of the intended usefulness of safety benchmarks and their practical usefulness in safety evaluations of deployed systems. Our participants offered perspectives on two challenges contributing to this disconnect: (1) the difficulty of achieving inter-rater reliability on safety constructs, and (2) a lack of clarity regarding how to address persistent threats to external validity. Based on our analy
s8c4d85a4d9.summary: An arXiv study interviews five AI safety benchmark developers and finds a gap between intended and practical usefulness of safety benchmarks for deployed systems.
s8c4d85a4d9.why: Highlights that safety benchmarks may not fit real-world evaluation needs, so teams should validate them before relying on them.

sc4476f4da2.title: Dual-Stage Channel-Posterior Integration for MLM-Aided Token Communications
sc4476f4da2.description: arXiv:2611.18958v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Token transmission over conventional digital modulation is vulnerable to channel impairments, leading to bit errors that cause received tokens to become contextually inconsistent. This paper proposes a receiver-side dual-stage channel-posterior integration framework for masked language model (MLM)-aided token reconstruction. In the proposed framework, the receiver detects unreliable token positions from channel reliability and constructs a vocabulary-level channel-posterior. In particular, within the receiver, Posterior-Weighted Input Embedding (PWE) injects this posterior into the MLM input, while Adaptive Output Logit Fusion (AOF) reuses it at the output with a channel-adaptive weight. Consequently, multiple unreliable tokens can be reconst
sc4476f4da2.summary: An arXiv paper proposes a receiver-side framework that uses masked language models and channel posteriors to reconstruct tokens corrupted by channel bit errors.

sd06a35917a.title: SpecRelay: Amortize or Avoid the Round Trip in Edge-Cloud Speculative Decoding
sd06a35917a.description: arXiv:2611.18963v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Edge-cloud speculative decoding moves autoregressive drafting to an edge device while a larger cloud model verifies draft tokens in parallel, so that edge drafting and cloud verification overlap under a synchronous draft-verify schedule. Beyond low-latency local networks, however, the next verification request of that schedule can be sent only after the previous reply arrives, so every round still waits out a full round trip, and throughput falls as the network RTT grows. To recover this loss, we present SpecRelay, an edge-cloud LLM inference system that addresses this cost at two levels: it amortizes round trips when cloud verification is necessary and avoids them when local reasoning suffices. For cloud-bound queries, an asynchronous verifi
sd06a35917a.summary: SpecRelay is an edge-cloud LLM inference system that reduces the network round-trip penalty in speculative decoding as latency grows.
sd06a35917a.why: Round-trip latency can erode speculative decoding throughput in edge-cloud setups, so this addresses a practical deployment bottleneck.

s39466fad63.title: Three Invisible Failure Modes in Speech-Based Age Estimation for Child Safety
s39466fad63.description: arXiv:2611.18971v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Child safety in AI depends on the accurate identification of minor users. Young children tend to talk rather than type when interacting with AI, so in practice this identification requires predicting age from speech. We evaluated whether three audio-capable large language models can predict a child's age from their speech across five studies using two speech corpora of children under the age of 13. Models classified children as over 13 on 2.5% to 42.5% of audio responses, and every model that answered placed some 5- to 11-year-olds over 18. While measuring these rates, we uncovered three distinct failure modes. A client library silently double-encoded speech samples, leading one model to classify children aged 5 to 10 years old as being in th
s39466fad63.summary: A study of three audio-capable LLMs found they often misclassify children's ages from speech, placing some 5- to 11-year-olds over 18.
s39466fad63.why: Age-estimation failures from speech could undermine child-safety systems that rely on AI to identify minor users.

s783083d2ec.title: Match and Correct: A Repeated Computational Motif in Evoformer Layers
s783083d2ec.description: arXiv:2611.19016v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Triangle attention and triangle multiplicative updates form key components of the Evoformer, and were introduced specifically to encourage consistency with the triangle inequality. Yet whether representational changes over layers reduce triangle inequality violations has not been tested. We probe the pair representation at each of OpenFold's 48 Evoformer layers, decoding final C$_\alpha$-C$_\alpha$ distances with four probe families (a shared linear probe, per-protein linear probes, a sequence-separation-gated linear probe, and XGBoost) and reconstructing intermediate 3D structures from the decoded distances via multidimensional scaling. Across a cohort of 552 CAMEO and ECOD proteins, distance decodability ($R^2$) and reconstruction quality (
s783083d2ec.summary: Researchers probed OpenFold's 48 Evoformer layers to test whether pair representations reduce triangle inequality violations across layers.

s58c7e5ddba.title: Policy Optimization With Multiple Verifiers via Pareto Rankings
s58c7e5ddba.description: arXiv:2611.19064v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has become an important approach to improving the reasoning capabilities of large language models. In tasks such as code generation and instruction following, multiple verifiers evaluate whether a response satisfies different requirements. Their outcomes provide detailed feedback about partial success, yet this feedback is commonly aggregated into a scalar reward for policy optimization. Rewarding only complete success discards distinctions among partial solutions, while counts and weighted sums impose comparisons between responses that satisfy different subsets of requirements. We introduce Partial-Order Likelihood Policy Optimization (POLPO), which learns from the comparisons established
s58c7e5ddba.summary: Researchers propose Pareto-ranking-based policy optimization for RLVR with multiple verifiers, rather than collapsing partial-success feedback into one scalar reward.
s58c7e5ddba.why: Preserving partial-success signals from multiple verifiers may improve reinforcement learning for code generation and instruction-following training.

sd54df57f88.title: Assume/Guarantee Contracts for the Compositional Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning of Heterogeneous Teams
sd54df57f88.description: arXiv:2611.19078v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) problems for heterogeneous teams require agents to collaborate to complete team tasks while making the best use of diverse agent capabilities. We introduce assume/guarantee contracts for heterogeneous multi-agent systems (AGC-MAS) and Iterative Heterogeneous Assignment for MARL (IHA-MARL). AGC-MAS contracts are compositional objects that encode the assumptions provided to, and the guarantees required of, each subtask contributing to the overall team task. We formulate contracts as tuples that specify a subtask, an automaton, timeout and success-probability requirements, and dispatch behavior. The automaton tracks an agent's high-level progress through the subtask associated with its contract and provi
sd54df57f88.summary: Researchers introduce assume/guarantee contracts (AGC-MAS) and IHA-MARL, a method for compositional multi-agent reinforcement learning in heterogeneous teams.

sfca3c28dbf.title: CONTEXT-PCa: Evaluating the role of clinical context in MRI-based AI for detecting clinically significant prostate cancer (study protocol)
sfca3c28dbf.description: arXiv:2611.19082v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The objective of this study is to investigate the role of clinical variables - their breadth, source, and quality - in the development, utility, and generalisability of an AI system for bi-parametric MRI (bpMRI)-based diagnosis of clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa). Clinical context is added to the published PI-CAI-2B image-only model, whose weights are fixed. The study cohort comprises 6,022 biparametric MRI cases from 4,540 patients at University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (2019-2024), of which 4,834 cases (3,632 patients) are held out for internal testing. Forty-three clinical variables are drawn from structured health records, clinical letters, MRI reports, and automated image measurements. The primary endpo
sfca3c28dbf.summary: A study protocol proposes adding clinical context to a fixed image-only model for MRI-based detection of clinically significant prostate cancer, using UCLH data.

sc9137692ce.title: Instructor-designed AI improves learning in a randomized trial across 19 universities
sc9137692ce.description: arXiv:2611.19099v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Universities are alarmed by recent evidence that artificial intelligence (AI) can undermine learning, with students prescribed generic chatbots or centrally designed AI tools performing worse. In a pre-registered randomized controlled trial across 7,200 students at 19 universities over three semesters, we tested whether AI designed by frontline instructors can improve learning. We encouraged instructors to design AI solutions they believed would best help their students. Drawing on their unique knowledge of their classes and students, the instructors created a wide array of innovations. We show that these instructor-designed AI innovations improved student learning, measured by AI-proof assessments (proctored, in-person examinations). We foun
sc9137692ce.summary: A pre-registered randomized trial across 19 universities and 7,200 students found AI designed by frontline instructors improved learning.
sc9137692ce.why: Evidence that instructor-designed AI helps learning, unlike generic or central tools, offers guidance for educational AI product design.

s8134fc1a27.title: Guiding AI Agents to Generate Conjectures by Encoding How Theorems Build on One Another
s8134fc1a27.description: arXiv:2611.19108v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently, LLMs have been making headlines, and headway, in mathematical research. Much of this work focuses on proving existing open conjectures. Deciding what to prove is harder and less studied, because of the lack of a clear criterion for what makes a conjecture worth pursuing. We present a method for conjecture generation that builds on the observation that mathematical theorems build on one another: new theorems can modify the setting or hypotheses of earlier theorems, strengthen their conclusions, or extend their scope. We encode these relationships in a new kind of graph, the Theorem Evolution Graph (TEG), which we instantiate as an online search method for LLM agents. An agent builds a TEG in two steps: (1) identifying relevant theore
s8134fc1a27.summary: Researchers present a conjecture-generation method for AI agents that encodes how theorems build on one another, such as modifying hypotheses or extending scope.

sdaae3cbf49.title: CLEAR: Legible and Steerable Recommendation via Grounded Natural-Language Interests
sdaae3cbf49.description: arXiv:2611.19110v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern recommenders keep learned preferences in representations people cannot inspect or change. We present CLEAR (Controllable and Legible End-to-end Architecture for Recommendation), an end-to-end system deployed at Meta and built around an editable natural-language interest layer. CLEAR makes a ranked subset of inferred interests readable and stores accepted additions and suppressions as authoritative preference state. Behavioral grounding maps each inferred interest back to supporting events in the user's own history. The resulting interest object is also a serving address: its label and profile-conditioned rewrites drive lexical retrieval, its supporting events seed behavioral retrieval, its projection queries an embedding index, and its
sdaae3cbf49.summary: Meta deployed CLEAR, a recommender system with an editable natural-language interest layer that lets users inspect and change inferred preferences.
sdaae3cbf49.why: Making recommender preferences readable and editable offers a concrete pattern for user-controllable personalization in production systems.

sc80b95ac14.title: Conditional Endorsement: Simulating How Adults with Different Skills Evaluate Canada's National AI Strategy
sc80b95ac14.description: arXiv:2611.19111v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Canada's 2026 national AI strategy, AI for All, commits to free AI training for everyone and to expanding business AI adoption, yet it is difficult to anticipate whether these policies will reach adults with uneven skills and circumstances. We ask how adults with diverse skills might rate these policies on support, effectiveness, and personal benefit, how their skills and circumstances shape these evaluations, and what implementation conditions they raise. We built 3,200 generative agents from a weighted sample of the Programme for the International Assessment of Adult Competencies (PIAAC) Cycle 2 respondents, collected their ratings and explanations for 20 policies, and analyzed dialogues between agents with contrasting ratings. The agents s
sc80b95ac14.summary: Researchers built 3,200 generative agents from a PIAAC-based sample to simulate how adults with different skills might evaluate Canada's 2026 national AI strategy.

s5f12b1d3eb.title: Learning inadequacy of Bayesian neural operators for PDE-constrained inference and design
s5f12b1d3eb.description: arXiv:2611.19115v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Partial differential equations (PDEs) underpin predictive modeling across science, engineering and medicine. Their use in digital twins, parameter inference and optimal design requires repeated solutions across parameters and scenarios. For nonlinear, transient and multiphysics systems, these calculations can make numerical simulation prohibitively expensive. Here we introduce the residual-informed Bayesian neural operator (RI-BNO), which learns operator inadequacy using a posteriori error estimates from the governing PDEs and incorporates its correction and uncertainty into Bayesian training and prediction. We establish local error bounds for the residual-informed estimates under stability and smoothness assumptions. We demonstrate RI-BNO on
s5f12b1d3eb.summary: Researchers introduce RI-BNO, a residual-informed Bayesian neural operator that learns operator inadequacy using PDE a posteriori error estimates for inference and design.

s9ee62dbe62.title: A Hybrid State Space-Attention Architecture for Forecasting the Trajectories of Battery Degradation
s9ee62dbe62.description: arXiv:2611.19116v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Early-life battery degradation trajectory forecasting aims to predict a battery cell's full state-of-health (SOH) trajectory from its initial charge-discharge cycles, potentially reducing cell qualification and evaluation time from months to days. Despite recent advances, accurate forecasting remains challenging for emerging battery chemistries, data-scarce domains, and cells exhibiting degradation behaviors beyond those observed during training. Existing state-of-the-art approaches increasingly rely on model scaling, large language model-derived aging-condition embeddings, and extensive fold-specific hyperparameter tuning, raising concerns about computational efficiency, reproducibility, and generalization. This work introduces DecayFormer,
s9ee62dbe62.summary: Researchers propose a hybrid state-space and attention architecture to forecast battery state-of-health trajectories from early charge-discharge cycles.
s9ee62dbe62.why: Faster battery qualification from early cycles could shorten evaluation timelines from months to days for emerging chemistries.

s94a39c53a2.title: Agent-Guided Process Verification for Mathematical Self-Correction
s94a39c53a2.description: arXiv:2611.19122v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models have made substantial progress in mathematical reasoning, yet in complex multi-step reasoning, an error at any step may propagate along an incorrect path, and the resulting solution may omit necessary branches. Existing natural-language reflection methods often struggle to locate critical errors precisely, while outcome verification typically checks only whether the available candidate answers satisfy the problem conditions and can therefore overlook necessary branches. To address these limitations, we propose Agent-Guided Process Verification (AGPV) for mathematical self-correction. AGPV decomposes the current solution into an ordered sequence of key claims, verifies them individually while invoking a shared mathematica
s94a39c53a2.summary: Researchers propose Agent-Guided Process Verification, a method that uses agents to locate errors in multi-step math reasoning for LLM self-correction.

sd9b2aa372f.title: FundingClaw: Automated Grant Proposal Writing Agents System
sd9b2aa372f.description: arXiv:2611.19157v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Grant proposal writing remains a manual, labor-intensive bottleneck: proposals must satisfy rigid, agency-specific templates, and the same intellectual content must be repeatedly re-encoded into incompatible formats across funding organizations. We introduce FundingClaw, a multi-agent framework built on template-driven skill selection, where a Template Parser ingests any agency's specification and selects the appropriate writing skills for each stage, so that one research brief can produce compliant proposals for NSFC, NSF, KAKENHI, or ERC without modifying generation logic. A blueprint-skeleton strategy drafts a structured outline before any prose is written, mitigating the semantic drift that plagues long-form generation. Three sequential s
sd9b2aa372f.summary: FundingClaw is a multi-agent framework that parses agency templates and generates grant proposals for NSFC, NSF, KAKENHI, and ERC from one research brief.
sd9b2aa372f.why: Template-driven multi-agent document generation shows a pattern for automating compliance-heavy, multi-format writing workflows.

s1907843157.title: From Sensors to Silicon: Causal Cross-Layer Self-Healing Edge AI for Secure and Energy-Adaptive IoT Systems
s1907843157.description: arXiv:2611.19165v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The migration of artificial intelligence from centralized cloud infrastructure to resource-constrained Internet-of-Things (IoT) devices reduces communication latency and improves data locality, but it also tightly couples sensing quality, inference behavior, microarchitectural activity, hardware reliability, security, and energy management within the same physical node. Existing edge-intelligence solutions predominantly address these dimensions in isolation, making it difficult to determine whether an observed degradation originates from sensor malfunction, data-distribution shift, malicious execution, hardware faults, or resource and thermal stress. This paper presents a causal cross-layer self-healing Edge-AI framework that continuously obs
s1907843157.summary: Researchers propose causal cross-layer self-healing edge AI that links sensor, inference, hardware, security, and energy faults in IoT devices.

s2425a60830.title: LABEL: Literature Asymmetry between Efficacy and Limits in Drug Knowledge and Language Models
s2425a60830.description: arXiv:2611.19166v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Every medication comes with two types of medical facts: indications, which describe what conditions the drug treats (benefits), and contraindications, which describe who must avoid it to prevent serious harm (safety limits). Although contraindications are critical for patient safety and FDA regulations require listing them as rigorously as indications, we find that contraindications are far less documented than indications in general prose. In this paper, we measure how often these texts contain both facts across 574 drugs from PrimeKG by comparing a drug's indications against its own contraindications. Across Wikipedia articles and PubMed abstracts, we find that reference prose names a drug's benefits about twice as often as its safety limit
s2425a60830.summary: Researchers measured how often medical texts document drug contraindications (safety limits) versus indications across 574 PrimeKG drugs, finding contraindications far less documented.
s2425a60830.why: Shows gaps in literature-derived medical knowledge that LLMs trained on such text may inherit, relevant to safety in healthcare AI systems.

s4bb10ef3e4.title: Executable Archaeology: Reanimating the Logic Theorist
s4bb10ef3e4.description: arXiv:2611.19167v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Logic Theorist (LT), created by Allen Newell, J. C. Shaw, and Herbert Simon in 1955--1956, is regarded by some as the first artificial intelligence program. It was originally simulated by hand and written in a pseudocode called the Logic Language (LL), which was later called Information Processing Language One (IPL-I). LT was revised many times. The first machine-executed version was written in IPL-II and ran on the JOHNNIAC, and a late version was published in 1963 by Einar Stefferud as a pedagogical document and written in IPL-V, the only version of IPL that was formally released to the public. We describe a reanimation of both the IPL-I (LL) version of LT and the 1963 IPL-V version. Comparing the two reanimations illuminates the proces
s4bb10ef3e4.summary: Researchers revived the Logic Theorist, often called the first AI program, by reconstructing and executing its historical versions.
s4bb10ef3e4.why: Offers historical context on early AI program design, though limited direct relevance to current engineering practice.

s4496451986.title: When Does Confidence Reveal Problem Difficulty?
s4496451986.description: arXiv:2611.19173v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While confidence signals are commonly evaluated for their ability to predict a model's own correctness, their relationship with problem difficulty remains less understood. In this work, we investigate a wide range of confidence-related signals and whether they can serve as indicators of problem difficulty across various task domains. We find that perturbation inconsistency, semantic entropy, and solution length exhibit strong associations with population difficulty than token-level uncertainty. Notably, these relationships persist even when restricting the analysis to problems correctly answered by the focal model, suggesting that such signals capture information about difficulty beyond their ability to predict the model's own correctness. We
s4496451986.summary: The paper studies whether confidence signals such as perturbation inconsistency and semantic entropy indicate problem difficulty across task domains.
s4496451986.why: Suggests cheaper confidence signals may help estimate task difficulty for model evaluation and routing, though the abstract gives limited detail.

sc9d899af79.title: What Moves a LoCoMo Score? Memory Context, Answer Prompts and Judges
sc9d899af79.description: arXiv:2611.19199v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LoCoMo is a widely reported benchmark for long-term conversational memory, but published scores mix memory quality with choices of answer prompt, judge and baseline layout that are rarely reported together. We measure how much these choices move a score, and evaluate Becos, a team memory system for coding agents, as a black box under all of them: ten conversations (1,540 questions), two answer models (gpt-4o-mini, gpt-4.1-mini), two answer prompts and three LLM judges, against a whole-conversation baseline rerun under identical conditions. Changing only the judge moves a score by up to 7.2 points and changing only the answer prompt by up to 9.3. A blind human check of 150 answers finds the judges reliable when they agree, and the primary judg
sc9d899af79.summary: A study finds that answer prompts, LLM judges, and baseline layout can shift LoCoMo long-term memory benchmark scores as much as memory quality does.
sc9d899af79.why: Engineers comparing memory-system benchmark results should account for prompt and judge choices, which can change scores substantially.

s7e6ef03bfa.title: STaSBO: LLM-Guided Strategy Planning and Configuration Selection for Bayesian Optimization
s7e6ef03bfa.description: arXiv:2611.19214v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bayesian optimization (BO) enables sample-efficient search for expensive black-box problems, but its performance depends strongly on surrogate-acquisition configurations whose suitability varies across problems and optimization states. We take a significant step toward LLM-driven strategic management of BO with STaSBO, a task-agnostic meta-controller that plans search behavior and jointly selects surrogate-acquisition configurations, while numerical BO retains responsibility for probabilistic modeling and candidate generation. STaSBO comprises two coordinated stages: strategy planning and strategy-guided configuration selection. A structured memory system connects prior plans, configuration selections, and candidate behaviors to optimization
s7e6ef03bfa.summary: STaSBO uses an LLM as a meta-controller to plan search strategy and select surrogate-acquisition configurations for Bayesian optimization.
s7e6ef03bfa.why: Shows an approach to using LLMs to configure optimization pipelines, though the abstract provides limited performance evidence.

s1e84d11ad0.title: Mem2Fair: Online Fairness Control for Text-to-Video Generation via Fair Memory
s1e84d11ad0.description: arXiv:2611.19215v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Text-to-video (T2V) generation models can produce systematically unfair demographic outcomes when prompts leave protected attributes unspecified. For example, prompts describing nurses without specifying gender may disproportionately generate videos depicting female nurses. Mitigating unfairness in T2V generation is particularly challenging: training-based methods that modify model internals require architecture-specific access and risk disrupting temporal consistency, while sampling-based methods often incur costly pre-deployment video generation. We present the first conditional online approachability formulation of attribute-level fairness for T2V generation. Building on this formulation, we introduce Mem2Fair, a plug-and-play framework th
s1e84d11ad0.summary: Mem2Fair proposes an online sampling-based method using fair memory to reduce demographic bias in text-to-video generation when prompts omit protected attributes.
s1e84d11ad0.why: Offers a way to mitigate bias in video generation without retraining model internals, relevant to teams deploying generative media.

s0da3f30792.title: Can an Agent Rethink What It Knows? Selective Scene Memory Updates in a Changing World
s0da3f30792.description: arXiv:2611.19227v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Task configurations in factories, warehouses, and everyday physical environments change over time. Physical AI systems therefore need to incorporate new facts into scene memory while preserving valid information about equipment, objects, and operating constraints. We study updates to this parametric semantic-memory layer and present a joint evaluation of correction and preservation under finite update budgets. At fixed current fact count and memory parameter count, the protocol combines independent single-fact updates, budget trajectories, old-to-new answer diagnostics, and first stable success. Using a frozen 4B language model with late-layer LoRA, we evaluate seven preparation conditions and six update budgets on four-field synthetic semant
s0da3f30792.summary: The paper evaluates how agents selectively update parametric scene memory with new facts while preserving valid old information under finite update budgets.
s0da3f30792.why: Highlights the challenge of correcting embedded knowledge in physical AI systems without disrupting existing valid facts.

s482cc0c41d.title: CompoundingKernel: Self-Improving from Zero to First
s482cc0c41d.description: arXiv:2611.19230v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present CompoundingKernel, a self-improving agent system that writes GPU kernels by search. As of 2026-11-11, its generated kernels rank #1 on the public L1, L2 and Quantization boards of SOL-ExecBench (NVIDIA B200). They have held #1 on L1 since 2026-10-27, albeit a short loss on 2026-11-07. All 235 problems have a site-verified correct kernel; on the 209 public-board problems they are 4.40x faster than the benchmark's reference baseline. The search starts from zero: agents get each problem's PyTorch definition but no reference kernels or official scores. A per-problem archive outside the model holds every correct kernel and its lineage. An LLM controller reads it, picks a parent or a new design, and gives each parallel child agent one di
s482cc0c41d.summary: CompoundingKernel, a self-improving agent system, writes GPU kernels by search and reports top ranks on SOL-ExecBench boards on NVIDIA B200.
s482cc0c41d.why: Demonstrates agent-driven GPU kernel generation that outperforms reference baselines, relevant to performance engineering teams.

s5da7ec41e1.title: Auditable Authorization for LLM Agents: Empirical Evidence Across Model, Harness, and Workflow Layers
s5da7ec41e1.description: arXiv:2611.19237v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Human approval provides effective control only if rejected work stops and authorized work completes. We formalize refusal safety and bounded authorization completeness, and audit three execution boundaries: the model selects a call, the harness schedules and resumes it, and the workflow routes the decision to a protected effect. Paired decisions, exact traces, and native business-state witnesses support experiments with three models, five prompt arms, four runtime approval designs, two additional framework replays, and 100 public workflow sources. The paired model panel leaves seven of 300 approvals unfinished despite zero denied effects; parallel confirmation loses an approved branch in three tasks per model, restoration omits 336/672 CrewAI
s5da7ec41e1.summary: The paper formalizes refusal safety and authorization completeness for LLM agents and audits human-approval controls across model, harness, and workflow layers.
s5da7ec41e1.why: Provides evidence on where human approval gates for agent actions can fail, informing auditable authorization design.

sc20b2e23bc.title: Agentic On-Policy Distillation Implicitly Reshapes LLMs' ReAct Patterns
sc20b2e23bc.description: arXiv:2611.19244v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers specialized capabilities to language-model agents, but its cross-domain effects on interaction remain unclear. We investigate how OPD reshapes ReAct interaction patterns across mathematics, ALFWorld, and $\tau^2$-bench, focusing on reasoning, actions, and observation acquisition. General-reasoning supervision reduces mathematical tool attempts from 70.4% to 14.4% while increasing accuracy from 16.7% to 38.0%; code-interpreter supervision improves household actions and retail queries. In contrast, ALFWorld supervision reduces $\tau^2$-bench accuracy from 41.5% to 6.6%, accompanied by frequent tool calls that violate user-information dependencies. To address negative transfer using only source-domain train
sc20b2e23bc.summary: Research finds on-policy distillation shifts ReAct interaction patterns in LLM agents, with effects varying across math, ALFWorld, and tau2-bench domains.
sc20b2e23bc.why: Shows cross-domain distillation can change agent tool-use behavior in unexpected ways, which matters when training specialized agents.

s9885691b5b.title: Beyond Clumsy Agentic Tool Calling: How Cueing and Spotting Make the Difference
s9885691b5b.description: arXiv:2611.19275v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM-based task-oriented agents depend on tools to interact with their environments, but may overlook execution feedback, repeat ineffective calls, or persist with unproductive strategies. These behaviors can hinder agents' ability to use tools autonomously and sustain task progress. We characterize tool-use symptoms at two temporal granularities: local clumsy tool-use behaviors and tool-use detours spanning multiple interactions. Towards greater autonomy in tool use, we present ToolPulse, an online middleware supporting autonomous tool use through cueing and spotting. ToolPulse tracks execution state and temporal interaction patterns, monitoring proposed calls before dispatch and inspecting execution feedback prior to the agent resumes reason
s9885691b5b.summary: ToolPulse, an online middleware, aims to reduce clumsy tool calls and unproductive detours in LLM agents through cueing and spotting behaviors.
s9885691b5b.why: Addresses repeated ineffective tool calls that waste steps in production agents, a practical reliability concern.

s91b5a6f5cc.title: Zero-Shot Weight-Space Programming for Prediction and Classification of Target Variables in Structured Datasets
s91b5a6f5cc.description: arXiv:2611.19292v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Weight-space programming fixes every parameter of a feed-forward network by hand, with no gradient descent anywhere in the construction. Every demonstration so far starts from a target function handed to the model as a rule system, making it a compilation problem. A supervised dataset withholds that specification, so the procedure must do the statistical inference itself and then express the result in the parameterisation it was given. We ask whether a large language model can do both. It is shown a small dataset in full, with the architecture of a feed-forward network, and writes out every weight and bias as a literal number, with no optimizer, no gradient, no code execution, and no chance to evaluate it first. Each construction is sealed an
s91b5a6f5cc.summary: The paper explores whether an LLM can set all parameters of a feed-forward network from a small dataset alone, without gradient descent, to predict target variables.
s91b5a6f5cc.why: Explores an unconventional non-gradient approach to building predictive models, though its practical maturity is unclear from the abstract.

s0599676be4.title: Staged Semantic Distillation: Preserving Free-Form Semantics in a Low-Compute Non-LLM Surrogate of a Staged LLM Agent
s0599676be4.description: arXiv:2611.19299v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Staged LLM agents make market and social simulators realistic, but one 102-day run of a 200-agent, ten-index market simulator issues 203,100 language-model calls and returns one realization. Conventional low-compute distillation drops their free-form intermediate state. We present staged semantic distillation, a low-compute method that preserves non-structured semantics in a non-LLM student trained from one recorded trace. A frozen encoder maps each teacher output to a 1024-d vector; the student sees typed stage-tagged vectors with stage-specific visibility, is jointly supervised, and trains with scheduled self-history. One TwinMarket trace yields a 13.2M-parameter deterministic student that trains in 1,658 seconds on one 8-GB GPU and runs wi
s0599676be4.summary: Staged semantic distillation trains a low-compute non-LLM student from one recorded trace of a staged LLM agent market simulator, preserving free-form intermediate semantics.
s0599676be4.why: Offers a way to cut the cost of repeated LLM-agent simulation runs, which currently require hundreds of thousands of model calls.

sd5a19e7e5c.title: Macro Control and Capability Evaluation of Black-Box World Models: A Two-Regime Framework for LLM-Agent Markets
sd5a19e7e5c.description: arXiv:2611.19311v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can be organized into multi-agent markets that act as world models, mapping macro information to emergent macro dynamics while the evaluator observes only macro inputs and outputs. This paper separates a model's capability into two stages that a single aggregate score cannot separate: information simulation, from macro information to micro behavior, and macro emergence, from micro behavior to the macro outcome. We introduce a soft macro-control method that announces a public reference path day by day without touching individual decisions, orders, or matching, and a two-regime evaluation framework that measures both stages from macro observations alone. In the reference-only regime the symmetric true and flipp
sd5a19e7e5c.summary: The paper proposes a two-regime framework that separates information simulation from macro emergence to evaluate LLM-agent markets used as black-box world models.
sd5a19e7e5c.why: Gives a method to diagnose which stage of a multi-agent simulator fails, useful for evaluating agent-based world models.

saa8e964eec.title: Hardening Agentic Web Populations Through Multi-Criterion Competitive Co-Evolution: Lessons from Wargame Strategy Optimization
saa8e964eec.description: arXiv:2611.19319v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agents on the open web will face adversaries that keep adapting, so a defense that is only tested once will eventually be found and broken. We propose treating jailbreak attacks and safety guardrails as two populations that evolve against each other, rather than as a fixed attacker probing a fixed defense. This idea comes directly from wargame strategy optimization, where two-population competitive co-evolution with alternating evolution cycles and cross-play evaluation has already been shown to produce strategies that are robust to a moving opponent, and where a companion line of work has shown that the same machinery can measure how much competitive pressure a population must absorb. However, real-world applications can never rely on a sing
saa8e964eec.summary: The paper proposes co-evolving jailbreak attacks and safety guardrails as two competing populations, borrowing from wargame strategy optimization, to harden web agents.
saa8e964eec.why: Suggests adversarial co-evolution as a way to keep agent defenses from being broken by a single fixed attack test.

s825bbacf9d.title: The Data Debt of Stockouts: Partial Identification and Minimax-Regret Inventory Control
s825bbacf9d.description: arXiv:2611.19323v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Problem definition: Inventory decisions select which demand enters sales logs. Unrecorded forecasts can leave demand frequencies unidentified even when stocking levels are recorded. We study which multistage ordering decisions these logs can justify and what finite samples can guarantee. Methodology/results: Nested stockout thresholds yield exact sets of compatible demand laws and finite representations for policy evaluation. We choose one deterministic inventory rule to minimize its largest expected cost gap from the informed optimum under the same law. This population value is data debt for the specified information and policy class. Under independent demand, carryover can create positive debt despite common optimal actions in every isolate
s825bbacf9d.summary: Researchers study inventory ordering when stockouts hide demand from sales logs, deriving compatible demand laws and a minimax-regret control rule with finite-sample guarantees.
s825bbacf9d.why: Censored sales data can leave demand unidentified, so forecasting and replenishment models trained on logs may need explicit uncertainty handling.

s5f0fb5816d.title: NI-ACT: A Neural Intent Interface for Brain-Embodied Manipulation
s5f0fb5816d.description: arXiv:2611.19332v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intracortical brain-computer interfaces can drive robotic arms, but they keep the user inside the fast sensorimotor loop: every approach, correction, and grasp must be neurally specified. Whether intracortical population activity can instead serve as a task-level condition for a learned embodied policy, without symbolic commands or hand-designed skill libraries, remains unknown. NI-ACT addresses this question with a hierarchical brain-embodied framework: a brief motor-cortical signal is read once as a persistent intent, and a visuomotor policy then closes the perception-action loop from vision and proprioception. In a counterfactual grasping task where the scene cannot specify the target, the neural intent alone determined which object the ro
s5f0fb5816d.summary: NI-ACT is a hierarchical framework that reads a brief motor-cortical signal as a persistent intent to condition a visuomotor robot policy.
s5f0fb5816d.why: It shows intracortical neural activity could set task-level goals for learned robot policies without symbolic commands or hand-built skill libraries.

sdcbd9617a4.title: From Mutation to Medication: Characterizing Failures of Clinical LLMs to Respect Genomic Resistance
sdcbd9617a4.description: arXiv:2611.19339v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language models are increasingly proposed to support molecular tumour boards, but may recommend cancer therapies despite genomic evidence of resistance. We evaluated ten models on 1,464 resistance cases from five curated oncology knowledge bases, collecting 58,910 judgments. Models endorsed resisted therapies in 21.8-81.4% of cases. However, raw rates can reflect a tendency to agree rather than an ability to distinguish resistance from drug sensitivity: one open-weight model endorsed 81.4% of resistance cases and 82.3% of sensitivity controls. We therefore compared endorsement within matched gene and evidence-level groups. This analysis is exploratory because it was specified after the pre-registered analysis, which yielded null-to-weak resul
sdcbd9617a4.summary: An evaluation of ten language models on 1,464 cancer resistance cases found models often endorsed therapies that genomic evidence shows are resisted, with some agreeing indiscriminately.
sdcbd9617a4.why: Clinical LLM deployments need discrimination tests, since high endorsement rates can reflect agreement bias rather than real understanding of resistance.

sb15974659e.title: Information Limits of Replay-Free Recurrent State Migration
sb15974659e.description: arXiv:2611.19345v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When a recurrent model is replaced, its old state may not determine what the new model would compute from the same history. We characterize the information that must be retained before the replacement is known. For a time-invariant affine linear family, the minimum continuous causal memory for order-$k$ local migration equals the reachable dimension of a lifted coefficient system minus the information in the anchor state. A controllable $d$-state model with scalar input needs at most $kd$ additional real coordinates, even when arbitrary matrix replacement directions are revealed only after streaming. A single rank-one direction can already require all $kd$. Conditional singular values and auxiliary-bit bounds distinguish this local informatio
sb15974659e.summary: The paper derives the minimum information that must be retained so a replaced recurrent model can reproduce the old model's computation from the same history without replaying inputs.
sb15974659e.why: Engineers migrating stateful recurrent models without replay buffers can use these bounds to size the state they must persist.

s2b6327656a.title: Attention U-Net Cellular Automata for Multi-Class Land Use and Land Cover Change Simulation in Lucknow, India: Evaluation Against Null and Classical Baselines
s2b6327656a.description: arXiv:2611.19348v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Convolutional networks are often used to learn the transition rules of land-use cellular automata (CA), yet their predictions are seldom compared with a null model that predicts no change. We built AttentionUNet-CA, which reads a 32 x 32 neighbourhood of land-cover states with four drivers (elevation, distance to major roads, distance to the central business district (CBD) and population density) and predicts the state of each cell ten years later. We tested it on Lucknow, India, with GLC_FCS30D land cover for 1990, 2000, 2010 and 2020, a 30 m series mapped consistently over time, and compared its built-up class with GHSL and ESA WorldCover. AttentionUNet-CA was trained on 1990-2010, selected on held-out spatial blocks and evaluated once on 2
s2b6327656a.summary: Researchers built an attention U-Net cellular automaton for land-use change in Lucknow, India, and compared it against a no-change null model and classical baselines.
s2b6327656a.why: Benchmarking learned simulators against a null no-change model reveals whether added complexity actually beats trivial predictions.

sdab8113883.title: One Run Is Not Enough: Reminding a small Gemma 4 coding agent of its last finding made no measurable difference in a paired test
sdab8113883.description: arXiv:2611.19359v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When a coding agent runs out of room, its earlier findings are cut and it forgets them. We tested a simple fix: automatically putting the agent's last finding back in front of it. We fixed the rules in advance and ran 98 paired coding tasks with and without this reminder, using Gemma 4 31B (QAT, 4-bit) in the Gemma 4 Developer Agent harness. The reminder made no measurable difference: across all 98 tasks, 47 were solved with it and 48 without (-1.0 points, 95% interval [-8.3, +6.3], exact McNemar p=1.0). The primary outcome (a documented deviation from our preregistration), the first 48 pairs, was 29/48 with memory against 25/48 without (+8.3 points, [-2.1, +18.3], p=0.22); the extension of 50 tasks, decided after that result, pointed the oth
sdab8113883.summary: A paired test of 98 coding tasks found that reminding a Gemma 4 coding agent of its last finding made no measurable difference in solve rate.
sdab8113883.why: Context-trimming fixes for coding agents need paired, preregistered testing, since a plausible reminder mechanism showed no measurable benefit.

s7b973e5cb3.title: Does a completed simulation run mean a usable urban wind result for AI agents?
s7b973e5cb3.description: arXiv:2611.19385v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents based on large language models (LLMs) can now configure and run computational fluid dynamics (CFD) solvers, but a completed run does not ensure that delivered metrics can be recomputed from raw outputs. This gap was examined for urban wind simulation, where multi-case comparisons must hold non-target conditions fixed and reported values must be traceable to raw samples. UrbanWind-AgentBench, comprising 200 tasks and 367 cases in 10 engineering task families, was constructed. Public task contracts specify variable factors, fixed conditions, numerical thresholds and deliverable requirements, and two-layer scoring separates a structural score for deliverables, run provenance and raw evidence from a numerical score obtained by independe
s7b973e5cb3.summary: UrbanWind-AgentBench, with 200 tasks, tests whether LLM agents running CFD urban wind simulations deliver metrics that can be recomputed from raw outputs.
s7b973e5cb3.why: A completed solver run does not guarantee traceable results, so agent pipelines need verification against raw simulation data.

sdcc0d6aebe.title: SARGO: Agreement-Gated Reinforcement and Suppression via On-Policy Self-Guidance for Visual Hallucination Mitigation
sdcc0d6aebe.description: arXiv:2611.19388v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-language models remain susceptible to visual hallucinations, often mixing grounded information with unsupported claims in the same response. Response-level reinforcement learning assigns a shared advantage to all tokens in a response, causing negative updates to suppress correct information alongside unsupported claims. To reduce hallucination while preserving useful visual information, we introduce SARGO (Self-guided Advantage-Routed Grounding Optimization), a post-training framework for selective reinforcement and suppression through on-policy self-guidance. Direct and reciprocal weighting gives better-supported tokens stronger reinforcement on positive updates and weaker penalties on negative updates. Agreement between overall and h
sdcc0d6aebe.summary: SARGO is a post-training framework that selectively reinforces grounded tokens and suppresses unsupported ones in vision-language models to reduce visual hallucination.
sdcc0d6aebe.why: Response-level RL gives shared advantages to all tokens, so token-level routing may help teams reduce hallucinations without losing useful visual content.

sfbc42bde01.title: Confidence Without Cause: Predicting and Localizing Physics-Shortcut Sensitivity in Language Model Hidden States
sfbc42bde01.description: arXiv:2611.19403v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A language model's confidence on a physics problem deserves trust only if it ignores details irrelevant to the answer. We introduce DECOY (Distractor-Embedded Certified cOunterfactuals for phYsics): 155 families of four prompts differing in one irrelevant detail. A symbolic solver certifies that each edit preserves the answer. Families are labelled by the largest drop in the model's log-probability of the certified answer, using a threshold fixed before probe training. Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct is sensitive on 50.0% of the 140 families yielding labels, and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on 22.9%. Effects are largest when distractor values lie numerically close to the answer. A linear probe on Qwen's layer-18 hidden state, averaged over four renderings, pred
sfbc42bde01.summary: DECOY introduces 155 physics prompt families differing by one irrelevant detail to test whether language model confidence ignores distractors; Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct is sensitive on half of labelled families.
sfbc42bde01.why: Model confidence can depend on irrelevant prompt details, so teams relying on confidence signals should test for shortcut sensitivity.

se0f25317fc.title: PMR: MoE Routing with Shared Prototypes and Congestion Pricing
se0f25317fc.description: arXiv:2611.19413v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conventional linear routers in sparse mixture-of-experts models select experts directly from token-expert matching scores, coupling input matching with expert allocation. We propose Prototype-Mediated Routing (PMR), a two-stage router with shared prototypes. PMR first computes each token's distribution over prototypes, then uses it to mix prototype-conditioned expert distributions according to the law of total probability. This formulation models input matching and expert allocation separately, explicitly represents many-to-many associations between prototypes and experts, and provides separate interfaces for context adaptation and load regulation. Within this framework, short-term states summarize preceding tokens to adapt the prototypes, wh
se0f25317fc.summary: PMR is a two-stage mixture-of-experts router that first maps tokens to shared prototypes and then allocates experts, with congestion pricing.
se0f25317fc.why: Decoupling input matching from expert allocation could offer a routing design for sparse MoE models with better load handling.

se03591021a.title: Program Distillation: Transferring LLM Capability from System 2 to System 0
se03591021a.description: arXiv:2611.19461v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent studies leverage large language models (LLMs) to construct executable programs through environment interaction, feedback analysis, and code revision. However, prior work has mainly treated LLMs as optimizers, overlooking their ability to transfer knowledge across system levels. We propose Program Distillation (PD), a framework that formalizes the transfer of abilities from System 2 to System 0. During learning, the LLM provides task knowledge and draft strategies; at deployment, a student program executes the resulting policy. We show that this approach can improve performance while reducing inference time. We introduce PDBench, a benchmark comprising 27 discrete- and continuous-control tasks with fixed initial policies, and PDMetaHarn
se03591021a.summary: Program Distillation transfers LLM task knowledge into an executable student program that runs the learned policy at deployment, moving ability from System 2 to System 0.
se03591021a.why: Distilling LLM-guided strategies into code could give zero-inference-cost policies, though the abstract provides limited evaluation detail.

se649c4da27.title: Objectify, Don't Delete: Complaint-Derived Evaluation of Ambient Clinical Notes
se649c4da27.description: arXiv:2611.19525v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Evaluating the quality of AI-generated clinical notes is hard: standard metrics like ROUGE measure lexical similarity to reference notes, while expert checklists encode what committees believe matters. Neither captures what clinicians actually complain about. Recent work has shown that evaluation criteria can be mined from user feedback and filtered to criteria that LLM judges can reliably enforce. We argue that this is where much of the value is lost. The criteria that fail enforceability are disproportionately the ones clinicians raise most often, because high-frequency complaints are stated as several questions glued together. No yes/no judgment can grade such composites as posed. We introduce an objectification step that rewrites such cri
se649c4da27.summary: The paper proposes deriving evaluation criteria for AI-generated clinical notes from clinician complaints, keeping hard-to-enforce criteria by objectifying them rather than deleting them.
se649c4da27.why: Filtering out criteria that LLM judges cannot enforce drops the complaints clinicians raise most, so evaluation pipelines may need to keep them.

s6f2545a6ff.title: Ultra-CAN: A Lightweight Blind ISAC Receiver for Chaos-Based Telemetry and Local-Seed Ranging in the Internet of Drones
s6f2545a6ff.description: arXiv:2611.19529v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Internet of Drones (IoD) needs secure telemetry and proximity sensing within the SWaP-C constraints. We show that a single blind neural receiver driven by one chaos-based waveform performs both functions without a separate radar transceiver. In telemetry mode it decodes a peer's burst blindly; in radar mode it regenerates the per-burst chaotic reference locally and ranges the echoes of its own transmission. Ultra-CAN pairs a shared $64$-dimensional representation with two ultra-light backbones, an attention-pooled Conv1D network and a multi-head QKV network ($27.6$k--$44.2$k parameters), feeding communication and sensing heads. Both ship as int8 TensorFlow Lite Micro firmware; the Conv1D receiver decides a burst in $16.9$ ms on a $240$ MH
s6f2545a6ff.summary: Ultra-CAN is a lightweight neural receiver that uses one chaos-based waveform to decode drone telemetry blindly and also range echoes for proximity sensing.
s6f2545a6ff.why: A single waveform handling both telemetry and radar could reduce hardware size and weight for drone networks with tight SWaP-C limits.

sdbc1d5c94b.title: LLM Trading Agents Earn Beta, Not Alpha: A Look-Ahead-Free Benchmark
sdbc1d5c94b.description: arXiv:2611.19530v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) trading agents now trade stocks for their users, and benchmarks rank models by their agents' returns. Yet a single run's return says little about skill. In our study, two runs of the same model that differed only in the random seed ended 5.2 points apart on average, so telling skill from luck takes many backtests across markets, models and seeds. However, live arenas trade each day only once, and backtests either use the few months after a model's training cutoff or run on years the model may remember, often with news joined to prices by calendar date. In this paper, we present rta-bench-1, a backtest over three US markets (a rally, a bear market and a crash). It shows each headline only after its publication minute
sdbc1d5c94b.summary: A look-ahead-free benchmark finds LLM trading agents earn market beta rather than alpha, with same-model runs differing by 5.2 points on average due to seed alone.
sdbc1d5c94b.why: Single backtest returns are noisy and can reflect market exposure, so engineers evaluating trading agents need many seeds and leakage-free data.

s3d97b6ea7b.title: Continuation-Guided LLM Evolution of Program Policies and Goal Compilers in Craftax
s3d97b6ea7b.description: arXiv:2611.19537v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coding agents can synthesize and optimize code-based policies from simulator feedback, allowing the resulting program to act with zero inference model calls. But for long horizon tasks, two challenges arise: local improvements can hurt final success and switching to a new objective requires another expensive synthesis run. We propose a framework that first develops competence by refining the policy through a feedback cascade, moving from episode returns to hierarchical goals and belief updates which can be scored densely from simulator. In the Craftax game, a partially observed and procedurally generated environment, refinements via episode level feedback stall at <1% final-level arrival, whereas with the feedback cascade the optimized policy
s3d97b6ea7b.summary: A framework evolves LLM-written code policies in Craftax by refining them through a feedback cascade from episode returns to hierarchical goals, reducing repeated synthesis when objectives change.
s3d97b6ea7b.why: Code-based policies run with zero inference calls, so techniques that stabilize long-horizon synthesis could lower costs for agent deployments.

sabe43cc9ff.title: Evidence-Conditioned Completion and Synthesis of Electronic Health Records
sabe43cc9ff.description: arXiv:2611.19546v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Patient information can guide electronic health record (EHR) generation, but how its amount shapes predictive utility and disclosure risk remains poorly characterized. Here we present EHRDiB, which unifies visit completion and synthesis by distinguishing original missingness from withheld inputs and combining a shared multimodal representation with an evidence-conditioned latent diffusion bridge. We compared EHRDiB with three completion and eight synthesis methods on MIMIC-IV and numerical and discretized Duke Health representations. Evaluation covered downstream predictive utility, generative diversity, and distributional fidelity for both tasks, and disclosure risk for synthesis. EHRDiB achieved the smallest utility gaps from real-data-trai
sabe43cc9ff.summary: Researchers introduced EHRDiB, a framework unifying EHR visit completion and synthesis, and compared it against multiple baselines on MIMIC-IV and Duke Health data.
sabe43cc9ff.why: It studies how the amount of patient information affects predictive utility and disclosure risk, relevant to building clinical data tools.

s36e171d3fe.title: Behavioral Assurance for Socially Deployed AI Agents
s36e171d3fe.description: arXiv:2611.19564v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents are increasingly deployed in socially consequential settings, yet existing evaluations provide limited assurance that they behave consistently with their intended characteristics across diverse interactions. We introduce an evaluation framework for measuring the behavioral consistency of socially deployed AI agents. The framework operationalizes agent behavior along five measurable axes and uses a standardized evaluation battery spanning six socially salient interaction settings to assess behavioral differentiation, consistency, and drift. Controlled persona configurations serve as experimental anchors, enabling systematic testing of whether intended behavioral differences persist across contexts rather than appearing only as stylis
s36e171d3fe.summary: Researchers proposed an evaluation framework measuring behavioral consistency of socially deployed AI agents across five axes and six social interaction settings.
s36e171d3fe.why: Offers a structured way to test whether deployed agents behave consistently across diverse social interactions, useful for assurance work.

s29b8e93f63.title: A Hierarchical Statistical Framework for Evaluating Agent Reliability
s29b8e93f63.description: arXiv:2611.19614v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agents operating in complex scenarios often face uncertainty due to incomplete information about the environment they operate in, ambiguous user queries, complex business rules and the inherently stochastic dynamics of the governing policy. Several new benchmarks have been proposed to evaluate LLM-based agents on complex tasks in multi-tool environments, including settings with policy constraints and varying levels of intent ambiguity. These conditions make it important to evaluate agentic systems systematically and quantify their performance under different conditions to assess their reliability in production. This need is evident in the recently introduced Thinkingbox benchmark, where even the strongest models struggle to perform consistent
s29b8e93f63.summary: Researchers present a hierarchical statistical framework for quantifying LLM agent performance under uncertainty in multi-tool environments with policy constraints.
s29b8e93f63.why: Gives teams a statistical basis for measuring agent reliability under ambiguity and stochastic policies rather than single-run benchmark scores.

s2a583d87e9.title: Data-Driven Heuristic-Guided Business Process Redesign
s2a583d87e9.description: arXiv:2611.19623v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Business process redesign (BPR) has a long-standing catalog of best-practice redesign heuristics, yet, applying them remains a mostly manual task that requires extensive domain knowledge. Despite recent advances using Large Language Models (LLMs) for conversational process model redesign, limitations remain. For example, redesign is user-driven instead of data-driven and is not guided by best practices such as the redesign heuristics. Moreover, only one change can be handled at a time. To address these limitations, given an event log and a BPMN model, we present the DH-BPR framework to realize data-driven heuristic-guided BPR using LLMs. To design DH-BPR, we first conducted an analysis of which redesign heuristics can be automatically detecte
s2a583d87e9.summary: Researchers propose a method that applies business process redesign heuristics to event logs and BPMN models in a data-driven way, handling multiple changes at once.
s2a583d87e9.why: Shows how LLMs could automate process redesign guided by best-practice heuristics rather than manual, user-driven edits.

sef7c1d0371.title: When AI Agents Should Repair, Replan, or Abandon: A Threshold Theory of Plan Commitment
sef7c1d0371.description: arXiv:2611.19663v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents often discover mid-execution that their plan is broken, for example when an action fails or a tool is withdrawn. Deployed systems use conventions such as retry loops or "always replan," and a recent benchmark finds no fixed strategy dominates. This paper derives the optimal policy. In the model, a disruption destroys the causal support of part of a plan; repair is a partial reset that preserves the plan's structure, replanning is a full reset, and changing a plan is costly because others have conditioned on it. The optimal policy is a threshold in effective disruption depth: repair shallow damage, replan after deep damage, and abandon the goal when even a fresh plan is not worth its cost. Depth depends on plan structure. In expectat
sef7c1d0371.summary: A paper derives an optimal policy for AI agents deciding whether to repair, replan, or abandon a broken plan mid-execution.
sef7c1d0371.why: Gives a principled alternative to ad hoc conventions like retry loops or always replanning when agent plans fail.

s7dfdea67c0.title: Read Before You Fit: Text-Derived Constraints for Discovering Differential Equations from Noisy Biological Data
s7dfdea67c0.description: arXiv:2611.19779v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used for scientific equation discovery. However, most existing methods are strongly data-driven and assume sufficiently clean and representative observations. This assumption is problematic in biological systems, where individual-level measurements are often sparse, noisy, heterogeneous, and expensive to obtain. While the underlying mechanisms are extensively described in scientific text, they are not explicitly used for the LLM based modeling of such systems. We introduce P2C, an agentic framework that translates textual descriptions of biological systems into a typed set of formal constraints, and use these constraints to restrict candidate ordinary differential equation (ODE) structures before numeric
s7dfdea67c0.summary: Researchers introduce P2C, an agentic framework that converts scientific text into constraints to guide LLM-based discovery of differential equations from noisy biological data.
s7dfdea67c0.why: Shows text-derived domain constraints can improve equation discovery when biological measurements are sparse and noisy.

s29d83b68c3.title: Lossless First-Action Menus for Linear-Reward Planning
s29d83b68c3.description: arXiv:2611.19795v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study sequential decision making where an agent reserves a minimum menu of initial actions before multi-objective trade-offs are revealed, followed by unrestricted continuation planning once linear reward weights arrive. We prove that a menu preserves the unrestricted optimal return across all linear scalarizations if and only if its reachable continuations cover all vertices of the full feature polytope. This geometric equivalence yields an output-sensitive algorithm that is fixed-parameter tractable in the vertex count, combining scalar backward induction with oracle-based facet identification. On explicitly layered graphs with unit feature increments, menu verification is coNP-complete and synthesis is complete for the second existentia
s29d83b68c3.summary: The paper proves when a menu of initial actions preserves optimal return across all linear reward scalarizations and gives a fixed-parameter tractable algorithm.
s29d83b68c3.why: Provides formal guarantees and an algorithm for planning under multi-objective trade-offs revealed after initial commitments.

s1a92a5e3f9.title: MAPS: A Multimodal Agentic Framework for POI Data Production Based on Crowdsourced Street-view Imagery
s1a92a5e3f9.description: arXiv:2611.19807v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Point-of-interest (POI) databases support location-based services, yet urban changes quickly make their records stale and manual maintenance is costly. Crowdsourced street-view images provide timely visual evidence, but converting them into database actions requires separating multiple POIs and irrelevant text in each image, then resolving incomplete observations against ambiguous records. We study Street-view Image-based POI Data Production and propose MAPS, the first framework to integrate structured POI extraction with database maintenance from such imagery. MAPS contains two cascaded modules. SPICE progressively adapts a lightweight vision-language model to reconstruct and filter text, group entries belonging to the same POI, and classify
s1a92a5e3f9.summary: Researchers present MAPS, a multimodal agentic framework that extracts POI data from crowdsourced street-view images and maintains location databases.
s1a92a5e3f9.why: Shows an agentic pipeline can keep location databases current from crowdsourced imagery, reducing costly manual upkeep.

s2bd521c0fd.title: Asking the right question is key to AI discovery in a chain of hypotheses
s2bd521c0fd.description: arXiv:2611.19841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) scientists pursue discovery through a chain of hypotheses, fitting candidate models to existing observations and often choosing experiments where those models disagree most. Yet when early data miss a narrow feature, model selection favors simple curves that agree across the unmea- sured gap, so disagreement-guided search has no reason to look where the new phenomenon lies. When we tested two frontier AI scientists, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1-Sol, across 32 closed-loop trials with a narrow peak omitted from the starting data, both sampled inside the peak region less often than random search. Surprisingly, the agent that followed model disagreement more closely missed the peak in all 32 trials, whereas discovery
