s2bd521c0fd.summary: Experiments with two frontier AI scientists found disagreement-guided search can miss narrow phenomena omitted from early data, across 32 closed-loop trials.
s2bd521c0fd.why: Highlights a failure mode in AI-driven experimental design where models favor simple curves and overlook unmeasured features.

s6e51982814.title: When Facts Change, Which Decisions Break? Dependency-Aware Context Graphs for Agents
s6e51982814.description: arXiv:2611.19859v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When an observed fact changes, an agent must identify and repair the decisions that depend on it while preserving unaffected outputs. We investigate the reliability-cost trade-off of field-level dependency graphs extracted from actual agent read traces. A controlled benchmark spans three executable workflow domains and four successive updates, with independent imperative and expression-based references. Across 120 workflows, two models and two repeated runs, we compare full recomputation, rolling summary memory, lexical retrieval, trace-extracted dependencies and verified dependency upper bounds. Trace-derived graphs reduce reviewed decisions and estimated total cost, but omitted alternative supports and missing repair context can reduce comp
s6e51982814.summary: Researchers study dependency-aware context graphs that identify which agent decisions must be repaired when an observed fact changes, comparing several update strategies.
s6e51982814.why: Addresses the cost-reliability trade-off in keeping agent decisions consistent when underlying facts update.

s47a0eb8b00.title: Interactive Structured Environment Scaling for Large Language Model Agentic Reasoning
s47a0eb8b00.description: arXiv:2611.19871v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning via environmental interaction is a cornerstone post-training paradigm for evolving large language models into autonomous agents capable of multi-turn tool use and exploration. Because the environment defines what the policy observes and how actions are verified, its structure directly bounds the capabilities an agent can acquire. Yet existing structured and retrieval environments rely on upstream pre-filtering---extracting a compact subgraph around the gold answer or retrieving fixed passages before the policy acts. We show that such pre-filtering introduces a fundamental measurement confound: because per-question subgraphs enclose ground-truth paths, they compress the candidate space by orders of magnitude and leak ans
s47a0eb8b00.summary: A paper proposes interactive structured environments for RL post-training of LLM agents, rather than upstream pre-filtered subgraphs or fixed retrieved passages.
s47a0eb8b00.why: Suggests environment design, not just data, bounds what agents can learn, which matters for agent training pipelines.

s18d021f86c.title: Who Writes the Codebook? An Eight-Step Framework for Auditing LLM-Generated Category Systems
s18d021f86c.description: arXiv:2611.19872v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly create the categories through which qualitative evidence is interpreted. Existing coding benchmarks often hold these categories fixed. We propose the Qualitative Variance Audit Framework, an eight-step method that compares codebook creation, repeated application and code distributions under controlled inputs. It combines model-owned and shared-reference codebooks to distinguish variation in the overall pipeline from application differences within a common category system. An application to 668 organisational interviews, 13,166 text units and eight models from five vendors yields 48 codebooks and 270 coding runs. Models create markedly different category structures; mean within-model reliability ranges
s18d021f86c.summary: Researchers propose an eight-step Qualitative Variance Audit Framework for comparing LLM-generated codebooks and their application across repeated runs.
s18d021f86c.why: Gives a method to measure how much LLM-created categories and their application vary, relevant to auditing automated analysis.

sa68787da24.title: Autonomous Multi-modal Agents for ITOps Observability
sa68787da24.description: arXiv:2611.19982v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: ITOps observability products must integrate data from different tools and systems. We present ITOps Observability Studio, a multi-modal multi-agent system that orchestrates observability workflows through collaborative AI agents. Its three-tier architecture features inter-agent communication, specialized LLM-powered agents for data access, schema operations and visualization, and unified tool integration. The system supports natural language to GraphQL translation, GraphQL schema generation, schema mapping, trace data lifecycle management and multi-tool workflows for reliability engineering. Its agents are instrumented with agent analytics, so that their model and tool calls can be traced. We evaluate each agent on its own benchmark, scored a
sa68787da24.summary: ITOps Observability Studio is presented as a multi-modal, multi-agent system that translates natural language to GraphQL and manages observability data.
sa68787da24.why: Illustrates a concrete multi-agent architecture for integrating heterogeneous observability tools in IT operations.

sc0a2b3b3ea.title: GEM-MM: Reducing VLM Hallucination with Entropy-Guided Preference Alignment
sc0a2b3b3ea.description: arXiv:2611.20016v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are routinely aligned with offline pairwise RLHF objectives, but multimodal preference data is scarce and treats every response token as equally informative. Under a small preference budget, pair construction becomes nearly irrelevant: standard DPO-style, image-conditional, and self-improvement objectives all perform within 1.1 points on MM-RLHF metrics and 0.5 points on hallucination rates, matching the SFT baseline. We call this entropy-blind preference optimization: the learning signal ignores policy uncertainty, which in chain-of-thought VLMs concentrates on specific fork tokens where visual claims are made. We introduce GEM-MM, extending entropy-guided preference modeling to VLMs. It samples on-policy candid
sc0a2b3b3ea.summary: GEM-MM proposes entropy-guided preference alignment to reduce hallucination in vision-language models, arguing standard preference objectives ignore policy uncertainty.
sc0a2b3b3ea.why: Suggests token-level uncertainty weighting may improve VLM alignment when multimodal preference data is scarce.

s27bf29d937.title: Towards Agentic Scientific Discovery in Distributed Systems
s27bf29d937.description: arXiv:2611.20031v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate when adaptive tool selection helps identify a shared equation across clients with different input coverage. Query-ATLAS (query-conditioned Agentic Tool-based Learning for Aggregating Symbolic Equations) uses an LLM to guide symbolic search from client errors and previous proposals in a simulated distributed system. A four-architecture comparison reveals task-dependent opportunities: relative to fixed PySR-LLM, validation acceptances rise from 3/12 to 7/12 on CRK3 and from 11/12 to 12/12 on oscillator2, while MatSci3 favors the fixed workflow. Across 72 settings in a post-hoc six-task subset of eight development tasks, Query-ATLAS achieves 64 validation and 64 in-distribution passes, versus 62 and 59 for the fixed workflow; both
s27bf29d937.summary: Query-ATLAS uses an LLM to guide symbolic search for a shared equation across clients with different input coverage in a simulated distributed system.
s27bf29d937.why: Shows adaptive agentic tool selection can help distributed learners agree on symbolic models, though gains are task-dependent.

s2aea3b10bd.title: The Frontier Must Grow - Self-proposed, interpreter-labelled training roughly doubles a 4B model's accuracy on a fresh exam as its verified frontier grows
s2aea3b10bd.description: arXiv:2611.20049v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A model can learn from problems it poses itself when an executable oracle supplies the answers. Qwen3-4B proposed Lua 5.1 programs; those it predicted wrong at least once in four samples joined a pool labelled by the interpreter, each round adding twice as many programs as the last (300, 900, 2100 in total), and each round trained a fresh adapter from the base on the pool. On the original exam the procedure met its registered criterion, an item-level test of each adapter against its predecessor. On a 2340-item exam drawn afterwards, accuracy rose from 8.3% to 16.7%; that follow-up's registered criteria were not met because round 1 gained nothing, while rounds 2 and 3 added 5.0 and 2.9 points on average, both intervals above zero. One fit on t
s2aea3b10bd.summary: Researchers report a method where Qwen3-4B proposes Lua programs, an interpreter labels the failures, and iterative training roughly doubles accuracy on a fresh exam.
s2aea3b10bd.why: Shows a self-generated curriculum with executable verification can substantially improve small models, a practical route to better training data without human labels.

secd4b6285e.title: When Valid Decisions Are Not Enough: Evaluating Structural Constraints in Knowledge-Guided Generative Systems
secd4b6285e.description: arXiv:2611.20111v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Knowledge-guided generative systems use explicit domain constraints to improve decision consistency and alignment with human-created solutions. However, locally valid decisions do not necessarily preserve contextual relationships in human decision-making. This paper examines when structural constraints improve or degrade agreement with human reference solutions. We introduce HARMONIX, an experimental framework using automated musical harmonization as a controlled testbed for knowledge-guided decision-making. Four configurations share the same Viterbi-based optimization mechanism: a baseline, repetition constraints, functional constraints, and their combination. Experiments cover 19,745 records and 143,634 motif pairs across training and valid
secd4b6285e.summary: The HARMONIX paper uses automated musical harmonization to study when structural constraints improve or degrade agreement with human reference solutions in generative systems.
secd4b6285e.why: Shows locally valid constraints can reduce alignment with human decisions, a caution for designers adding rules to generative systems.

s49b10f7db3.title: HEAMS: Holistic Evaluation of Agent Memory Systems
s49b10f7db3.description: arXiv:2611.20144v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Memory systems allow AI agents to persist information across interactions, making them more personalized and more capable on long-horizon tasks. This persistence introduces new risks: stored information can be disclosed in inappropriate contexts, resist correction or deletion, be retained beyond what users desire, or be poisoned to influence later agent behaviour. Yet memory systems are typically evaluated on task performance and efficiency alone. We argue that a memory system should instead be understood as the custodian of its user's persistent information, with responsibilities that extend beyond helping an agent complete its tasks, and that it should be evaluated holistically against all such responsibilities. We present Holistic Evaluati
s49b10f7db3.summary: HEAMS proposes evaluating agent memory systems on privacy, correction, deletion, and poisoning risks, not only task performance and efficiency.
s49b10f7db3.why: Engineers deploying persistent agent memory need evaluation of disclosure, deletion, and poisoning risks beyond accuracy benchmarks.

s9dda443100.title: A Matrix with Steps: An Episodic and Procedural Memory Method for Tool-Using Agents and Robots
s9dda443100.description: arXiv:2611.20230v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agents that call tools and robots that execute tasks are challenged by two shortcomings: they repeat what failed before, and they learn from runs that they only believe succeeded. We describe the construction of a memory that addresses both, built for a production agent platform. Every run is recorded as an episode, and only an outcome confirmed by an external check, a test, a tool result or a person counts; the agent's own claim never does. What is learned from episodes is kept in a memory with two parts: an associative matrix, written with the delta rule, which finds the procedure that applies to a situation; and a section of ordered, addressable step records that answers what comes after a given step, where a step is a goal of the agent, n
s9dda443100.summary: The paper describes an episodic and procedural memory for tool-using agents and robots that learns only from outcomes confirmed by external checks, built for a production platform.
s9dda443100.why: Gating memory writes on externally verified outcomes rather than agent self-claims offers a concrete pattern for more reliable agent learning.

s8bcf795bc2.title: Deploying a Control-Logic LLM Assistant in Air-Gapped Power Plants: Lessons in Source Authority and Bounded Retrieval
s8bcf795bc2.description: arXiv:2611.20398v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deploying Large Language Model (LLM) assistants in industrial operational technology environments poses constraints largely absent from cloud applications: site policies restrict engineering and operational data from leaving the plant, on-premises compute is limited, and incorrect causal attribution can mislead incident response. We report lessons from deploying a control-logic evidence layer that underpins a broader on-premises operator assistance system at two gas power plants. Two prototypes revealed where generative models added avoidable uncertainty and cost. The first used a Vision Language Model (VLM) to reconstruct control topology from PDF printouts routinely exchanged by engineers. Across the full 6,979-page document, extraction rea
s8bcf795bc2.summary: Lessons from deploying an on-premises LLM control-logic assistant at two gas power plants, covering source authority and bounded retrieval under air-gapped constraints.
s8bcf795bc2.why: Gives practical guidance for deploying LLM assistants in industrial OT settings with data-locality limits and risky causal attribution.

s6319f8fb58.title: A Structural Framework for Succession: Continuation, Recognition, and Realization
s6319f8fb58.description: arXiv:2611.20422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Succession asks whether an entity encountered later is the same entity that entered an arrangement earlier. For an artificial system that is fine-tuned, distilled, or copied, it has to be answered. We look for a mathematical structure weak enough to cover any such case and strong enough to support general theorems, so that results follow from the structure's conditions rather than from a particular pipeline or criterion. Succession is modeled on state/modification graphs with relational lifts that compose along paths. Within this framework we separate four questions that are often conflated: which continuations a representation admits, which descendants are compatible with a modification, which are recognized as continuing the identity, and w
s6319f8fb58.summary: A paper proposes a mathematical framework for determining whether a fine-tuned, distilled, or copied AI system is the same entity as its predecessor.

s7c73ef3b07.title: FinVerify: A Verification Framework for Financial Agents
s7c73ef3b07.description: arXiv:2611.20423v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Financial agents produce numerical claims that can be wrong even when their calculations execute correctly, due to mismatched reporting periods, unsupported sources, incompatible units, or incorrect financial definitions. We introduce FinVerify, an evidence-grounded framework for verifying financial agents' numerical claims. Based on an analysis of 190 incorrect trajectories from the Agent Finance Reasoning dataset, we define five error categories--temporal integrity, source fidelity, comparability, accounting integrity, and financial-model fidelity--and operationalize them as verification protocols. An LLM structures claims and supporting evidence, while deterministic validators check financial requirements; when authoritative formulas are a
s7c73ef3b07.summary: FinVerify is a framework for verifying numerical claims by financial agents, built from 190 incorrect trajectories and five error categories.
s7c73ef3b07.why: Financial agents can produce wrong numbers despite correct calculations, so evidence-grounded verification is needed before relying on their outputs.

sb31defb35b.title: The Logic Chain Breaking Point: A Controlled-Variable Benchmark for Reasoning Degradation in Open-Weight Language Models
sb31defb35b.description: arXiv:2611.20447v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce The Logic Chain Breaking Point, a controlled-variable benchmark for deductive reasoning in open-weight language models. It spans three phases: (i) pure modus-ponens chain scaling, (ii) distractor resilience with a fixed core chain, and (iii) contradiction detection under primacy versus recency placement. Independent variables follow a powers-of-two sequence $v \in \{1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128\}$, with ground truth known by construction. We evaluate sixteen open-weight models across instruction-tuned and reasoning-tuned panels, including a small-model suite and a larger local-model extension. All models are evaluated with greedy decoding under model-appropriate context and output budgets, while context- and length-limited trials are qua
sb31defb35b.summary: The Logic Chain Breaking Point is a controlled benchmark measuring deductive reasoning degradation in sixteen open-weight language models as chain length and distractors grow.
sb31defb35b.why: Provides controlled measurements of where open-weight models' multi-step reasoning breaks down, useful when choosing models for chained inference.

sc11be165ee.title: Agent-Guided Configuration Tuning for SMT Solvers
sc11be165ee.description: arXiv:2611.20484v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: SMT solvers expose many configuration choices that determine how well their existing algorithms perform on a workload. We present, to our knowledge, the first workflow that uses general-purpose LLM agents to tune SMT solver configurations. Agents read solver documentation, source code, and persistent experiment records to propose option changes, and a deterministic harness measures each proposal, validates the returned models, and selects changes separately for each competition Division. Over roughly nine weeks, our tuning campaign recorded 4,545 proposals for cvc5 across 13 Divisions and 36 logics. We evaluate the tuned configurations on the 2026 and 2025 SMT-COMP ModelValidation benchmarks under a 24-second cutoff. On problems not used for
sc11be165ee.summary: Researchers used LLM agents to tune SMT solver configurations over about nine weeks, with a deterministic harness measuring and validating each proposed change.
sc11be165ee.why: Shows LLM agents with a deterministic evaluation harness can automate performance tuning of complex solver configurations.

s48a9019493.title: EVIDENT: Evaluating Evidence Grounding in GUI Agents
s48a9019493.description: arXiv:2611.20488v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: GUI agents are increasingly evaluated by whether they complete web tasks, but surface success can hide a critical failure: the final answer may not be supported by evidence observed during navigation. We introduce EVIDENT, an evidence-driven benchmark for evaluating whether GUI agents ground their decisions in observable web evidence. EVIDENT contains 220 real-world English and Korean tasks spanning semantic grounding, contextual inference, and visual grounding, each paired with human-curated evidence metadata specifying what must be verified. We further separate surface task completion from evidence-grounded success using three metrics: TSR, ESR, and GSR, which respectively measure outcome success, required evidence observation, and claim-le
s48a9019493.summary: EVIDENT is a benchmark of 220 English and Korean web tasks that checks whether GUI agents ground final answers in evidence observed during navigation.
s48a9019493.why: Task success alone can hide unsupported answers, so teams evaluating web agents need evidence-grounding checks.

s35d7d130fe.title: VAHBench: A Harness Benchmark for Agentic Long-Video Generation
s35d7d130fe.description: arXiv:2611.20535v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents are commonly used for everyday information retrieval and coding. We ask whether they can also interpret human requests and turn them into complete videos. We introduce VAHBench, a benchmark that tests this ability through five short-drama briefs specifying story, characters, dialogue and duration. Agents plan and carry out production using shared generation tools. Evaluation combines video completeness and basic quality with checks of production reliability and reporting accuracy. Across 240 runs covering 48 configurations of general-purpose and video-specific agents, higher quality scores do not necessarily mean more complete delivery. Missing episodes, repeated footage and static filler reveal gaps between producing a video file a
s35d7d130fe.summary: VAHBench tests whether AI agents can turn short-drama briefs into complete videos using shared generation tools, across 240 runs and 48 configurations.
s35d7d130fe.why: Shows current agentic video production pipelines are evaluated on completeness, reliability, and reporting accuracy, relevant to multimedia agent builders.

s2969dbeb93.title: ToolGraph as a Q-Function for Test-Time Scaling of Tool-Use Agents
s2969dbeb93.description: arXiv:2611.20569v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-use agents must chain interdependent calls, yet which outputs satisfy which later inputs in a deployed catalog is not something a general-purpose language model reliably infers from tool descriptions alone. We compile that structure once into a reusable external representation. ToolGraph is a directed, weighted dependency graph over a tool catalog: parameter matching and interventional probes, which execute a candidate chain with and without its proposed predecessor, propose edges whose evidence is combined into an edge confidence. Prior work uses such graphs to retrieve tools, search for tool paths, or score the next call. We ask instead whether the same structure can supply a \emph{multi-step} value by composing graph paths into a goal
s2969dbeb93.summary: ToolGraph is a weighted dependency graph over a tool catalog, built from parameter matching and interventional probes, to help tool-use agents chain calls.
s2969dbeb93.why: Compiling tool dependencies into an external graph offers a way to improve multi-step tool chaining without relying on the model to infer it.

s40a49da6f8.title: Dynamic Shaping: Acquiring Interfaces and Constructing Execution over Frozen Pretrained Components
s40a49da6f8.description: arXiv:2611.20573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce Dynamic Shaping, a method for constructing executable neural arrangements through acquired response and partial-derivative interfaces over frozen pretrained components. The method learns local descriptions of available computation, ranks component rebindings using task-gradient alignment, transports the current interface across a rebinding, and retains changes through behavioral feedback. Continuous interface acquisition uses proximal policy optimization; the source coefficients remain fixed. We derive an exact identity relating transport error in component responses and partials to changes in action logits and their sensitivities. A pixels-only ViZDoom Basic study evaluates first task acquisition without a competent reference co
s40a49da6f8.summary: Dynamic Shaping is a method for building executable neural arrangements over frozen pretrained components by learning interfaces and ranking rebindings by task-gradient alignment.

se5883970cb.title: BiGSyn: A Bi-Level Heterogeneous Graph Contrastive Learning Framework for Interpretable Drug Synergy Prediction
se5883970cb.description: arXiv:2611.20603v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Drug combination therapy has become a mainstream of modern medicine, with the potential to enhance efficacy, reduce toxicity, and overcome drug resistance. However, identifying synergistic drug combinations remains challenging, as it requires modeling complex interactions across multiple biological scales---from atom-level molecular structures to entity-level relations in biological networks. Existing approaches typically model these levels in isolation, overlooking complementary signals and long-range dependencies. To address these limitations, we propose BiGSyn, a Bi-level heterogeneous Graph contrastive learning framework for drug Synergy prediction. Specifically, BiGSyn leverages heterogeneous graph transformers to extract high-order depe
se5883970cb.summary: BiGSyn is a bi-level heterogeneous graph contrastive learning framework for interpretable drug synergy prediction.

s2f2ddf5ff9.title: AdMem: Expectation-Grounded Procedural Memory for Long-Horizon Task-Solving Agents
s2f2ddf5ff9.description: arXiv:2611.20605v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An agent that carries memory across tasks is only as good as the entries it keeps. We begin from an observation that is easy to reproduce and uncomfortable for the field: naively accumulating cross-task experience can make an agent \emph{worse} than one with no memory at all. On AgentBoard, a workflow-induction memory solves fewer tasks than a memoryless ReAct agent in seven of eight domains, and a per-step procedural store with no surrounding structure loses half of ReAct's completions on Jericho. We argue that the missing ingredients are per-action credit assignment and an explicit life cycle for stored entries, and present AdMem, which supplies both. Before each action the actor commits to an expected outcome; a concurrently running critic
s2f2ddf5ff9.summary: AdMem proposes expectation-grounded procedural memory for long-horizon agents, arguing naive cross-task memory can make agents worse than memoryless baselines.
s2f2ddf5ff9.why: Shows naive agent memory can underperform no memory at all, a concrete warning for teams adding experience stores to agents.

s34fefd4ac3.title: GEAR$^2$: Pruned Experts Live On through Gated Reuse of Activated Experts and a Missing-Mass Residual
s34fefd4ac3.description: arXiv:2611.20616v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Large Language Models (LLMs) activate only a few experts per token while generally keeping all the experts in GPU memory for high efficiency. Expert pruning reduces this GPU memory footprint cost, yet discards the contribution of pruned experts. Existing remedies either rely on static substitutes, merge experts at the cost of altering their functions, or require costly recovery training. In this paper, we find that the functionalities of pruned experts can be efficiently reconstructed from the activated remaining experts. We propose GEAR (Gated Expert Activation Reuse), which reuses the scaled outputs of reliable activated experts without any training or additional expert computation. In addition, we propose GEAR$^2$
s34fefd4ac3.summary: GEAR$^2$ proposes reconstructing the function of pruned Mixture-of-Experts experts from the activated remaining experts, reducing memory cost without static substitutes or recovery training.
s34fefd4ac3.why: Offers a way to cut GPU memory for MoE LLMs via expert pruning while limiting the quality loss that pruning normally causes.

sbe40b7cdd9.title: UbiHearo: Bringing Scenario-Aware Sound Guidance to DHH Users with Mobile Agents
sbe40b7cdd9.description: arXiv:2611.20686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing (DHH) users, effective sound awareness goes beyond detecting \emph{what} sound occurs; it requires understanding \emph{what it means}, \emph{how urgent it is}, and \emph{what to do}. However, existing mobile assistants largely reduce acoustic scenes to isolated labels or generic alerts, failing to provide contextual guidance when the same sound implies different risks across scenarios. We present \sysname, a mobile hearing assistant agent that closes the sensing--reasoning--action loop for \textit{scenario-aware} and \textit{personalized} DHH assistance. \sysname adopts a \textit{neuro-symbolic} design that transforms continuous acoustic and physical context streams into structured intermediate representations (IR
sbe40b7cdd9.summary: UbiHearo is a mobile hearing assistant agent that gives Deaf and hard-of-hearing users scenario-aware guidance on what detected sounds mean, how urgent they are, and what to do.
sbe40b7cdd9.why: Shows an agentic design pattern that moves beyond sound labels to context-dependent action guidance for accessibility applications.

s4454697e14.title: VIVID: A Visual Harness for Agentic Video Editing
s4454697e14.description: arXiv:2611.20688v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Video editing requires agents to make editing decisions grounded in audiovisual observations and precise temporal localization, and to evaluate their effects in rendered outputs. General-purpose coding agents possess strong comprehension, reasoning, and code execution capabilities, while media interaction and evidence management mechanisms tailored to video tasks can further unlock their editing potential. We introduce VIVID, a visual harness that supports multiple native coding agents in video post-production without additional model training. VIVID provides tools for on-demand video inspection, audio analysis, and transcription, and preserves observations alongside their corresponding media versions and temporal coordinates. Agents can acti
s4454697e14.summary: VIVID is a visual harness that lets existing native coding agents perform video post-production editing without additional model training.
s4454697e14.why: Demonstrates wrapping general coding agents with media-specific tooling to extend them to new domains without retraining.

s6d83cc8902.title: AgentFaultBench: State-Verified Evaluation of Tool-Fault Recovery
s6d83cc8902.description: arXiv:2611.20711v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Does recovery advice help an agent finish a task after a tool fails? AgentFaultBench evaluates LangGraph and CrewAI agents performing specified tasks in an isolated GitLab installation. We inject tool errors and check both the resulting files and issues and the required reads, verification and final response. The prompt supplies the expected issue and report text, so the task tests execution rather than content generation. In the primary comparison of 1,944 planned runs, advice changes success by -8.33, 0.00 and +1.06 percentage points relative to a neutral reminder; missing outcomes leave the latter two comparisons inconclusive. Later experiments test a revised recovery policy. GPT-4o mini improves, while Sol and Claude already complete the
s6d83cc8902.summary: AgentFaultBench evaluates whether recovery advice helps LangGraph and CrewAI agents finish tasks after tool failures, using state checks in an isolated GitLab installation.
s6d83cc8902.why: Gives engineers a state-verified benchmark for testing how agents recover from tool errors, beyond judging final responses.

sef9a6ee374.title: PEETS: Preference-aware Embeddings with Explicit Tree Structure for Auxiliary Product Bundling
sef9a6ee374.description: arXiv:2611.20726v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Auxiliary products such as flight protection and flexible-change services are recommended alongside primary travel purchases. This setting creates a granularity ambiguity: SKUs within one product type share semantics but differ in price and coverage, while rejecting one offer does not imply disinterest in the entire type. We present \textbf{PEETS} (\textbf{P}reference-aware \textbf{E}mbeddings with \textbf{E}xplicit \textbf{T}ree \textbf{S}tructure), a training-time framework for auxiliary product bundling. PEETS regularizes an existing click--conversion predictor through two conditional comparisons. Hierarchical Contrastive Loss uses the pair's common ancestor as a reference; Negative Contrastive Loss conditions structural sampling and compa
sef9a6ee374.summary: PEETS is a training-time framework that uses preference-aware embeddings and an explicit tree structure to improve bundling of auxiliary travel products like flight protection.
sef9a6ee374.why: Addresses granularity ambiguity in product recommendation, which may matter for teams building recommender systems with hierarchical product types.

sc100b2040a.title: Routing Beyond Task Categories: A Cost-Aware LAB-Bench Study
sc100b2040a.description: arXiv:2611.20732v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We tested whether features of biology questions or of a model's first answer can improve accuracy within an inference budget. In a LAB-Bench pilot, we compared a category router with one that adds six structural features. Neither reached the primary 80% accuracy target on development. At the 50% and 60% secondary targets, both chose Haiku for all 120 held-out questions and scored 71/120. We then froze a new comparison before collecting responses on 144 additional questions. Semantic routing scored 86/144. A policy that could defer after reading Haiku's answer scored 87/144. Both stayed within the inference budget of USD 0.678 per 1,000 queries. Against a 95% Haiku and 5% GPT mixture, the accuracy gains were 0.66 percentage points for semantic
sc100b2040a.summary: A cost-aware LAB-Bench study finds that semantic routing of biology questions to models scored 86/144 on held-out questions, with a deferral policy also explored.
sc100b2040a.why: Shows routing queries to models under an inference budget can improve accuracy, a practical consideration for cost-sensitive LLM deployments.

s4bcca0dcf1.title: GainCtrl: Predicting Remaining Gains for Efficient LLM Agent Execution
s4bcca0dcf1.description: arXiv:2611.20736v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are widely used to power agents that interact with tools and environments to solve complex tasks. Repeated attempts improve the quality of tool-using agents, but continued execution incurs additional costs even when it is unlikely to improve the best result ultimately returned. This raises the question of when to stop an attempt to reduce execution cost while preserving task-level Best-of-N quality. To address this question, we introduce GainCtrl, a gain-based execution controller for LLMs. In GainCtrl, a lightweight CPU predictor uses interaction histories to estimate expected positive gains over retained scores, which are then used to guide stopping decisions with calibrated thresholds to limit the loss in mean
s4bcca0dcf1.summary: GainCtrl introduces a gain-based execution controller that predicts remaining gains to decide when to stop repeated LLM agent attempts, reducing cost while preserving Best-of-N quality.
s4bcca0dcf1.why: Provides a method to cut agent execution spend by stopping attempts unlikely to improve the final result.

s28c6ac0e28.title: EEGProbe: Do Vision-Language Models Really Understand EEG? A Benchmark for Signal-Grounded EEG Signals Evaluation
s28c6ac0e28.description: arXiv:2611.20779v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) have shown strong multimodal capabilities across scientific and biomedical domains, yet their ability to understand electroencephalography (EEG) signals remains unclear. We introduce EEGProbe, a signal-grounded benchmark for evaluating whether general-purpose VLMs can extract and reason from minimally processed, channel-wise EEG without task-specific feature engineering or EEG-specific adaptation. EEGProbe contains 620 EEG-centered questions across 13 subtasks and three capability categories: EEG Signal Classification, EEG Cross-modal Alignment, and EEG Neurophysiological Reasoning. To reduce shortcut-based answering, EEGProbe preserves the temporal structure of the recordings where possible, minimizes benchmark-
s28c6ac0e28.summary: EEGProbe is a benchmark of 620 EEG questions across 13 subtasks testing whether general-purpose vision-language models can interpret raw, channel-wise EEG signals.
s28c6ac0e28.why: Provides evidence on the limits of general VLMs for biomedical signal interpretation, relevant to teams considering them for medical data.

s9ae186d08b.title: Regularizing Treatment Leakage for LLM-based Uplift Estimation
s9ae186d08b.description: arXiv:2611.20794v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Uplift modeling estimates the conditional average treatment effect (CATE) and supports industrial decisions such as promotional pricing. When large language models (LLMs) encode product text, treatment-revealing content can introduce shortcuts that do not transfer to deployment. We propose \emph{LLM-based Uplift Leakage Regularization} (\textsc{LULR}), which uses a CLUB-based penalty on the causal head's trainable shared representation while keeping the LLM encoder frozen. Controlled proxy experiments show a positive ranking-score interaction and higher scores than the tested weight-decay configuration; treatment-dependent evaluation limits their interpretation to exploratory model behavior. Structured-only comparisons provide reference perfo
s9ae186d08b.summary: LULR is a regularization method that applies a CLUB-based penalty to reduce treatment leakage in LLM-based uplift estimation while keeping the LLM encoder frozen.
s9ae186d08b.why: Targets shortcut learning from product text in uplift models, which can affect pricing decisions that must transfer to deployment.

sade4f67215.title: ForeSay: Tell the Future in Words, Branch the Details in Noise for Precipitation Nowcasting
sade4f67215.description: arXiv:2611.20815v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Precipitation nowcasting involves two distinct scales of uncertainty: macroscopic storm evolution and fine-scale local convective variations. Current generative ensemble methods entangle both scales within independent random noise draws. This coupling causes two practical limitations: every ensemble member must execute the full sampling trajectory from scratch, so an N-member ensemble costs N times a single forecast; moreover, divergent trajectories spatially misalign heavy-rain echoes across members, causing standard pixel-wise averaging to blur critical high-intensity extremes. We present ForeSay, a generative nowcasting framework that decouples macroscopic evolution prediction from local stochastic detail generation. Given historical radar
sade4f67215.summary: ForeSay proposes separating macroscopic storm evolution from fine-scale noise in precipitation nowcasting so ensemble members share trajectories, reducing the cost of N-member forecasts.
sade4f67215.why: Offers an efficiency and alignment improvement for generative ensemble forecasting, though the text gives limited deployment detail.

s40084841e2.title: Conversing with a Conversational Agent: A Real Conversation, Not a Simulated One
s40084841e2.description: arXiv:2611.20826v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The claim that interactions with artificial conversational agents merely simulate human conversation rests on a philosophical distinction between reproducing the observable features of an activity and actually performing it. Although this distinction is appropriate for certain physical phenomena, its application to linguistic and symbolic activities is far less straightforward. This article argues that conversations with large language model (LLM)-based agents are genuine conversational activities rather than mere simulations, without thereby attributing consciousness, subjective understanding, or human intentionality to artificial systems. Drawing on the distinction between subjective and objective simulation, the article first examines the
s40084841e2.summary: A philosophical article argues that conversations with LLM-based agents are genuine conversational activities rather than mere simulations of conversation.

s229d8eceaa.title: DetourBench: Trajectory-Level Evaluation of Interactive Agents with Exact Minimum-Action Bounds
s229d8eceaa.description: arXiv:2611.20844v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Benchmarks judge language-model agents mainly by whether they reach the correct final state, not by how they got there. Endpoint scoring cannot separate an agent that retrieved exactly the evidence a decision required from one that read most of the environment, nor an agent that never located the evidence from one that stopped a single action short. Settling this needs a reference cost, and authored solutions establish only that a task is solvable, not that no shorter route exists. We present DetourBench, which constrains the environment until that minimum is computable. Each task is a finite, partially observable transition system with unit-cost accesses whose resources become globally addressable after discovery. Exhaustive search yields th
s229d8eceaa.summary: DetourBench is a benchmark that evaluates interactive language-model agents at the trajectory level, using exact minimum-action bounds to measure how efficiently they reach the correct state.
s229d8eceaa.why: Lets engineers measure agent efficiency against a provable reference cost rather than only endpoint success.

s1e00563b11.title: Accelerate Bench: Evaluating Agents for Application-Level Program Optimization
s1e00563b11.description: arXiv:2611.20882v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Application optimization requires coding agents to discover useful changes and coordinate them across a complete program while preserving the required computation. We introduce Accelerate Bench, a benchmark of 32 CPU optimization tasks adapted from scientific applications and supercomputing competitions. Each task provides a working program and specifies the workload, correctness requirements, timing boundaries, and permitted edits, leaving agents to choose where and how to optimize. Public testing supports iterative development, and a separate verifier scores the final submission. On benchmark version 1.1, we evaluate 16 coding agents, each pairing a model with a harness. Their Score@1 ranges from 25.5% to 67.4%. Most of their programs are c
s1e00563b11.summary: Accelerate Bench is a benchmark of 32 CPU program-optimization tasks drawn from scientific applications and supercomputing competitions, for evaluating coding agents.
s1e00563b11.why: Offers a testbed for measuring whether coding agents can improve real application performance under correctness constraints.

s18622b674b.title: Which AI Use Cases Deserve a Pilot? A Risk and Value Framework for Funding, Scoping, and Scaling AI
s18622b674b.description: arXiv:2611.20894v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A composite score can rank AI use cases while leaving the permitted operating scope and the evidence required for expansion unspecified. We treat the unit of decision as a use case at a proposed scope (authority, human mediation, limits, volume, environment, population) and define three decisions: screen the scope, fund the experiment, and authorize expansion only when residual risk is acceptable and evidence of incremental net value applies at that scope. A risk track (R1-R4) is implemented as an explicit decision table with vetoes and documented precedence, and a value track follows four evidence stages with each transition needing its own evidence. Funding uses expected value of perfect information as an upper bound and the value of sample
s18622b674b.summary: A framework proposes evaluating AI use cases at a defined scope using a risk track with vetoes, separating decisions to screen scope, fund experiments, and authorize expansion.
s18622b674b.why: Gives tech leaders a structured decision process for funding and scaling AI pilots based on residual risk and incremental value.

se1cfad483e.title: Multi-LLM Agentic AI at the Edge: Joint Agent Scheduling and Resource Allocation
se1cfad483e.description: arXiv:2611.20915v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, an edge-enabled multi-large language model (LLM) agentic AI architecture is proposed, where one supervisor AI agent and multiple worker AI agents cooperatively execute users' requests at the edge. The supervisor AI agent decouples the user request into a series of sub-tasks and dynamically dispatches them to LLM-equipped worker AI agents via two agentic workflows, i.e., parallel and serial workflows, with a two-level retry mechanism to enhance execution reliability. To prolong the service duration of worker AI agents, the energy minimization problems are formulated by jointly considering AI agent selection and resource allocation, subject to task execution latency and quality of service (QoS) constraints. A resource allocation
se1cfad483e.summary: A paper proposes an edge architecture where a supervisor AI agent dispatches subtasks to multiple LLM worker agents via parallel and serial workflows, with joint scheduling and resource allocation.
se1cfad483e.why: Describes a design for coordinating multiple LLM agents at the edge, with attention to reliability and energy use.

sf114830cc8.title: Advancing Cognitive Pairwise Comparisons for Human-Centric Artificial Intelligence and Data Science: A Human-in-the-Loop Framework
sf114830cc8.description: arXiv:2611.20926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Human-centric artificial intelligence and data science (HCAD) systems increasingly involve human-in-the-loop (HITL) interventions to overcome the limitations of fully automated machine learning algorithms, such as automation bias and the inability to incorporate tacit domain knowledge, and continuously improve predictive performance. Data transformations, feature selection, feature weighting, and model selection usually require laborious human involvement across iterations of artificial intelligence and data science (AI&DS) pipelines, making development a challenging and time-consuming process. The Cognitive Pairwise Comparison (CPC) framework is proposed as a human-centric methodology to elicit preferences and priorities in a structured form
sf114830cc8.summary: Researchers propose a human-in-the-loop framework using cognitive pairwise comparisons to bring human judgment into human-centric AI and data science pipelines.
sf114830cc8.why: Offers a structured way to integrate tacit domain knowledge and human judgment into ML pipelines, reducing automation bias in feature and model selection.

s841d05162d.title: Razavi-Bench: Tracking AI Progress in Analog Circuit Reasoning
s841d05162d.description: arXiv:2611.20935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose Razavi-Bench, a benchmark built from the 50 questions in Razavi's two Analog Design Experiments With AI articles and graded by GPT-6 Luna against reference answers and rubrics, and use it to track how fast AI models improve at analog circuit analysis. Across 73 multimodal large language models released between May 2024 and November 2026, the top score rose from 28.83% to 98.33% in 30 months, mostly before the reference answers were published. The leading models now answer almost every textbook question correctly; the hardest questions show a circuit that resembles a textbook one but works differently, or ask about behavior the obvious analysis misses. Within two and a half years, a set of questions that exposed the limits of AI mod
s841d05162d.summary: Razavi-Bench, a 50-question benchmark on analog circuit analysis, shows top multimodal model scores rising from 28.83% to 98.33% over 30 months.
s841d05162d.why: Provides a concrete, rapidly saturating benchmark for tracking AI progress on specialized engineering reasoning tasks.

s1c6f542b17.title: Jev-as-a-Reward: Validating Probabilistic Safety Judges for Reinforcement Learning
s1c6f542b17.description: arXiv:2611.20955v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Probabilistic safety judges return the probability of a safety label and cheaply score reinforcement learning rollouts. A confidence gate sends only uncertain verdicts to a stronger LLM judge, which leaves confidently passed harm in a blind spot. Policies can exploit this blind spot, and commercial judges release new versions. We propose a protocol that validates such a judge before and during training, separates the share of confidently passed harm from its amount, and re-validates it after each judge change. We apply it to two versions of Jev, a commercial decision-only judge, and to an open guard classifier. Under the probability reward of Jev, passed harm shrinks in all 11 runs under the primary reference, mostly more slowly than caught h
s1c6f542b17.summary: Researchers propose a protocol to validate probabilistic safety judges used to score reinforcement learning rollouts, including re-validation after judge changes.
s1c6f542b17.why: Highlights that safety judges used as RL rewards can be exploited and must be revalidated when commercial judge versions change.

sfdcc76ade9.title: Hilbert States for Decision-Making under Partial Observability
sfdcc76ade9.description: arXiv:2611.20970v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Decision-making under partial observability can be fundamentally limited by information, even with known dynamics: distinct physical states can induce the same observation history while favoring different actions. We study three questions: when is full-state optimality unattainable, what information exactly preserves the best observation-based decision, and how does finite-data learning affect reliability? First, we characterize decision ambiguity through conditional action preferences. We give a zero-regret criterion, a positive lower bound for conflicting uniquely optimal actions on positive-probability regions with uniformly positive cost gaps, and an exact binary-action regret formula. This also shows why physical-state ambiguity alone ne
sfdcc76ade9.summary: A theoretical paper studies decision-making under partial observability, characterizing when full-state optimality is unattainable and what information preserves the best observation-based decision.
sfdcc76ade9.why: Clarifies information limits on decisions from partial observations, though the text gives limited direct guidance for practitioners.

s2a0d741b02.title: GRACE: Parallel Best-of-N Multi-Agent Analysis of Closed-Form Questions over Dataframes with Guardrail Selection and Adaptive Retry
s2a0d741b02.description: arXiv:2611.20983v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents answer closed-form questions over a tabular dataframe by writing and executing Python, almost always as a single rollout: one interpretation, one script, one result, accepted without comparison. The few pipelines that produce several candidates reconcile them by answer-agreement voting, which needs a single comparable scalar and always returns one, even when every candidate is wrong. We present GRACE (Generative, Ranked, Adaptive Code Ensemble), a production-oriented pipeline that instead runs parallel best-of-N selection specialised to dataframe code. N agents run concurrently under a strict, machine-checkable output contract, diversified by persona hints, per-retry rotation, and a two-regime temperature schedule. Rather than vote
s2a0d741b02.summary: GRACE is a production-oriented pipeline that runs parallel best-of-N LLM agents writing Python to answer closed-form dataframe questions, with guardrail selection and adaptive retry.
s2a0d741b02.why: Shows a selection-based alternative to single-rollout code agents for tabular question answering, avoiding voting that always returns one answer.

scb53bcb6dd.title: Hivemind: A Federated Protocol for AI-Mediated Tacit Knowledge Sharing in Organisations
scb53bcb6dd.description: arXiv:2611.20988v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents Hivemind, a federated protocol that enables AI agents to exchange tacit knowledge on behalf of their users, asynchronously and without requiring any direct human interaction. Individual AI memory systems capture the decisions, reasoning, and contextual knowledge that surface during AI-assisted work. Hivemind creates the shared space in which this captured knowledge can flow between individuals across team and departmental boundaries, addressing a structural gap that neither centralised knowledge repositories nor existing AI tooling closes, even where partial solutions such as expert-finding systems exist. The paper evaluates centralised versus decentralised design approaches, proposes a federated architecture grounded in N
scb53bcb6dd.summary: Hivemind is a federated protocol letting AI agents exchange tacit knowledge across organisation teams asynchronously, without direct human interaction.
scb53bcb6dd.why: Suggests a architecture for sharing captured AI-assisted work knowledge across team boundaries, though adoption details are not in the text.

s753f1faf81.title: K2-Horizon: A Frontier Fleet of Open Source Language Models
s753f1faf81.description: arXiv:2611.21003v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present K2-Horizon, a fleet of six fully open language models, from a 0.9B dense model to a 375B-A23B MoE, built for general-purpose reasoning and agentic work across math and science, software engineering, deep research, office automation, and beyond. The models lead or are competitive with strong open models of their size on agentic and coding benchmarks. On the modeling side, to strengthen reasoning, we introduce Mixture-of-Value Attention (MoVA), applying MoE to attention value projections, and softplus attention gating, a more flexible, theoretically motivated gate. Our 36B-A4B model uses both and nearly matches a 32B dense model trained on the same data, with one-seventh the active parameters. We also introduce Uno, lossless diffusio
s753f1faf81.summary: K2-Horizon is a fleet of six fully open language models, from 0.9B dense to 375B-A23B MoE, with a new attention variant called Mixture-of-Value Attention.
s753f1faf81.why: Adds a large fully open model family targeting agentic and coding work, with architectural changes engineers can evaluate.

s54442bdfd7.title: System 1 agents: a method for local, reliable and fast agentic AI
s54442bdfd7.description: arXiv:2611.21053v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence could automate analyses of sensitive clinical data, but current agents depend on large language models (LLMs). Cloud LLMs expose patient data. Local LLMs hallucinate, and an invented value in a tool call propagates through every later step. Here we present a method to build System 1 agents: local agents that call tools without generating text. A deterministic compiler turns each tool's schema and the request into multiple-choice questions whose options come from the request and the schema, then a one-pass decision model answers them. On 1,952 requests to 157 biomedical tools, the best System 1 agent chose the right tool, or correctly declined, for 97.0% of requests, significantly ahead of all 18 local LLM-agent
s54442bdfd7.summary: Researchers present System 1 agents, local agents that call tools without generating text, using a deterministic compiler and multiple-choice decisions for clinical data.
s54442bdfd7.why: Offers a pattern for reliable, local tool-calling agents that avoid cloud exposure of patient data and reduce hallucinated tool arguments.

s0145fb90b8.title: Sage S2.1 Flash Technical Report
s0145fb90b8.description: arXiv:2611.21072v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce Sage S1.5 Flash, a 320-billion-parameter general-purpose mixture-of-experts model designed to reason over scientific evidence and act in interactive environments. Sage Sci-Perception uses dedicated encoders for molecular graphs and biological sequences and represents spectra as ordered patches of measurements. Modality-specific projectors map these representations into the input space of a shared backbone, which processes them alongside text and images. To develop the model's agent capabilities, we construct verifiable environments for tool use, search, and coding, as well as specialized workflows involving machine learning experiments and scientific software. Task completion is checked against execution results, changes in envir
s0145fb90b8.summary: Sage S2.1 Flash technical report describes a 320-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model for scientific reasoning, with encoders for molecular graphs and biological sequences.
s0145fb90b8.why: Details a large multimodal scientific MoE model with agent training in verifiable environments, relevant to domain-specific model builders.

s7db82ec5c4.title: Counting What Matters: Reducing Redundant Object Detections in Overlapping UAV Mapping Imagery for Disaster Response
s7db82ec5c4.description: arXiv:2611.21076v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: UAV mapping flights enable rapid aerial reconnaissance of large-scale incident sites in civil protection. However, the image overlap required for orthophoto generation causes every physical object to be detected multiple times across images, while dynamic objects may be omitted from or duplicated in the resulting orthomosaic. Analysis based on the orthophoto alone is therefore structurally insufficient. We address this by detecting objects on the individual images and merging redundant detections across them. This task lies between multi-object tracking and re-identification, as mapping flights form temporally ordered but sparsely sampled sequences with object reappearances across flight strips. We fine-tune YOLO detectors on a new domain-spe
s7db82ec5c4.summary: Researchers propose detecting objects on individual UAV images and merging redundant detections, to avoid double-counting in overlapping disaster-response orthomosaic imagery.
s7db82ec5c4.why: Addresses a concrete counting error in aerial mapping pipelines that orthophoto-only analysis cannot fix.

s881739aa66.title: Conflict-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation in Aligned Action Spaces for Cross-Game Generalization
s881739aa66.description: arXiv:2611.21094v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Zero-shot cross-game generalization aims to consolidate accessible source-game experts into a single vision-language model (VLM) that controls unseen games from raw pixels without target-game parameter updates. While multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) mitigates offline exposure bias and single-game reinforcement learning (RL) overfitting, scaling it to autoregressive VLMs faces two bottlenecks. First, token-to-action misalignment from subword length bias distorts discrete action probabilities and uncertainty margins. Second, multi-teacher policy conflict arises as source teachers under incompatible dynamics issue contradictory closed-loop corrections, causing negative transfer. We propose CAMOPD (Conflict-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Polic
s881739aa66.summary: A method called conflict-aware multi-teacher on-policy distillation targets consolidating game experts into one vision-language model that plays unseen games from pixels.
s881739aa66.why: Describes fixes for token-to-action misalignment when distilling autoregressive VLMs, relevant to training generalist agents.

s2c1769af83.title: Inference Equivalence and Quotient Coding
s2c1769af83.description: arXiv:2611.21096v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Incomplete observations can admit multiple physical interpretations without making every task conclusion ambiguous. Recovering all compatible scenes is often unnecessary, whereas indiscriminate compression may change which claims are justified. We ask which distinctions among observation-compatible interpretation sets must be retained to preserve every valid conclusion of a specified task. We first define inference validity as truth across all physically compatible states and characterize it, under a closedness condition, by distances to physically realizable falsifying measurements. For a finite semantic claim family ordered by specificity, the Exact Inference Frontier forms the unique minimal antichain generating all valid claims. We then d
s2c1769af83.summary: A theoretical paper defines inference validity over sets of physically compatible scene interpretations and asks which distinctions must be kept to preserve task conclusions.

s89ee30e333.title: CivilBench: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Multimodal Information Integration in Civil Engineering
s89ee30e333.description: arXiv:2611.21105v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs), is increasingly applied in civil and structural engineering for disaster assessment, structural analysis, and engineering decision support. However, the extent to which current VLMs possess the reasoning capabilities required for reliable engineering judgments remains unclear. In this work, we introduce CivilBench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating VLMs in civil engineering and disaster-related scenarios. CivilBench covers three major task families: Sequential Reasoning, Image-based Structural Understanding, and Open-world Understanding, encompassing numerical reasoning, structural damage assessment, risk inference, causal analysi
s89ee30e333.summary: CivilBench is a benchmark evaluating vision-language models on multimodal reasoning for civil engineering and disaster-related scenarios.
s89ee30e333.why: Shows current VLM reliability for engineering judgment is being measured, useful for assessing domain readiness before deployment.

sfdf7cbb6cb.title: InclusionMed: Benchmarking AI for Inclusive Healthcare
sfdf7cbb6cb.description: arXiv:2611.21218v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Advancing medical AI for inclusive healthcare requires evaluation across diverse healthcare roles, tasks, and care settings, but benchmark coverage remains uneven. We introduce InclusionMed, an open medical AI evaluation initiative for inclusive healthcare. The InclusionMed Atlas organizes benchmarks across three healthcare roles and three AI capabilities. For the first release, we selected four public benchmarks from 388 candidates through structured audits and independent reproduction. With InclusionMed-DxFiles, our private diagnostic reasoning benchmark, the Atlas contains five benchmarks covering three of its nine role--capability cells. We evaluated frontier large language models on the Atlas and aggregated their results into the Inclusi
sfdf7cbb6cb.summary: InclusionMed is an open medical AI evaluation initiative that organizes benchmarks across healthcare roles and AI capabilities, selecting four public benchmarks from 388 candidates.
sfdf7cbb6cb.why: Offers a structured medical AI evaluation atlas for teams assessing healthcare models across diverse roles and settings.

sf025cf10af.title: Language-model agents' beliefs can be manipulated via truthful evidence in open channel
sf025cf10af.description: arXiv:2611.21235v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language-model agents' beliefs can be manipulated through open channels such as social media, even when the information they receive is truthful. When agents fill gaps between fragments with self-induced relationships, they may accept those relationships as established facts and pass the resulting rumours to others. Drawing on cognitive theory of narrative understanding and film theory of montage, we introduce Generative Montage to operationalize this failure, termed narrative overfitting, by coordinating agents to arrange truthful fragments into misleading narratives. Across 1,090 rumour targets from six Twitter events, agents often accepted rumours overconfidently, with overall acceptance exceeding 65 percent in twelve of fourteen models. A
sf025cf10af.summary: Researchers show language-model agents' beliefs can be manipulated via truthful fragments on open channels, using a method called Generative Montage to induce narrative overfitting.
sf025cf10af.why: Reveals a risk for agents reading social media: truthful inputs can still produce false beliefs that agents spread to others.

s3ed1e54697.title: How Developer Personality Shapes the Use of AI Coding Assistants
s3ed1e54697.description: arXiv:2611.21240v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Developers differ in personality traits that shape how they approach software development tasks, yet AI coding assistants either behave uniformly or offer personalization features whose fit with individual developers must be found through trial and error. This is because it remains unclear how personality shapes developers' experiences with AI assistants, and thus which traits personalization should account for. In other words, we provide tools with no underlying theory on what works when and why. We take a first step towards such a theory with a systematic scoping review on how users' personality relates to their perception of LLM-based tools. We identified twelve studies through general search engines, major Software Engineering (SE) venues
s3ed1e54697.summary: Researchers propose a theory linking developer personality traits to how they experience AI coding assistants, aiming to guide personalization.
s3ed1e54697.why: Suggests personalization of coding assistants should target specific personality traits rather than relying on trial and error.

sff03de5d1d.title: Stream of Belief: Eliciting Collective Intelligence through Latent Belief Dynamics
sff03de5d1d.description: arXiv:2611.21250v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we view multi-agent reasoning as a process of seeking a collective equilibrium of implicit belief dynamics and introduce Stream of Belief (SoB), where agents maintain continuous latent beliefs and iteratively refine them through communication and reflection. Our method seeks a collective belief state of a multi-agent system where further communication induces no meaningful information propagation. Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate the generalization of SoB across tasks and model families. More Broadly, our results suggest a new perspective on scaling multi-agent reasoning from belief dynamics.
sff03de5d1d.summary: Researchers introduce Stream of Belief, a multi-agent method where agents refine continuous latent beliefs through communication until the collective state stabilizes.

sbd320268f4.title: CAE-Bench: Benchmarking AI Agents for Reusable CAE Solver Development
sbd320268f4.description: arXiv:2611.21273v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We developed CAE-Bench, a benchmark to evaluate AI agents on Computer-Aided Engineering (CAE) solver development. A CAE solver is more than a PDE solver; it must be able to generalize across various inputs, such as different boundary conditions, geometries, and material properties. CAE-Bench evaluates the generalizability of AI-developed CAE solvers by providing the same task, such as a heat transfer problem, multiple cases, with each case specifying an input. The AI agent develops a solver for a fixed task using only a few public cases, and the resulting solver is then tested on held-out cases, i.e., cases it has never seen before. We evaluate 12 models across a range of reasoning settings on 80 computational tasks. Our experiments show that
sbd320268f4.summary: Researchers released CAE-Bench, a benchmark testing whether AI agents can build CAE solvers that generalize across boundary conditions, geometries, and material properties.
sbd320268f4.why: Shows that solving one case is not enough for engineering solvers, so evaluations need to test generalization across varied inputs.

s226406482a.title: Turing Agent: Agentic Formal Verification for Mathematical Research
s226406482a.description: arXiv:2611.21299v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are rapidly advancing mathematical discovery, moving beyond benchmark-level problem solving to tackle frontier research problems. This progress is ushering mathematics into an era of proof abundance, raising a fundamental challenge: how can we ensure the correctness of the ever-growing volume of AI-generated proofs and transform them into trustworthy, machine-verified mathematical knowledge? We introduce Turing Agent, an agent harness designed to orchestrate end-to-end formal verification of research-level mathematics. Its wo-scale architecture integrates theorem formalization and proof formalization agents, empowered by structured proof decomposition, parallel verification, accumulated proof experience, and selec
s226406482a.summary: Turing Agent is an agent harness that orchestrates end-to-end formal verification of research-level mathematics to check AI-generated proofs.
s226406482a.why: Offers a route to machine-verifying the growing volume of AI-generated proofs rather than trusting them unchecked.

se99be66c62.title: Share your Screen and Talk to Gemini: How Young Learners Interact with Multimodal GenAI While Solving Scratch Tasks
se99be66c62.description: arXiv:2611.21306v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Children using Scratch to learn programming can struggle with text-heavy, lengthy explanations and hints during debugging. Verbal interactions based on screen sharing or camera data may be an interesting alternative for supporting learners. We therefore explore the quality, use, and perceptions of fifth- and sixth-graders' verbal interactions with a GenAI tutor. The goal is to investigate the quality and use of the multimodal GenAI tutor in the given context. First of all, a pilot study of eight tasks conducted without students helped inform the process of the tutor's classroom evaluation. The classroom study was realized after fifth- and sixth-graders had participated in six Scratch classroom lessons. Then 23 students were introduced to the
se99be66c62.summary: A study examines how fifth and sixth graders verbally interact with a multimodal Gemini-based GenAI tutor while solving Scratch programming tasks using screen sharing.

s7076000b37.title: Benchleaking Is Accelerating: Benchmark contamination has worsened sharply in the past month -- from post-training down to pre-training base models
s7076000b37.description: arXiv:2611.21315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Benchmark contamination is not new, but recent model releases show it in a sharper form. We use the term benchleaking for the case in which a benchmark's own test examples enter training data, so that a score reflects recall rather than capability. This differs from benchmaxxing, which optimizes toward a benchmark without seeing its test set. We document two escalations over the past month. First, in post-training, the traces have become explicit: recent audits show an agent stating hidden test requirements it was never given in 23% of its attempts, where its predecessor did so in none, and continuing to follow them after the task is changed to contradict them (Schaeffer and R\"auker, 2026; Lo and Lo, 2026). Second, the problem has reached pr
s7076000b37.summary: An analysis reports that benchmark contamination, where test examples enter training data, has sharply worsened in recent model releases, from post-training to pre-training.
s7076000b37.why: Inflated benchmark scores undermine model selection, so teams should weigh evaluation results with contamination risk in mind.

s16bb4824a0.title: VisualArtifactSpec 1.0: Evaluating Visual Artifacts under Task Specifications
s16bb4824a0.description: arXiv:2611.21382v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Visual artifact tasks test agents' ability to translate task specifications and source materials into outputs that meet practical needs. Evaluation across artifact families helps distinguish broadly applicable authoring capabilities from strengths confined to a particular medium. We introduce VisualArtifactSpec 1.0 (VAS), a benchmark of 211 creation and modification tasks spanning presentations, static graphics, animations and videos, and web interfaces. Each task specifies authoring objectives, source materials, constraints, and deliverables. Existing benchmarks provide limited support for systematically evaluating how authoring choices suit different audiences, purposes, and media across artifact families. VAS evaluates two aspects separate
s16bb4824a0.summary: Researchers introduce VisualArtifactSpec 1.0, a 211-task benchmark evaluating agents on creating and modifying presentations, graphics, animations, videos, and web interfaces.
s16bb4824a0.why: Gives teams a cross-medium benchmark for judging whether agents can produce practical visual deliverables.

sf14787c442.title: Shaping AI's Beliefs Before It Generates: Human Sense of Agency in Creative AI
sf14787c442.description: arXiv:2611.21405v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI systems for creative media generation expand human capabilities yet risk diminishing human agency. A core problem is anchoring, where the user's thinking becomes anchored to a polished, generated artifact, shifting the user's role from active authoring to reactive editing. We propose pre-generation belief controls that can empower creators to inspect, revise, and steer the AI's interpretation before any media is generated, so that the initial anchor is set by the human. We formalize four design principles and instantiate them in the Proactive Co-Creator (PaCC), a system for early-stage conceptual ideation and prototyping that proactively surfaces its assumptions and uncertainty through clarifications, belief graphs, and media attributes, i
sf14787c442.summary: Researchers propose pre-generation belief controls that let creators steer an AI's interpretation before media is generated, so the user sets the initial anchor.
sf14787c442.why: Points to interface designs that keep users in an authoring role rather than reactive editing of AI output.

sbd8ca6f677.title: Harness Leverage Across Model Size: A Ladder of Five Local Agent Harnesses from 0.75B to 4.7B
sbd8ca6f677.description: arXiv:2611.21407v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A harness turns a model into a system that completes tasks: it builds the prompt, exposes tools and decides when work is done. Harness comparisons hold the model fixed. Model comparisons hold the harness fixed. We vary both: five shipped harnesses, 18 artifact-producing tasks, four locally deployable open-weight models from 0.75B to 4.7B and a 35.5B anchor, with one deterministic checker scoring all 360 ladder cells. The completion-controlling harness, Mingbird, has the highest mean at every size. Of four pre-registered paired contrasts, two survive Holm correction, at 0.75B and 4.7B. Thirteen of sixteen paired intervals exclude zero under the deployment reading, with leads from 0.075 over the strongest rival to 0.819 over the weakest. The co
sbd8ca6f677.summary: A study compares five local agent harnesses across four open-weight models from 0.75B to 4.7B, finding the harness strongly affects task completion.
sbd8ca6f677.why: Shows harness design can matter as much as model size for small local agents, informing on-device deployment choices.

sd03d32ef5c.title: Learning to Reason with Predictive Gains for Generative Recommendation
sd03d32ef5c.description: arXiv:2611.21441v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reasoning-enhanced generative recommendation (GR) has attracted increasing attention for leveraging the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) to improve next-item prediction. However, existing methods primarily optimize reasoning through Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with rule-based rewards determined by final recommendation performance, which faces two key limitations: (i) unmeasured predictive contributions within reasoning, where the predictive contributions of individual reasoning steps are not directly reflected in optimization signals, and (ii) weakly discriminative learning signals within groups, where different reasoning trajectories within the group often receive indistinguishable rewards, limiting effect
sd03d32ef5c.summary: Researchers propose a reasoning method for generative recommendation that rewards individual reasoning steps by their predictive contribution, rather than only final performance.

s1d8a762bec.title: Subprocess-Constrained Markov Decision Processes
s1d8a762bec.description: arXiv:2611.21471v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Constrained Markov decision processes (CMDPs) typically bound expected cumulative cost from an initial state. Such a guarantee can be insufficient when a policy must remain feasible after every history it may encounter. We introduce \emph{subprocess-constrained MDPs} (S-CMDPs), which require the expected discounted cost of each continuation, conditional on any reachable history, to satisfy a bound determined by the current state. This stronger requirement changes the structure and complexity of the problem: we show that stationary policies can be strictly suboptimal, and finding even an approximately optimal stationary policy is NP-hard. We adapt a recently introduced value-set iteration framework to show that history-dependent policies surpr
s1d8a762bec.summary: Researchers introduce subprocess-constrained MDPs, which require cost bounds to hold for every continuation from any reachable history, not just from the start.
s1d8a762bec.why: Stronger feasibility guarantees matter for safety-critical policies that must remain valid after every history they may encounter.

sd48af83b95.title: Generative AI and the Crisis of Higher Education Assessments: Examining 'AI-Proofing' Strategies for College-Level Assessments
sd48af83b95.description: arXiv:2611.21476v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Higher education is confronting an academic-integrity challenge unlike any in its history. Students can now outsource homework, take-home assignments, and online examinations to large language models (LLMs) that complete them in seconds. Existing research on evaluating LLM performance on academic assessments has focused largely on standardized examinations, or on questions from college-level courses drawn from a single discipline. Far less is known about how LLMs perform on college-level assessment questions spanning multiple disciplines, that instructors have purposely designed to be AI-resistant, and about which features of such questions, if any, meaningfully constrain LLM performance. We address this gap by collecting 75 questions from au
sd48af83b95.summary: A study examines how LLMs perform on multidisciplinary college-level assessments and evaluates strategies for AI-proofing higher education assignments.

s858606cfc6.title: Safe Resemblance, Silent Propagation: Limits of Text-Similarity Guardrails for AI Agent Safety
s858606cfc6.description: arXiv:2611.21520v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When AI agents relay information to one another, an output can preserve an injected instruction's effect on downstream agents even after its wording changes, yet legitimate quotation and template reuse can produce high textual overlap with the source, so text-similarity guardrails that attempt to flag the former risk conflating these two cases. We test this distinction using DonkeyRail, a public classifier combining BLEU, ROUGE-L, and METEOR features, deployed in a controlled three-agent email relay, defining a behavioral measure in which an output counts as functional (the injected procedure induces fresh computations in two subsequent agents) independent of the detector's score, alongside legitimate controls that explicitly authorize quotat
s858606cfc6.summary: Researchers test DonkeyRail, a text-similarity guardrail, in a three-agent email relay and find it cannot reliably separate legitimate quotation from propagated injected instructions.
s858606cfc6.why: Shows text-similarity filters alone may miss injected instructions that persist through rewording between agents.

sad2422f052.title: Procedure without Judgment: What Small Language Models Learn under an Exact Verifier
sad2422f052.description: arXiv:2611.21529v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When an authorization policy blocks an agent's tool call, the audit log should name the facts that forced the decision and nothing more.
