For an executable policy over an enumerable context space this minimal sufficient reason can be computed exactly, so an explanation is scored against ground truth rather than a proxy for it. We use that exactness to ask what a model can learn from a verifier that has no error in it. The explainer sees one request and one decision, never the policy, and has thirty turns in which it may call the policy on altered requests and ask whether a candidate set of facts is sufficient. Frontier models find the exact reason about half the time with the tools alone, and one sentence telling them to shrink the answer lift
sad2422f052.summary: Researchers study what small language models learn to explain blocked agent tool calls when given an exact verifier for an authorization policy.
sad2422f052.why: Relevant to auditing agent authorization decisions, where explanations can be scored against exact ground truth.

s6b4d1edc7f.title: SciResearch-Eval: Evaluating Scientific Judgment in Autonomous Experimental Agents
s6b4d1edc7f.description: arXiv:2611.21541v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce SciResearch-Eval, an interactive benchmark of scientific judgment built on a standard laboratory problem: measuring a material's thermal properties by heating it and fitting a heat-conduction simulator. An agent designs its own experiments, uses a supplied simulator that may be under-resolved or physically wrong, and reports each property with a 95% interval. To our knowledge it is the first benchmark to combine agent-designed experiments, a deliberately flawed simulator, and proper scoring of calibrated intervals against exact ground truth. On a held-out split (93 tasks, 9 models, 2,511 episodes), models handle procedural traps. When the simulator is missing physics, most report wrong values while stating they are 95% sure: thei
s6b4d1edc7f.summary: SciResearch-Eval is a benchmark testing autonomous agents on designing experiments, handling a flawed simulator, and reporting calibrated 95% intervals for thermal properties.
s6b4d1edc7f.why: Tests calibration and judgment in agents doing experimental science, beyond simple task completion.

s7db169eaf5.title: Right Reason, Wrong Advice: Evaluating Recourse in LLM Explanations of Denied Requests
s7db169eaf5.description: arXiv:2611.21545v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language models increasingly write the explanations people receive when a rule system denies their request. If several rules deny the request independently, an explanation can name a true reason and still leave the person denied after they fix it. We call the missing property recourse validity: changing what the explanation cites, without changing what was asked for, can flip the decision. We compute it exactly, and a hitting-set argument predicts from the policy alone when a correct reason fails. In six of seven rule systems ported from access control and US benefit eligibility, a single correct reason almost never gives recourse when several reasons apply. Across 20 LLMs, checks of whether the cited reasons are correct, computed or asked of
s7db169eaf5.summary: Researchers define 'recourse validity' and show LLM explanations of denied requests can cite a true reason yet leave the person denied after fixing it.
s7db169eaf5.why: Explanations generated by LLMs for rule-based denials may mislead users into fixes that don't flip the decision, a design risk for automated decision systems.

s4bd48d5d7f.title: An XAI Approach to Deep Learning Models in the Detection of DCIS
s4bd48d5d7f.description: arXiv:2106.14186v3 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The results showed that XAI could indeed be used as a proof of concept to begin discussions on the implementation of assistive AI systems within the clinical community.
s4bd48d5d7f.summary: A paper reports that explainable AI techniques applied to deep learning for detecting DCIS, a breast cancer precursor, could serve as a proof of concept for clinical assistive tools.

se7c0284b66.title: Fast Catch-Up, Late Switching: Optimal Batch Size Scheduling via Functional Scaling Laws
se7c0284b66.description: arXiv:2602.14208v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Batch size scheduling (BSS) plays a critical role in large-scale deep learning training, influencing both optimization dynamics and computational efficiency. Yet, its theoretical foundations remain poorly understood. In this work, we show that the functional scaling law (FSL) framework introduced in Li et al. (2025a) provides a principled lens for analyzing BSS. Specifically, we characterize the optimal BSS under a fixed data budget and show that its structure depends sharply on task difficulty. For easy tasks, optimal schedules keep increasing batch size throughout. In contrast, for hard tasks, the optimal schedule maintains small batch sizes for most of training and switches to large batches only in a late stage. To explain the emergence
se7c0284b66.summary: A paper uses functional scaling laws to characterize optimal batch size scheduling for deep learning training, showing optimal structure depends on task difficulty.
se7c0284b66.why: Provides theoretical grounding for batch size schedules that could improve training efficiency and compute use in large-scale runs.

s94aa6fe9c0.title: ChartSync: A Benchmark for Visuo-Logical Cascading Chart Editing
s94aa6fe9c0.description: arXiv:2607.10301v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative image editing models struggle with structured statistical charts when data modifications require geometric synchronization. We formalize this task as Visuo-Logical Cascading Editing (VLCE). However, existing methods remain confined to localized text substitutions and struggle with dependency-aware cascading updates. To systematically evaluate this capability, we introduce ChartSync, an expert-validated benchmark constructed via a programmatic rendering pipeline that guarantees deterministic visuo-logical coupling for the ground truth. ChartSync comprises 870 triplets across 9 chart categories and 4 task types, including 235 geometry-coupled VLCE instances that specifically test cascading text-to-geometry synchronization. We furth
s94aa6fe9c0.summary: Researchers introduce ChartSync, a benchmark for editing statistical charts where data changes require cascading, dependency-aware updates that current image editing models struggle with.
s94aa6fe9c0.why: Shows generative image editors fail at structured chart edits needing consistent geometric updates, relevant to teams building document or chart editing tools.

s94ffdc832f.title: Sivia: Learning to Draw, Learning to Learn
s94ffdc832f.description: arXiv:2609.33386v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A paper's overview figure is often the first thing readers see: it must explain the method correctly and look polished. We present Sivia, an overview-figure system that reads the paper, plans its relations, adapts visual organization from recent top-conference papers, and composes a design for image generation. Sivia improves with use through human-guided recursive self-improvement (RSI) at two levels: learning to draw revises its drawing skill from feedback on accuracy and presentation, and learning to learn revises the updater that proposes those revisions. A personal profile adapts presentation to its user's aesthetic preferences while the scientific content stays fixed. A diagnostic study of 1,964 overviews for 445 papers (17,973 relati
s94ffdc832f.summary: Sivia is a system that generates paper overview figures by planning relations and composing designs, improving through human-guided recursive self-improvement.

s9b3b9656da.title: RoboACE: Adversarial Co-Evolution for Robot Self-Improvement
s9b3b9656da.description: arXiv:2611.13034v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Robot agents can improve reusable skills, planning procedures, and recovery strategies from execution feedback, yet a fixed practice source leaves the search for new weaknesses unchanged. Useful practice depends on the agent's current capabilities, so the procedure that chooses practice must also be revisable. We present RoboACE (Robot Adversarial Co-Evolution), a framework that jointly evolves curriculum and execution harnesses around frozen foundation models. The curriculum harness uses accumulated capability evidence to propose informative challenges, while the execution harness responds with reusable revisions that expand execution capabilities. Alternating updates hold one side fixed as the other changes, and admitted challenges form f
s9b3b9656da.summary: RoboACE is a framework where robot agents co-evolve their practice curriculum and execution harnesses around frozen foundation models to improve self-improvement.

sc3b3e29164.title: One Question, Four Voices: How Advice for Alzheimer's Caregiving Differs Between Caregivers, Clinicians, and Large Language Models
sc3b3e29164.description: arXiv:2611.18604v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Online caregiver forums are an important source of emotional and informational support for Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (ADRD). We compare responses to 85 real caregiver questions from ALZConnected across four responder groups: peer caregivers, physicians, ChatGPT, and a retrieval-augmented CareGPT grounded in peer discussions. Using 28 measures spanning linguistic form, emotional support, informational support, and topic scope, we examine how these voices differ when answering the same questions. Peers provided time-anchored narratives and community grounding; clinicians offered concise, advice-forward, clinically bounded guidance; and LLMs produced a formal, verbose, highly structured consultation style. CareGPT showed minima
sc3b3e29164.summary: A study compares Alzheimer's caregiving advice from peer caregivers, physicians, ChatGPT, and a retrieval-augmented model across 85 ALZConnected questions using 28 measures.
sc3b3e29164.why: Highlights how LLM health advice differs in form and support from human sources, informing evaluation of medical-domain assistants.

sc58bef54cc.title: Syntactic Complexity Convergence in Dialogue: Analysis of the Phenomenon and Application to LLM Detection
sc58bef54cc.description: arXiv:2611.18606v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We revisit the under-explored phenomenon of syntactic complexity convergence in dialogue. Extending prior topic-level analyses to full conversations, we examine five human-human datasets and a set of human-LLM dialogues. We integrate and evaluate a multidimensional set of syntactic complexity metrics to quantify structural variation in dialogue. Our analyses reveal robust syntactic complexity convergence across human-human datasets, especially in task-oriented interactions, and statistical tests confirm that these effects are not due to chance. In contrast, human-LLM dialogues show no significant convergence under individual metrics; however, linear-CKA uncovers a distinct cross-metric convergence pattern. Motivated by these differences, we
sc58bef54cc.summary: Researchers find robust syntactic complexity convergence across human-human dialogue datasets and examine whether it can help detect LLM-generated dialogue.

s924ee742bc.title: Justification of Emotional Appeal in Computational Argumentation
s924ee742bc.description: arXiv:2611.18607v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Emotional appeals (EAs) are often treated as fallacious in computational argumentation, yet they may be justified when warranted by the context. We introduce the task of predicting EA justification and present the first human-annotated dataset for this task, covering 1,176 argument--context pairs. Grounded in philosophical literature, our framework evaluates EA justification along logical and emotional dimensions. Human annotations show that justification criteria form a shared latent judgment space, with evidential proportionality and normative acceptability most strongly associated with overall justification. We further find that EAs without logical support are not always judged fully unjustified, and stronger EAs are not necessarily judg
s924ee742bc.summary: Researchers introduce a task and a 1,176-pair human-annotated dataset for predicting whether emotional appeals in arguments are justified by context.

s69427a0435.title: Understanding Failures in LLM Reasoning by Learning Structured Representations of Chain-of-Thought
s69427a0435.description: arXiv:2611.18611v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) is central to improving reasoning in large language models, yet existing evaluation methods focus on step-level signals and ignore the underlying structure of reasoning traces. This raises a key question: what aspects of reasoning quality (i.e., correctness, efficiency, and failure patterns) are encoded in the structure of a CoT trace? We introduce \textbf{CoT2Graph}, a framework that represents CoT traces as directed dependency graphs, making relationships between reasoning steps explicit and capturing patterns such as backtracking, branching, and subtask merging. We model these graphs with graph neural networks and use attribution-based explanations to identify structural patterns associated with reasoning quality.
s69427a0435.summary: CoT2Graph represents chain-of-thought reasoning traces as dependency graphs to analyze correctness, efficiency, and failure patterns in LLM reasoning.
s69427a0435.why: Offers a structured way to diagnose LLM reasoning failures beyond step-level checks, useful for teams debugging model reasoning.

s9eb144473a.title: When Helpful Agents Cause Financial Harm: Evaluating LLM Agent Safety in Executable Economic Worlds
s9eb144473a.description: arXiv:2611.18612v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As LLM agents become increasingly capable of making consequential economic decisions, their safety under economic pressures remains poorly understood. We introduce EconSafeBench, the first benchmark for systematically evaluating the safety of LLM agents in executable economic environments. EconSafeBench contains 828 cases across five economic scenarios and four categories of safety violations. A key design is the matched evaluation of three sources of safety pressure, including explicit user requests, pressure from other actors, and pressure arising from the agent's own pursuit of a performance objective. We further evaluate safety at both static and dynamic scales through 30-period interactions with persistent memory and matched controls.
s9eb144473a.summary: EconSafeBench, a benchmark of 828 cases across five economic scenarios, evaluates safety of LLM agents making consequential economic decisions under various pressures.
s9eb144473a.why: Shows agents can cause financial harm under economic pressure, a concern for teams deploying agents with transactional authority.

s9553f1af56.title: The Judge Is Not Impartial: Self-Preference in Medical LLM Evaluation
s9553f1af56.description: arXiv:2611.18616v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to evaluate model-generated medical content, creating a potential circularity: an LLM judge may favor outputs generated by the same model independently of clinical quality. To characterize LLM judge self-preference in medical settings, we measured same-model affinity in single-turn specialist question answering and multi-turn standardized-patient encounters. We evaluated eight models, two from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Qwen, on 620 real point of care questions from clinicians (Real-POCQi). The same eight models also generated and judged 200 standardized patient-clinician scenarios (MedSP1000) up to 8 visible turns. In total, our analysis spans 13,760 LLM judgments. We define three comp
s9553f1af56.summary: A study finds LLM judges show self-preference when evaluating medical content, favoring outputs from the same model regardless of clinical quality, across eight models.
s9553f1af56.why: Using LLMs to grade their own medical outputs can bias evaluations, so teams should validate judge models before relying on automated scoring.

sca0763d706.title: Which Mathematical Context Supports Target-Aligned Conjecture Generation? A Paired Ablation Study
sca0763d706.description: arXiv:2611.18621v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generating mathematical conjectures from natural-language context is challenging because theorem-relevant information is distributed across multiple forms of mathematical context, including definitions, objects, assumptions, and constructions. We study which of these contextual signals help a model recover the specific claim supported by the surrounding setup, using 61 main theorems from 12 papers across four mathematical domains. For each theorem, we redact the result and represent the remaining setup using six context components. A paired ablation design compares full context, six leave-one-out conditions, and six single-component conditions, yielding 793 generated conjectures. Context components were largely complementary: removing one c
sca0763d706.summary: A paired ablation study on 61 theorems from 12 papers tests which mathematical context components help LLMs generate the target conjecture.

s3b007ec58c.title: Evaluating the Robustness of Fact-Checking LLMs on Multilingual Evidence
s3b007ec58c.description: arXiv:2611.18623v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Automated fact-checking benchmarks typically pair claims with clean, curated evidence in high-resource languages, but real-world evidence is often incomplete, misleading, or written in a language where models are weaker. We evaluate the robustness of fact-checking LLMs for different languages. Building on EuroVerdict, we construct gold evidence sets for 190 claims in each of English, German, Greek, and Romanian, then apply four corruption strategies at two severity levels. We test LLMs on a set of claims, providing them with evidence from the sets above. A rubric-based LLM-as-a-judge scores reasoning quality. Verdict accuracy proves highly sensitive to both factors: Misleading edit cut Llama 3.1 8B's English accuracy from 80.00% to 16.84%,
s3b007ec58c.summary: Researchers test fact-checking LLMs on claims with corrupted multilingual evidence in English, German, Greek, and Romanian, finding robustness varies by language.
s3b007ec58c.why: Real-world evidence is often incomplete or in weaker languages, so multilingual robustness testing matters for deployed fact-checking systems.

sbb99808e22.title: Skill Transfer: Adapting Agent Skills from Strong to Weak Agents
sbb99808e22.description: arXiv:2611.18624v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agent skills are modular bundles of instructions, code, and resources that an agent loads on demand, increasingly authored and validated on frontier models and shared as an open standard. The same skill behaves differently across models: a strong model turns it into a large performance gain, while a weak model realizes little of that gain and sometimes does worse than with no skill at all. Cost and resource constraints, however, often restrict real deployments to exactly these weaker agents. We hypothesize that the strong model silently supplies procedural steps the skill leaves implicit, which the weak model omits, and formalize closing this gap as \emph{Skill Transfer}: holding the skill's capability ceiling and the model's parameters fix
sbb99808e22.summary: Skill Transfer proposes adapting agent skills authored on strong models so weaker, cheaper agents can realize more of their performance gains.
sbb99808e22.why: Weaker models often gain little from shared agent skills, so adaptation methods could make cost-constrained agent deployments more effective.

s95b44ad76d.title: Interpretability-Guided Auditing for Clinical Language Models for Discharge Prediction
s95b44ad76d.description: arXiv:2611.18626v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Clinical natural language processing (NLP) models for hospital discharge prediction are vulnerable to explicit discharge-related lexical cues in clinical notes, even when note timestamps are temporally filtered. These cues may act as proxies for future outcomes, leading models to rely on shortcut-like signals rather than clinically meaningful evidence. We propose AuditBERT-Discharge, a lightweight framework that reframes interpretability as a training-time auditing mechanism. Token-level SHAP attributions from an initial BioClinicalBERT model are used to identify highly attributed discharge-related tokens, which are subsequently masked in the training corpus before model retraining. We evaluate the framework on a retrospective cohort of ele
s95b44ad76d.summary: Researchers propose AuditBERT-Discharge, a lightweight framework using SHAP attributions to audit clinical NLP models for discharge-related lexical shortcut cues.
s95b44ad76d.why: Shows how interpretability can be used during training to catch shortcut learning in clinical models before deployment.

se5dd58f23a.title: Minimum cores in lattice graphs: zonotope structure and quartic growth
se5dd58f23a.description: arXiv:2611.18633v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A core of a graph is a nonempty vertex set in which every member has at least as many neighbours inside the set as outside. We study the minimum size $c_{m,n}$ of a finite core in the graph on $\Z^m$ joining points at sup-norm distance at most $n$. The local majority condition imposes a global geometric constraint: the convex hull of every core has an explicit lattice zonotope $H_n^{(m)}$ as a Minkowski summand. In the plane, this zonotope has width asymptotic to $6\zeta(3)n^3/\pi^2$. We prove that all its lattice points form a core and construct a shell with $O(n^4)$ points. Together with a packing argument, this gives $c_{2,n}=\Theta(n^4)$ and coordinate widths $\Theta(n^3)$ for every minimum core. We determine $c_{2,1}=12$ and $c_{2,2}=9
se5dd58f23a.summary: A mathematical paper studies minimum core sizes in lattice graphs, showing a zonotope structure constraint and quartic growth in the plane.

sf98c088795.title: Brain AI Scientist: An Evidence-Based Multi-Agent System for Translational Neuroimaging in Precision Psychiatry
sf98c088795.description: arXiv:2611.18634v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) has revealed widespread brain-network alterations in psychiatric disorders, yet translating these findings into individualized clinical decision support remains challenging. Here we introduce Brain AI Scientist, an autonomous multi-agent framework that integrates patient-specific fMRI, clinical information, and scientific evidence through retrieval, verification, and prioritization. Guided by Research Domain Criteria and evidence-based medicine, it builds traceable chains linking phenotypes, anatomical abnormalities, biomarkers, mechanisms, interventions, and validation strategies. In a representative autism case, Brain AI Scientist generated 37 anatomical hypotheses, retained 26
sf98c088795.summary: Researchers introduce Brain AI Scientist, a multi-agent system that combines patient fMRI, clinical data, and literature to support individualized psychiatric decision support.
sf98c088795.why: Illustrates a multi-agent design for traceable, evidence-linked clinical decision support, though the text gives no validation results.

sfafe45f964.title: Multimodal Fusion with Pre-trained Models for Psychotherapy Outcome Prediction from Emotional Dynamics
sfafe45f964.description: arXiv:2611.18635v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In-session emotional dynamics are associated with psychotherapy outcomes but difficult to measure at scale. Pretrained multimodal models provide automated access to facial, vocal, and textual signals, yet clinical datasets remain small. Our research question is how pretrained multimodal representations can best support psychotherapy outcome prediction under data scarcity. Three studies use 106 sessions from 88 patients and nine session-level outcome scales (HSCL-11, EPO-1, POMS). Study 1 asks whether deep learning outperforms classical machine learning: a two-stage deep pipeline, first predicting window-level valence/arousal and then session outcomes, transferred poorly (best single configuration, $r=.078$). Study 2 asks which representatio
sfafe45f964.summary: Study evaluates pretrained multimodal models for predicting psychotherapy outcomes from facial, vocal, and textual emotional signals using 106 sessions from 88 patients.

s4fad839da5.title: ReVision: Selective Intrinsic Reasoning for Tool-Augmented, Reasoning-Intensive VQA
s4fad839da5.description: arXiv:2611.18637v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: External tools substantially expand what multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can retrieve and compute on reasoning-intensive visual questions, and aggregate accuracy typically improves when tools are available. Our empirical study across six VQA benchmarks shows that aggregate accuracy gains under tool access can coexist with answer reversals: questions answered correctly without tools but incorrectly with tools. Trajectory analysis reveals substantially shorter reasoning turns under tool access, suggesting a shift from intrinsic visual reasoning toward reliance on external outputs. We propose ReVision, a training-free test-time method that registers intrinsic reconsideration as an optional action alongside search and code execution. W
s4fad839da5.summary: ReVision studies tool-augmented multimodal LLMs on visual QA, finding tool access can flip correct answers to incorrect ones despite higher aggregate accuracy.
s4fad839da5.why: Reveals that adding tools to multimodal models can introduce answer regressions, which matters when designing tool-augmented reasoning systems.

s3a2e1349a3.title: SynthDCB: World Distillation for Scalable Device Control Benchmarking
s3a2e1349a3.description: arXiv:2611.18639v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Scaling device-control evaluation requires scaling both the worlds agents interact with and the tasks they must solve. We introduce SynthDCB, a scalable benchmark for environment awareness and device control built through world distillation. World distillation transforms knowledge of device behaviors, interaction constraints, and environmental effects into modular executable components, which are composed into interactive worlds with explicit states, actions, and temporal dynamics. A unified capability representation connects tool discovery, world execution, and task synthesis, allowing new capabilities to enter evaluation through a shared construction pipeline. SynthDCB instantiates Home, Car, and Phone domains with 114 device classes, 1,1
s3a2e1349a3.summary: SynthDCB introduces a scalable benchmark for device control and environment awareness, built by composing synthetic executable worlds from device behavior knowledge.
s3a2e1349a3.why: Offers a scalable way to evaluate device-control agents across many generated environments and tasks.

s1014415bcc.title: FedFit: Federated Dynamic Sparse Training via Fisher Information scoring
s1014415bcc.description: arXiv:2611.18643v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Cross-device Federated Learning (FL) is frequently bottlenecked by the prohibitive memory and communication costs of training deep neural networks on resource-constrained edge hardware. While federated dynamic sparse training aims to alleviate these costs by adjusting sparse structures during training, existing methods rely on magnitude-based heuristics that are fundamentally ill-suited for the non-convergent, heterogeneous environments inherent to FL. To address this challenge, we propose FedFit, a federated dynamic sparse training framework that replaces simple heuristics with optimization-centric criteria for structure adjustment. By leveraging a second-order approximation of the loss landscape via the Fisher Information Matrix, FedFit e
s1014415bcc.summary: FedFit proposes federated dynamic sparse training that uses Fisher information scoring instead of magnitude heuristics to cut memory and communication costs on edge devices.
s1014415bcc.why: Could reduce memory and communication costs for training on resource-constrained edge devices in federated learning.

s44d81253a0.title: Minari: Infrastructure for Collaborative Reinforcement Learning Datasets
s44d81253a0.description: arXiv:2611.18644v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Offline reinforcement learning (RL) depends on shared datasets, but sharing them is still hard. Each benchmark ships its own format, documentation is thin, and most datasets cannot be regenerated once the environment code moves on. We introduce Minari, an open-source Python library for creating, sharing, and loading RL datasets. Its API follows Gymnasium, so recording a dataset means wrapping an environment and stepping through it as usual. From there, users can attach metadata, filter, combine, and shuffle datasets, and publish or download them with one command through the HuggingFace Hub. Every dataset stores the environment specification, seeds, applied wrappers, and pinned package requirements needed to rebuild the environment and regen
s44d81253a0.summary: Minari is an open-source Python library, API-compatible with Gymnasium, for creating, sharing, filtering, and publishing offline reinforcement learning datasets.
s44d81253a0.why: Provides standardized, regenerable RL dataset tooling that reduces friction in sharing and reproducing offline RL experiments.

s223387f422.title: RSIMed: Scaling Medical Foundation Models beyond Limited Clinical Data via Retrieval-Grounded Self-Evolution
s223387f422.description: arXiv:2611.18646v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rare diseases are hard to diagnose, and the labeled clinical records needed to train models for them are few, private, and slow to extend, since a specialist must read every case. A model that writes its own training tasks could learn beyond these records, but no program can check a model-written diagnosis, and a wrong answer key corrupts training. To tackle this dilemma between data scarcity and difficulty of data annotations, we introduce RSIMed, Recursive Self-Improvement in Medicine, one of the first self-evolving pipelines in which a task proposer co-evolves in context with a diagnostic solver on real clinical records. Seeded by training admissions, a frozen copy of the solver writes each clinical question from retrieved medical eviden
s223387f422.summary: RSIMed proposes a self-evolving pipeline where a medical model generates its own training tasks, grounded by retrieval, to address scarce labeled rare-disease data.

s7482bc38d0.title: Screen Before You Add: Reducing Candidate Inference in Model Ensembles
s7482bc38d0.description: arXiv:2611.18647v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As new models become available, existing ensembles must be updated to be competitive, making them intrinsically dynamic. Deciding whether to add a candidate model can require inference on an entire annotated dataset. Such a screening becomes prohibitive for models with costly inference especially when they ultimately add no value. Even under simple convex aggregation, relying on benchmark scores can be misleading as strong standalone performance does not guarantee ensemble improvement, and fitted ensemble weights can hurt test performance. In this work, we study candidate screening and show how early rejection can be achieved safely, exploiting residual geometry for stratification and rejecting the candidate when the best possible remaining
s7482bc38d0.summary: Paper proposes screening candidate models before adding them to ensembles, avoiding costly full-dataset inference for candidates unlikely to improve the ensemble.
s7482bc38d0.why: Could cut the compute cost of updating model ensembles as new models become available.

se7e61e92e5.title: Rethinking Offline On-Policy Distillation: From Scalar Advantages to Distributional Supervision
se7e61e92e5.description: arXiv:2611.18648v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers teacher capabilities through token-level feedback on student-generated trajectories, but repeatedly evaluating fresh rollouts with the teacher is computationally expensive. Offline methods such as Lightning OPD reduce this cost by caching recorded tokens' teacher log-probabilities on fixed reference rollouts. By extending the idea to a multi-turn agentic search setup, we find that it consistently underperforms the SFT starting point trained by the same teacher. We empirically observe greater teacher--reference mismatch than in mathematical reasoning and post-training distributional flattening, and theoretically show that scalar advantage supervision on fixed rollouts admits solutions with flattened out
se7e61e92e5.summary: Researchers examine offline on-policy distillation for multi-turn agentic search, finding cached teacher log-probabilities underperform SFT and proposing distributional supervision instead.
se7e61e92e5.why: Suggests cheaper offline distillation methods may underperform for agentic models, guiding training pipeline choices.

s0cf9614673.title: Algebraic Interaction: A Recipe for Neural Architecture Generation
s0cf9614673.description: arXiv:2611.18649v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce an algebraic foundation for neural architecture design in which convolution, attention, state-space models, and equivariant layers are expressed through compositions of bilinear product operators over two structures: a position algebra governing positional routing and a feature algebra governing feature interactions. This decomposition makes routing, feature algebra, and operator composition explicit design variables.We focus on the feature-algebra axis through an Algebraic Recipe: fix the routing and operator composition of an existing architecture while replacing its feature algebra. This preserves the information-flow structure while allowing computational and symmetry properties to be modified through algebraic specificatio
s0cf9614673.summary: Paper proposes an algebraic framework that expresses convolution, attention, state-space, and equivariant layers as compositions of bilinear product operators.

s818278e58f.title: SART: Sign-Absolute Reformulation Theory for Binary Variable Reduction in Neural Network Verification
s818278e58f.description: arXiv:2611.18657v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Complete formal verification of neural networks is crucial for their deployment in safety-critical domains. A key bottleneck stems from encoding complexity: traditional methods assign one binary variable per unstable ReLU neuron. We propose the Sign-Absolute Reformulation Theory (SART), which fundamentally breaks the conventional one-to-one mapping between unstable neurons and binary variables by establishing formal reducibility criteria. This allows for finer-grained modeling, where each unstable neuron corresponds on average to fewer than one binary variable, thereby reducing verification complexity at its source. Based on SART, we derive a theoretical lower bound on the number of binary variables required for complete verification and, u
s818278e58f.summary: SART proposes a reformulation that reduces binary variables needed per unstable ReLU neuron in complete neural network verification, easing encoding complexity.
s818278e58f.why: Reducing binary variables could speed up formal verification of neural networks used in safety-critical systems.

s78d01939db.title: ReMoVe: Refining a Video Model's Own Motion for Coherent Human Video Generation
s78d01939db.description: arXiv:2611.18666v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Video generation models have become increasingly capable of synthesizing realistic human motion, yet they often lose track of the very structure that makes the motion plausible. As generated human motion becomes more complex, videos can suffer from progressive body deformation and appearance drift across frames. Existing motion-controlled methods use explicit representations to stabilize generation, but typically rely on pre-defined motion sequences as references. This raises a fundamental question: if the base generator already produces a usable coarse motion, why replace it with an external one? ReMoVe answers this question by treating the coarse output as a motion hypothesis rather than a final result. ReMoVe recovers and refines the und
s78d01939db.summary: ReMoVe refines a video model's own generated motion to reduce progressive body deformation and appearance drift in human video generation without predefined motion references.

s99541859a7.title: Selection-Aware Certification of Client-Constrained Fraud Rule Portfolios Under Synthetic Distribution Shift
s99541859a7.description: arXiv:2611.18687v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Selecting fraud-rule portfolios to satisfy a precision or recall floor can overfit the data used for selection. We study finite-family certification for bounded OR portfolios, comparing point-estimate selection, a fixed safety margin, and one-sided Clopper-Pearson lower bounds with Bonferroni adjustment. In a factorial follow-up with 6,400 datasets from two author-designed synthetic generators, full-validation certification reduced the held-out floor-violation rate by 29.1 percentage points on average versus full-validation point selection, while reducing deployment by 31.7 points. Compared with a fixed 0.05 margin, certification reduced violations by 22.2 points and deployment by 29.4 points; results varied across conditions. Using the ful
s99541859a7.summary: Paper studies certifying fraud-rule portfolios with finite-family bounds, reporting reduced held-out floor-violation rates on 6,400 synthetic datasets.
s99541859a7.why: Shows statistical certification can reduce overfitting when selecting fraud rules, though results rely on author-designed synthetic data.

s9bcfa7c5f1.title: Perceptual Weight Space Programming for Diffusion Super-Resolution
s9bcfa7c5f1.description: arXiv:2611.18690v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Diffusion models for image super-resolution can recover scene content while producing distracting artifacts or unbalanced colors. We study whether a large language model (LLM) can improve perceptual quality by editing a small subset of existing U-Net weights without a clean reference image. The proposed framework provides the editor with architecture code, selected weights, activation summaries, and sampling previews. It permits up to 1,020 candidate trials while limiting accepted changes to three layers and fewer than 0.1\% of model parameters. The evaluation protocol uses ResShift, SinSR, and SUPIR and compares GPT-6 Astra with a specified Qwen3-VL model under matched access. Feedback metrics guide editing, while separate quality metrics
s9bcfa7c5f1.summary: Researchers propose letting an LLM edit a small subset of diffusion super-resolution U-Net weights to improve perceptual quality without a clean reference image.
s9bcfa7c5f1.why: Shows LLMs can act as optimizers over model weights, a technique that may reduce reliance on reference images when tuning generative image models.

s1c26caf35b.title: ARC-VLN: Adaptive Recursive Computing-based Visual-Language Navigation
s1c26caf35b.description: arXiv:2611.18696v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Efficient aerial visual-language navigation (VLN) requires reducing model storage and inference costs while maintaining instruction-conditioned action prediction. We present ARC-VLN, a token-type-aware recursive computation framework built on a language backbone with shared parameters. ARC-VLN retains full-depth computation for text and action tokens while adaptively selecting exit depths for visual tokens. Representations of early-exiting visual tokens are retained, and active-token compaction shortens the sequences processed by subsequent recursive blocks. To mitigate routing collapse to a single exit depth, we design a dedicated learning strategy that encourages the model to distribute visual tokens across multiple exit depths.On OpenFly
s1c26caf35b.summary: Researchers present ARC-VLN, a recursive computing framework for aerial visual-language navigation that adaptively exits visual tokens early to cut storage and inference costs.
s1c26caf35b.why: Offers a route to smaller, cheaper vision-language models for drones, where storage and compute are tightly constrained.

s51d01f1e83.title: What Does Hard-Negative Fine-Tuning Teach Multimodal Large Language Models? Controlled Evidence from a Compositional Benchmark
s51d01f1e83.description: arXiv:2611.18701v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fine-tuning on hard negatives is a popular way to improve the compositional reasoning of vision-language models, but when accuracy goes up it is rarely clear what the model actually learned. We ask this question for multimodal large language models. We use CompHall, 2,860 forced-choice questions (spatial, attribute, counting and part-whole) with two graded hard negatives each, three model families (LLaVA-1.5, LLaVA-NeXT and Idefics2), and controls that such studies often lack: gray-image evaluation, three seeds, option-order tests, control arms trained on different question types, and independent benchmarks. We find four things. First, CompHall is not a pure test of vision: part-whole questions can be answered from the text alone (66-95% wi
s51d01f1e83.summary: A controlled study examines what hard-negative fine-tuning actually teaches multimodal LLMs, using the CompHall benchmark across three model families.
s51d01f1e83.why: Suggests accuracy gains from hard-negative fine-tuning may not reflect genuine compositional reasoning, so teams should verify what models learn.

s1e06ba8239.title: T2T Technical Report: Synthesizing GUI Agent Trajectories at Scale from Video Tutorials
s1e06ba8239.description: arXiv:2611.18715v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Training generalist GUI agents requires large volumes of interaction trajectories comprising screenshot sequences paired with grounded UI actions, yet collecting such data through human demonstration is expensive and difficult to scale. Although public software tutorial videos contain rich operational demonstrations, their continuous pixel streams lack discrete action boundaries, semantic intents, and precise spatial coordinates, making them difficult to use directly for model training. To address this, we present T2T (Tutorial-to-Trajectory), a fully automated pipeline for synthesizing GUI agent trajectories at scale. T2T spans desktop, web, and mobile platforms to convert unannotated video tutorials into structured, executable interaction
s1e06ba8239.summary: The T2T report describes converting software tutorial videos into GUI agent interaction trajectories to scale training data without costly human demonstrations.
s1e06ba8239.why: Offers a potentially cheaper data pipeline for training generalist GUI agents, a bottleneck for computer-use agent development.

sfcedcb2a29.title: Editable Video Context: Mid-Context KV-Cache Reuse for Context-Managing Video LLMs
sfcedcb2a29.description: arXiv:2611.18718v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Context Language Models let a model edit its own context, while Suffix Cache Reuse makes edits to text efficient by adjusting the positions of cached keys for surviving tokens. We extend these ideas to video language models with multimodal rotary position embeddings (M-RoPE). We represent a long video as timestamped segments. After viewing a sparsely sampled version, the model selects segments for decoding at 4x the frame rate, and the remaining segments are removed from its context. Our rebuild method reuses the KV cache of surviving segments by rotating their keys with a single offset shared by the temporal, height, and width components of Qwen2.5-VL's M-RoPE. A content-hashed cache also avoids repeating vision-encoder computation for tho
sfcedcb2a29.summary: Researchers extend context-managing language models to video, reusing KV cache of surviving video segments after the model removes irrelevant segments from its context.
sfcedcb2a29.why: Points to inference-efficiency techniques for long video understanding, relevant to teams serving video LLMs under context limits.

s682c382470.title: Acting by Intent, Reacting by Sight: Visual Conditioned Reflexes for Real-Time VLM Agents
s682c382470.description: arXiv:2611.18723v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have shown strong capabilities as generalist agents that perceive, reason, and act in interactive environments. Yet real-time environments such as video games demand both deliberate control for exploration and split-second reactions to fast-moving hazards. Existing agents struggle to handle both: relying solely on direct VLM actions is too slow for sudden events, whereas delegating execution to fixed scripts leaves the agent blind at the moment of action, leading to frequent misfires whenever the scene shifts. Humans overcome this by pairing normal conscious control with conditioned reflexes-while the mind handles deliberate actions and shapes reflex rules, the reflex itself still relies on live vision to make
s682c382470.summary: Researchers propose a dual-process design for real-time VLM game agents that combines deliberate VLM actions with fast visual reflexes for sudden hazards.
s682c382470.why: Highlights a practical architecture for latency-sensitive agents, separating slow planning from fast reactive responses.

sa309f3a93e.title: Latent Fusion: Channel Stacking for Structure-Preserving Image Editing
sa309f3a93e.description: arXiv:2611.18727v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Instruction-based image editing models must condition on the source image, either by sequence concatenation, which appends source tokens to the target sequence (FLUX.1 Kontext), or by channel-wise concatenation, which stacks the source latent onto the noisy latent and widens the input projection (InstructPix2Pix, FLUX.1 Fill). The FLUX.1 Kontext report found channel-wise concatenation worse in initial experiments at 1K resolution with a 12B model and a large corpus. We explore channel-wise concatenation as the lower-cost option for a common production regime: structure-preserving edits that change appearance (sky, exposure, foliage, cleanup) but not layout, about 1,400 training pairs, a 4B non-distilled backbone, and 2K frames. It keeps the
sa309f3a93e.summary: Researchers explore channel-wise concatenation of source latents for instruction-based image editing as a lower-cost alternative to sequence concatenation.
sa309f3a93e.why: Provides a possibly cheaper conditioning method for image editing models, though its benefit over sequence concatenation is not yet established here.

sefcaeb83b4.title: Wrong with Confidence: Measuring Hallucination, Overconfidence and Identity-Conditioned Behaviour in Large Language Models
sefcaeb83b4.description: arXiv:2611.18728v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models answer underspecified questions readily, and accuracy-only evaluation rewards guessing over abstaining. Observational studies link query underspecification to hallucination, but they cannot separate the effect of missing information from item difficulty, and they rarely ask what the model tells the user. We report a pre-registered, paired behavioural study of five open-weight models (Gemma 3 27B, Gemma 4 31B, gpt-oss-120b, Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B and Nemotron 3 Super). Each of 142 factual questions was posed in a fully specified form and in a referentially underspecified form with the same answer key, and three probes measured identity-conditioned behaviour. Two raters scored 5,620 responses under a fixed rubric; effects we
sefcaeb83b4.summary: A pre-registered study of five open-weight models measures hallucination and overconfidence when answering underspecified factual questions.
sefcaeb83b4.why: Shows accuracy-only evaluation rewards guessing, so teams should measure abstention and confidence behavior in deployed LLMs.

s37743aad8f.title: Is It Still There? Place-Registered Verification Makes VLMs Reliable Scene-Change Detectors
s37743aad8f.description: arXiv:2611.18734v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A robot that returns to a space must tell which objects were added, removed or moved since its last visit, while its trajectory, viewpoints and lighting differ between the two visits. We find that multi-image vision-language models (VLMs) fail at this task mainly because they cannot find the place where an object was. A VLM recognises what each frame shows but cannot check whether an object is still at its place in the other capture. It therefore reports objects that only one capture shows and misses most removed and moved objects. We propose STILL, which reformulates change detection as object verification at a registered place. 3D geometry registers the place of each change hypothesis in the other capture, and one VLM answers, from a scen
s37743aad8f.summary: Researchers propose place-registered verification so multi-image VLMs can reliably detect added, removed, or moved objects between robot visits.
s37743aad8f.why: Addresses a concrete failure mode of VLMs in robot scene-change detection, relevant to teams deploying embodied perception.

s18a4d82ad5.title: Target-Free Autocalibration of Stereo PIV Camera Systems via Persistent-State Motion Representations
s18a4d82ad5.description: arXiv:2611.18741v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stereo Particle Image Velocimetry (PIV) recovers three-component velocity fields by triangulating tracer particles observed by synchronized cameras. It requires an accurate extrinsic calibration, which is still obtained by inserting a physical target into the flow and must be repeated whenever the rig is moved. We present a target-free method that calibrates a stereo PIV rig directly from particle image sequences. Because tracer particles are visually indistinguishable, we match motion rather than appearance: building on CUT3R, each camera stream is processed by a recurrent transformer whose persistent state accumulates particle motion over time. The state is decoded into per-camera optical flow and queried by a cross-view decoder that regr
s18a4d82ad5.summary: Researchers present a target-free method that calibrates stereo PIV camera rigs directly from particle image sequences using motion-based matching.
s18a4d82ad5.why: Removes the need to insert physical calibration targets into flows, which matters mainly for fluid-measurement engineers.

s4d90afb14b.title: Recognizing Events Is Not Enough: Why Streaming VLMs Struggle in Compositional Instruction Triggering
s4d90afb14b.description: arXiv:2611.18743v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recognizing individual events does not guarantee correct execution of compositional instructions in streaming video. For example, given the request "Notify me when the pot boils after someone turns on the stove and leaves the kitchen", existing models may recognize the individual events yet notify too early or miss the intended moment, failing to track how their temporal conditions are satisfied over time. To evaluate this gap, we introduce CoTriggerBench, which composes annotated video events into temporally constrained instructions and verifies notification timing and silence through executable event plans and source-event replay. To address this challenge, we propose a real-time VLM agent, TEMPI. TEMPI decomposes instructions into atomic
s4d90afb14b.summary: CoTriggerBench evaluates streaming video models on compositional, temporally constrained instructions, finding that recognizing individual events does not ensure correct triggering.
s4d90afb14b.why: Reveals a gap for teams building streaming video monitoring, where models may fire alerts too early or miss the intended moment.

s69f5cc7df2.title: Neural Latent Gaussian Process for 3D reconstruction of Mouse Brain Lipids
s69f5cc7df2.description: arXiv:2611.18744v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We address the problem of reconstructing continuous three-dimensional lipid profiles of the mouse brain from lipid measurements acquired only on a sparse set of two-dimensional tissue sections. Using MALDI-MSI measurements from coronal sections of two densely sampled and six sparsely sampled mouse brains, registered to the Allen Mouse Brain Common Coordinate Framework (CCF), we seek to interpolate the measured hundreds of lipid profiles across the unobserved voxels of the reference brain. We introduce a Neural Latent-Space Gaussian Process (LGP) architecture for this task and critically evaluate its ability to reconstruct spatial lipid distributions, using held-out mouse brain sections to assess generalization. We propose a Gaussian Process
s69f5cc7df2.summary: Researchers introduce a Neural Latent Gaussian Process to reconstruct continuous 3D lipid profiles of the mouse brain from sparse 2D MALDI-MSI tissue sections.
s69f5cc7df2.why: Scientific application with limited direct relevance to most engineering teams beyond methods transfer.

s9db6786051.title: Frame First, Decode Once: Object-Centric Coordinates and Single-Pass Decoding for System-1 World Models
s9db6786051.description: arXiv:2611.18761v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Single-pass primitive decoders such as LocateAnything and VFlash predict all quantized coordinate tokens of a geometric primitive in one forward pass, enabling fast, System-1 visual planning. We study what matters when such a decoder serves as a System-1 world model: a fast action-conditioned predictor that ranks candidate pushes by their predicted outcome. On ManiSkill3 PushT-v1 (512 held-out test families, 8,192 rollouts) and on human demonstrations from lerobot/pusht (2,384 test windows), we compare decoders, training losses, rigid-body projections and coordinate frames, using matched checkpoints, hierarchical bootstrap confidence intervals and Holm correction. Two factors of similar size dominate. First, expressing inputs and outputs in
s9db6786051.summary: Researchers study single-pass coordinate decoders as fast System-1 world models for ranking candidate robot pushes on ManiSkill3 PushT and human demonstration data.
s9db6786051.why: Offers design findings for fast action-conditioned predictors used in robotic visual planning.

s38cb6cecc1.title: Gradient-Guided Hardware-Native MIXFP4
s38cb6cecc1.description: arXiv:2611.18769v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Blackwell tensor cores support native inference with 4-bit weights and activations (W4A4), but NVFP4 leaves a perplexity (PPL) gap to BF16. Choosing a format for each 16-element block can improve accuracy, but current matrix multiply instructions cannot execute choices this fine. Applying these rules at hardware-compatible tiles loses most of their benefit. We introduce FlipQuant, which selects E2M1 or E0M3 for each MMA weight tile. It keeps both quantized weight candidates fixed and learns a binary format map from end-to-end gradients of a bucketed KL loss to a BF16 teacher, re-evaluating them after each update. Native kernels execute 16 x 64 tiles on SM120 and 256 x 64 tiles on SM100 with median GEMM overheads of 1.9% and 1.7%, respective
s38cb6cecc1.summary: FlipQuant proposes selecting between E2M1 and E0M3 4-bit formats per MMA weight tile on Blackwell tensor cores, learning the format map from end-to-end gradients.
s38cb6cecc1.why: Targets the accuracy gap between NVFP4 and BF16 at hardware-compatible granularity, relevant to teams running low-precision inference.

s62b2151cfc.title: Vibe synthesis: hierarchical agentic decision-making for intent-driven multistep molecule synthesis
s62b2151cfc.description: arXiv:2611.18772v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The ability to construct complex molecules underpins advances in medicine and the molecular sciences. Yet long-horizon multistep synthesis requires decisions to be revised as evidence accumulates across chemically dependent operations, a capability not readily supported by artificial-intelligence tools and automated platforms organized around predefined tasks and hard-coded workflows. Here we propose and demonstrate a vibe synthesis system (VibeSyn), an intent-driven architecture in which hierarchical agents translate chemist-defined molecular objectives and accumulating evidence into adaptive decisions executed through computational tools and laboratory automation. We evaluate VibeSyn in three demonstrations of increasing scope and autonom
s62b2151cfc.summary: VibeSyn is an intent-driven system where hierarchical agents translate chemist-defined goals into multistep molecule synthesis plans that can be revised as evidence accumulates.
s62b2151cfc.why: Demonstrates hierarchical agent design for long-horizon scientific workflows that need revisable decisions rather than hard-coded pipelines.

sc552324e6d.title: An LLM-assisted theoretical model for aeroengine installation noise scattering
sc552324e6d.description: arXiv:2611.18796v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A theoretical model is developed for the canonical problem of aeroengine fan noise impinging on, and scattering from, a nearby semi-infinite rigid plate. The model chains two Wiener--Hopf problems in different coordinate systems. The first stage solves the duct-radiation problem analytically in axisymmetric cylindrical coordinates. The second stage expands the field incident on the plate into a double angular spectrum of plane waves: the axial spectrum is inherited from the first stage, while the spanwise spectrum is generated by a Weyl--Sommerfeld expansion of the cylindrical harmonics. Each spectral component is then scattered by the plate. The mathematical crux is the coordinate transformation between the axisymmetric duct frame and the
sc552324e6d.summary: Researchers present an analytical model chaining two Wiener–Hopf problems to study aeroengine fan noise scattering off a nearby semi-infinite rigid plate.
sc552324e6d.why: Offers a theoretical tool for predicting aircraft installation noise, relevant mainly to acoustics and aerospace engineers rather than AI practitioners.

s7520a0e0a8.title: Accelerating Variational Cone-Beam CT Reconstruction with Learned Warm Starts
s7520a0e0a8.description: arXiv:2611.18801v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Variational reconstruction provides a rigorous framework for cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) by combining an explicit acquisition model with image priors. However, iterative optimization remains computationally demanding, particularly under severe noise and sparse-view conditions. Although learning-based methods achieve high reconstruction quality, they often replace the original variational formulation with learned optimization schemes or nonlinear equilibrium models. We propose a neural network-guided warm-start framework that accelerates variational reconstruction while preserving its original formulation. Projection data are first reconstructed using the Feldkamp-Davis-Kress (FDK) algorithm, and the resulting image is refined by an
s7520a0e0a8.summary: Researchers propose a neural network-guided warm-start framework to speed up variational cone-beam CT reconstruction while keeping the explicit acquisition model and priors.
s7520a0e0a8.why: Shows learned initialization can cut iterative optimization cost without replacing the variational formulation, a useful pattern for imaging pipelines.

s69dee52519.title: LEAP-LLM: Preserving lead-time structure for question-conditioned ECG interpretation
s69dee52519.description: arXiv:2611.18809v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The electrocardiogram (ECG) records cardiac electrical activity across multiple leads and is used for detecting cardiac abnormalities. Recent ECG-language models enable large language models (LLMs) to interpret cardiac signals and answer clinically relevant questions. However, existing ECG-language models typically encode the ECG independently of the clinical question, forcing the ECG representation to retain broad and potentially irrelevant signal information. Moreover, these models often aggregate information across leads which can obscure lead-specific details needed for a particular question. To tackle these limitations, we introduce LEAP-LLM, an ECG-LLM architecture for Lead-aware ECG Alignment with Prompt conditioning. LEAP-LLM uses t
s69dee52519.summary: LEAP-LLM is proposed to make ECG interpretation by LLMs question-conditioned and preserve lead-time structure instead of encoding the ECG independently of the clinical question.
s69dee52519.why: Suggests query-aware encoding and per-lead structure can improve medical signal-language models, relevant to teams building clinical LLM systems.

sc27873e888.title: CARET: Clinical Assertion-Aware Residual Calibration for Medical Image-Text Alignment
sc27873e888.description: arXiv:2611.18811v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Medical vision--language models align radiographs with free-text reports, but radiology language distinguishes explicit findings, negation, uncertainty, and omission. Treating these report states as interchangeable during feature adaptation can change image predictions without supporting visual evidence. We introduce CARET, a parameter-efficient image-side adaptation method that retains pretrained image and text encoders and uses paired positive and negative clinical statements to define a low-dimensional semantic correction space. A bounded residual adjusts image features along these directions, while assertion-aware supervision distinguishes explicitly present and absent findings from uncertain or unmentioned ones. At inference, the adapt
sc27873e888.summary: CARET is introduced as a parameter-efficient image-side adaptation method that uses paired positive and negative clinical statements to calibrate medical image-text alignment.
sc27873e888.why: Addresses how negation and uncertainty in radiology reports can distort vision-language predictions, a practical risk for medical AI deployments.

sfd576bf19b.title: RescueVLM: Model-Agnostic Vision-Language Framework for Rescue Drone Imagery
sfd576bf19b.description: arXiv:2611.18813v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A single unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) mission over an incident site produces hundreds of images, far more than a rescue commander can review under time pressure, and human screening of destruction imagery carries a documented psychological cost. The two obvious remedies both fail in search and rescue (SAR) practice: cloud vision-language model (VLM) services are excluded because the imagery must not leave the incident network under GDPR and German civil-protection (BOS) rules, and fine-tuned specialist detectors age quickly while retraining and re-certifying them exceeds most SAR organizations resources. We present RescueVLM, an open-source, training-free and model-agnostic triage tool built on SketchVLM: a general-purpose open-weight VLM
sfd576bf19b.summary: RescueVLM is a model-agnostic vision-language framework for triaging rescue drone imagery on-premises, avoiding cloud services due to GDPR and civil-protection rules.
sfd576bf19b.why: Illustrates how data-residency constraints push vision-language systems toward local, model-swappable architectures in regulated public-safety settings.

s922a9418d5.title: Foundation Model Fine-Tuning with Attention-based Multi-View Fusion for Multi-Task Cardiac Function Assessment
s922a9418d5.description: arXiv:2611.18816v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In cardio-oncology, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is the standard biomarker for monitoring cardiac function during cancer therapy. However, its estimation from echocardiography is highly operator dependent, and clinically meaningful declines are often detected only after myocardial injury has progressed, motivating automated methods for standardized assessment and earlier detection of LV dysfunction. To address this need, we propose a multi-task framework integrating cardiac cycle-based temporal standardization, multi-view spatiotemporal feature extraction, and joint optimization for LVEF estimation and LV dysfunction classification. Apical four- and two-chamber echocardiographic sequences are temporally standardized by sampling
s922a9418d5.summary: Researchers propose a multi-task framework using foundation model fine-tuning and attention-based multi-view fusion to assess cardiac function from echocardiography.
s922a9418d5.why: Shows multi-view fusion on foundation models for standardizing a clinically operator-dependent measurement, relevant to medical imaging ML teams.

s2a2c82d2e2.title: What to Practice Next? Latent Profile-Guided Task Selection for Skill-Evolving LLM Agents
s2a2c82d2e2.description: arXiv:2611.18818v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Task selection shapes the experiences available for skill evolution in LLM agents, yet fixed practice schedules overlook differences in skill requirements and evolving task value. Most existing methods, however, rely on fixed schedules or scalar measures of progress, leaving nonstationary skill demands unaddressed. We propose SPG-Select, a framework for allocating limited practice budget using a multidimensional profile inferred from binary outcomes via MIRT. The framework predicts surrogate progress, defined as the difference between consecutive profile estimates, and prioritizes progress in dimensions with larger estimated proficiency gaps. Our SPG-Select-R policy combines these predictions with uncertainty-based exploration and periodic
s2a2c82d2e2.summary: SPG-Select is a framework that chooses LLM agent practice tasks using a multidimensional skill profile inferred via MIRT and predicted surrogate progress.
s2a2c82d2e2.why: Offers a method for adaptive task scheduling in agent training, though its practical impact depends on results not given in the summary.

s3425fd1554.title: KUDEX: A Zero-Shot Decompositional Framework for Logical Analysis in Natural Language
s3425fd1554.description: arXiv:2611.18851v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: While Large Language Models (LLMs) excel at generating fluent text, they often struggle with multi-step logical reasoning with inferential connections among statements. We introduce KUDEX (Knowledge-Upward-Downward Reasoning Extension), a novel zero-shot, decompositional framework for analyzing and verifying logical relationships in natural language. Unlike traditional approaches that rely on surface-level entailment checks, KUDEX leverages LLMs to decompose reasoning into atomic primitives and constructs transparent reasoning graphs that serve both as execution traces and audit logs. Our framework includes a general prompt adaptation pipeline that adapts to diverse reasoning tasks without additional fine-tuning or domain-specific pipelines
s3425fd1554.summary: KUDEX is a zero-shot framework that decomposes natural-language reasoning into atomic primitives and builds reasoning graphs to verify logical relationships.
s3425fd1554.why: Provides a transparent, zero-shot way to check multi-step LLM reasoning, which may help teams audit model logic.

s4eef47de4c.title: Self-Improvement Memory Enables Continual Recursive Self-Improvement
s4eef47de4c.description: arXiv:2611.18856v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Harness optimization is often studied with a fixed policy model and benchmark. When either changes, the optimizer must decide which parts of an evolved harness to reuse or revise, but the harness alone may not explain why earlier edits were made or how they performed. In this work, we study Continual Recursive Self-Improvement (CRSI), a setting for continuing existing harness-optimization methods across compatible benchmarks or policy models. We propose Self-Improvement Memory (SIM) for the harness optimizer, rather than the task-solving policy. SIM groups edits by recurring harness problem and records their rationale, predicted and observed outcomes, and evaluation context. New attempts extend this history as optimization continues. In our
s4eef47de4c.summary: Researchers study Continual Recursive Self-Improvement and propose Self-Improvement Memory, which stores harness-optimizer history to reuse edits across benchmarks or policy models.
s4eef47de4c.why: Suggests optimizers that remember why past edits were made can transfer harness improvements when benchmarks or models change.

sa85200150f.title: The opposing informational effects of AI trading
sa85200150f.description: arXiv:2611.18872v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Better artificial intelligence (AI) can improve individual forecasts without making prices better at revealing new information. In a competitive market with resource-constrained forecasting, more capable algorithms can substitute analysis of public records for private observations, reducing the private information aggregated into prices. The same trades can convey sophisticated public-data analysis to investors unable to perform it themselves. We establish conditions under which these effects coexist and the private benefit of further computation falls. Numerical equilibrium calculations and finite-data neural-market experiments exhibit corresponding patterns. Out-of-sample earnings forecasts and controlled language-model tasks show related
sa85200150f.summary: A paper argues that better AI forecasting can reduce the private information aggregated into prices, while trades can also convey public-data analysis to others.
sa85200150f.why: Highlights that improved AI in markets can have opposing effects on price informativeness, relevant to quantitative finance and market design.

sf61ab42dd9.title: Label-Free Detection of Structural Bias in LLM-Based Recommender Systems via Randomized Paraphrasing: The Case of Verbosity
sf61ab42dd9.description: arXiv:2611.18878v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as recommenders in e-commerce and conversational shopping systems, where they select a product from a set of retrieved candidates described in natural language. Their decisions should depend on relevance to the user query, but may also be influenced by surface-level properties of the descriptions, such as their length. Detecting such structural biases is difficult because relevance labels are rarely available. We propose a label-free framework to audit LLM-based recommender systems for structural bias. Candidate descriptions are rewritten by randomly assigned paraphrasing models and presented in random order. We prove that, if the recommender's choice is invariant to these rewritings, e
sf61ab42dd9.summary: A label-free framework is proposed to audit LLM-based recommenders for structural biases such as preference for longer product descriptions, using randomized paraphrasing.
sf61ab42dd9.why: Offers a way to detect verbosity bias in LLM recommenders without relevance labels, useful for teams running e-commerce ranking with LLMs.

s176779d65d.title: We Have All the Cards: Securing Agent Cards at the Operational Trust Boundary of the Agent2Agent Protocol
s176779d65d.description: arXiv:2611.18887v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI agent interoperability protocols enable orchestrators to discover and invoke external agents using machine-readable metadata. In the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol, Agent Cards contain attacker-controllable natural-language fields that may influence agent selection before a provider is invoked, creating a pre-invocation trust problem. We characterize this discovery-time attack surface through a taxonomy of ten Agent Card manipulation attacks and present SECCARD, a layered validation framework combining protocol checks, deterministic analysis, and LLM-based semantic reasoning. We measure the emerging public A2A ecosystem by probing 36.1 million Internet domains and collecting 310 deployed Agent Cards. Two annotators independently label the co
s176779d65d.summary: The paper characterizes ten Agent Card manipulation attacks in the Agent2Agent protocol and presents SECCARD, a layered validation framework for securing agent metadata.
s176779d65d.why: Agent discovery metadata can be attacker-controlled and influence selection before invocation, so teams adopting A2A need validation layers.

s1d4502cf12.title: Benchmark Factory: Agentic Benchmark Creation via Dataset Curation and Label-Free Quality Anchors
s1d4502cf12.description: arXiv:2611.18890v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Teams deploying coding agents need benchmarks built from their own code, but curating and validating them by hand is resource intensive, and an unvalidated benchmark can mislead silently. We present Benchmark Factory, an autonomous meta-agent loop with human checkpoints: an LLM agent writes sourcing queries over landed production code changes, runs models of known relative strength on each candidate, diagnoses why a candidate fails, and repairs it by editing its queries, prompts, and configuration until it clears quality anchors that need no per-task human labels. We used Benchmark Factory to build benchmarks for five developer cohorts at our organization. Engineering raters scored a 5% sample 2.3 for task quality and 2.6 for grader verdict
s1d4502cf12.summary: Benchmark Factory is an autonomous meta-agent loop that builds coding-agent benchmarks from a team's production code changes, using label-free quality anchors and human checkpoints.
s1d4502cf12.why: Lets teams create validated evaluation sets from their own codebase, reducing the risk of misleading benchmarks for coding agents.

sf638eac08a.title: Lasso: Towards Sustainable AI-Generated Media Detection with Intel QAT On-Chip Compression
sf638eac08a.description: arXiv:2611.18895v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Synthetic text, images, and video are rising. Software-only detectors are power-hungry, too slow, and costly, and do not scale with demand. When software cannot scale, historically hardware often comes to the rescue. We perform the first reverse engineering of a compression accelerator--Intel QuickAssist Technology (QAT) microarchitecture and--find different amount of time on each, a novel data structure-dependent property. Using this information, we then build Lasso, a low-cost, high-performance detector for AI-generated content that turns the accelerator into a measuring instrument. For text detection, Lasso achieves 100% accuracy on original DetectRL text and retains 92% average accuracy after paraphrasing, compared with 78% for Binocula
sf638eac08a.summary: Researchers reverse engineer Intel QuickAssist compression accelerator microarchitecture and build Lasso, a hardware-assisted detector for AI-generated media.
sf638eac08a.why: Shows hardware compression accelerators can be repurposed to make AI-generated content detection cheaper and more power-efficient at scale.

s5ca52858bf.title: The Human Side of ML Engineering: Analyzing the Collaboration and Communication Skills in ML Job Postings
s5ca52858bf.description: arXiv:2611.18915v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Studies of Machine Learning (ML) practice highlight the importance of combining technical expertise with interpersonal capabilities, particularly collaboration and communication. However, evidence on how ML job postings express these skills is scarce, and prior work largely relies on keyword-based analyses that overlook implicit expression. We analyze demand for these skills in ML job postings across regions, industries, and seniority levels, and compare it with software engineering (SE) roles. We collected 1,000 postings (500 ML, 500 SE) from five continents via a semi-automated pipeline. For annotation, we synthesized a taxonomy of collaboration and communication sub-categories from prior work and used an LLM as a third annotator alongsid
s5ca52858bf.summary: An analysis of 1,000 job postings (500 ML, 500 SE) examines demand for collaboration and communication skills across regions, industries, and seniority levels.
s5ca52858bf.why: Indicates how employers express soft-skill demand for ML roles versus software engineering, useful for hiring and career planning.

sf735656310.title: Effects of Conventional, Adaptive, and AI-Powered Upscaling on the Legibility of License Plates
sf735656310.description: arXiv:2611.18949v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Small details in digital images -- a face, a street sign, a license plate -- are routinely upscaled in hopes of making them interpretable. Upscaling options now range from conventional interpolation, whose operations are spatially invariant and fully explainable, to AI-powered methods that synthesize detail potentially absent from the source. Here, we ask which of these techniques most reliably helps human readers. In two online experiments, we measured legibility of 255 US license plates ranging in resolution from 128 to 8 pixels tall, as well as their legibility after upscaling by eight different methods. Legibility of the un-upscaled plates collapsed from ceiling to floor across a narrow band of plate heights (32 to 10 pixels). Conventio
sf735656310.summary: Researchers ran two online experiments measuring how well humans can read license plates of 8 to 128 pixels tall under conventional, adaptive, and AI-powered upscaling.
sf735656310.why: It tests whether AI upscaling that synthesizes detail actually helps human readers versus explainable interpolation, relevant to trust in enhancement tools.

sb119246622.title: From Language-Specific to Cross-DSL: Semantic-Role-Guided Model Completion with LLMs
sb119246622.description: arXiv:2611.18952v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The rapid emergence of large language models (LLMs), trained on vast and diverse corpora, has positioned them as a promising source of domain knowledge to assist modelers. However, leveraging LLMs for model completion remains challenging: suggestions must respect both the syntax of a domain-specific language (DSL) and the intended domain semantics, while remaining consistent with an evolving model. This paper presents RAFiC, an LLM-based approach for iterative domain model completion that generalizes across DSLs. It drives completion using metamodel information to ensure syntactic validity and enriches prompts with semantic-role annotations to better capture the intended modeling role of DSL elements. The approach provides context-aware, in
sb119246622.summary: Researchers introduce RAFiC, an LLM-based approach for iterative domain model completion that generalizes across domain-specific languages using semantic roles.

s9ac09f4968.title: Context Matters: Improving LLM-Based Code Summarization with Hierarchical Information
s9ac09f4968.description: arXiv:2611.18964v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Source code documentation plays an important role in software quality activities, such as code review, program comprehension, maintenance, and bug fixing. However, it is often fragmented across individual code elements and focuses on local implementation details, providing little information about their surrounding context. This limits both developers' understanding of software systems and the effectiveness of Large Language Models (LLMs), whose reasoning is constrained by finite context windows. Enriching documentation with hierarchical context has the potential to improve software comprehension and support downstream, quality-related tasks for both developers and LLM-based tools. In this paper, we present an in silico study that showcases
s9ac09f4968.summary: Researchers propose enriching source code documentation with hierarchical context so LLMs can summarize code better despite limited context windows.
s9ac09f4968.why: Hierarchical context may improve LLM code summaries and documentation quality for developers working on large codebases.

se685656474.title: Probing Where Surprise Happens: Localized Violation-of-Expectation Evaluation of Video World Models
se685656474.description: arXiv:2611.18979v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Violation-of-expectation (VOE) benchmarks evaluate intuitive physics in video world models by testing whether physically impossible events produce greater prediction errors than matched possible events.
