sda98bdffc4.why: Reusable curation criteria could make pretraining data selection more transferable across runs, which matters for teams managing training budgets.

s0e1737dc20.title: Where Should LLM Agents Adapt at Test Time? In Context, in Weights, or Both
s0e1737dc20.description: arXiv:2611.19700v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM agents operating repeatedly in the same environment, such as a code repository, a database, or an application suite, encounter tasks that share latent structure. Experience can reveal this structure, allowing agents to reuse environment knowledge and learn from environmental feedback. Agents can adapt at test-time using this experience through two channels: retaining it in context and updating their weights. These channels are usually studied separately, leaving unclear what each contributes and when they complement each other. We compare in-context learning (ICL), reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards using GRPO, and self-distillation using SDPO, alone and in combination, using a shared online protocol and modular framework. A
s0e1737dc20.summary: A study compares whether LLM agents should adapt at test time through in-context experience, weight updates, or both, across repeated environments.
s0e1737dc20.why: Choosing between context-based memory and weight updates affects agent architecture and cost for repeated-task deployments.

scae229f8c3.title: Cache or Denoise Less? Residual Reuse in a Flow-Matching World Action Model
scae229f8c3.description: arXiv:2611.19709v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Flow-matching robot policies generate each action chunk through repeated network evaluations, one per denoising step. Cross-cycle caches such as C$^3$ache reuse computation from earlier replanning calls, but whether they beat simply taking fewer steps is unclear. We compare the two in Fast-WAM, a 6B-parameter world action model, on LIBERO-Goal. Two uncached steps keep the success of ten: on all 500 initial states they are non-inferior within two percentage points, for one checkpoint and noise seed. Under PyTorch's default compile mode, they also cut a replanning call on an RTX A6000 from 202 to 92 ms. This leaves little room for caching. A cache that keeps two fresh steps cannot be faster than two uncached steps: every call still encodes th
scae229f8c3.summary: Researchers compare cross-cycle caching against taking fewer denoising steps in Fast-WAM, a 6B-parameter flow-matching robot world action model.
scae229f8c3.why: Two uncached steps matched the success of ten on LIBERO-Goal, suggesting simpler step reduction can rival caching for robot policy latency.

s2b03c36655.title: Joint Learning of Factual and Counterfactual Worlds for Causal Prior-data Fitted Networks
s2b03c36655.description: arXiv:2611.19710v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Estimating treatment effects is central to science across many disciplines and requires counterfactual reasoning about alternative worlds. In the real world, however, each unit reveals its outcome only under the factual world. Thus, the factual and counterfactual outcomes can never be jointly learned by any model trained on real data. The problem is therefore tractable only in synthetic settings, where both worlds can be generated. Recent progress on prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) has shown that models pre-trained purely on synthetic data can transfer to real-world prediction. This paradigm has since carried over to causal effect estimation. Despite this fully synthetic setup, existing causal PFNs carry the real-world constraint into the
s2b03c36655.summary: Researchers propose joint learning of factual and counterfactual worlds in causal prior-data fitted networks, pretrained on synthetic data for treatment effect estimation.

s26fdb2d4a7.title: An Interpretable Acoustic Coordinate System for Japanese Consonant Morae in Dysarthric Speech
s26fdb2d4a7.description: arXiv:2611.19714v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Dysarthria reduces speech intelligibility, requiring self-directed rehabilitation based on fine-grained feedback to capture gradual articulatory changes. For Japanese speakers, such feedback is naturally provided in mora units due to its distinct moraic timing and consonant-vowel structure. While recent visualization methods have explored distance-based feedback, most are limited to vowels. Extending them to consonants is challenging, as generative embeddings often smooth transient spectral structures. We propose a visualization system for Japanese consonant morae that maps articulatory deviations onto a two-dimensional space defined by temporal and spectral distances from healthy reference speech. Experiments show consistent geometric sepa
s26fdb2d4a7.summary: Researchers propose an interpretable acoustic coordinate system giving distance-based visual feedback on Japanese consonant morae for dysarthric speech rehabilitation.

s4fa634b17e.title: Exploration of Reinforcement Learning in Generative Recommendation Models
s4fa634b17e.description: arXiv:2611.19742v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Traditional cascaded recommender systems balance accuracy and efficiency over large item spaces, but misaligned stage-wise objectives hinder end-to-end optimization. Generative recommendation unifies these stages in an autoregressive framework, providing a natural interface for reinforcement learning (RL) to optimize the entire generation process. However, directly applying RL often leads to unstable optimization and degraded recommendation quality. We revisit Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) and other ratio-based objectives through a unified logit-gradient view. We identify three issues: (i) clipped surrogates create dead-gradient regions, under-utilizing samples; (ii) negative-advantage updates can become effectively unbounded as
s4fa634b17e.summary: A study revisits GRPO and ratio-based objectives for reinforcement learning in generative recommendation models, addressing unstable optimization and degraded quality.
s4fa634b17e.why: Applying RL end-to-end to generative recommenders is unstable with naive GRPO, so practitioners need stabilizing objectives before adopting it.

s80d3d4572c.title: How Far Is Too Far? Object Recognition Declines Monotonically with Semantic Distance
s80d3d4572c.description: arXiv:2611.19747v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision models are sensitive to object-background context, yet it remains unclear how recognition changes as the semantic distance between objects and backgrounds increases. We introduce ImageNet-OOC1k, a benchmark enabling graded control of object-background relationships along a continuous consensus visual-semantic dissimilarity axis. This formulation reveals a highly consistent monotonic decline in recognition accuracy across 35 models spanning convolutional neural networks, Vision Transformers, and vision-language models. Internal analyses of Vision Transformers reveal patterns consistent with aggregation failure, where object evidence is present at the patch level but not consolidated into the final prediction. Using this characterizati
s80d3d4572c.summary: ImageNet-OOC1k benchmark shows object recognition accuracy declines monotonically as semantic distance between object and background grows, across 35 vision models.
s80d3d4572c.why: Vision models degrade predictably with object-background semantic mismatch, a robustness consideration for deployed perception systems.

s3e51287e13.title: StaleBench: Isolating Stale Retrieval in Agent Memory, and Pricing the Fix
s3e51287e13.description: arXiv:2611.19752v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An agent that stores facts over time eventually stores several versions of the same fact. Asked a value-agnostic question - "which team does X play for now?" - a similarity retriever cannot prefer the current version, because every version matches the entity the query names. StaleBench isolates this stale-retrieval failure on 892 real updating facts, with currency labels from the source (Wikidata validity years via TempLAMA), never from a retrieval score. Our central result is that retrieval metrics can rank memory policies backwards: a retention policy and its retain-everything control return the identical statement at rank 1 for every test query, yet differ by 29.5 and 65.6 points in reader accuracy on two readers when no date is shown. C
s3e51287e13.summary: StaleBench isolates stale retrieval in agent memory using 892 updating facts and finds retrieval metrics can rank memory policies backwards.
s3e51287e13.why: Agents storing evolving facts may retrieve outdated versions, and standard retrieval metrics can misleadingly rank memory designs.

s7020765129.title: Learning Autoregressive Neural Operators on Solver-Defined Physical Constraint Manifolds
s7020765129.description: arXiv:2611.19753v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Autoregressive neural operators approximate time-dependent PDE solvers by repeatedly composing a learned transition, although the resulting states need not remain feasible under the discrete constraints of the numerical problem. We study this issue for incompressible flow, where each velocity state must satisfy solver-level incompressibility together with prescribed boundary values. We formulate autoregressive operator learning as a map between solver-defined affine feasible sets and introduce PCM-NO, a projected-residual realization of this feasible-transition principle. The neural backbone predicts a candidate state increment, a fixed tangent projection extracts its admissible component, and a metric retraction maps the advanced state to
s7020765129.summary: PCM-NO is a projected-residual autoregressive neural operator that keeps predicted incompressible flow states within solver-defined physical constraints.
s7020765129.why: Enforcing solver constraints during autoregressive rollouts could make learned PDE surrogates more reliable for engineering simulation.

s1f2bd0ea99.title: Eliciting Research Taste in LLMs through Future Research Direction Choice
s1f2bd0ea99.description: arXiv:2611.19794v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Research taste is increasingly discussed in the context of AI scientists, yet remains little studied or measured in LLMs. This judgment matters especially in open-ended research, where a direction must be chosen before a verifiable objective is available. We operationalize research taste through one task of the scientific workflow: choosing which future research direction to pursue given a research goal and current results. Rather than predicting downstream scientometric metrics or treating author choices as objectively correct, we evaluate models against human-authored future-work directions and report author alignment, stable divergence, and unstable choice as behavioral measures of research-direction preference. We construct an order-con
s1f2bd0ea99.summary: Researchers propose evaluating LLM research taste by having models choose which future research direction to pursue, given a research goal and current results.
s1f2bd0ea99.why: It offers a way to measure LLM judgment in open-ended research, where no verifiable objective exists before a direction is chosen.

s62daea9a39.title: Reasoning in the loop: antibody lead optimization by probing mechanism and measurement
s62daea9a39.description: arXiv:2611.19812v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Lab-in-the-loop systems, in which a model proposes molecules, automated assays measure their properties and the results retrain the model, are a popular approach to antibody lead optimization. These systems optimize for a specification defined with metrics computed from instrument signals, so their success depends on how well those metrics serve as proxies for the properties a drug candidate needs. When a metric is a poor proxy, neither a better model nor more data will fix it, and identifying the problem usually requires expert review. We report two campaigns run on BigHat Biosciences' Milliner platform, one on an anti-albumin nanobody (VHH) and one on an anti-mesothelin single-chain variable fragment (scFv), in which a research team and a
s62daea9a39.summary: Researchers examine lab-in-the-loop antibody lead optimization, arguing that metrics computed from instrument signals can be poor proxies that better models or more data cannot fix.
s62daea9a39.why: Teams building closed-loop ML systems should validate that optimization metrics actually reflect the properties they need, since proxy failures are not solved by more data.

sa70b4304ea.title: GraphPass: A Study of Graph Neural Networks for Compiler Pass Selection
sa70b4304ea.description: arXiv:2611.19821v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Compiler pass selection is usually governed by fixed pipelines (-O2, -O3) or hand-written heuristics. We study whether a graph neural network (GNN) over a program's control-flow graph (CFG) can select among a fixed menu of five pass sequences in a single forward pass. GraphPass encodes each CFG with a graph attention (GAT) or graph convolutional (GCN) encoder and classifies it into one of the five sequences. On a synthetic benchmark of 5,000 generated CFGs in five program families, both encoders agree with the benchmark's reference label on about 92% of held-out programs, versus 68.4% for a hand-written rule-based heuristic and 85% for a flat MLP. An edge ablation indicates that this gain comes from per-block processing rather than from CFG
sa70b4304ea.summary: Researchers study GraphPass, a graph neural network that reads a program's control-flow graph to select among five compiler pass sequences in one forward pass.
sa70b4304ea.why: It suggests learned models could replace fixed -O2/-O3 pipelines and hand-written heuristics, though results are on a synthetic benchmark only.

sa936459d4f.title: The Flip Test: Video World Models Fail to Learn the World State
sa936459d4f.description: arXiv:2611.19822v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Video world models promise to predict the future of a scene from its present. Do current models keep this promise? We probe this question counterfactually. When a small change to the present flips the future, such as a box resting a few millimeters before or past a table edge, a model that tracks the state of the world must flip its prediction too. We build FlipTest, a three-level hierarchy of increasingly strict tests over 1,680 initial frames from 10 simulated and 15 real-world tasks. At the base, visual minimal pairs, two nearly identical frames whose true futures differ, test whether predictions change across the boundary; matched controls go further and test whether they change only where the future does; and dense sweeps, the strictes
sa936459d4f.summary: Researchers introduce FlipTest, a hierarchy of counterfactual tests showing that video world models often fail to track the underlying state of a scene.
sa936459d4f.why: Teams relying on video world models for prediction or planning should not assume they track physical state, since these tests show frequent failures.

s1efc8b0f11.title: EfficientSkill: Learning Skills for Token-Efficient Multi-Turn Agents
s1efc8b0f11.description: arXiv:2611.19823v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reflective skill optimizers improve multi-turn LLM agents by revising instructions from failed and successful rollouts, yet accumulating edge-case rules bloats prompts, inflates token use, and pushes agents into long, error-prone loops. We introduce EfficientSkill, a two-step framework that first discovers a reliable skill without token penalties, and then warm-starts accuracy-guarded pruning from that skill to compress instructions, bound agent turns, and offload reusable code into workspace utilities with zero implementation prompt cost. Across four frontier, mid-tier, and open-weight models on MATH-500, ALFWorld, and SpreadsheetBench, EfficientSkill cuts output tokens over unconstrained EvoSkill on 11 of 12 configurations (by up to 80%)
s1efc8b0f11.summary: Researchers present EfficientSkill, a framework that prunes and compresses agent skill instructions to reduce token use and turns in multi-turn LLM agents.
s1efc8b0f11.why: Reducing prompt bloat and agent loop length can cut inference cost and error rates for teams running multi-turn agents.

s489829fb62.title: Bridging the Terminology Gap: A Data-Centric Alignment Framework for Multilingual Translation in Cross-Border Corporation
s489829fb62.description: arXiv:2611.19858v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As globalization accelerates the demand for seamless cross-border enterprise collaboration, multilingual translation remains bottlenecked by insufficient domain-specific terminology, rigid terminology translation, weak instruction-following capabilities, and high inference latency in long-instruction scenarios. To overcome these barriers, we propose Bridging the Terminology Gap (BTG), a data-centric framework. First, BTG mines cross-lingual term alignments from domain documents and leverages LLMs to synthesize terminology-rich parallel corpora. Second, a hybrid filtering strategy combining heuristics and XCOMET scoring ensures high data fidelity. Third, a two-stage training paradigm employs supervised fine-tuning (SFT) for targeted terminol
s489829fb62.summary: Researchers propose BTG, a data-centric framework that mines cross-lingual terminology and synthesizes terminology-rich parallel corpora to improve enterprise translation.
s489829fb62.why: Enterprises with domain jargon across languages may benefit from terminology-focused data synthesis, though the text gives no benchmark results.

sb60df3a98c.title: Local Order Matters: A Lightweight CPU-Trainable CNN for Website Fingerprinting on Defended Tor Traffic
sb60df3a98c.description: arXiv:2611.19864v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Website fingerprinting (WF) attacks let a passive adversary infer which site a Tor user visits from the encrypted cell sequence. On undefended traffic, hand-crafted-feature attacks are already near-ceiling, so deep learning offers only a marginal advantage there. We show that the decisive regime is defended traffic: against the FRONT padding defense, which injects dummy cells that corrupt the volume and count features feature attacks rely on, a compact 95,103-parameter 1-D convolutional network trained on the raw cell-direction sequence, on CPU only, stays robust while three implemented direction-only feature baselines degrade. On the closed-world WFlib FRONT set (95 sites), our model reaches 54.2% top-1 accuracy versus 38.5% for the strong
sb60df3a98c.summary: Researchers show a compact 1-D CNN trained on CPU can perform website fingerprinting against Tor traffic defended by the FRONT padding scheme.
sb60df3a98c.why: It shows defended Tor traffic remains vulnerable to learned attacks, relevant to teams assessing anonymity and traffic-analysis risk.

se50353f462.title: HalluProbe: Exploiting VLM Hallucinations for Backdoor Detection
se50353f462.description: arXiv:2611.19868v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are vulnerable to backdoor attacks introduced through data poisoning, making effective backdoor detection a critical security challenge. In this paper, we uncover a novel connection between VLM hallucinations and backdoor behaviors and exploit this connection for backdoor detection. Our key insight is that poisoned training data induces strong language priors toward the backdoor target token, while such priors are also a major source of hallucinations. This suggests that enhancing hallucinations can expose hidden backdoor-related priors. Specifically, backdoored VLMs tend to hallucinate backdoor target tokens more frequently across diverse inputs, while the hallucinated tokens of clean VLMs are largely random a
se50353f462.summary: Researchers propose HalluProbe, which uses vision-language model hallucinations to expose backdoor behavior induced by data poisoning.
se50353f462.why: Security teams deploying VLMs get a possible detection signal for poisoned backdoors, though the text gives no detection performance figures.

s386cbafd14.title: Let Execution Do the Teaching
s386cbafd14.description: arXiv:2611.19875v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Improving a coding model is a sequence of decisions: find the limiting behavior, create useful practice, and determine which attempts deserve reinforcement. We investigate a practical way to make those decisions increasingly repeatable by grounding feedback in execution. Starting from GLM-4.7-Flash, the work combines whole-file supervised fine-tuning, targeted C++ repair curricula, group-relative reinforcement learning, and verifiers that turn program behavior into structured rewards. Compiler errors and failing tests provide specific contexts for repair practice, while executable checks score the resulting programs. We evaluate the trained models on 26 C++ coding tasks, measuring both initial success and completion after test feedback. The
s386cbafd14.summary: Researchers describe improving the GLM-4.7-Flash coding model using supervised fine-tuning, C++ repair curricula, and reinforcement learning with execution-based rewards.
s386cbafd14.why: Using compiler errors and test results as structured rewards offers a practical recipe for improving code models without relying only on human labels.

sca93143628.title: Large Language Model-based Optimization for Wireless Communication: A Survey
sca93143628.description: arXiv:2611.19876v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The growing complexity and dynamism of modern wireless communication frameworks have made real-time optimization essential for efficient resource allocation. Traditional optimization and machine-learning techniques often struggle with generalization, adaptability, stability, and scalability in heterogeneous, time-varying environments. Large language models (LLMs) have recently emerged as powerful tools capable of reasoning over structured prompts and generating context-aware decisions in real time without domain-specific retraining. This survey provides a comprehensive review of LLM-driven optimization techniques applied to wireless communication problems such as power control, bandwidth allocation, task offloading, and intelligent surface
sca93143628.summary: A survey reviews how large language models are being applied to real-time optimization and resource allocation in wireless communication systems.
sca93143628.why: Engineers in telecom may find it useful as an overview of where LLMs can complement traditional optimization, though it reports no new results.

s9d761bb41f.title: Recovery Gone Too Far: Understanding and Repairing Risky Fallback in LLM Agents
s9d761bb41f.description: arXiv:2611.19886v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents interact with their environments through tools, reading repositories, running builds, and pushing code. When a tool fails with an ordinary error, such as a rate limit or a timeout, the agent can fall back to a substitute tool and still complete the task. However, the same fallback that completes a task in one environment can cross an action boundary in another. For example, after a push is rejected, a forced push in one repository replaces only the agent's own commits, while in a different repository it also removes another author's commits. We call such a fallback a risky fallback. To understand this phenomenon, we conduct an empirical study on 304 scenarios that span eight domains and cover 55 real CVEs.
s9d761bb41f.summary: Researchers study how LLM agents fall back to substitute tools after ordinary errors, showing the same fallback can be safe in one environment and risky in another.
s9d761bb41f.why: Agents with tool fallback can cross action boundaries, such as forced pushes that overwrite others' work, so teams need guardrails tied to context.

s973bc75528.title: AgenticJevNav: Agentic Object Search and Navigation via Event-Driven Verification
s973bc75528.description: arXiv:2611.19912v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agentic navigation must maintain goals and adapt actions from incomplete evidence despite execution failures and delayed inference. We present AgenticJevNav, which links goal-directed planning, evidence memory, event-triggered verification, and bounded execution. The Agent plans from RGB, odometry, memory, and feedback, retaining goal ownership while authorizing a bounded action set. Jev reviews structured evidence after blocked/failed execution or two consecutive low-progress segments. Version, freshness, and once-only checks govern decision application. A single executor and independent RGB reflex constrain motion. Goal revisions revoke obsolete requests and actions before replanning. Across six simulated task families, AgenticJevNav achi
s973bc75528.summary: Researchers present AgenticJevNav, an agentic navigation system that triggers event-driven verification after failed actions or repeated low-progress segments.
s973bc75528.why: It illustrates bounded action sets and verification triggers for embodied agents, a pattern relevant to teams building reliable autonomous navigation.

sbad308418d.title: The Vocabulary Tax: Safely Trimming Unused Tokens from LLMs for On-Device Use
sbad308418d.description: arXiv:2611.19913v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Open large language models (LLMs) and speech models ship vocabularies of up to 262k tokens, and every user downloads the tables those tokens index (the input embedding, an untied output head and, in recent on-device models, per-layer embeddings), whatever languages they need. We call the bytes in rows a deployment never uses the vocabulary tax and measure it, without downloading weights, for 1,244 generative and speech-recognition models on the Hugging Face Hub. For a Thai and English deployment it is a median 4.4% of model bytes below 0.5B parameters and 2.1% above 8B, and 1.93 GB in Gemma 4 E2B: it falls hardest on the small models that edge devices run. Keeping only the rows of the deployment's writing systems is exact. Keeping the token
sbad308418d.summary: Researchers quantify unused vocabulary rows in 1,244 open models on Hugging Face and propose safely trimming them to reduce on-device model size.
sbad308418d.why: Teams shipping models on-device could cut download size substantially by removing vocabulary rows their deployment never uses.

s5c828de2d5.title: Learning When to Continue and When to Stop: Termination-Aware OPSD
s5c828de2d5.description: arXiv:2611.19925v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) improves language model reasoning by distilling from a frozen teacher initialized identically to the student and conditioned on privileged information. However, we identify an underexplored termination mismatch in OPSD: the student fails to reliably learn when to continue and when to stop. This mismatch manifests in two opposing failure modes-premature termination, where reasoning stops before sufficient progress is made, and repetition-driven over-generation, where the model continues generating after reasoning has stalled. Our analysis shows that the teacher-student discrepancy on EOS grows during OPSD training, while length-capped trajectories are frequently dominated by unproductive repetition. To addr
s5c828de2d5.summary: Researchers identify a termination mismatch in on-policy self-distillation, where students stop reasoning too early or over-generate, and propose a termination-aware fix.
s5c828de2d5.why: Reasoning models that stop prematurely or repeat endlessly waste compute or give wrong answers, so stopping behavior is a practical training concern.

s149e25e587.title: Equal Dose, Different Coverage:Tracing Rate and Duration in Image Editing
s149e25e587.description: arXiv:2611.19955v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Benchmarks for scientific image editing test whether a model draws the outcome of a described process, leaving open which representations carry its errors and whether correcting them yields the right quantity. We study this question with an airbrush of fixed deposition profile, under which exchanging rate and duration preserves the dose and should preserve the endpoint, yet changes the edited coverage. Matched-norm activation patches across text positions and denoising stages show that, in distilled FLUX with Chinese prompts, representations at unchanged text positions (context) carry this discrepancy: early context transfers 3.51 of the 3.98 percentage-point (pp) signed route difference, against 0.09 pp for equal-norm updates at the two ch
s149e25e587.summary: Researchers find that in distilled FLUX with Chinese prompts, errors in scientific image editing stem from representations of rate and duration, not just the endpoint.
s149e25e587.why: It highlights that correct final outputs can hide wrong internal dynamics, relevant to teams debugging or steering image-editing models.

se6a42326cb.title: Value and Policy Calibration from Execution Feedback for Socially Compatible Driving
se6a42326cb.description: arXiv:2611.19969v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Autonomous vehicle (AV) decisions at intersections affect the delay, braking, and motion smoothness of surrounding human-driven vehicles (HDVs). Learning socially compatible behavior requires connecting imagined interaction outcomes with feedback from executed actions. We propose a world-model reinforcement learning framework combines imagined policy improvement with direct value and policy calibration from finalized interactions, balancing AV progress with HDV interaction burden. An interaction-aware latent model supports imagination, while off-policy correction and replay updates enable observed rewards and transitions to supervise both the critic and actor. Simulation experiments at an unsignalized intersection achieve a 100% success and
se6a42326cb.summary: Researchers propose a world-model reinforcement learning framework that calibrates value and policy from executed interactions so autonomous vehicles balance progress with burden on human drivers at intersections.
se6a42326cb.why: Shows how learning from real execution feedback, not just imagined rollouts, may help AV planners reduce disruption to surrounding human drivers.

s070ace2d76.title: Federated Dataset Simulation: Inducing Label-Free Heterogeneity Across Tasks
s070ace2d76.description: arXiv:2611.19975v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Federated Learning enables collaborative model training across decentralized clients without sharing raw data. While the field has seen rapid growth, the datasets underpinning FL evaluation have not kept pace: real federated datasets remain scarce, and most studies rely on small-scale centralized classification datasets partitioned via Dirichlet label skew, a one-dimensional proxy for the multi-dimensional heterogeneity present in real federations. Moreover, label-based partitioning is by construction inapplicable to non-classification tasks such as segmentation and detection, for which no principled simulation method exists. We cast the conversion of centralized datasets into federated benchmarks as the task of Federated Dataset Simulation
s070ace2d76.summary: Researchers introduce a method to simulate federated datasets with label-free heterogeneity, aiming to replace label-skew partitioning that does not apply to non-classification tasks.
s070ace2d76.why: Gives FL engineers a more realistic way to evaluate federated systems beyond Dirichlet label-skew splits, including for non-classification tasks.

s88f6283efe.title: CreaTrace: Video Creative Plagiarism Detection and Evidence Tracing
s88f6283efe.description: arXiv:2611.19976v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Video creative plagiarism refers to the unauthorized reproduction of creative ideas across videos despite substantial differences in visual appearance, posing a new challenge to video copyright protection. However, existing video copy detection methods primarily focus on visual content similarity, struggling to capture abstract creative that are entangled with specific visual realizations. To address this issue, we introduce a novel task, named Video Creative Plagiarism Detection (VCPD), and propose an iterative creative evidence tracing framework, termed CreaTrace, to verify creative similarity and accurately localize the corresponding evidence segments. Specifically, we design a Multimodal Semantic Event Segmentation strategy to divide si
s88f6283efe.summary: Researchers define Video Creative Plagiarism Detection, a task for finding reused creative ideas across videos that differ visually, and propose an iterative evidence-tracing framework.
s88f6283efe.why: Highlights that visual copy detection misses idea-level copying, relevant to teams building video copyright or content-moderation tooling.

sabf78fa32d.title: Morphology-Decoupled Segmentation for Multiple Tunnel Defects Under Complex Environments
sabf78fa32d.description: arXiv:2611.19981v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Automated tunnel-lining inspection must segment different defect geometries: cracks are thin, elongated, and connectivity-sensitive, whereas leakage, lining falling off, and segment damage are spatially extensive and context-dependent. Existing approaches generally apply a common decoder across defect classes or introduce boundary, topology, and directional mechanisms as isolated enhancements. This paper introduces Morphology-Decoupled Segmentation (MDS), in which defect morphology becomes the organising principle for feature routing, decoding, and interaction. A supervised routing module partitions multiscale encoder features into complementary linear and areal streams. The linear stream employs Deformable Strip Attention with image-condit
sabf78fa32d.summary: Researchers propose Morphology-Decoupled Segmentation, which routes features and decoding by defect shape to segment cracks and other tunnel-lining defects in complex environments.

s10b7da688d.title: What Matters for Cross-Modal Alignment
s10b7da688d.description: arXiv:2611.20000v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis posits that models trained on different modalities converge toward a shared representation. Related work aligns frozen image and text encoders on natural images without paired data. We test zero-pair alignment on five datasets across four modalities: natural images, environmental audio, chest radiographs, and 3D computed tomography (CT). It succeeds only on COCO and fails on the other four. We analyze the failures and find that alignment must first locate the subspace where the modalities co-vary and then orient the mapping within it. Consistent with previous studies, medical imaging is the hardest case: its shared subspace carries the smallest fraction of the variance. When this fraction is small, ali
s10b7da688d.summary: Researchers test zero-pair alignment of frozen encoders across five datasets and four modalities, finding it succeeds only on COCO natural images and fails on audio, radiographs, and CT.
s10b7da688d.why: Suggests cross-modal alignment without paired data does not generalize beyond natural images, a caution for teams assuming it transfers to medical or audio domains.

sb52d351a52.title: The novelty exposed: ablation, reproducibility and transparency in 40 technical reports of open-weight large language models (LLMs)
sb52d351a52.description: arXiv:2611.20003v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In 2025 alone, 48 new large language model (LLM) architectures were added to the Hugging Face transformers library, and many of them arrive with a technical report that presents the model as new. What is actually new in these models, and is it tested? We put this question to LLM technical reports. We look at three things: what the reference code shows about how new open-weight architectures differ from earlier ones; what 40 randomly sampled technical reports claim as new and whether they support it with ablation studies; and what they disclose for reproducibility and transparency. In the library, 39 of the 48 architectures added in 2025 take at least two of their three core blocks from another model, most often Llama, although part of this
sb52d351a52.summary: A study of 40 sampled open-weight LLM technical reports examines whether claimed architectural novelties are supported by ablation studies and what reproducibility details are disclosed.
sb52d351a52.why: Helps engineers judge how much weight to give novelty claims in open-weight model reports, given how many new architectures appear each year.

s8c6ede389b.title: ReactBench-AD: Do Driving VLAs and World-Action Models React to Imminent Hazards in Their Path?
s8c6ede389b.description: arXiv:2611.20011v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) and World-Action Models (WAMs) have emerged in autonomous driving with the promise of strong generalization to long-tail scenarios. Although these models achieve state-of-the-art results on autonomous driving benchmarks, most existing benchmarks are dominated by nominal scenarios and therefore cannot test this promise. To test one such long-tail capability that is critical for safety, we introduce ReactBench-AD, a benchmark that measures how driving models react to objects that appear in the ego vehicle's path. Built on real NAVSIM and PhysicalAI-Autonomous-Vehicles scenes, ReactBench-AD composites a crossing pedestrian, a standing pedestrian, or a stationary car consistently across all camera views and
s8c6ede389b.summary: Researchers introduce ReactBench-AD, a benchmark testing whether driving VLA and world-action models react to imminent hazards appearing in the ego vehicle's path.

s8c6821a111.title: D'BEAST: Logged Bad Experiences as Explanation for Autonomous Driving Agents
s8c6821a111.description: arXiv:2611.20019v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reinforcement learning agents learn from mistakes, yet their decisions can be difficult to trace back to those experiences. We investigate whether a tabular agent's decisions can be explained by its bad experiences, defined as the training transitions associated with safety or task events. A fixed training log is replayed from the same initial Q-table under three conditions. FULL retains all updates, SKIP omits bad-experience updates, and NEUTRALIZE retains those updates without their event penalties. We illustrate the method on six classic Markov decision processes and evaluate it in closed-loop driving in CARLA. On the full driving task, FULL reached the goal from 33 of 40 test starts, whereas SKIP and NEUTRALIZE reached it from none, ind
s8c6821a111.summary: Researchers present D'BEAST, which replays a tabular RL training log under three conditions to test whether agent decisions can be explained by logged bad experiences.
s8c6821a111.why: Offers a replay-based method for tracing RL agent decisions to safety-relevant training events, relevant to explainability work in autonomous driving.

Second, we use representation theory to characterize linear layers equivariant to multiple permutations, including wreath-product symmetries. Third, we study permutation-invariant set representations that preserve containment, establish dimensional bounds and impossibility results, and introduce MASNet. Finally, we propose FSW-GNN, a message-passing architecture co
sc1c834b248.summary: A thesis investigates the expressive power of graph neural networks and symmetry-aware architectures, introducing EGenNet and characterizations of equivariant linear layers.

s695d1f9a1c.title: Google's AI answers reducing search traffic by 40%
s695d1f9a1c.description: Article URL: https://revscope.co/blog/search-seo-geo-2026/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50540178 Points: 182 # Comments: 127
s695d1f9a1c.summary: A Hacker News post links to a blog claiming Google's AI answers have cut search traffic by 40%.

sbc1083d540.title: Nvidia’s startup stakes ballooned to $65B, but Huang’s exit puts future deals in doubt
sbc1083d540.description: The value of Nvidia’s private investments has nearly tripled over the past nine months, fueled by Jensen Huang’s aggressive dealmaking and rising valuations of its existing portfolio companies.
sbc1083d540.summary: Nvidia's private investment stakes have nearly tripled in nine months to about $65B, driven by Jensen Huang's dealmaking and rising portfolio valuations, but future deals are uncertain after his exit.
sbc1083d540.why: Signals that Nvidia's investment pipeline, a major force in AI funding, may slow under new leadership, affecting startups that depend on its capital.

sbcd79b1222.title: NEBench R1: a Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating Nuclear Domain Competence in Large Language Models
sbcd79b1222.description: arXiv:2611.21682v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being explored for knowledge-intensive and safety-critical applications in nuclear engineering. However, existing nuclear-domain benchmarks provide limited content coverage or focus primarily on answer accuracy without systematically evaluating the quality of the underlying reasoning. This study introduces NEBench R1, a reasoning-oriented benchmark comprising 7,546 unique multiple-choice questions extracted from U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) reactor operator licensing examinations covering 18 nuclear facilities. Each question is classified according to the NRC Knowledge and Abilities catalogs and accompanied by an official explanation serving as a reference for reasoning evaluation. Six
sbcd79b1222.summary: Researchers introduced NEBench R1, a reasoning benchmark with 7,546 multiple-choice nuclear engineering questions drawn from NRC reactor operator licensing exams.
sbcd79b1222.why: Gives teams building LLMs for safety-critical nuclear applications a reasoning-focused evaluation, not just answer accuracy.

s7a9e51a5ea.title: Chain-of-Thought Controllability Can Reduce Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
s7a9e51a5ea.description: arXiv:2611.21799v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring is a promising tool for detecting hidden goals, off-task behavior, and other failures in AI agents. One risk is that models could deliberately shape their reasoning to make it opaque to monitors. We stress-test this risk through persona-control training: supervised fine-tuning on mathematical reasoning traces rewritten in the voices of diverse personas. This induces a broader ability to control CoT, even though training contains no monitor-evasion examples. In covert side-task evaluations, traces in which a gpt-oss-20b model organism completes the hidden side task contain less monitorable evidence than the base model's. Averaged across evaluations and CoT lengths, weighted by side-task-success counts, the CoT
s7a9e51a5ea.summary: A study finds that training models to control their chain-of-thought reasoning can make that reasoning less monitorable for detecting hidden goals or failures.
s7a9e51a5ea.why: Suggests CoT monitoring, a key agent oversight tool, may be weakened if models learn to shape their reasoning.

s9c46afe5a3.title: How Much of SAR Vehicle Recognition Is the Vehicle? Background Shortcuts, Angle Gaps and Partial Libraries on MSTAR and ATRNet-STAR
s9c46afe5a3.description: arXiv:2611.21827v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep networks score near 99% on the MSTAR vehicle benchmark, and the newer ATRNet-STAR benchmark was built to be harder. We ask how much of these scores comes from the vehicle itself. With a modern network (ConvNeXt-Small, 3 seeds) we first reproduce the known MSTAR result: with the central 96x96 pixels zeroed out, accuracy is still 73.3% (chance 10%). The same shortcut is present in ATRNet-STAR, which was collected across several scenes: with the vehicle removed, accuracy is 63.3% on the 40-class SOC split (chance 2.5%). Under the official scene-change split, the background stops helping and starts hurting. Accuracy is 22.8% on full chips and 30.8% when only the vehicle is shown. A SAR foundation model, SARATR-X, leans on the background more
s9c46afe5a3.summary: Researchers show SAR vehicle recognition benchmarks MSTAR and ATRNet-STAR can be solved well above chance using background shortcuts with the vehicle masked out.
s9c46afe5a3.why: Shows benchmark scores can overstate true recognition, a caution for evaluating vision models on shortcut-prone datasets.

sb5c3132bda.title: Auditors Struggle to Catch Sabotage In End-to-End Transcripts of AI Safety Research
sb5c3132bda.description: arXiv:2611.21832v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As AI systems are increasingly used to automate AI R&D, misaligned systems could sabotage research intended to improve model safety and alignment. To stress-test defenses against such sabotage, we use a human expert as a proxy saboteur on AI safety research. We conduct a red-team/blue-team game where a human researcher runs AI safety experiments from scratch and auditors try to tell which were sabotaged and how. Given access to the full research transcript and the ability to run experiments, human auditors mostly fail to distinguish sabotaged from benign research: they achieve an AUROC of 0.59, not significantly better than chance, and fully identify the specific sabotage in only 17% of cases. Despite not being allowed to run experiments, the
sb5c3132bda.summary: A red-team study finds human auditors mostly fail to detect sabotage planted in end-to-end transcripts of AI safety research experiments.
sb5c3132bda.why: Indicates human review alone may not reliably catch sabotage in AI-automated R&D pipelines, pointing to need for stronger defenses.

s9fe3e937f5.title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
s9fe3e937f5.description: arXiv:2611.21885v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language models are trained once, frozen and deployed: improving one again takes another training run, and a prompt, a scaffold or extra computation at inference is gone once the task ends. A frontier model has been shown to edit the weights of a much smaller one. We ask whether a model can rewrite its own weights to make itself better, and find that it can, by its own reasoning, with no gradients and no training; we call this self-rewriting. Given its weights, graded answers and the ability to run itself, a 27B model diagnoses its failure and edits the weights behind it. It surpasses itself: its own edit makes it 6.6 points more accurate on 490 problems it never saw, in a test fixed in advance, and another session's edit also makes it signif
s9fe3e937f5.summary: Researchers report a 27B language model can diagnose its own failures and edit its weights through reasoning alone, without gradients or training.
s9fe3e937f5.why: Suggests a new self-improvement route that avoids retraining, though the abstract gives limited detail on robustness or scope.

s7195ca0e67.title: DNeo: Your Parallel Draft Model Needs Better Target Feature Encoding
s7195ca0e67.description: arXiv:2611.21925v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Speculative-diffusion decoding uses a small parallel drafter model to generate b draft tokens in one forward pass, which then undergo parallel verification via a larger target model. Faster inference can be achieved when multiple draft tokens pass verification simultaneously. Recent parallel draft architectures (DFlash, DSpark) improve draft quality by conditioning on rich features computed by the target, through a mechanism known as feature encoding. However, standard feature encoding mechanisms have three limitations: (1) they are lossy, applying encoding projections that are destructive to the underlying target feature-space via a discovered effect known as residual mixing, (2) they are memory-less, with no record of previously processed p
s7195ca0e67.summary: DNeo proposes improved target feature encoding for parallel draft models used in speculative-diffusion decoding to speed up LLM inference.
s7195ca0e67.why: Targets inference speedups via better drafter conditioning, relevant to teams optimizing LLM serving latency.

scdb8ae8b75.title: SLED: Sensor SLicing from Edge to Datacenter
scdb8ae8b75.description: arXiv:2611.21937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern sensing systems generate large volumes of heterogeneous data streams from multiple sensor modalities, increasing reliance on datacenters for computation, artificial intelligence/superintelligence (AI/SI) inference, and AI/SI training. Each sensor stream may have different network and compute requirements depending on its type and data volume. However, current wireless systems typically allocate resources at the device level, leading to contention among co-located sensor streams, where bulk data transfers may starve latency-critical telemetry. To this end, this paper introduces Sensor Slicing (SL). SL provides deterministic, medium access control (MAC)-level isolation for individual sensors within a single user equipment (UE) in open ra
scdb8ae8b75.summary: SLED proposes allocating network and compute resources per sensor stream, rather than per device, across edge-to-datacenter wireless systems.

se1fbba8ab1.title: Conserved Verdicts, Drifting Commitments: Identifying Harmful Overthinking
se1fbba8ab1.description: arXiv:2611.21946v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A reasoning model that has reached a correct answer can lose it by continuing to think. Deciding whether to stop means comparing two probabilities at the same point of a chain: that the answer the model would give if stopped now is correct (its commitment), and that the answer it will finish with is correct (its verdict). We show that the verdict alone, which is what final-correctness probes estimate, cannot make this comparison. As a forecast of a fixed outcome it has no predictable drift, whether continuing helps or hurts. The commitment-verdict gap equals the expected remaining change in answer quality and the accuracy gained by stopping. A second identity splits any accuracy-versus-budget curve into answer change within chains and change
se1fbba8ab1.summary: Researchers propose distinguishing a reasoning model's commitment from its verdict to decide when continued thinking harms a correct answer.
se1fbba8ab1.why: Shows final-correctness probes alone cannot decide when a reasoning model should stop, which matters for designing early-stopping in inference pipelines.

s6cb2ad0128.title: Honest Brokers in AI Regulation: How Public Comments Introduce Evidence to Regulators
s6cb2ad0128.description: arXiv:2611.21948v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The regulation of Artificial Intelligence is susceptible to various forms of capture by industry actors that hold undue influence over the policymaking process, due in part to their information advantage in developing these technologies. In the following paper, we investigate the roles of public commenters in providing evidence to potential regulation in the USA. We build a corpus of 40 potential regulations, and 2,664 public comments submitted by a variety of stakeholders. We computationally process these texts to extract evidence meant to inform regulators, in the form of formal citations and informal references. We find significant differences in the type and amount of evidence supplied: Holding comment length constant, business commenters
s6cb2ad0128.summary: A paper examines how public comments on proposed AI regulations introduce evidence to US regulators, using a corpus of 40 regulations and 2,664 comments.
s6cb2ad0128.why: Highlights how stakeholder comments shape AI policy and how industry information advantages can influence rulemaking.

sddcb912129.title: DiscoveryAgent: A Framework for Scientist-centric Agentic AI
sddcb912129.description: arXiv:2611.21950v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents can assist scientific research, but balancing autonomous investigation with scientists' ability to inspect and redirect ongoing work remains a central design challenge. We present DiscoveryAgent, a domain-agnostic, scientist-centric system that combines autonomous investigation with scientist-directed hypothesis steering. Scientists select, refine, or replace hypotheses between research rounds, while audit agents interrogate checkpointed records to trace claims, reproduce analyses, and inform subsequent decisions. Across two predictive modeling tasks, DiscoveryAgent produced the best variable-star classifier among evaluated baselines and, with scientist steering, a protein variant-effect predictor surpassed by only one of 106 Protei
sddcb912129.summary: DiscoveryAgent is a scientist-centric agentic AI framework that lets researchers select, refine, or replace hypotheses between autonomous research rounds.
sddcb912129.why: Offers a design pattern for keeping humans in control of autonomous agents, with checkpointed records for auditing claims.

s9c24b96ea7.title: WebAgents: Unbundling Agent Creation, Hosting, and Execution for an Agent-Native Web
s9c24b96ea7.description: arXiv:2611.21978v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models are moving from isolated assistants toward autonomous agents that can plan, use tools, and coordinate with others, motivating an emerging Agentic Web of independently developed agents and services. Realizing this vision requires agent behavior to move across creators, hosts, and runtimes without coupling publication to a particular execution environment or transferring authority over user resources. We introduce WebAgents, which unbundles these roles through a signed agent.pkg that carries portable workflows, skills, schemas, and resource requirements. An OpenClaw-based agent-native browser/runtime verifies the package, obtains authorization, and binds it at run time to user-controlled models, tools, permissions, and bud
s9c24b96ea7.summary: WebAgents proposes separating agent creation, hosting, and execution, using a signed agent.pkg format to make agents portable across runtimes.
s9c24b96ea7.why: Outlines an architecture for moving agents across hosts without tying publication to one execution environment or transferring user authority.

s209de93253.title: KV-LTM: Persistent Per-Session KV Caches as Long-Term Memory for Personal Assistants
s209de93253.description: arXiv:2611.21998v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Personal assistants accumulate months of conversations, but today's long-term memory stacks put derivation or selection between a question and its evidence. In a system-level comparison on LongMemEval, two commercial assistants scored well below the same model reading the history offline [1], consistent with, but not isolating, content loss between write and read. We propose KV-LTM: a memory tier storing each session's raw text plus its KV cache under a fixed reader model, answering by restoring cached sessions and appending the question. KV-LTM is complementary to, not a replacement for, retrieval and indexing. Text is the memory of record; the cache is a recompute-free prefill accelerator, degrading gracefully to text. We specify the design
s209de93253.summary: KV-LTM stores each session's raw text plus its KV cache as long-term memory for personal assistants, restoring cached sessions to answer questions.
s209de93253.why: Suggests a memory design that may avoid content loss from derivation or selection in conventional long-term memory stacks.

s3843f46054.title: On Formal Counterfactual Explanations
s3843f46054.description: arXiv:2611.22010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Counterfactual explanations are often seen as counterfactual conditionals under closest-world semantics, requiring one to reason over all minimally distant counterexamples. In contrast, formal XAI typically relies on feature-based abductive explanations (AXps) and contrastive explanations (CXps), which admit efficient computation and a minimal hitting-set duality. This paper bridges these perspectives by (i) characterizing closest-world counterfactual explanations explicitly as a disjunctive normal form over all minimally distant counterexample instances, and (ii) introducing conjunctive counterfactual explanations (CFXps), a subclass of counterfactual antecedents restricted to conjunctions of feature literals that guarantee prediction change
s3843f46054.summary: A paper links closest-world counterfactual explanations to formal XAI methods, characterizing them as a disjunctive normal form over minimally distant counterexamples.
s3843f46054.why: Connects counterfactual explanations with feature-based abductive and contrastive explanations, which may help in building efficient explainability tooling.

s14a1f345f6.title: SkillBuffBench: Measuring What Agent Skills Contribute across Harnesses, Models, Skill Access Modes and Memory
s14a1f345f6.description: arXiv:2611.22017v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent Skills, file-based packages of procedural knowledge that a coding agent can discover and load on demand, are now shipped by every major agent harness, yet the evidence for how much they help comes almost entirely from settings in which the right Skill is hand-picked for the task and the agent starts from a blank slate. Neither holds in deployment, where an agent chooses from whatever library happens to be installed and frequently carries memory from earlier work. We present SkillBuffBench, a benchmark and paired evaluation protocol that treats Skill access as a three-level factor (no Skill, a curated Skill, and automatic invocation from an installed library), crosses it with memory (off and on), with four agent harnesses and with multip
s14a1f345f6.summary: SkillBuffBench is a benchmark that measures how agent skills contribute across harnesses, models, skill access modes, and memory in realistic deployment settings.
s14a1f345f6.why: Challenges claims about agent skill value by testing realistic conditions where agents choose from installed libraries and carry memory.

s164ad1122d.title: What Does an Agent Need? Bundle-Aware Agent Resource Composition
s164ad1122d.description: arXiv:2611.22030v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An agent resource's value depends on its backbone and companion resources and is known only after execution. Token-based generators remain tied to their training catalog, while independent resource scoring misses complementarities and reused bundles target other tasks. We formulate Task-Conditioned Agent Resource Composition (AgentComposition): jointly selecting a backbone model and a tool-skill bundle to maximize end-to-end execution utility. Our Retrieval-Grounded Bundle-Aware Agent Generation retrieves candidate resources and past configurations of similar tasks. A fine-tuned generator reads resource descriptions and recombines candidates through constrained beam search, allowing new resources without retraining. A bundle-aware critic rank
s164ad1122d.summary: Researchers formulate AgentComposition, jointly selecting a backbone model and tool-skill bundle for a task, using retrieval-grounded bundle-aware generation.
s164ad1122d.why: Suggests that agent configuration should consider model and tool combinations together rather than scoring resources independently.

s3818a96d04.title: Thinking Harder Doesn't Lead to Better Choices: Reasoning Effort Increases the Confidence but Not the Correctness of LLM Shopping Agents
s3818a96d04.description: arXiv:2611.22033v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous shopping agents that process multimodal product listings (consisting of visual and text data) and recommend purchases on behalf of consumers. Naturally, one might assume that models with more thinking power would make higher-quality purchasing decisions. To test this belief, we ask two questions about such agents: does asking a model to think harder make it choose better products, and does the confidence it reports tell us the likelihood it may be wrong? We benchmark ten frontier models on three product-choice benchmarks built from WebShop, Amazon's SQID and Wayfair's WANDS platforms to see if LLMs with more thinking power actually make better-quality product purchase decisi
s3818a96d04.summary: A benchmark of ten frontier LLMs finds that more reasoning effort raises shopping agents' confidence but not the correctness of their product choices.
s3818a96d04.why: Warns that higher reasoning budgets and reported confidence do not guarantee better autonomous purchasing decisions.

s38e1c821de.title: A Hybrid Exact-Heuristic Solver for the Integrated Passenger and Parcel Transportation Problem
s38e1c821de.description: arXiv:2611.22043v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe the solver we submitted to the second round of the SOICT 2026 contest on the Integrated Passenger and Parcel Transportation problem, a selective pickup-and-delivery routing problem with time windows, open routes and heterogeneous taxis. The solver is a single-file, standard-library Python program that combines (i) a constant-time insertion test based on latest-arrival slack, (ii) greedy insertion, local search and an Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search (ALNS) with simulated-annealing acceptance, and (iii) an exact route-selection engine that enumerates, for every taxi, the best feasible route for each request set and then solves the resulting set-packing problem by branch-and-bound strengthened with route-based large neighborhood s
s38e1c821de.summary: A team describes its contest solver for the Integrated Passenger and Parcel Transportation problem, combining heuristics, ALNS, and an exact route-selection engine.
s38e1c821de.why: Offers a practical example of hybrid exact-heuristic optimization for routing, though its relevance beyond the contest is limited.

saca8585783.title: MedGuardBench: A Patient-Oriented Benchmark for Personalized Guardrail Development
saca8585783.description: arXiv:2611.22069v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Safety is personal: the same action can be safe for one person but unsafe for another. Yet current guardrails judge content without considering who is affected. Using medication safety, we introduce \textit{patient-conditioned medication guarding}, which predicts a safety verdict and 17 risk categories from a patient profile and prescription. We release \textbf{MedGuardBench}, a drug-disjoint benchmark of 5{,}001 scenarios across 87 medications. We find that standard guardrails rely on surface cues, such as wording and profile presence, rather than patient facts. To address this, we develop \textit{personalized reasoning guardrails} with three components. \textbf{Personalized Reasoning Distillation} links risks to relevant patient fields. \te
saca8585783.summary: MedGuardBench introduces a patient-conditioned medication safety benchmark with 5,001 scenarios across 87 medications, finding standard guardrails rely on surface cues.
saca8585783.why: Shows generic guardrails miss patient-specific risk, which matters for teams deploying safety filters in healthcare settings.

sffe81ed8f2.title: Can You Undo It? Reversibility Classes for AI Agent Actions
sffe81ed8f2.description: arXiv:2611.22075v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-using AI agents change files, databases, access rights and public information, yet permission to call a tool does not establish whether a mistake can be undone. We present Reversibility Classes, a declared five-level vocabulary with argument-sensitive rules, conservative defaults and an explicit prior-state capture contract. The pinned implementation and evidence-linked registry cover 536 tools across 20 MCP servers. All 738 rule-case checks conform to declared expectations, while native annotation mapping differs from draft registry labels for 118 of 481 comparable tools. One AI-assisted reviewer approves 148 ratings, 75 matching the registry; this is not independent agreement. On 2,158 recorded runs, the implemented session guard gates
sffe81ed8f2.summary: Reversibility Classes proposes a five-level vocabulary for whether AI agent tool actions can be undone, covering 536 tools across 20 MCP servers.
sffe81ed8f2.why: Gives engineers a way to gate agent actions by reversibility, since tool permission alone does not show whether a mistake can be undone.

sd3649c9361.title: When Lower Harm Misleads: Auditing Concept Corrections
sd3649c9361.description: arXiv:2611.22084v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An expert who corrects a concept prediction, such as a BI-RADS descriptor in breast ultrasound, expects the diagnosis to improve. Objectives that reduce the harm of such corrections are judged by harm and accuracy, yet harm also falls when a model responds less to every correction or starts from a worse uncorrected prediction, the reference for harm. We propose a correction audit, a reproducible evaluation protocol that separates these explanations: it splits each correction into harm and useful gain on identical events, separates the starting prediction from the correction response, and compares objectives with amplitude baselines matched in source harm. On three breast-ultrasound sources, worst-case correction training, evaluated from the m
sd3649c9361.summary: A correction audit protocol separates reductions in harm from concept corrections into explanations based on model responsiveness and starting-point accuracy.
sd3649c9361.why: Warns that lower correction harm can reflect a weaker model or worse baseline rather than real improvement, affecting how teams evaluate expert-in-the-loop systems.

sa9f6d39d69.title: ATLAS-Finance: Benchmarking AI Agents in Realistic Banking Environments
sa9f6d39d69.description: arXiv:2611.22085v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Professional work involves under-specified assignments, where relevant information is spread across workplace applications and may conflict or change over time. To evaluate how well frontier agents can perform economically valuable work in such settings, we introduce ATLAS-Finance, a benchmark of 100 end-to-end investment-banking tasks across 13 simulated firms. As in real banking workflows, agents must search email, chat, calendars, notes, and files to identify requirements, gather information, reconcile conflicts/updates, and then build complex financial models. Tasks were developed by experienced bankers based on their real deal work and take them 15-30 hours to complete. Agent deliverables are evaluated with expert-authored rubrics (media
sa9f6d39d69.summary: ATLAS-Finance benchmarks AI agents on 100 end-to-end investment-banking tasks across 13 simulated firms that require searching email, chat, and files.
sa9f6d39d69.why: Provides a realistic enterprise benchmark for agent work involving conflicting and changing information across workplace tools.

s9abe45a7a6.title: EvoDisco: Strategy Discovery for Evolving Agent Memory
s9abe45a7a6.description: arXiv:2611.22102v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model agents accumulate experience in memory, and how that memory evolves during interaction is as important as what it stores. Recent methods update memory online, yet both the operators that transform memory and the rules that select them remain fixed by design. We propose EvoDisco, which formulates agent memory evolution as evolutionary strategy discovery: the agent must discover which operator to apply, when to apply it, and how to instantiate it, rather than rewriting memory under a static operator schedule. A learnable policy conditions on the current memory state and recent task history, then selects and instantiates one of four semantic operators---Abstract, Refine, Bridge, and Reframe---which respectively compress rela
s9abe45a7a6.summary: EvoDisco frames agent memory evolution as strategy discovery, with a learnable policy choosing which memory operator to apply, when, and how.
s9abe45a7a6.why: Proposes learning memory-update policies instead of fixed schedules, which may affect how long-running agents manage accumulated experience.

s97d0bd5979.title: From Sorry to QED: Refining LLM Math Proofs via Angelic Execution
s97d0bd5979.description: arXiv:2611.22103v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can now generate Lean proof scripts that capture the high-level structure of many mathematical arguments. However, these scripts frequently fail on complex theorems: a single missing side condition or misapplied lemma can cause the prover to abort early and discard an otherwise viable proof outline. This paper presents MathEye, a framework that converts imperfect LLM-generated proof scripts into fully verified Lean proofs by combining symbolic reasoning with minimal human interaction. At the core of MathEye is angelic proof checking, an optimistic execution model that replaces failing proof fragments with placeholders while preserving the overall structure of the argument. This optimistic check produces an angelic
s97d0bd5979.summary: MathEye is a framework that turns imperfect LLM-generated Lean proof scripts into fully verified proofs using symbolic reasoning and minimal human input.
s97d0bd5979.why: Shows a route to salvaging failed LLM proof drafts in formal verification, reducing the cost of getting machine-checked proofs.

s0e9137d72d.title: RegimeCouncil: Paired-Evidence Routing For Memory Conflict Governance In LLM Agents
s0e9137d72d.description: arXiv:2611.22113v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language agents rely on long-term memory to personalize responses across extended interactions, yet stored facts quietly go stale as the world changes, and an agent often learns that using memory hurt only through delayed feedback after acting on an outdated record. Before the memory store is updated, how far should that negative feedback propagate: should it suppress memory use only on future queries for that same fact (a local policy), or also across other stored facts (a global policy)? Existing memory systems implicitly fix one of these two sharing scopes at design time. We formulate this online scope choice under hidden validity and delayed feedback as memory conflict governance, and prove that neither fixed policy is sufficient on its o
s0e9137d72d.summary: RegimeCouncil proposes paired-evidence routing to govern memory conflicts in LLM agents, deciding whether negative feedback on stale facts should apply locally or globally.
s0e9137d72d.why: Addresses how agents with long-term memory should handle outdated stored facts, a practical reliability problem for deployed agents.

s4920d00e28.title: TeleChat to Xing4: Advancing Frontier Agentic Models on Domestic Chips and Frameworks
s4920d00e28.description: arXiv:2611.22115v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present Xing 4, a series of large language models that extends the TeleChat lineage through coordinated advances in model architecture and training infrastructure on Ascend. This report describes the design principles and systems engineering behind the series, spanning architecture selection, large-scale pretraining, and reasoning and agentic post-training. We study how sparse activation, attention design, model depth and width, and speculative decoding balance model capacity with computation, memory access, and execution overhead. Our pretraining infrastructure builds on MindSpore HyperParallel, combining topology-aware hybrid sharding, efficient distributed optimizer execution, and coordinated management of long-sequence workloads and ac
s4920d00e28.summary: TeleChat's team released Xing 4, a series of LLMs built on Ascend chips, covering architecture, pretraining, and agentic post-training.
s4920d00e28.why: Documents training and inference engineering for frontier-scale agentic models on domestic Chinese hardware and frameworks.

se4a01defea.title: LoCaR: Localized Canvas Retrieval With Frozen Vision-Language Model
se4a01defea.description: arXiv:2611.22131v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Whole image embeddings can under represent small objects and local attributes that distinguish relevant images for localized queries. We present LoCaR, a training free framework for localized text to image retrieval with frozen vision language models. LoCaR constructs and utilizes independent proposals (SAM2) focusing on the object so as to get a more localized representation that independently encodes each region using the frozen visual encoder. We further study paired-support adaptation as an optional residual that uses matched text region exemplars without updating the underlying encoders. We also introduce LOCFG, a Visual Genome derived benchmark designed to evaluate localized retrieval for smaller and more challenging referents. Across s
se4a01defea.summary: LoCaR is a training-free method for localized text-to-image retrieval that encodes SAM2-proposed regions with a frozen vision-language model.
se4a01defea.why: Offers a no-training way to improve retrieval of small objects and local attributes, useful for search over image collections.

sad984d9790.title: Big Brains, Tiny Board: Pupavision, an Agentic Physical AI Instrument for Monitoring Drosophila Pupariation and Lifecycle Transitions
sad984d9790.description: arXiv:2611.22136v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many biology experiments are limited by the availability and ease of use of instruments that monitor and record them. For example, the timing of pupariation in the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster, a widely used model organism, can provide biologically relevant information about growth regulation and is often recorded manually. Here, we present Pupavision, a small physical AI instrument built from a single-board Linux computer and a day/night camera for roughly 45 to 75 US dollars in parts. The key idea is that a frontier coding agent runs its agentic harness directly on the tiny board. The model thinks in the cloud, but the agent works on the device. The agent assists image capture, writes code to repair errors, and checks the experiment ev
sad984d9790.summary: Pupavision is a low-cost physical AI instrument, built from a single-board Linux computer and a camera, that monitors Drosophila pupariation with a coding agent.
sad984d9790.why: Illustrates a low-cost pattern of agentic coding systems controlling physical sensing hardware for lab automation.

sc627ed034f.title: Long-Context Generation Is a Sampling Problem (When You Turn Up the Heat)
sc627ed034f.description: arXiv:2611.22148v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Open-weight language models are widely observed to get worse the longer they generate. Often, attempts to fix this involve more training. At high temperature, The sampler, i.e. the rule that picks the next token out of the model's probabilities, decides whether long and agentic generation survives and/or thrives. We test 29 open-weight models from 1B to 122B parameters on ten established benchmarks plus needle retrieval out to one million tokens, covering SWE-bench Verified coding agents, long chain-of-thought reasoning, long-form writing, long structured output and long-context reading. Samplers that keep their pool of candidate tokens small and steady as temperature rises don't lose accuracy. Samplers that let in low-probability tokens fall
sc627ed034f.summary: The study tests 29 open-weight models up to 122B parameters and finds long-generation quality depends heavily on the sampler, especially at high temperature.
sc627ed034f.why: Suggests sampler choice, not just more training, may determine whether long agentic generations hold up in production.

scfe4994145.title: Not All Evidence Is Admissible: Evidence Governance for Tool-Augmented Medical Agents
scfe4994145.description: arXiv:2611.22169v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-augmented medical agents treat whatever their tools return as evidence. We show that this default is costly: medical tools fail silently, and a frozen reasoner cannot ignore what enters its context, so many cases it would have answered correctly are flipped to wrong once tool outputs are added. We call this evidence hijacking. $\mathcal{V}$-information explains the phenomenon: the reasoner has lost the option to ignore, so a tool output can carry negative usable information, and moving the decision of what to keep outside the reasoner restores that option. The theory further shows that part of any filtering gain comes merely from letting the reasoner see less, and only selection by content lets it see better. Building on this, we recast
scfe4994145.summary: The paper introduces evidence hijacking, where tool outputs in medical agents flip correct answers to wrong, and proposes governing which evidence is kept.
scfe4994145.why: Shows tool outputs can degrade agent accuracy, so engineers need explicit evidence filtering in tool-augmented pipelines.

s36c0da284c.title: Readie: Low-Latency Code Sandboxes for AI Agents
s36c0da284c.description: arXiv:2611.22171v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: From quantitative research to personal assistance, AI agents act by iteratively generating and executing code. To decouple the agent harness from code execution, many agents offload execution to dedicated systems called code sandboxes. However, existing code sandboxes suffer from slow startup. Whether they rely on custom snapshots or a single fat image, the root cause is the same: it is hard to build a compact, pre-warmed snapshot that can be shared across diverse agent-generated code while covering nearly all the artifacts (e.g., packages, datasets) it requires. In this work, we propose learned startup snapshots for low-latency code sandboxes. Our insight is that while it is hard for a single snapshot to be both compact and cover most worklo
s36c0da284c.summary: Readie presents low-latency code sandboxes for AI agents, using pre-warmed shared snapshots to address slow startup times.
s36c0da284c.why: Startup latency in code execution sandboxes directly affects agent responsiveness and infrastructure design.

s7d1c9600a8.title: Reconfiguring Procedural Knowledge for Compositional Robot Skill Adaptation
s7d1c9600a8.description: arXiv:2611.22174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: General-purpose behavior models increasingly internalize broad procedural knowledge during training, making their adaptation to new goals and skill interfaces less a problem of learning entirely new behaviors than of reconfiguring existing competence. We study this capability as reconfigurability, the ability to realize new behaviors by cost-efficiently restructuring existing components and relations under sparse governing information, where task specifications provide high-level goals and procedure specifications expose a limited set of reusable factors, leaving the concrete bindings and compositions required for execution underdetermined. We propose RecPo, a framework that represents skills task-agnostically through multiple procedure views
s7d1c9600a8.summary: The paper studies reconfigurability, adapting general-purpose robot behavior models to new goals by restructuring existing skill components under sparse guidance.
s7d1c9600a8.why: Points toward adapting robot skills by recombining learned components rather than training new behaviors from scratch.

sad8a29a08d.title: The Only Edge Was Memorized in Training: LLM Trading Agents Around Earnings and Bad News
sad8a29a08d.description: arXiv:2611.22177v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) trading agents are tested on news, but news reaches stock prices within minutes, and a benchmark that replays headlines at their publication time finds no alpha in trading on them. Money can then remain in two places, before news whose date is known, such as earnings announcements, and after bad news, if the market's fall went too far. However, studies of LLMs and earnings read documents published with or after the announcement, and studies of reversal sort monthly portfolios, so neither tells whether an agent can trade these moments after costs. In this paper, we test LLM agents at both moments on the same look-ahead-free benchmark, before 598 earnings announcements and after 409 bad-news drops of large US stocks.
