These assumptions are problematic in partially observable environments, where task-relevant objectives, affordances, and dynamics must be discovered through interaction rather than disclosed a priori. We formalise this problem setting by introducing WATERFALL, an iterative population-based workflow for automated reward discovery under the str
s88e4c16e91.summary: WATERFALL proposes a workflow that uses evolutionary, foundation-model-driven reward formulation to automate reward design in partially observable RL settings.
s88e4c16e91.why: Targets the reward-design bottleneck in sparse-reward RL, which could reduce manual engineering effort for training agents.

s1ddde3bbc8.title: Learning Agent-Centric Vision-Language-Action World Models for Autonomous Driving
s1ddde3bbc8.description: arXiv:2611.22880v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent progress in integrating vision-language-action (VLA) models with world modeling has significantly advanced end-to-end autonomous driving by allowing systems to reason about imagined futures instead of merely reacting to current observations. However, most world VLA models generate future frames at the pixel level with plenty of dense visual tokens. Although such generated futures can be visually plausible, they preserve many driving-irrelevant appearance details, i.e., only a small portion of the tokens directly encode critical planning-relevant factors, such as agent geometry, motion dynamics, and interactions. This introduces a significant performance bottleneck. An important question thus arises: what world state should a world VL
s1ddde3bbc8.summary: A paper proposes agent-centric vision-language-action world models that imagine driving-relevant future states instead of dense pixel-level frames.
s1ddde3bbc8.why: Suggests more efficient planning representations for autonomous driving by discarding appearance details irrelevant to planning.

s06f0df07c7.title: Stopping Is Not the Limit: Understanding and Eliciting Agent Capability in Long-Horizon Vulnerability Exploitation
s06f0df07c7.description: arXiv:2611.22888v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vulnerability exploitation tests whether language model agents can develop working exploits from known software flaws. Sequential test-time scaling can improve exploitation performance, but larger budgets do not ensure sustained exploration: agents often stop with budget remaining. Yet what happens when execution continues beyond stopping remains underexplored. We investigate this gap on ExploitBench using DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 and MiMo-V2.6-Pro. We find additional verified gains after the first stop response, but gains diminish over longer execution. We identify two patterns associated with less productive continuation: an increasing proportion of stop responses within the same context and earlier stopping associated with summaries retain
s06f0df07c7.summary: Researchers study long-horizon vulnerability exploitation by LLM agents on ExploitBench, finding additional verified gains continue after agents first stop.
s06f0df07c7.why: Shows agents often halt with budget left and that continuing execution yields further gains, relevant to evaluating autonomous security agents.

s4d6e23e305.title: When Do Typed Decision Models Work in Transportation? Evidence from Travel Choice and Traffic Signal Control
s4d6e23e305.description: arXiv:2611.22926v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Typed decision models combine natural-language understanding with a structured interface that returns a selected action and an option-level probability distribution without generating lengthy textual responses. Their low inference cost and response latency make them attractive for transportation problems with predefined alternatives. This paper investigates their effectiveness, robustness, and efficiency in two representative transportation tasks: individual travel-mode choice prediction and sequential traffic signal control. We systematically evaluate TypeSafe Jev and GPT-6 Luna Decisions against conventional transportation methods, reinforcement learning algorithms, and four chat-based large language models. Experiments on the Swissmetro
s4d6e23e305.summary: A paper evaluates typed decision models, which return a selected action and option probabilities, on travel-mode choice and traffic signal control.
s4d6e23e305.why: Indicates low-latency structured LLM decision interfaces may suit transportation tasks with predefined options, though robustness is still under study.

s15f90f8c79.title: Projected Penalty-Gradient Tracking for Communication-Efficient Byzantine-Resilient Federated Learning
s15f90f8c79.description: arXiv:2611.22929v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate communication-efficient federated learning over heterogeneous datasets in the presence of Byzantine adversaries capable of uploading arbitrary information. Penalty-based methods bound the influence of each worker through the bounded gradient of a penalty function; however, the bound is lost once the uploads are compressed, since a Byzantine worker can accumulate an unbounded state at the server. To retain the Byzantine resilience under compressed uploads, we propose a projected penalty-gradient tracking framework, where each honest worker uploads a compressed residual of its penalty gradient and the server projects each reconstructed state onto the known penalty-gradient ball. The framework accommodates any contractive compre
s15f90f8c79.summary: A paper proposes projected penalty-gradient tracking to keep Byzantine resilience in communication-efficient federated learning with compressed uploads.
s15f90f8c79.why: Addresses a gap where compression breaks Byzantine robustness guarantees, relevant to federated systems over heterogeneous data.

se8b0406393.title: Hierarchical Diffusion Transformer for End-to-End Image Generation
se8b0406393.description: arXiv:2611.22962v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Pixel-space diffusion learns visual representations and image generation jointly in a single end-to-end training stage, without a separately pretrained visual encoder. However, plain pixel-space Transformers still trail leading two-stage latent diffusion models in generation quality and training efficiency. We hypothesize that part of this gap arises from retaining one token per patch throughout the backbone, which does not explicitly encourage a visual hierarchy that summarizes related content at progressively coarser levels. To address this, we introduce Hierarchical Diffusion Transformers (HiT), which progressively group related tokens and represent each group with a single token. The main Transformer bottleneck processes these compact g
se8b0406393.summary: A hierarchical diffusion transformer is proposed for pixel-space end-to-end image generation, aiming to close the gap with latent diffusion models.

sfe2ef82693.title: High-Dimensional Black-Box Optimization via Guidance Sampling of Diffusion Models
sfe2ef82693.description: arXiv:2611.22965v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many real-world optimization problems involve optimizing black-box objectives for which only a limited number of evaluations are available. Bayesian optimization (BO) is a powerful framework for such problems, but its effectiveness often deteriorates in high-dimensional spaces. Recent work leverages diffusion models for black-box optimization, often through pre-training a reward-conditioned score network to steer generation towards high-reward samples. Alternatively, gradient-based guidance methods assume access to a differentiable reward function from which guidance gradients are queried. However, these approaches either require large amounts of labeled data for offline training or access to exact reward gradients, limiting their applicabi
sfe2ef82693.summary: A paper proposes guidance sampling with diffusion models for high-dimensional black-box optimization where evaluations are limited.

sc294c9f8f8.title: CodeReel: Accelerating Code-to-Video Agents with Exact Frame Reuse and Blocking-Aware Scheduling
sc294c9f8f8.description: arXiv:2611.22967v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coding agents make videos by writing and refining programs in a build--inspect--edit loop. A finished film costs a median of $2.85 in model calls and 11 minutes, over a third of that time in builds that block the agent. We find that much of this time is avoidable, for two reasons. First, 37.5% of the frames of a session's later films were drawn before, many shifted in time or inside an edited scene. Second, half of the builds stop at a check, where the agent needs only the verdict, but which builds stop is unknown until the checks finish. We present CodeReel, a training-free execution layer behind agents' existing commands. Exact frame reuse keys each frame by its drawing commands, regardless of its position in time, and reuses each frame w
sc294c9f8f8.summary: CodeReel proposes reusing previously drawn frames and scheduling builds to speed up coding agents that generate videos via programs.
sc294c9f8f8.why: Shows how caching and non-blocking build scheduling can cut latency and cost in iterative coding-agent loops.

s6a43b2749f.title: SEAM: Computer-Use Agents Know the Harm Between Screens, and Commit It Anyway
s6a43b2749f.description: arXiv:2611.22971v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Safety benchmarks for computer-use agents (CUAs) place the harm either in the intent of the task or on a single screen: a malicious instruction, an injected command, a phishing page. An agent that checks the task and each screen in isolation can pass them, so they do not test whether it combines facts seen on different screens. Yet in delegated work, harm often arises exactly this way: a fact about a person on one screen, a fact about an item on another, and a legitimate task that binds them. We introduce SEAM (Safety Execution Across Multiple screens), a benchmark of such cross-screen compositional harm: 600 multi-step, cross-application OSWorld tasks in which the instruction and every single observation are benign and only their combinati
s6a43b2749f.summary: SEAM is a new safety benchmark testing whether computer-use agents detect harm arising from combining facts across multiple screens.
s6a43b2749f.why: Existing single-screen safety tests may miss cross-screen harms, so agent evaluations need multi-step checks before deployment.

s7532ce56e0.title: Large Language Models Have Not Yet Transformed Science
s7532ce56e0.description: arXiv:2611.22975v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The emergence of large language models (LLMs) in late 2022 has raised questions about the future of science, but assessing their impact requires understanding how scientific practices were already evolving. We analyze 2.5 million full-text papers across five disciplines from 2015 to 2025, tracing trends over a broad spectrum of lexical, structural, epistemological, and social dimensions. Aside from frequency shifts in some words, most pre-2023 trends continued with limited detectable breaks. Among the notable exceptions, growth in computer science coauthor teams accelerated significantly in Asia, while apparent declines in biomedical topic diversity largely reflected standardization in article formats. Our study establishes an empirical fou
s7532ce56e0.summary: An analysis of 2.5 million full-text papers from 2015 to 2025 finds most pre-2023 science trends continued, with few detectable LLM-driven breaks.

s2683b96f65.title: How Web Research Agents Interpret User Priorities
s2683b96f65.description: arXiv:2611.22989v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Web research agents gather information online and write cited reports, including financial analysis. Users can state a priority to guide this research, but a priority may not say how to judge the options, leaving the agent to choose the criteria. We examine how two such agents, built on OpenAI and Anthropic models, interpret a stated priority. In 36 runs, the agents compared Microsoft and Alphabet as businesses. Prompts asked for special attention to growth or resilience, or gave no priority. We analyzed reports, searches, returned sources and cited sources. Of the 24 reports given a priority, 21 focused on it, but their criteria varied. Under the growth priority, OpenAI reports that ranked the companies accounted for risk or predictability
s2683b96f65.summary: A study of two web research agents built on OpenAI and Anthropic models finds they interpret stated user priorities inconsistently when comparing companies.
s2683b96f65.why: Shows that agent outputs depend on criteria the agent picks when a user's priority is vague, which affects reliability of research workflows.

sa14c425cd6.title: Check Your Blind Spots: Decision-Guided Perception by Probing the Planner with Hypothetical Objects
sa14c425cd6.description: arXiv:2611.23030v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Not every perception error changes the planner's action. Yet adaptive-resolution perception chooses where to spend high-resolution computation from image cues, which can neither reliably point to an object that low resolution missed nor tell which objects matter to the planner. We observe that the planner can say where an object would matter before anything is seen: inserting a hypothetical object at a location tests whether its action would change. Decision-Guided Speculative Perception (DGSP) treats the low-resolution scene and its action as a draft and probes the planner in this way to obtain a decision-sensitivity field, the locations where an unseen object would change the action. Only this field and the support, the detections on whic
sa14c425cd6.summary: DGSP probes a planner with hypothetical inserted objects to decide where to spend high-resolution perception compute.
sa14c425cd6.why: Offers a way to direct perception compute based on whether errors would change the planner's action.

sac17f62c66.title: ReTouchGS: Ultralight Render-free Aesthetic Color Enhancement and Transfer for 3D Gaussian Splatting
sac17f62c66.description: arXiv:2611.23054v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables photorealistic scene reconstruction. Existing 3DGS color transfer and interactive editing methods are guided by reference images and user-specified color adjustments. However, in many applications, users simply want aesthetically guided color enhancement that automatically makes the scene more visually appealing while maintaining consistent colors and tones across viewpoints. We present ReTouchGS, to our knowledge the first framework for reference-free aesthetic color enhancement of pretrained 3DGS models. It predicts a scene-level color lookup table (LUT) from the model and its associated camera parameters. ReTouchGS also supports reference-guided color transfer by fitting a scene-level LUT using one ed
sac17f62c66.summary: ReTouchGS introduces a reference-free method for automatically enhancing the aesthetic color of pretrained 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes.

sfaece97052.title: Runtime Verification of Multiple Natural Language Criteria for Agent Governance
sfaece97052.description: arXiv:2611.23074v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI agents are governed by hundreds of natural language criteria, yet existing verifiers cannot efficiently evaluate an agent's output against a large set of such criteria and report which are satisfied, violated, or inapplicable. We introduce the VFM, a tree-attention verifier that encodes the shared context and target text, and scores N natural language criteria in parallel, returning independent per-criterion ternary verdicts. The VFM is pretrained on CriteriaBank, a corpus of 394K (context, target, criterion, verdict) tuples spanning over 321K distinct criterion strings. A finetuned VFM-4B outperforms GPT-5.4 on a synthetic governance benchmark. On the DynaBench multi-criterion benchmark, it outperforms DynaGuard-4B on trace-level failur
sfaece97052.summary: VFM is a tree-attention verifier that scores many natural language criteria in parallel, giving per-criterion verdicts for agent outputs, trained on CriteriaBank.
sfaece97052.why: Makes checking agent outputs against hundreds of governance rules more efficient, relevant to production agent oversight.

sff3ee5a269.title: Learning to Undo: Transfer Reinforcement Learning under State Space Transformations
sff3ee5a269.description: arXiv:2611.23081v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Transfer learning in reinforcement learning (RL) has shown strong empirical success. In this work, we take a more principled perspective by studying when and how transferring knowledge between MDPs (a source and a target) can be provably beneficial. Specifically, we consider the case where there exists an undo map such that applying this map to the target's state space recovers the source exactly. We propose an algorithm that learns this map by matching state feature statistics gathered from both MDPs, and then uses it to transfer the source policy to the target. We theoretically justify the algorithm by analyzing the setting when the undo map is linear and the source is linearly-$Q^\star$ realizable, where our approach has strictly better
sff3ee5a269.summary: The paper studies when transfer reinforcement learning between MDPs is provably beneficial, using a learned undo map that aligns the target state space with the source.

se9539cf41a.title: BugGen 2.0: Rethinking the Roles of LLMs for Scalable RTL Bug Synthesis
se9539cf41a.description: arXiv:2611.23091v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI-assisted RTL localization and debugging need ground-truth bug datasets with known locations and observable failures, while testbench grading uses injected bugs to measure detection capability. Creating such datasets at scale remains a major EDA challenge. BugGen 1.0 shows that Large Language Models (LLMs) can generate context-aware RTL mutations. Still, it relies on the model for both choosing where to mutate and generating the edit, which increases inference costs and can lead to invalid choices. BugGen 2.0 changes this division of labor. Deterministic algorithms handle structural analysis, target selection, and validation, while the LLM focuses on localized semantic rewriting. Across four OpenTitan IP blocks and FabScalar with three LL
se9539cf41a.summary: BugGen 2.0 separates the roles of LLMs in generating RTL bug datasets, aiming to lower inference costs and reduce invalid mutation choices.
se9539cf41a.why: Offers a cheaper, more reliable route to large bug datasets for hardware verification and debugging tools.

s7406c3c17e.title: What's in a Tree ? Hierarchical $n$-gram models as controlled approximators of language
s7406c3c17e.description: arXiv:2611.23093v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hierarchical models have been proposed as synthetic settings for studying language. However, their relevance to realistic language corpora remains underexplored. In this work, we introduce tree-grams, autoregressive generative $n$-gram models that build the conditional probability tensor $p(x_n \mid x_{1:n-1})$ through a hierarchical composition of order-2 and order-3 tensors. $n$ controls the maximal context window, whereas a rank hyperparameter $d$ controls model capacity, yielding an interpretable and systematically scalable family of approximators of language. We show how tree-grams outperform existing $n$-gram baselines, while remaining competitive with deep transformer-based language models. We demonstrate the utility of such controll
s7406c3c17e.summary: The paper introduces tree-grams, hierarchical n-gram models with controllable context window and capacity, as approximators of language.

sc0b2981adb.title: Natural Language Programming: Rethinking Language, Memory, and Cognition in the Era of Generative AI
sc0b2981adb.description: arXiv:2611.23106v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence is transforming the role of natural language in computational systems. In classical Natural Language Processing (NLP), language was treated as an object of computation: something to analyse, classify, translate, or generate. Large Language Models (LLMs) challenge this perspective, enabling natural language to function increasingly as an executable cognitive medium through which humans structure reasoning, orchestrate problem solving, and regulate hybrid human/AI workflows. This paper introduces Natural Language Programming (NLPg) as a theoretical and epistemological extension of traditional NLP. Rather than focusing on language understanding alone, NLPg conceptualises prompts as dynamic cognitive artefacts
sc0b2981adb.summary: A paper argues natural language is becoming an executable cognitive medium for orchestrating reasoning and hybrid human-AI workflows.

sc1dcf2e2fc.title: Mind the Gap: A Deployed Multi-Agent System for Documentation Maintenance
sc1dcf2e2fc.description: arXiv:2611.23142v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The "AI revolution" has enabled teams across the technology industry to deliver software features at unprecedented velocity. While code evolves faster than ever, customer-facing documentation often struggles to stay up to speed. As users increasingly rely on LLM-based agents that consume documentation as their primary interface, the impact of this documentation gap worsens: stale information propagates and is treated as authoritative. Signals for identifying where documentation has fallen behind already exist in abundance, both explicit (e.g., resolved support tickets revealing what documentation lacks) and implicit (e.g., code-documentation discrepancies detectable from automated loops). We deploy a multi-agent system, built around a triag
sc1dcf2e2fc.summary: A deployed multi-agent system is described for finding and maintaining stale customer-facing documentation as code changes.
sc1dcf2e2fc.why: Addresses stale docs that LLM agents consume as authoritative, a concrete problem for teams shipping fast-changing software.

saeaa43eb80.title: Learning Stratified Policies for Inference-Time Objectives
saeaa43eb80.description: arXiv:2611.23154v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Inference-time scaling improves the performance of large language models by sampling multiple responses and evaluating their collective utility. However, many existing approaches obtain these samples by repeatedly sampling from a single policy. In this work, we study if the sample budget at inference time can instead be allocated across a population of policies. We introduce stratified policies, where each of $k$ learned policies contributes one response to a $k$-sample inference-time objective. We realize this policy population using separate LoRA adapters on a shared language model backbone and optimize it for pass@$k$. We theoretically motivate the approach by analyzing the linear setting; a population of LoRAs can achieve zero best-of-$
saeaa43eb80.summary: The paper proposes stratified policies, where k learned policies each contribute one response to a k-sample inference-time objective.
saeaa43eb80.why: Suggests spreading inference sampling budget across policy populations rather than one policy, a possible lever for better test-time scaling.

s0db4b8d588.title: Attribution Through the Decoder: Prediction-Space Explanations for Structured Outputs
s0db4b8d588.description: arXiv:2611.23161v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Networks that predict angles, gaze directions, and rotations do not output these quantities directly: they emit raw coordinates that a fixed decoder, such as normalization, maps to the final prediction. Attribution methods are usually applied to the raw coordinates, so they can credit inputs for changes the decoder discards, such as rescaling a vector when only its direction matters. The resulting explanation can highlight inputs that have no effect on the prediction. We instead attribute through the decoder differential, which for normalization decoders reduces to a scaled tangent projection. We characterize invariance to output rescaling, show that every fixed smooth scalar target on a sphere has points of zero tangential sensitivity, and
s0db4b8d588.summary: The paper proposes attributing predictions through a fixed decoder such as normalization, so explanations ignore inputs the decoder discards.

s165f256efb.title: Inference after coding agents
s165f256efb.description: arXiv:2611.23174v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Empirical research is changing rapidly as AI coding agents are becoming increasingly proficient in every step of it, from writing code to manipulating data. We argue that while the potential of coding agents for science is vast, their use in hypothesis testing poses a substantial threat to classical inference, as these agents enable a supercharged form of selective inference. In particular, we argue that coding agents carrying out empirical research introduce a new type of post-selection inference that combines human-like, open-ended search over an implicit space of estimators with programmatic replayability of both the selection and the estimation process. Indeed, we find that on simulated data with zero effects, four frontier agents repor
s165f256efb.summary: The paper argues AI coding agents enable a new form of post-selection inference that threatens the validity of classical hypothesis testing in empirical research.
s165f256efb.why: Warns that agent-driven analysis can inflate false findings, relevant to anyone using agents for data analysis.

seb0ce0b58a.title: Say Less, Hallucinate Less? Diagnosing and Restoring Object Coverage in Preference-Optimized Vision-Language Models
seb0ce0b58a.description: arXiv:2611.23179v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Preference optimization (PO) is the standard way to reduce object hallucination in large vision-language models. We find that four public PO checkpoints of LLaVA-1.5-7B also lower object coverage. They name fewer object categories, and their lower hallucination rates bring no significant gain in set-level object F1 on CHAIR. We therefore ask how much of the PO gain the base model can reproduce by stopping earlier. A positive end-of-sequence (EOS) logit bias lets the base model reach the recall of each PO model, and this early stopping alone reproduces 58 to 86 percent of the CHAIRi gain of three checkpoints on two disjoint COCO sets. Writing longer does not bring the lost categories back. Under greedy decoding, a negative EOS bias recovers
seb0ce0b58a.summary: Researchers found four public preference-optimized LLaVA-1.5-7B checkpoints name fewer objects, and a base model with an EOS logit bias can match their recall.
seb0ce0b58a.why: Reducing hallucination via preference optimization may silently cut object coverage, so teams should measure recall alongside hallucination rates.

s5063a37858.title: Retrieval-Augmented Correction for Generalist Medical Image Segmentation
s5063a37858.description: arXiv:2611.23189v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Automated segmentation is routinely used as the first step in quantitative image-based clinical workflows, where predicted masks are subsequently reviewed and corrected by human operators. Automated correction of the residual structural errors is currently addressed one anatomy at a time, so the number of trained correctors scales with the number of segmentation targets. We present GRACE, a retrieval-augmented refiner that edits an input mask under context drawn from a shared knowledge base of verified prior cases. The refiner is trained once on a multi-organ corpus spanning compact organs, cavities, branching vessels, and tumour lesions. In the held-out dataset-transfer evaluation, three held-out datasets query a fixed knowledge base built
s5063a37858.summary: GRACE is a retrieval-augmented refiner that corrects medical image segmentation masks using a shared knowledge base of verified prior cases, trained once across anatomies.
s5063a37858.why: A single shared corrector could reduce the need to train separate correction models for each segmentation target in clinical workflows.

s954964cde4.title: Structure--Residual Inductive Biases for Language Model Pretraining
s954964cde4.description: arXiv:2611.23197v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Next-token prediction is relied upon to learn both predictive behavior and internal representations. We ask whether representation structure itself should be an explicit inductive bias. Motivated by the two-part coding view of Kolmogorov complexity, we study a structure--residual principle in which a representation separates structure from realization detail. We instantiate this principle in two complementary ways. Boundary Bottleneck Concept (BBC) routes information from token segments through boundary carriers while preserving local autoregressive computation. Continuous Concept (CC) regularizes representation geometry and induces a spectral decomposition into low-frequency structure and high-frequency residual. We derive coding bounds fo
s954964cde4.summary: Researchers propose structure-residual inductive biases for language model pretraining, separating representation structure from realization detail, inspired by Kolmogorov complexity.

s198c4b1551.title: Fine-Tuning Gemma 4 Edge Models for MATLAB Signal-Processing Code with SFT and QLoRA on a Laptop iGPU
s198c4b1551.description: arXiv:2611.23205v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Small language models that run on a laptop are attractive for writing signal-processing code offline, but they make systematic errors on digital signal processing (DSP) conventions. We apply supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to the Gemma 4 edge models E2B and E4B with 66 checked examples covering 11 signal-processing MATLAB subtasks, using low-rank adaptation (LoRA) and quantized LoRA (QLoRA) on the integrated GPU (iGPU) of a laptop, and deploy the 8-bit integer (int8) models with the adapters through OpenVINO. On held-out variants scored by deterministic checkers, the pass rate rises from 18/66 to 37/66 (LoRA) and 37/66 (QLoRA) for E2B and from 32/66 to 47/66 for E4B (QLoRA). Reading all 159 failing programs shows that the adapters remove most
s198c4b1551.summary: Researchers fine-tuned Gemma 4 edge models with SFT and QLoRA on 66 examples for MATLAB signal-processing code, deploying int8 models via OpenVINO on a laptop iGPU.
s198c4b1551.why: It shows small local models can be specialized for niche code domains on consumer hardware using modest data and open tooling.

sd3943358cd.title: Reading Scene States: Uncovering Safety Failures in Vision-Language Models
sd3943358cd.description: arXiv:2611.23206v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can provide harmful assistance by interpreting visual events, even without an explicit request for the underlying harmful objective. We identify this \textbf{scene-state safety vulnerability} and introduce \textbf{SceneSafetyBench}, comprising 375 image--question pairs spanning Initial, Medium, and Ultimate scene states and five visual presentations. Across eight VLMs, scene-state inputs elicit harmful assistance with attack success rates (ASRs) of 45.6--72.3\%. Comparative analysis across three VLMs shows that scene-state inputs most closely resemble QR-related images in their layer-wise safety-related signal profiles, while exhibiting lower average late-layer readouts and distinct signal dynamics during gener
sd3943358cd.summary: SceneSafetyBench, with 375 image-question pairs, finds eight VLMs give harmful assistance to scene-state inputs at 45.6–72.3% attack success rates.
sd3943358cd.why: Safety filters that only check explicit harmful requests may miss harm inferred from visual scenes, a gap teams deploying VLMs should test for.

s2e072b3182.title: Higher-Scoring Coding Models Did Not Get More Work Done
s2e072b3182.description: arXiv:2611.23216v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: New coding models advertise themselves on score improvements of coding benchmarks. Yet no study has tested if a model that scores higher on these benchmarks gets more real work done. On June 12, 2026, a U.S. export control directive banned access to Claude Fable 5 for 19 days, which forced users to switch to other models. During this time, most former Fable 5 users switched to Opus 4.8 (11 points lower on SWE-Bench Pro compared to Fable 5). We treat this suspension as a natural experiment, where the people and projects stayed the same and only the model changed, so we could isolate the effect of Fable 5 on user productivity. We tracked GitHub pull requests of 297 Fable 5 users before, during, and after the suspension. We used 8,908 develope
s2e072b3182.summary: A study uses a June 2026 U.S. export control suspension of Claude Fable 5 as a natural experiment to test whether higher-scoring coding models get more real work done.
s2e072b3182.why: It questions whether coding benchmark gains translate into productivity, relevant when choosing models based on leaderboard scores.

sc1d68dd9f2.title: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?
sc1d68dd9f2.description: arXiv:2611.23219v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM agents increasingly drive their own learning. Self-improvement methods delegate various components of model optimization to the models themselves. As models become more capable, this motivates a basic question: do these increasingly capable models still need us to specify how they should self-improve? In this paper we study an autonomous paradigm in which, given basic primitives, resources, and a general goal for self-improvement, agents construct their own self-learning algorithm for context-based optimization. Using the setting of gameplay as a testbed, a frozen LLM agent is given a compute budget and tools for collecting experience and updating text documents, and allowed to freely experiment without an externally imposed loop or acc
sc1d68dd9f2.summary: The paper studies whether LLM agents, given basic primitives and a goal, can construct their own self-improvement algorithms for context-based optimization without human-specified methods.

sbbcad6cddc.title: StringQFT: A Multiuse Textbook Resource for AI-Assisted Theoretical Physics
sbbcad6cddc.description: arXiv:2611.23225v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present StringQFT as a textbook collection for string constructions of quantum field theory and as infrastructure for AI-assisted theoretical physics. The collection comprises 18 volumes, 190 chapters and 3,795 pages, covering brane probes, brane webs, geometric engineering, F-theory constructions, wrapped M5-branes and exact worldsheet constructions. Its open-book benchmark inventory contains 1,073 items, including 499 with automatic finite-answer checking. For retrieval-augmented generation, it provides 1,371 section records linked to textbook sources and PDF locations, together with a local lexical retriever. Training-data preparation is illustrated by 21 private, source-linked examples. For agents, it exposes 19 calculation tools wit
sbbcad6cddc.summary: StringQFT is a 18-volume, 190-chapter open textbook collection on string constructions of quantum field theory, with a 1,073-item benchmark and RAG records for AI-assisted physics.

sb9bf99bdba.title: Ambient LLMs: Data-Efficient Supervised Fine-tuning via Temperature Matching
sb9bf99bdba.description: arXiv:2611.23229v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Collecting large-scale, diverse, and high-quality post-training datasets for autoregressive language models is challenging. Consequently, Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) is typically applied to datasets significantly smaller than those used for pre-training, which leads to overfitting and the catastrophic forgetting of the tails of the data distribution. To prevent this collapse, we introduce Ambient SFT, a principled framework for leveraging imperfect predictions to augment the fine-tuning set. In our method, a "frozen" version of the pre-trained model serves as a noisy teacher that the fine-tuned model must match at a coarse level. In particular, we require that the high-temperature versions of the conditional distributions produced by the p
sb9bf99bdba.summary: Ambient SFT is a method that uses a frozen pre-trained model's imperfect predictions to augment small fine-tuning sets, aiming to avoid overfitting and catastrophic forgetting.
sb9bf99bdba.why: Offers a data-efficient fine-tuning technique for teams with limited post-training datasets who risk overfitting or forgetting.

sfb5f5b4c25.title: AI Simulations Grounded in Rich Self-Reports Increase Accuracy and Reduce Distortion
sfb5f5b4c25.description: arXiv:2411.10109v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: AI simulations of people built from demographic prompts often misjudge individuals and distort sample-level patterns. We test whether rich self-report data reduce these problems. We developed an AI voice interviewer and conducted two-hour interviews following the American Voices Project protocol with 1,052 U.S. adults, who also completed surveys and behavioral experiments. For each participant, we compared simulations prompted with demographic attributes, self-authored personas, survey responses, interview responses, or combined surveys and interviews. We evaluated accuracy on held-out responses, and measured eight statistical distortions at the sample level: biased averages, compressed variance, distorted response distributions, over-cor
sfb5f5b4c25.summary: A study with 1,052 U.S. adults finds AI simulations grounded in rich interview and survey self-reports are more accurate and less distorted than demographic-prompted simulations.
sfb5f5b4c25.why: Richer individual data appears to improve simulation fidelity over demographic prompts, relevant to teams building persona-based AI simulations.

sde58ad536c.title: Exploring Explainable Multi-agent MCTS-minimax Hybrids in Board Game Using Process Mining
sde58ad536c.description: arXiv:2503.23326v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Monte-Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) is a family of sampling-based search algorithms widely used for online planning in sequential decision-making domains and at the heart of many recent advances in artificial intelligence. Understanding the behavior of MCTS agents is difficult for developers and users due to the frequently large and complex search trees that result from the simulation of many possible futures, their evaluations, and their relationships. This paper presents our ongoing investigation into potential explanations for the decision-making and behavior of MCTS. A weakness of MCTS is that it constructs a highly selective tree and, as a result, can miss crucial moves and fall into tactical traps. Full-width minimax search constitutes t
sde58ad536c.summary: The paper presents ongoing work on explaining MCTS-minimax hybrid agents in board games using process mining to interpret decision-making.

sd4b7ed38e3.title: Building verifiable databases at scale from the chemical literature via a multi-agent system
sd4b7ed38e3.description: arXiv:2507.20230v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Accelerating chemical research with artificial intelligence requires high-quality databases. However, many reactions exist only as graphics drawn for human readers, which machines must read exactly. Specialist software is precise but rigid, whereas multimodal language models are flexible yet often write incorrect structures; neither flags errors. We present ChemEAGLE, a multi-agent system where tools supply structures and a language model extends their reach through judgments that programs apply. On 424 published graphics, its F1 score for exactly correct reactions was 82.2%, against 47.7% for a tool-equipped generalist agent, and calibrated confidence limited review to 35% of reactions at 96.6% accuracy. Without review, it built a 60,103
sd4b7ed38e3.summary: ChemEAGLE is a multi-agent system combining specialist chemistry tools with a language model to extract verifiable reaction databases from published chemical graphics, reporting F1 on 424 graphics.
sd4b7ed38e3.why: Pairing deterministic tools with LLM judgment offers a pattern for building verifiable structured data from unstructured documents.

sfccba1fce1.title: Humans and AI respond similarly to task difficulty when reasoning about content moderation dilemmas
sfccba1fce1.description: arXiv:2508.20262v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large reasoning models (LRMs) generate intermediate reasoning steps before producing answers, improving performance on challenging problems by iteratively developing solutions. There is evidence that LRMs expend more effort on the problems that take people longer to solve, but it is unclear whether these relationships hold on more subjective tasks without verifiable answers. This study addresses this issue through an experiment using a content moderation task, where task difficulty is manipulated by varying the relative offensiveness of two different options. Comparing six large reasoning models with 1,854 human subjects, we find that models expend more reasoning effort, measured using the length of the chain-of-thought (CoT), on the kind
sfccba1fce1.summary: A study finds large reasoning models vary their reasoning effort with task difficulty on content moderation dilemmas in a similar way to humans.

s87c752d4fa.title: AutoPBO: LLM-powered Optimization for Local Search PBO Solvers
s87c752d4fa.description: arXiv:2509.04007v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Pseudo-Boolean Optimization (PBO) provides a powerful framework for modeling combinatorial problems through pseudo-Boolean (PB) constraints. Local search solvers have shown excellent performance in PBO solving, and their efficiency is highly dependent on their internal heuristics to guide the search. Still, their design often requires significant expert effort and manual tuning in practice. While Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated potential in automating algorithm design, their application to optimizing PBO solvers remains unexplored. In this work, we introduce AutoPBO, a novel LLM-powered framework to automatically enhance PBO local search solvers. We conduct experiments on a broad range of four public benchmarks, including o
s87c752d4fa.summary: AutoPBO uses LLMs to automate the design and tuning of heuristics in local search pseudo-Boolean optimization solvers, reducing manual expert effort.
s87c752d4fa.why: LLM-driven algorithm tuning could cut manual effort in optimization solver engineering, though the text gives limited detail on results.

s0729daceec.title: Toward AI epidemiology: a measurement standardization framework for prospective risk detection
s0729daceec.description: arXiv:2512.15783v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper proposes a measurement standardization framework that compresses expert-AI interactions into structured, comparable fields for prospective risk detection in deployed AI systems, without access to model internals. This concept paper defines the framework's scope, semantically and statistically, and specifies a protocol for its empirical testing. The population-level claims it is designed to support therefore belong to a staged research program rather than to results claimed here. Measurement standardization underpins three claims. The first is a reliability claim: under bounded conditions, large language models can produce reliable, standardized assessments of the evidential and policy alignment of expert-AI interactions. The se
s0729daceec.summary: A concept paper proposes a measurement standardization framework that turns expert-AI interactions into structured fields for prospective risk detection in deployed AI systems, without model internals.
s0729daceec.why: Standardized incident-style data could help organizations detect risks in deployed AI, though the paper is a proposal without empirical results.

s4240183896.title: CORE: Concept-Oriented Reinforcement for Bridging the Definition-Application Gap in Mathematical Reasoning
s4240183896.description: arXiv:2512.18857v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often solve challenging math exercises yet fail to apply the concept right when the problem requires genuine understanding. Popular Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) pipelines reinforce final answers but provide little fine-grained conceptual signal, so models improve at pattern reuse rather than conceptual applications. We introduce CORE (Concept-Oriented REinforcement), an RL training framework that turns explicit concepts into a controllable supervision signal. Starting from a high-quality, low-contamination textbook resource that links verifiable exercises to concise concept descriptions, we run a sanity probe showing LLMs can restate definitions but fail concept-linked quizzes, quantif
s4240183896.summary: Researchers introduced CORE, an RL training framework that uses explicit mathematical concepts as a supervision signal to improve conceptual application in LLMs.
s4240183896.why: It targets a gap where RLVR rewards final answers but not conceptual understanding, which matters for building reliable reasoning models.

sb217f619bd.title: GCD: GCM-consistent Diffusion for Zero-shot Downscaling across Heterogeneous GCMs
sb217f619bd.description: arXiv:2601.21760v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Climate downscaling of General Circulation Models (GCMs) is an ill-posed inverse problem, as GCM outputs and reanalysis fields arise from different dynamical systems and lack fine-scale temporal pairing. Supervised methods thus rely on synthetic degradations or model-specific adaptation, limiting generalization across heterogeneous GCMs. Zero-shot diffusion posterior sampling (DPS) avoids paired supervision by combining a high-resolution climate prior with inference-time constraints from coarse GCM inputs, but faces consistency and efficiency challenges. We propose GCM-consistent Diffusion for Zero-shot Downscaling (GCD), which addresses these challenges with geographic conditioning, spectrally filtered measurement guidance, and distillat
sb217f619bd.summary: Researchers propose GCD, a zero-shot diffusion method for downscaling climate model outputs across heterogeneous GCMs without paired training data.

s44704ffa19.title: Do Multi-Agents Dream of Electric Screens? Achieving 100% on AndroidWorld Through Task Decomposition
s44704ffa19.description: arXiv:2602.07787v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present Minitap's mobile-use, a multi-agent system for Android UI control, and evaluate it on the 116 tasks of AndroidWorld, on Android emulators in Minitap's cloud device infrastructure, real Pixel 7 phones from our device farm and the stock emulator. On fresh, held-out task instances (three pre-registered seeds never used during development), the final system reaches a pass@3 of 100.0% (95% CI 96.8-100.0); pass^3 is 94.0% (95% CI 89.7-97.4) and the mean success rate 98.0% (95% CI 96.0-99.7). Minitap decomposes each task across five LLM agents (planning, subgoal tracking, state capture, decision, execution) and deterministic nodes, with mechanisms that read typed text back from the device, verify the goal on device evidence and detect
s44704ffa19.summary: Minitap's mobile-use multi-agent system reports 100% pass@3 on the 116-task AndroidWorld benchmark, using task decomposition across five LLM agents.
s44704ffa19.why: It shows multi-agent task decomposition can reach near-perfect results on a mobile UI control benchmark, a useful reference for agent design.

s93dedfe475.title: EmbeWebAgent: Embedding Web Agents into Custom Enterprise UIs
s93dedfe475.description: arXiv:2602.14865v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Most web agents operate at the human interface level, observing screenshots or raw DOM trees without application-level access, which limits robustness and action expressiveness. In enterprise settings, however, explicit control of both the frontend and backend is available. We present EmbeWebAgent, a framework for embedding agents directly into existing UIs using lightweight frontend hooks (curated ARIA and URL-based observations, and a per-page function registry exposed via a WebSocket) and a reusable backend workflow that performs reasoning and takes actions. EmbeWebAgent is stack-agnostic (e.g., React or Angular), supports mixed-granularity actions ranging from GUI primitives to higher-level composites, and orchestrates navigation, man
s93dedfe475.summary: EmbeWebAgent is a framework for embedding web agents directly into custom enterprise UIs using frontend hooks and backend workflows rather than screen observation.
s93dedfe475.why: Enterprises with access to frontend and backend can integrate agents with explicit application control, which may improve robustness over screenshot-based agents.

s02e361a45e.title: Evaluating and Understanding Scheming Propensity in LLM Agents
s02e361a45e.description: arXiv:2603.01608v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: As frontier language models are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents pursuing complex, long-term objectives, there is increased risk of scheming: agents covertly pursuing misaligned goals. Prior work has focused on showing agents are capable of scheming, but their propensity to scheme in realistic scenarios remains underexplored. To understand when agents scheme, we decompose scheming incentives into agent factors and environmental factors. We develop realistic settings allowing us to systematically vary these factors, each with scheming opportunities for agents that pursue instrumentally convergent goals such as self-preservation, resource acquisition, and goal-guarding. Across 11 frontier models and four scenarios, we find almost
s02e361a45e.summary: Researchers study how often LLM agents covertly pursue misaligned goals, varying agent and environmental factors across realistic scenarios.
s02e361a45e.why: Understanding when agents scheme in realistic settings informs risk assessment for deploying autonomous agents with long-term objectives.

s1eb13b7245.title: Seeing with You: Perception-Reasoning Coevolution for Multimodal Reasoning
s1eb13b7245.description: arXiv:2603.28618v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has substantially enhanced the reasoning capabilities of multimodal large language models (MLLMs). However, existing RLVR approaches typically rely on outcome-driven optimization that updates both perception and reasoning using a shared reward based solely on the final answer. This shared reward blurs credit assignment, frequently improving reasoning patterns while failing to reliably enhance the accuracy of upstream visual evidence extraction. To address this perception bottleneck, we introduce PRCO (Perception-Reasoning Coevolution), a dual-role RLVR framework with a shared policy. PRCO consists of two cooperative roles: an Observer that generates an evidence caption tailored to the
s1eb13b7245.summary: Researchers propose a multimodal RLVR approach that separates perception and reasoning rewards to improve visual evidence extraction in MLLMs.
s1eb13b7245.why: A shared final-answer reward can blur credit assignment, so separating perception rewards may improve reliability of multimodal reasoning.

s21c647cc3b.title: Scaling Causal Reasoning with Increasingly Complex Causal Simulators
s21c647cc3b.description: arXiv:2605.09079v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Despite surpassing human performance across mathematics, coding, and other knowledge-intensive tasks, large language models (LLMs) continue to struggle with causal reasoning. A core obstacle is the target data itself: causal systems are complex and often expressed in non-executable forms, while ground-truth answers to causal queries are inherently scarce. We introduce CauSim, a framework that turns causal reasoning from a scarce-label problem into a scalable supervised one. CauSim constructs increasingly complex causal simulators: executable structural causal models (SCMs), incrementally built by LLMs, that scale to globally complex systems while maintaining verifiable answers to causal queries. CauSim operates across representations by f
s21c647cc3b.summary: Researchers introduce CauSim, a framework that builds increasingly complex executable causal simulators to generate scalable supervision for LLM causal reasoning.
s21c647cc3b.why: Scalable executable simulators could address scarce labeled data for causal reasoning, a known weakness of current LLMs.

s5c0e032693.title: CardioLoom: A Report-Guided Electrocardiogram Foundation Model for Cross-Domain Cardiovascular Phenotyping
s5c0e032693.description: arXiv:2605.25446v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Routine electrocardiogram (ECG) reports offer scalable supervision for cardiovascular representation learning. In this retrospective study, we pretrained CardioLoom, a report-guided ECG foundation model, on 2,781,289 ECG-report pairs from 1,298,359 patients. Downstream development used a separate cohort of 721,317 ECGs from 233,798 patients. Evaluation covered 89 targets, with external testing in nine cohorts. Across 45 internal ECG diagnoses, macro area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) was 0.624 versus 0.615 for DeepECG-SSL. Across 203 external ECG evaluations, corresponding means were 0.425 and 0.424. Using labels from 10% of training patients, CardioLoom achieved macro-AUPRC 0.559, exceeding supervised training with all labels
s5c0e032693.summary: CardioLoom is a report-guided ECG foundation model pretrained on millions of ECG-report pairs, evaluated across 89 cardiovascular targets and external cohorts.

sdaf544e82c.title: Optimization-like Reasoning in LLMs over Expanding Search Spaces
sdaf544e82c.description: arXiv:2606.05464v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Verifiable reward training has improved mathematical and coding reasoning, but these domains capture only part of step-by-step decision making. Many real-world tasks require finding a high-value feasible plan among many valid alternatives. We introduce OPT*, a scalable family of optimization-style tasks for training and evaluating LLM step-by-step optimization-like reasoning along a complexity axis: each task provides a feasibility checker and evaluator, while a complexity parameter expands the search space without requiring new human labels. This motivates studying these tasks in two regimes: (i) solver-guided online policy optimization, which uses a solver as a value oracle for partial states and applies rank-based reward shaping to rei
sdaf544e82c.summary: Researchers introduce OPT*, a scalable family of optimization-style tasks with feasibility checkers and evaluators to train LLMs on step-by-step optimization reasoning.
sdaf544e82c.why: Verifiable optimization tasks with adjustable complexity offer a way to train planning beyond math and coding domains.

sf6f61838db.title: Rhythm of the Deep: Two-tier acoustic organization of sperm-whale codas from click waveforms to coda sequences
sf6f61838db.description: arXiv:2606.16084v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Sperm-whale codas are usually described by the number and timing of their clicks. These measures reveal patterns in whale communication, but do not describe how individual clicks sound. We ask what click waveforms add beyond timing and how acoustic information is organized within codas and across sequences of codas. We analyze 1,952 codas, using frozen audio encoders to identify recurring forms of clicks and whole codas independently. Direct spectral and envelope measurements then test whether the click forms differ in recorded sound. Within codas, click-form composition improves the measured prediction of whole-coda form beyond timing alone. Click spacing also remains related to whole-coda sound when the same click forms are present. Nei
sf6f61838db.summary: Researchers analyze 1,952 sperm-whale codas using frozen audio encoders to examine how click waveforms and coda sequences are acoustically organized.

s50d853646a.title: Latent Goal Prediction from Language for Model-Based Planning
s50d853646a.description: arXiv:2606.20627v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) enable agents to plan in latent space by imagining the outcomes of candidate actions, yet task specification remains a bottleneck. Visual targets provide precise local gradients but poor distant guidance, while language is flexible yet limited by noisy cross-modal alignment or dependence on distinct large generative models. We introduce LAGO (Latent Goal Prediction from Language), a hierarchical world model in which a single predictor both forecasts action-conditioned dynamics and grounds language instructions as sequences of intermediate latent subgoals, training both modes with a single regression objective over a shared latent space. At each planning step, LAGO predicts a sequence of lat
s50d853646a.summary: Researchers present LAGO, a hierarchical world model where one predictor forecasts action-conditioned latent dynamics and grounds language goals for model-based planning.
s50d853646a.why: Grounding language goals in a latent world model could simplify task specification for planning agents.

s39ece3f80b.title: Process Advantage Signal Shaping: Advantage Construction for Process-Supervised Reinforcement Learning in LLM Reasoners
s39ece3f80b.description: arXiv:2606.29296v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Dense process supervision provides local evaluations, but leaves open how these scores should become policy advantages. We introduce PASS (Process Advantage Signal Shaping), an advantage-construction method for group-relative policy optimization (GRPO). PASS separately normalizes and fuses reward channels, constructs batch-shared credit units from variation in the fused score trace, and normalizes return-to-go by the remaining unit count. These operations connect feedback scale, credit resolution, and accumulation horizon in a single computation. We evaluate learned process reward model (PRM) feedback for mathematical reasoning and teacher-derived token feedback for multi-hop question answering (QA). Across seven mathematics benchmarks, P
s39ece3f80b.summary: Researchers propose PASS, an advantage-construction method for process-supervised GRPO that normalizes and fuses reward channels to shape credit assignment in LLM reasoners.
s39ece3f80b.why: Better conversion of dense process scores into policy advantages could improve RL post-training efficiency for reasoning models.

s80d5cacbaa.title: RL Post-Training Builds Compositional Reasoning Strategies
s80d5cacbaa.description: arXiv:2607.07646v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Does RL post-training merely amplify primitive skills already latent in a base model, or can it compose primitive skills into new higher-level strategies? We study this question in a fully observable rewrite-grammar environment where the pretraining distribution is known and every generated rewrite can be audited. A Transformer is pretrained on primitive symbol-rewrite chains and post-trained on a Trace-based reasoning task with only a binary final-answer reward. RL solves held-out problems that remain rarely solved by the pretrained model even under much larger sampling budgets, while rejection fine-tuning improves early but plateaus. Trace analysis shows that RL reorganizes primitive competence through a phased compositional mechanism:
s80d5cacbaa.summary: A study using a rewrite-grammar environment finds RL post-training can compose primitive skills into new higher-level reasoning strategies rather than only amplifying latent ones.
s80d5cacbaa.why: It offers evidence on whether RL post-training creates new capabilities, relevant to how teams should expect RL to change model behavior.

seb78fe1318.title: Test-Time Coverage: Test-Conditioned Data Curation for Deployment-Aware Learning
seb78fe1318.description: arXiv:2607.22697v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Deployed AI systems are often trained from broad candidate data pools, necessitating data curation towards the deployment test distribution. However, standard data curation methods score training-side criteria rather than directly optimizing deployment match. We introduce TTCov (Test-Time Coverage), a data-level test-conditioned curation method that uses test-side information before training instead of updating model weights at inference. TTCov decomposes deployment-conditioned curation into coverage and distribution. To represent coverage, it builds a task Atlas, a collection of LLM-based atomic propositions (APs) describing deployment-relevant concepts, seeded from open task knowledge and expanded with unmatched APs extracted from unlab
seb78fe1318.summary: Researchers introduce TTCov, a test-conditioned data curation method that selects training data to match deployment test distributions before training.
seb78fe1318.why: Curating training data toward the deployment distribution, rather than generic criteria, can improve match between training and production.

s2d223d77da.title: Alternating Abduction and Planning over Temporal Dynamic Knowledge Graphs
s2d223d77da.description: arXiv:2607.27287v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Knowledge graphs change over time, but the effects of actions on them are only partly stated: the ontology entails further consequences, facts that an action needs are often unknown, and an action may make the graph inconsistent. We study these problems for Temporal Dynamic Knowledge Graphs (TDKGs), that is, SROIQ knowledge bases whose actions are rules with delete/insert templates and whose events lie on an intrinsic timeline. We present three tools: temporal projection, the exact test of plans; DDA (Direct-Derivation Abduction), which explains an observation by assuming its negation and negating what the reasoner newly derives; and APT (Abduction and Planning over TDKGs), which plans backwards from a goal, assumes the facts that the pla
s2d223d77da.summary: Researchers present tools for alternating abduction and planning over temporal dynamic knowledge graphs, handling action effects, missing preconditions, and inconsistency.

s13e0408d52.title: Explore, Map, Remember, Decide: A Benchmark for VLM Readiness in Safety-Critical Scenarios
s13e0408d52.description: arXiv:2608.08077v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are often deployed as embodied controllers for robotics, yet it remains unclear how well they can explore an environment, maintain an internal map, and ground safety-critical decisions in long-horizon sequential trajectories. In this work, we introduce EMRD, an evaluation framework that decouples spatial reasoning into four stages: Explore (what the agent observes), Map (what it records and where), Remember (what it retains), and Decide (whether its final choice is justified), scored across 18 stage-specific metrics. We use EMRD to evaluate eleven open- and closed-weight VLMs across 16 buildings under nominal conditions and three environmental stresses (darkness, smoke, and motion noise), where an embodied VL
s13e0408d52.summary: Researchers introduced EMRD, a benchmark that splits VLM spatial reasoning into Explore, Map, Remember, and Decide stages for safety-critical robotics tasks.
s13e0408d52.why: It shows where vision-language models may fail as embodied controllers, which matters before deploying them in safety-critical robotics.

see1f264494.title: Multi-Granularity Context-Enhanced RAG over Multimodal Knowledge Graphs
see1f264494.description: arXiv:2608.25986v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Knowledge graph (KG)-based retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) leverages structured knowledge to provide large language models (LLMs) with high-quality external information. Building on these works, recent studies have explored multimodal knowledge graphs (MMKGs) as knowledge bases for GraphRAG. This enables GraphRAG to integrate knowledge across multiple modalities, thereby further enhancing its performance. However, existing MMKG-based RAG methods generally follow a common pipeline in which different modalities are largely processed independently before being fused. As a result, textual context is only used to a limited extent during visual information extraction and subsequent multimodal knowledge fusion. This brings a semantic gap be
see1f264494.summary: Researchers propose a multi-granularity context-enhanced RAG method over multimodal knowledge graphs, arguing existing approaches process modalities largely independently.

sebbf32604e.title: The Memory Trust Gap: Reliance on Stale Evidence Across Model Scales in LLM Agents
sebbf32604e.description: arXiv:2609.01852v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Persistent-memory agents can follow stale information despite current authoritative evidence. We study stale-evidence reliance across Qwen3 0.6/1.7/4/8B checkpoints using two controlled, action-scored suites: a Benefit suite requiring stored information and a Safety suite providing current evidence as static prompt text. We distinguish stale-value reliance from net accuracy loss relative to no memory. Benefit-suite reliance is 0.92-1.00 across checkpoints. In the Safety suite, larger checkpoints resist a plain stale note but incur substantial harm when it appears newer. A full $2\times2\times2\times2$ factorial manipulates label, recency, source authority, and position. Direct cross-size contrasts identify stronger recency effects in the
sebbf32604e.summary: A study of Qwen3 checkpoints from 0.6B to 8B finds LLM agents often rely on stale stored information, with larger models resisting a plain stale note but still incurring losses.
sebbf32604e.why: Persistent-memory agents can act on outdated information even when current evidence is available, a reliability risk for production agent design.

sa0bbad81ae.title: PhysAlign: A Benchmark for Evidence-Grounded Role Alignment in Multimodal Physics Reasoning
sa0bbad81ae.description: arXiv:2609.33319v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A key challenge in physics diagram understanding is correctly associating visual information with the physical entities, relations, and conditions it describes. Even when a value, symbol, or other local element is accurately recognized, assigning it to the wrong entity or scope can distort the underlying physical premise and lead to incorrect reasoning. To systematically study this challenge, we introduce \textbf{PhysAlign}, a benchmark designed to assess whether multimodal models correctly associate information recognized from physics diagrams with its intended physical role. By disentangling visual recognition from physical-role assignment through localized probes and controlled variants, PhysAlign isolates correspondence errors from re
sa0bbad81ae.summary: Researchers introduce PhysAlign, a benchmark testing whether multimodal models correctly associate recognized values and symbols in physics diagrams with the right entities.

s58b3130961.title: Code4Scene: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Constructing and Editing 3D Scenes
s58b3130961.description: arXiv:2609.36777v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Frontier coding agents can now write and execute code that authors 3D environments, but whether they reliably understand 3D structure and precisely control scene state remains unclear. The generated 3D scene is a persistent, executable artifact: a convincing render can hide incorrect spatial relations, intersecting objects, or unintended modifications. We introduce Code4Scene, a benchmark of 170 Unreal Engine cases built from human-assembled scenes that evaluates coding agents on two complementary settings under a shared execution interface. Construction tests scene-level spatial reasoning from open-ended language specifications, where many realizations are valid; editing tests precise control of scene state, where the agent must recover
s58b3130961.summary: Researchers introduce Code4Scene, a benchmark of 170 Unreal Engine cases evaluating whether coding agents reliably build and edit 3D scenes.
s58b3130961.why: Rendered outputs can hide spatial errors, so engineers relying on coding agents for 3D content need execution-based checks.

s486f1cc694.title: Mingbird: A Local-First Agent Harness Enabling Small Open Models to Complete Real Tasks
s486f1cc694.description: arXiv:2610.02001v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Small open-weight language models now run on a laptop, but they fail at multi-step work in ways a large model does not: they stop with the files missing, repeat one action until the budget ends, and report success without checking. At the one-to-nine-billion-parameter tier the harness supplies almost all of the procedural control that a large model supplies for itself.We present Mingbird, an open-source harness for that tier on a consumer graphics card: 12k lines of Python, a 628-test suite, and eighteen mechanisms for context economy, completion, time budget and the host boundary, plus a crawl guard outside those four groups. Its design point is completion control: the harness runs executable checks on the working directory and refuses a
s486f1cc694.summary: Mingbird, an open-source agent harness, is presented to help small open-weight models of one to nine billion parameters complete multi-step tasks on a consumer GPU.
s486f1cc694.why: It suggests that orchestration harnesses can supply procedural control that small local models lack, enabling local-first agent workflows.

sdeb9f68b9f.title: When Terminal-Agent Training Stalls: Demystifying Data Generation and Verification Challenge
sdeb9f68b9f.description: arXiv:2610.02405v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Automated terminal-agent training relies on generated environments and verifiers to turn open-ended interaction into reward. Yet a runnable Docker image and executable test suite do not guarantee that the resulting reward is faithful, informative, or even attributable to agent behavior. We present a pipeline that generates containerized terminal tasks and their executable verifiers, and use it to demystify failure modes in task generation and live-environment evaluation. Our analysis separates four requirements that are often conflated: structural validity, verifier faithfulness, policy solvability, and infrastructure reliability. In a GRPO training of Qwen3.5-9B, it overfits on a relatively easy dataset within 20 steps. Conversely, in a
sdeb9f68b9f.summary: Researchers present a pipeline generating containerized terminal tasks and verifiers, and analyze failure modes where runnable Docker images and test suites fail to yield faithful rewards.
sdeb9f68b9f.why: Training terminal agents depends on reward quality, so unverified environments and tests can silently stall learning.

s0abc112f40.title: Reliable Self-Evolution with Imperfect Proxy Rewards
s0abc112f40.description: arXiv:2610.02975v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based self-evolving search is a promising approach to scientific discovery. However, high-fidelity evaluation of every candidate is prohibitively expensive in some domains. Self-evolving systems in such settings therefore rely on low-cost but imperfect proxy rewards, which may assign high scores to infeasible candidates. These false positives may contaminate both the final output and the feedback used to guide subsequent generations. This motivates statistically calibrated reward intervals for more reliable self-evolving search. We propose Conformal Interval-Driven Self-Evolution (CISE), which constructs candidate-specific reward intervals using conditional conformal inference and iteration-wise online density-r
s0abc112f40.summary: Researchers propose statistically calibrated reward intervals so LLM-based self-evolving search can rely on imperfect, low-cost proxy rewards for scientific discovery.
s0abc112f40.why: Cheap proxy evaluators can score infeasible candidates highly, contaminating outputs; calibrated intervals aim to make automated search more reliable.

s5a38ebac45.title: Realtime-Bench: Can Frontier Models Solve Real-time Interactive Problems?
s5a38ebac45.description: arXiv:2610.22155v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Real-time interaction requires agents to perceive evolving environments and act under temporal constraints, yet existing evaluations of real-time streaming models focus on conversational quality and streaming perception, leaving effective action under strict temporal constraints untested. We introduce Realtime-Bench, a suite of carefully curated dynamic tasks where delayed actions directly affect success. Under Wall Clock, where environments advance according to actual inference latency, the best success rate reaches only 44% and the best Pass^3 is only 36%, demonstrating that real-time interaction remains challenging. To separate serving latency from models' real-time streaming capability, we compare Wall Clock with Paused Clock, which r
s5a38ebac45.summary: Realtime-Bench, a suite of time-sensitive interactive tasks, finds frontier models reach only 44% success under wall-clock conditions where latency matters.
s5a38ebac45.why: Real-time agent deployments must account for inference latency, since frontier models perform poorly when delayed actions cost success.

sadc455a09b.title: Agentic In-Context Learning: What Algorithms Can Transformers Learn in Closed-Loop Interaction?
sadc455a09b.description: arXiv:2610.23051v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The learning algorithm view of in-context learning (ICL) studies how fixed-parameter Transformers learn from supplied examples. Language model agents extend this setting through interaction: their actions determine what evidence enters context next. We call this regime Agentic In-Context Learning (Agentic ICL). Existing studies largely depend on externally supplied contexts or reward-bearing interaction histories, while work on general tool-using agents lacks a learning algorithm view. We represent an interactive learner by its state, update, and decision rule, covering active learning, bandits, and online reinforcement learning (RL). For expressivity, we construct causal Transformers that approximate these algorithms over a finite horizo
sadc455a09b.summary: Researchers define Agentic In-Context Learning, studying what learning algorithms transformers can acquire when their actions shape the evidence they receive in closed-loop interaction.

s06eb403e9a.title: A Conditional No-Hair Theorem for Transformers: How Language Models Forget Their Prompt
s06eb403e9a.description: arXiv:2610.24133v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A black hole retains only a few conserved charges of the matter it formed from. We are inspired to make the analogy and we ask how much an autoregressive transformer retains of its prompt after generating $t$ tokens. For two prompts followed by the same continuation, the difference of their hidden states decays approximately as a power law $t^{-\alpha}$, where $\alpha=1$ is the rate at which a fixed prompt's share of uniform attention shrinks. Beyond the first layers, trained models forget faster ($\alpha\approx0.55$--$0.7$) than untrained ones of the same architecture ($\alpha\approx0.2$--$0.5$). For finite-depth pre-LN softmax transformers with bounded attention logits and non-degenerate pre-norm activations, we prove that this offset i
s06eb403e9a.summary: A paper proposes a conditional no-hair analogy for transformers, showing hidden-state differences from prompts decay as a power law, with trained models forgetting faster than untrained ones.

sf1feb2e4bb.title: AI is killing All About Berlin
sf1feb2e4bb.description: Article URL: https://nicolasbouliane.com/blog/death-by-ai Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50542705 Points: 550 # Comments: 518
sf1feb2e4bb.summary: A blog post argues that AI is killing the All About Berlin website, shared on Hacker News with 550 points and 518 comments.

sc38beb9bd9.title: This smell startup says its AI nose is as good as a human’s
sc38beb9bd9.description: In a lab near Newark Airport in New Jersey, a team of around 30 experienced human sniffers are slowly working their way through every odor on Earth. Their careful notes—“nutty,” “peachy,” “marine”—are cross-referenced with a chemical analysis to create a rich set of training data for what AI startup Osmo calls the world’s first foundation…
sc38beb9bd9.summary: AI startup Osmo is building a smell foundation model trained on notes from about 30 human sniffers cross-referenced with chemical analysis.

This post explores when FFT outperforms LoRA across key benchmarks, examines the spectral properties of model weight matrices behind the quality gap, shares practical hyperparameter tuning guidelines, and shows how to get started.
s1980ba7046.summary: Amazon SageMaker AI Serverless Model Customization now supports Full Fine-Tuning, with analysis of when it outperforms LoRA on benchmarks.
s1980ba7046.why: Gives engineers benchmark-based guidance on choosing full fine-tuning versus LoRA, plus hyperparameter tuning practices for serverless customization.

sc8a4b2ac13.title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explains why he asked 60K employees to quit
sc8a4b2ac13.description: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explained why he offered buyouts to 60,000 of his employees in October, essentially urging them to voluntarily quit, rather than reducing the workforce via another massive layoff. The short answer is AI, but not in the way you might expect.
sc8a4b2ac13.summary: Satya Nadella explained that Microsoft offered buyouts to 60,000 employees in October, urging voluntary departures instead of another large layoff.
sc8a4b2ac13.why: Signals how a major tech employer is using AI-era workforce restructuring instead of mass layoffs, which matters to tech leaders planning headcount.

s07bd5650af.title: AI will not make you rich (2025)
s07bd5650af.description: Article URL: https://colossus.com/article/ai-will-not-make-you-rich/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50555093 Points: 63 # Comments: 38
s07bd5650af.summary: A Colossus article argues that AI will not make people rich, shared on Hacker News with 63 points and 38 comments.
s07bd5650af.why: The text gives only a title and link metadata, so the article's actual argument is unclear.

sf1ae0f2c9d.title: Human-AI Mutualism Is Unstable under Capability Asymmetry
sf1ae0f2c9d.description: arXiv:2611.23322v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: One hope for a good human future alongside advanced AI rests on enduring mutualism: humans and AI will need each other, so the relationship will stay good for both. We argue that this hope fails as AI capability grows. Bargaining guarantees each side only what it would get if bargaining failed. For humans, this can be less than they had before AI. In a simple game-theoretic model, humans stay as well off as before AI without alignment only while they have leverage over the AI: either the AI depends on what they supply, or they can impose costs on the AI that are large relative to what the AI can produce. Once humans have neither kind of leverage, they stay as well off as before AI only if the AI is aligned with them. If the AI's goals are ins
sf1ae0f2c9d.summary: An arXiv paper argues that human-AI mutualism is unstable as AI capability grows, since bargaining may leave humans worse off than before AI without alignment.
sf1ae0f2c9d.why: Offers a theoretical argument that cooperative human-AI relationships may not hold as capabilities diverge, relevant to long-term alignment planning.

sb37da287b0.title: Training Language Models for Introspective Oversight
sb37da287b0.description: arXiv:2611.23365v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language models increasingly exhibit behaviors that are difficult to detect in transcripts, such as reward hacking, deception, and sycophancy. Asking the assistant follow-up questions about its actions is unreliable, since models are generally not trained to report their own misbehavior. As a result, approaches to oversight typically involve querying external models.
