These face limitations: external transcript monitoring operates only on visible model outputs, and activation decoders lack full context and are prone to confabulation. We introduce introspective oversight, which trains a new role in the model to answer arbitrary questions about the assistant, rewarding answers that are verified against the assistant's actual behavior. We impleme
sb37da287b0.summary: An arXiv paper introduces a method for training language models to introspectively report on their own misbehavior, such as reward hacking or deception.
sb37da287b0.why: Explores whether models can be trained to self-report misbehavior, a potential complement to external monitoring, though the description is abstract.

s571da62993.title: Where the Tokens Go: Heat, Entropy and Error in Agentic Coding
s571da62993.description: arXiv:2611.23375v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coding agents are billed by the token, yet software engineering says nothing about what a token actually buys. Here we introduce a theory of software thermodynamics. The theory draws analogues from classical and stochastic thermodynamics, extends them, and applies them to modern agentic coding. We count the tokens an agent generates as its cost and divide that cost into work and heat. The test suite acts as a software Maxwell's daemon that judges every coding change. We test the theory with an analogue of the experiments in which a single molecule is pulled open and let fold again: an agent makes a change to a repository (coding) and then undoes it (uncoding), many times over, and we count the tokens of every model call. The cycle returns the
s571da62993.summary: An arXiv paper proposes a 'software thermodynamics' theory that splits the tokens a coding agent generates into work and heat, judged by the test suite.
s571da62993.why: Offers a framework for thinking about what coding agent token spend actually produces, which may inform cost measurement for agentic development.

s7b8d691960.title: HardwareDx: A Foundational Graph Model System for Datacenter Machine Repairs
s7b8d691960.description: arXiv:2611.23398v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid scale-up of AI infrastructure has made datacenter reliability a cornerstone of the cloud business economy. Since hardware failures in hyper-scale AI clusters can stall multi-million dollar training workloads, the downtime of individual machines can cause outsized economic losses. Minimizing machine downtime, therefore, is more important than ever. To address this, we present Hardware Diagnoser (HardwareDx), an AI-driven hardware diagnosis system that applies a graph foundation model approach to automated datacenter maintenance. It allows a single model to diagnose many platforms and accelerate onboarding of new hardware products. Deployed at production scale at Google, HardwareDx yields substantial efficiency gains across diverse co
s7b8d691960.summary: An arXiv paper presents HardwareDx, an AI system using a graph foundation model to diagnose datacenter hardware failures and reduce machine downtime.
s7b8d691960.why: Targets costly downtime in AI clusters, relevant to infrastructure teams running large training workloads.

sd849ebb68b.title: RFBench: A Simulator-Grounded Multimodal Benchmark for Passive RF Layout Design and Understanding
sd849ebb68b.description: arXiv:2611.23410v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While multimodal language models can interpret diagrams and generate structured outputs, their capacity to connect passive radio-frequency (RF) design intent, layout geometry, and electromagnetic behavior remains largely untested. To address this gap, we introduce RFBench, a simulator-grounded dataset and benchmark for passive RF layout design and understanding. The dataset contains 10,000 two-port planar layouts simulated using ADS Momentum, with each layout represented by editable geometric primitives, a raster image, a 16x16 occupancy grid, complex S-parameters at 201 frequency points, a structural category, and an RF response label. Building on these aligned representations, we define seven tasks spanning specification-conditioned layout
sd849ebb68b.summary: An arXiv paper introduces RFBench, a simulator-grounded dataset and benchmark of 10,000 passive RF layouts for testing multimodal models on RF design.
sd849ebb68b.why: Provides a domain benchmark for testing whether multimodal models understand RF layout and electromagnetic behavior.

s84e21402df.title: Why Sub-4-Bit Vision CNNs Collapse and Where Mixed-Precision Recovery Stops
s84e21402df.description: arXiv:2611.23445v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep vision models operating in resource-constrained environments depend heavily on low-bit quantization, yet compressing weights below 4 bits frequently induces catastrophic accuracy collapse. While mixed-precision recovery strategies aim to rescue accuracy by selectively retaining high-precision parameters, the fundamental mechanics of where and why these models collapse remain poorly understood. In this study, we systematically analyze the anatomy of quantization collapse across standard Vision CNNs (including ResNet and EfficientNet backbones) evaluated on the full 50,000-image ImageNet-1k validation set. First, we map the exact progression of degradation, demonstrating that collapse is highly non-linear and concentrated in late-stage poi
s84e21402df.summary: An arXiv paper analyzes why vision CNNs collapse under sub-4-bit weight quantization and where mixed-precision recovery stops working.
s84e21402df.why: Clarifies limits of aggressive quantization for resource-constrained vision deployments, informing compression decisions.

sbccfb76873.title: LusoClin: A Synthetic Clinical Note Dataset for Medical Information Retrieval in European Portuguese
sbccfb76873.description: arXiv:2611.23454v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Access to large-scale clinical text collections is crucial for advancing medical information retrieval research, including clinical note search, patient cohort identification, and domain-adapted retrieval models. However, real clinical notes are rarely available due to privacy regulations, which particularly limits progress for low-resource languages such as European Portuguese. We present LusoClin, a publicly released dataset of synthetic clinical notes in European Portuguese, created to support privacy-preserving research on clinical text retrieval. LusoClin was generated by pre-processing real clinical data, fine-tuning the open-source Llama 3.2 (3B) instruction-tuned model using Quantized Low-Rank Adaptation, and applying prompt-based cli
sbccfb76873.summary: Researchers released LusoClin, a publicly available synthetic clinical note dataset in European Portuguese for medical information retrieval research.
sbccfb76873.why: Offers a privacy-friendly dataset for building clinical retrieval systems in a low-resource language.

s5c8a08fdfd.title: VeriMath: Human-in-the-Loop Generation and Verification of Curriculum-Aligned Mathematics Assessment Items
s5c8a08fdfd.description: arXiv:2611.23456v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automatic generation of mathematics assessment items is a growing area in educational artificial intelligence, yet classroom deployment remains challenging. Generated questions must satisfy multiple constraints: mathematical correctness, curriculum alignment, appropriate cognitive difficulty, and educator reviewability. While prior work has advanced text generation, reliable assessment authoring requires granular control over localized examination formats and expert educational judgment. To address this challenge, we present VeriMath, a generalized, human-in-the-loop framework for generating rigorous, curriculum-constrained mathematics assessment drafts. Using annotated reference items, the framework anchors generation to the requested examin
s5c8a08fdfd.summary: An arXiv paper presents VeriMath, a human-in-the-loop system for generating and verifying curriculum-aligned mathematics assessment items.

s24648c435c.title: GUARD: Stabilizing Recursive Self-Improvement with Regret Guidance
s24648c435c.description: arXiv:2611.23476v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous AI agents pair a frozen base model with an editable harness of prompts, skills, tool rules, and memory. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) adapts this harness from experience without weight updates, yet self-editing without external graders often backfires: reflection and scalar scores conflate what an edit newly broke with what remains unsolved, causing local regressions, skill forgetting, and memory bloat. We introduce GUARD (Grader-free Unsupervised Environment Design [UED] with Adaptive Rule Distillation), a closed-loop framework for reference-free continual harness evolution. Our key insight is to decompose each task into pre-execution self-checks and guide harness updates via directional regret. Each round grades trajectories a
s24648c435c.summary: An arXiv paper introduces GUARD, a grader-free framework to stabilize recursive self-improvement of AI agent harnesses, reducing regressions and memory bloat.
s24648c435c.why: Addresses regressions and skill forgetting when agents self-edit prompts, tools, and memory without external graders.

s6dda97006b.title: Diagnostic Accuracy and Navigation Behavior of Vision-Language Model Agents Reading Emergency CT and MRI Examinations
s6dda97006b.description: arXiv:2611.23480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Purpose. To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy and image navigation behavior of vision-language model (VLM) agents under varying exploration strategies. Materials and Methods. In this retrospective study, six VLMs read 100 emergency CT and MRI examinations published in a public archive (March 2025-August 2026) under four conditions (free navigation, navigation from a key slice, and all slices or key slices in a single request), twice each (4800 runs). Nine radiologists read 30 of those cases. A large language model judge validated against two radiologists graded the answers. Conditions were compared with generalized estimating equations clustered by case. Results. Pooled accuracy was lowest under free navigation (32.6%; 391/1200), followed by n
s6dda97006b.summary: A retrospective arXiv study tested six vision-language model agents reading emergency CT and MRI exams under different navigation strategies, compared with nine radiologists.
s6dda97006b.why: Shows how exploration strategy affects VLM diagnostic accuracy in a high-stakes medical setting, a caution for deploying such agents.

s9dc2fbd8f9.title: SpecLook: Speculating Where to Look for Fast and Reliable Agentic MLLMs
s9dc2fbd8f9.description: arXiv:2611.23483v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic multimodal large language models (MLLMs) that think with images interleave reasoning with zoom-in tool calls. However, this sequential loop is slow, and its answers carry no reliability score. Prior speculation of tokens, reasoning steps, or answers keeps the loop, and answer speculation also accepts confident errors. We find that the loop mostly adds one zoom-in step, with which a small model is ahead of the agent on most splits. Our key insight is to speculate the agent's next observation, which, unlike a drafted answer, can be verified, corrected, and used to test the answer. We propose SpecLook, a training-free speculate-and-verify framework with three levels. A small model drafts a glimpse and re-answers from it, and the question
s9dc2fbd8f9.summary: An arXiv paper proposes SpecLook, which speculates an agentic multimodal model's next image observation to speed up zoom-in reasoning and add verifiability.
s9dc2fbd8f9.why: Targets latency and reliability problems in agentic image-reasoning loops, relevant to teams building multimodal agents.

sc0ed4e9a41.title: BOS Summary: The First Token Matters
sc0ed4e9a41.description: arXiv:2611.23508v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) and language models (LLMs) often exhibit attention sinks, whereby particular positions, such as the beginning-of-sequence (BOS) token, receive a disproportionate share of attention. Under standard causal masking, however, the BOS query attends only to itself, so the representation that later tokens repeatedly access carries no information about the input. We introduce BOS Summary, a training-free inference-time method that repurposes this persistent pathway to carry input context. At a single transformer layer during prefill, BOS Summary relaxes the causal constraint for the BOS query row alone, letting BOS aggregate all visual and textual input tokens into a self-derived context representation while every
sc0ed4e9a41.summary: An arXiv paper introduces BOS Summary, a training-free inference-time method that uses the beginning-of-sequence token to carry input context in LLMs and LVLMs.
sc0ed4e9a41.why: Offers a no-training technique to make attention-sink positions carry useful input information, potentially improving inference.

sa1312471f7.title: GRAFT: Execution-Guided Genetic Recombination for Agent Design
sa1312471f7.description: arXiv:2611.23509v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated agent design searches for executable architectures that improve LLM-based agent performance, with evolutionary methods using language-model crossover to recombine promising mechanisms for task decomposition, model coordination, and verification. This search, however, is typically guided by aggregate fitness alone, which hides the instance-level successes and failures behind each score. We introduce Execution Guided Genetic Recombination for Agent Design (GRAFT), which uses aggregate fitness for selection and survival and parent-specific execution evidence to guide semantic crossover with integrated mutation. Its feedback harness reuses bounded samples of successful and failed runs from fitness evaluation, withholding reference answe
sa1312471f7.summary: An arXiv paper presents GRAFT, an evolutionary method that uses per-instance execution results to guide recombination when automatically designing LLM agents.
sa1312471f7.why: Suggests using instance-level execution feedback rather than aggregate fitness alone when searching for better agent architectures.

s2cf26a3792.title: BeFit: Shifting Complexity from Weights to Bernstein Activations for Resource-Constrained Sensing
s2cf26a3792.description: arXiv:2611.23520v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time-series sensing increasingly relies on neural networks, yet deployment on resource-constrained microcontrollers remains challenging. Aggressive model compression can reduce accuracy, while restricting weights to multiplication-free representations introduces further losses. We present BeFit, an end-to-end framework that shifts model capacity from weights to learnable Bernstein polynomial activations. BeFit (i) finds compact Bernstein-activated convolutional neural networks (BeCNNs) through hardware-aware neural architecture search and trains them via knowledge distillation; (ii) projects their weights to multiplication-free codes, freezes the codes, and recovers the resulting accuracy loss through the learnable activations; and (iii) gene
s2cf26a3792.summary: BeFit proposes shifting neural network capacity from weights to learnable Bernstein polynomial activations for time-series sensing on resource-constrained microcontrollers.
s2cf26a3792.why: It offers a path to running accurate time-series models on microcontrollers without aggressive compression or multiplication-free weight restrictions.

scce97e4917.title: FACET - Facet Aware Contrastive Embeddings for Traits- Big Five Estimation from Life Narratives
scce97e4917.description: arXiv:2611.23560v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Personality is only weakly and inconsistently signaled by written language, and existing text-based methods typically combine language-model and psycholinguistic representations at the input or decision level. It remains open whether a more deliberate combination of the two views, and a decomposition of the prediction target, can recover more of the signal. We present a three-phase framework for estimating Big Five personality domain scores from life-narrative interview text. It encodes text and psycholinguistic features separately and combines them by concatenation or by a learned weighting, decomposes each domain into contrastively trained facet embeddings instead of predicting the domain directly, and pools the facet embeddings by attentio
scce97e4917.summary: FACET is a three-phase framework that combines language-model and psycholinguistic features to estimate Big Five personality scores from life-narrative interview text.

s04c157b96f.title: LProp: Propagating Latent Uncertainty through Evidence-Conditioned Belief Revision in LLM Agents
s04c157b96f.description: arXiv:2611.23564v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When LLM agents pass intermediate judgments downstream without uncertainty, later decisions may treat tentative assumptions as facts. Effective uncertainty propagation must preserve information for correction and update inherited beliefs as new evidence arrives. Yet scalar scores omit information needed for revision, while detailed descriptions and reflection incur additional costs. We introduce Latent Uncertainty, a latent-space estimator that preserves uncertainty-relevant information without lengthy descriptions. Building on this, we propose LProp (Latent Uncertainty Propagation), which revises inherited answer distributions using latent representations and new evidence without additional trajectory sampling. We evaluate both methods acros
s04c157b96f.summary: LProp introduces Latent Uncertainty, a latent-space estimator meant to propagate uncertainty between LLM agents so tentative judgments are not treated as facts downstream.
s04c157b96f.why: Multi-agent pipelines can carry unverified assumptions forward as facts, so preserving uncertainty across handoffs targets a real reliability problem.

scb7adb9abc.title: Receiver-Conditioned Clarification for Multi-Agent Food Assistance
scb7adb9abc.description: arXiv:2611.23572v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Food insecurity creates a pressing need for guidance that helps households find usable food resources and assess food choices in light of their circumstances. Such guidance must connect eligibility requirements, practical access constraints, and dietary needs rather than return isolated listings or generic nutritional advice. Multi-agent food assistants can coordinate these tasks, with uncertainty indicating when clarification or verification is needed before a recommendation. However, uncertainty can be lost across agent handoffs, allowing tentative interpretations to propagate as facts and obscuring opportunities for correction. Moreover, confidence that a service requirement has been interpreted correctly is not confidence that a recommend
scb7adb9abc.summary: The paper presents a receiver-conditioned clarification approach for multi-agent food assistants, aiming to keep uncertainty from being lost across agent handoffs.
scb7adb9abc.why: Uncertainty lost across agent handoffs can lead to tentative assumptions becoming recommendations, a general multi-agent design concern.

s4982f2beba.title: ARISE: Practical Self-Evolving Memory for Accurate and Cost-Efficient Enterprise Agents
s4982f2beba.description: arXiv:2611.23588v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Enterprise LLM agents operate in dynamic environments where foundation models evolve rapidly, workflows update frequently, and deployments need to satisfy accuracy and cost requirements. We propose ARISE (Agent Refinement through Iterative Self-Evaluation), a practical memory architecture in which the agent's memory evolves from its own failures without updating model weights, tools, or workflow logic. ARISE uses the model itself or a teacher model to attribute the failures and propose corrections. Then, ARISE keeps the corrections as retrievable micro memory, consolidates them into macro rules, and accepts a rule update only if held-out accuracy rises. Across 14 enterprise-workflow domains from SOP-Bench and $\tau^2$-bench using 5 models, AR
s4982f2beba.summary: ARISE is a memory architecture where enterprise LLM agents learn corrections from their own failures, stored as retrievable memory, without updating model weights, tools, or workflows.
s4982f2beba.why: It suggests improving enterprise agent accuracy and cost without retraining models or changing workflow logic, which matters for teams with frequent model and workflow changes.

s0d6d6ad6fc.title: RefinementGuard: Counterexample-Directed Semantic Qualification for Hidden Agent-Tool Execution
s0d6d6ad6fc.description: arXiv:2611.23611v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool runtimes can lower an agent-selected operation into a hidden parallel graph, reducing latency and context while risking semantic mistranslation. We introduce RefinementGuard: translation validation for hidden, effectful agent-tool lowerings, coupled to artifact-bound, fail-closed runtime admission. Qualification compares a candidate graph with an independent reference on isolated state using explicit parent-operation obligations. We evaluate two repository-level contracts, bug localization and patch validation, on controlled repositories. Among 100 activated, non-equivalent development/qualification faults adjudicated by one human, parent-semantic validation rejects 49/100 (operator-cluster bootstrap 95% CI [33.7%, 64.8%]). The objective
s0d6d6ad6fc.summary: RefinementGuard applies translation validation to hidden parallel graphs that tool runtimes create when lowering agent-selected operations, with fail-closed runtime admission.
s0d6d6ad6fc.why: Tool runtimes that silently rewrite agent operations into hidden graphs can mistranslate semantics, so validating them before execution addresses a safety gap for agent tooling.

sc48f903c29.title: Searching the Pareto Front: Multi-Objective Retrieval for Heterogeneous Scientific Modalities
sc48f903c29.description: arXiv:2611.23639v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In cosmology, surveys span different sky regions and wavelength ranges, resulting in uneven modality coverage across observational datasets. Such heterogeneity can be addressed through either multimodal foundation models (FMs), which learn shared embedding spaces, or independently learned modality embeddings combined via late fusion. We investigate whether the latter provides an adaptive alternative to FM-based scientific retrieval. We evaluate this approach on a galaxy retrieval task spanning diverse modalities--history of star formation, spectra of light emitted, and multi-wavelength observations from two telescopes--comparing an FM baseline with separately trained embeddings fused through multi-objective optimization based on Pareto optima
sc48f903c29.summary: The paper investigates late fusion of independently learned modality embeddings as an alternative to multimodal foundation models for galaxy retrieval across uneven cosmology survey data.

s4dcdc96330.title: Evaluating Governed LLM-Driven ML Experimentation: Lifecycle, Provenance, and Failure Metrics
s4dcdc96330.description: arXiv:2611.23678v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous agents that run ML experiments are usually judged by the best score they reach. That score says nothing about how it was reached: whether the agent stayed within the files it was allowed to edit, whether failed trials were kept or silently dropped, and whether each keep or discard decision can be traced to its evidence. We propose evaluating such systems on their experimental process as well as their outcome, and we build a governed harness that makes this possible. A control plane, not the LLM that proposes changes, owns each trial's lifecycle, checks its edit scope, decides keep or discard, and appends one record per trial to an append-only ledger. Governance metrics such as the invalid-action rate, the repeated-bad rate and prov
s4dcdc96330.summary: The paper proposes evaluating autonomous ML experimentation agents on their process, including file-scope compliance, retained failed trials, and decision provenance, using a governed harness.
s4dcdc96330.why: Judging agents only by best score hides whether they stayed within permissions and kept failed trials, so process metrics matter for auditing agent-run experiments.

s81f7397512.title: Auditable Clinical Support with Decision Agents
s81f7397512.description: arXiv:2611.23700v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Clinicians reviewing a diagnostic work-up will ask what was considered at each step and why the assessment changed. Agents powered by free text can reach physician-level diagnostic accuracy, but their written reasoning does not always reflect the factors that went into the decision. Here, we present Decision2Care, a decision agent that works up the acutely ill patient without producing any text. A decision model assigns a probability to each permitted EHR action, and fixed rules carry out the most probable one. We evaluated Decision2Care on the records of 546 emergency admissions across 12 diseases. Decision2Care reached a diagnostic accuracy of 86.5%, compared with 86.1% for the MIRA-v2 agent, and required a median of 2.2 s per work-up, comp
s81f7397512.summary: Decision2Care is a clinical decision agent that picks EHR actions via a probability model and fixed rules, producing no free text, and was evaluated on acutely ill patient work-ups.
s81f7397512.why: Replacing free-text reasoning with auditable action probabilities addresses traceability concerns for agents in clinical settings.

s64c2a355e9.title: KnowMe Paper Radar: Lightweight Discovery of Promising Papers in the Age of Autoresearch
s64c2a355e9.description: arXiv:2611.23702v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The growing volume of topically similar papers makes it difficult to identify new work that can offer useful research insights or methodological guidance. We present KnowMe Paper Radar, a lightweight discovery tool that combines multiple sources of evidence into personalized reading priorities. Users specify topics, priorities, exclusions and dates; the system brings together topical relevance, recency, author research histories, collaboration paths and direction-specific institutional context. By exposing each score component and its supporting sources, KnowMe helps readers select promising papers for their current questions and discover relevant work beyond familiar authors. Automatic acquisition, version merging and graph-cache reuse keep
s64c2a355e9.summary: KnowMe Paper Radar is a lightweight tool that ranks papers for personalized reading using topical relevance, recency, author histories, and exposed score components.

sebcc9f35bc.title: Modeling LLM Reasoning Dynamics with Structural Representations
sebcc9f35bc.description: arXiv:2611.23749v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language-model reasoning alternates between sustained activities and local operations. We study how this temporal structure predicts continuation and the computation needed to analyze it. T/E/S combines text, local events, and spans of activity. Across reasoning and information-seeking tasks, events and spans improve next-outcome prediction in 70 of 76 evaluation groups for a Transformer and 74 of 76 for Qwen with LoRA. Span duration and preceding events are associated with transitions, and retaining event history across span boundaries improves prediction. We formulate budget-allocation counting and action-conditional continuation queries, prove counting hardness under explicit encodings, and derive conditions for affordable decision certifi
sebcc9f35bc.summary: The paper introduces T/E/S, a structural representation combining text, local events, and activity spans, which improves next-outcome prediction of LLM reasoning in most tested groups.
sebcc9f35bc.why: Modeling reasoning structure could help predict LLM reasoning continuations, which is useful for engineers analyzing model behavior, though gains are research-stage.

sd447126fcb.title: Thinking Fast, Anywhere: One System-1 for the Decision Points of Any Agent Workflow
sd447126fcb.description: arXiv:2611.23751v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous LLM agents incur substantial cost and latency by invoking a large model (System-2) at every step, even when many intermediate actions choose among a small set of known candidates. Existing dual-system agents offload such decisions to a lightweight System-1 model, but rely on workflow-specific hooks authored per environment. We present AnyS1, a framework that turns human-authored procedural skills, whose instructions naturally specify where choices arise and which options apply, into a shared, domain-general source of decision points. Offline, AnyS1 mines grounded enumerable decisions across over 1,000 public skills, gathers execution-grounded trajectory states inside isolated containers to construct Any-DP, and trains a single cali
sd447126fcb.summary: AnyS1 turns human-authored procedural skills into domain-general decision points so a lightweight System-1 model can handle choices instead of a large model at every agent step.
sd447126fcb.why: Routing routine agent decisions to a smaller model could cut cost and latency across agent workflows without workflow-specific integration hooks.

s5eca248851.title: Continual Tool-Space Extension Learning for Multimodal Agents
s5eca248851.description: arXiv:2611.23810v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal agents largely rely on generic tools such as cropping, search, and code execution, leaving specialist vision models outside their tool space. However, bringing such a model into an already trained agent is not straightforward. The challenge is to learn each new tool efficiently while retaining the ability to use existing ones. This work proposes COTEX, continual tool-space extension learning, that adds new tools at efficient adapter-level cost. COTEX locates two sets of parameter directions; one triggers a tool call and thereby opens a multi-turn reasoning trajectory, while the other determines which tool is chosen. The adapter of a new tool is restricted to the calling directions that leave earlier tool choices unaffected by ortho
s5eca248851.summary: COTEX proposes continual tool-space extension, adding specialist vision models as new tools to trained multimodal agents at adapter-level cost while retaining existing tools.
s5eca248851.why: Adding new tools to an already trained agent without losing existing capabilities is a practical concern for teams extending multimodal agent systems.

s7abc015cee.title: Metrics-in-the-Loop: Complexity Feedback Reshapes Agent-Written Code
s7abc015cee.description: arXiv:2611.23817v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coding agents now write whole codebases in long autonomous runs, guided mainly by whether their tests pass. Yet passing tests alone does not reveal accumulating complexity or gaps in test coverage, which then persist as agents extend their own code. We introduce metrics-in-the-loop, an inference-time intervention that gives agents in-flight feedback: cheap, automatically computed code metrics injected into the agent's context during the trajectory. After each code-changing agent turn, we insert short feedback messages naming changed functions whose cyclomatic complexity exceeds a limit (complexity feedback) or changed lines that are skipped by tests (coverage feedback), giving the agent the opportunity to refactor code or strengthen tests bef
s7abc015cee.summary: The paper introduces metrics-in-the-loop, which injects automatically computed code complexity and coverage metrics into coding agents' context during autonomous runs to shape the code they write.
s7abc015cee.why: Passing tests alone does not reveal accumulating complexity, so in-flight code metrics offer a practical way to steer long autonomous coding runs.

sbbdb3cd067.title: Evidence-Based Credit Assignment for Search-Augmented Language Models
sbbdb3cd067.description: arXiv:2611.23824v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning from terminal answer rewards enables search-augmented language models to interleave reasoning and retrieval without step-level annotations, yet outcome supervision assigns identical credit to every search in a trajectory regardless of whether it retrieved useful information. This limitation is especially severe when all sampled rollouts for a question fail, collapsing group-centered outcome advantages to zero even when trajectories gather markedly different evidence. We present Evidence-based Credit Assignment (ECA), which augments terminal outcome rewards with a training-only auxiliary signal measuring how retrieved documents improve the likelihood of a reference answer. Rather than scoring the full dialogue prefix, EC
sbbdb3cd067.summary: Evidence-based Credit Assignment (ECA) assigns credit to individual searches in search-augmented LM reinforcement learning based on the evidence each retrieved, rather than uniformly across trajectories.
sbbdb3cd067.why: Outcome-only rewards give identical credit to every search and collapse to zero when all rollouts fail, so evidence-aware credit could improve training of retrieval-augmented models.

sf85b04bdd7.title: A System 1 Decision Model for Medical Multiple-Choice Questions Built on Frozen Language Models
sf85b04bdd7.description: arXiv:2611.23832v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A System 1 model answers a multiple-choice question in a single pass. A frozen language model turns the question and each option into vectors, two small, trained heads place them in a shared space, and the closest option wins. The design has been shown on agent decisions, but we are not aware of a study of how far it goes on exam questions that need medical knowledge, where the right option is often no more similar to the question than the wrong ones. We rebuilt the recipe from scratch for MedMCQA and trained only two projection heads and one temperature on top of frozen Qwen3.5-0.8B, Granite-4.2-3B and Qwen3-8B, using a contrastive loss with in-batch and hard negatives and a mask for repeated answers. With plain last-token vectors, both smal
sf85b04bdd7.summary: Researchers rebuilt a single-pass System 1 decision model on frozen language models and tested it on MedMCQA medical exam questions, training only two projection heads and a temperature parameter.
sf85b04bdd7.why: It tests whether cheap, single-pass embedding-based answer selection can handle knowledge-heavy medical questions, relevant to building low-cost medical QA systems.

sa98e0642db.title: RoboBuilder: Agentic Robot Co-Design with Real-world Video Feedback in the Loop
sa98e0642db.description: arXiv:2611.23855v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can AI agents design robots that work in the real world? We introduce RoboBuilder, a benchmark in which coding agents co-design a robot's hardware and program from standard parts, motors and a custom 3D-printed part, and every design that passes in simulation is built and tested on a physical course. Simulation alone is not enough: under public part data, none of 15 initial passing designs crossed the real course, so an agent learns the simulator from measurements it requests and videos of real runs. Across four frontier coding agents, ten obstacles at three difficulty levels, 16,427 simulations of 12,774 distinct robots and 135 physical robots built in an estimated 240 hours, agents solve nearly all easy obstacles and invent mechanisms our s
sa98e0642db.summary: RoboBuilder is a benchmark where coding agents co-design robot hardware and software, with designs passing simulation also tested on a physical course.
sa98e0642db.why: It shows simulation alone missed real-world failures, so agent-driven hardware design needs physical feedback loops to be trustworthy.

s6d5ce1eaa9.title: Asking but Missing: Decision Coverage in Natural-Language Data Querying
s6d5ce1eaa9.description: arXiv:2611.23864v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to translate natural language questions about structured data into executable programs. A fundamental challenge is recognizing when a question admits multiple computational interpretations and identifying the decisions needed to resolve them. We investigate whether language models recognize these unresolved decisions before generating code, or silently adopt assumptions that may lead to incorrect results. We refer to the latter behavior as Underspecified Decision Completion (UDC). To distinguish different causes of UDC, we introduce Grounded Code Generation (GCG), a diagnostic protocol that separates the identification of unresolved decisions, their resolution using evidence, and their translation i
s6d5ce1eaa9.summary: The paper studies whether language models recognize unresolved decisions in natural-language data questions before generating code, or silently adopt assumptions, a behavior it calls Underspecified Decision Completion.
s6d5ce1eaa9.why: Silent assumptions in text-to-query code can yield plausible but wrong results, a risk for teams deploying LLM data querying tools.

sece56c6b4b.title: Risk-Controlled Correction for Frozen Multimodal Models under Missing Modalities
sece56c6b4b.description: arXiv:2611.23886v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A deployed multimodal predictor may face missing modalities after its weights can no longer be changed. This raises a question that training-time repair does not answer: what part of the resulting error is still correctable from the information that remains? We show that this part is characterized by the Bayes gap, the difference between the model's prediction and the Bayes prediction given the observed modalities. For cross-entropy and squared error, excess risk measures this gap in the geometry of the loss; ambiguity in the observed modalities cannot be removed. Thus, a badly degraded prediction is not necessarily a correctable one. Estimating the Bayes prediction normally requires labels. However, when a model observing more modalities is
sece56c6b4b.summary: The paper characterizes how much error a frozen multimodal model can still correct when modalities are missing, using a Bayes gap measured by excess risk.
sece56c6b4b.why: Engineers deploying fixed multimodal models can use this framing to estimate which errors remain correctable when inputs are missing at inference.

sa80e309f04.title: EVA-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of Video Evaluators for Judging Temporal Quality
sa80e309f04.description: arXiv:2611.23890v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Video evaluators play an important role in video generation, yet they miss motion defects, limiting the quality of generated videos. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) has made strong progress in mathematics and coding, where explicit verifiers provide reliable feedback on a single goal. Video evaluation poses two difficulties for RSI: it has no verifier, and it must judge many dimensions at once, such as physics, smoothness and dynamics, where a gain on one can cost another. We introduce EVA-RSI, a multi-agent framework for exploring RSI under these two constraints. We build a fixed proxy exam with construction-defined targets by applying controlled changes to videos, such as temporal reversal and frame dropping. These edits supply supervision
sa80e309f04.summary: EVA-RSI is a multi-agent framework that applies recursive self-improvement to video evaluators so they can judge multiple temporal quality dimensions without an explicit verifier.
sa80e309f04.why: Better automated video judges could improve filtering and evaluation of generated video, though the text gives limited detail on results.

sd8fdc9f2df.title: Evaluating invariance training with certified answer-changing controls in neural graph algorithms
sd8fdc9f2df.description: arXiv:2611.23907v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Invariance training aims to make neural algorithmic reasoners robust to answer-preserving input changes and is judged by accuracy and by how rarely such edits change predictions. We ask whether this evaluation detects lost sensitivity to answer-changing edits on minimum spanning trees of synthetic graphs, where both directions can be certified. Attaching a subgraph through one bridge provably preserves every original label. Attaching it through two edges, oracle-selected to change a label, and lowering one weight inside the graph serve as answer-changing controls; a response is a changed prediction on an edge whose label changes. A reproduced graph transformer (GDT) within its published accuracy range changes a provably fixed label on 53.3-65
sd8fdc9f2df.summary: The paper tests whether invariance training in neural graph algorithms loses sensitivity to answer-changing edits, using certified controls on minimum spanning tree tasks.
sd8fdc9f2df.why: Standard robustness metrics may miss lost sensitivity to meaningful input changes, so evaluation methods for neural reasoners need stronger controls.

s0a1f59888c.title: Training-Free Domain Generation for One-Shot Federated Learning with Server-Side Pre-trained Diffusion Models
s0a1f59888c.description: arXiv:2611.23908v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: One-shot federated learning (OSFL) has attracted increasing attention for its ability to substantially reduce communication overhead by limiting client-server interaction to a single communication round. Nevertheless, this limited interaction makes learning from heterogeneous client distributions challenging. Diffusion-based OSFL approaches seek to address this challenge by synthesizing data that approximate client distributions. However, existing diffusion-based approaches often impose substantial computational costs on clients and lack effective visual guidance to generate data aligned with client distributions. To address these limitations, we propose FedDoG, a training-free Domain Generation framework that leverages server-side pre-traine
s0a1f59888c.summary: The paper proposes a training-free method for one-shot federated learning that uses server-side pre-trained diffusion models to generate data approximating heterogeneous client distributions.
s0a1f59888c.why: It aims to cut client-side compute costs in one-shot federated learning, a practical concern for distributed training deployments.

s31262d5f30.title: MLE Agents: Autonomous ML Engineering in Large-scale Recommendation Systems
s31262d5f30.description: arXiv:2611.23910v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The typical workflow for improving large-scale ranking and recommendation models is slow and tedious: an engineer forms a hypothesis, implements it as a code change, trains a model, and evaluates it both offline and online, often relying on their own intuition and experience along the way. Autonomous LLM agents promise to speed this up by running the loop on their own, but it is still unclear whether they can do this in industry-scale systems rather than on benchmarks or small proxy tasks. We build human-on-the-loop machine learning engineer (MLE) agents that propose, implement, train, and evaluate model changes on large-scale search rankers. Engineers retain control over objective design, search direction, and final-model review. We identify
s31262d5f30.summary: The paper introduces MLE Agents, human-on-the-loop autonomous LLM agents that run the hypothesis-code-train-evaluate loop for large-scale ranking and recommendation models in an industrial setting.
s31262d5f30.why: It offers evidence on whether autonomous agents can handle industry-scale recommendation ML workflows rather than only small benchmarks.

sa17ced2f44.title: Vanguard: Knowing When to Trust the Draft in Speculative Vision-Language Agents
sa17ced2f44.description: arXiv:2611.23917v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-language agents that browse websites, operate phones and act in homes reason before every action, so every step waits for a large model, a latency and cost that stand in the way of deployment. Step-level speculation lets a small model draft each step and calls the large model only on rejected drafts, but its outcome rests on the judge, and a judge that reads only a step's text cannot tell whether the step fits the screen it acts on. We find that a few samples of a small model can contain a correct step about as often as the large model gets the step right, and not always on the same steps: checked against the screen, small drafts can be not only cheaper but better. We present Vanguard, a training-free judge that leaves the draft and ta
sa17ced2f44.summary: Vanguard is a speculative decoding method for vision-language agents that uses a judge reading screen context to decide when a small model's drafted step can be accepted.
sa17ced2f44.why: Reducing reliance on large models per step could lower latency and cost for deployed browsing and phone-operating agents.

sc712951c63.title: Cardiac MRI-informed electrocardiography enables biologically grounded cardiomyopathy detection
sc712951c63.description: arXiv:2611.23925v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Precise myocardial phenotyping at population scale is limited by the cost and accessibility of cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), whereas electrocardiography (ECG) is widely available but reflects electrical rather than structural and functional information. Here we develop MyoECG, a cross-modal representation learning framework that distils myocardial structural and functional knowledge from CMR into standard 12-lead ECGs, enabling imaging-informed cardiomyopathy detection and subtype classification from ECGs alone. MyoECG was pretrained on 45,241 paired ECG-CMR examinations from UK Biobank and a tertiary cardiovascular centre, then developed and validated across more than 1.8 million ECGs from seven independent datasets. Across internal and
sc712951c63.summary: MyoECG is a cross-modal framework that distills cardiac MRI knowledge into standard 12-lead ECGs to detect cardiomyopathy and classify subtypes from ECG alone.
sc712951c63.why: It suggests low-cost ECGs could carry structural heart information usually requiring MRI, relevant to clinical AI product design.

sf3e831e87f.title: Can you make models believe false facts in the prompt?
sf3e831e87f.description: arXiv:2611.23938v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Making LLMs believe false facts is useful for alignment evaluations and for building model organisms. Previous work explored doing so with Synthetic Document Finetuning (SDF). But SDF requires fine-tuning one new model for each set of injected false beliefs. To enable larger scale SDF-powered alignment evaluations, we attempt to produce a single model that believes any fact placed in a tag in the prompt. To do so, we explore doing prompt-conditioned SDF: fine-tuning a model on synthetic documents covering thousands of facts, with each document conditioned on a fact presented in the prompt. We evaluate how deeply the model believes the facts provided in the prompt using evaluations from prior work and a new Jacobian lens evaluation. We find th
sf3e831e87f.summary: The paper explores prompt-conditioned synthetic document finetuning to produce a single model that believes arbitrary false facts placed in a prompt tag, instead of fine-tuning one model per belief set.
sf3e831e87f.why: A single model that accepts injected false facts via prompt could make alignment evaluations and model organism building far more scalable.

sf808c16380.title: GLIDE: Scalable and Event-Aware Inductive Forecasting over Evolving Logistics Graphs
sf808c16380.description: arXiv:2611.23942v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate forecasting of order volume at scale-effect hotspots (SEHs), spatially coherent groups of logistics flows that serve as distributed optimization units for real-time many-to-one dispatch, is a prerequisite for efficient order pooling in on-demand food delivery (OFD) platforms such as Meituan. However, real-world logistics networks present unique challenges that render standard spatiotemporal prediction model ineffective. (i) Dynamic Topology: Unlike static road networks, logistics graphs are ephemeral, with hotspot emerging and vanishing continuously; (ii) Scale--Volume Heterogeneity: Graph sizes vary from $10^2$ to $10^4$, while zero-inflated, long-tailed volumes create computational bottlenecks and bias predictions toward inactivity
sf808c16380.summary: GLIDE is an event-aware inductive forecasting method for order volume at scale-effect hotspots in evolving logistics graphs, evaluated in on-demand food delivery at Meituan.
sf808c16380.why: It addresses forecasting on dynamic graphs where topology changes, a practical challenge for real-time logistics optimization systems.

s973b7c2f93.title: SCAFFOLD: Toward Warrant-Preserving Evidence Transport for Reusable LLM-Agent Skills
s973b7c2f93.description: arXiv:2611.23990v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An agent skill that succeeded yesterday may be executable today without being justified for reuse today. Tests may cover only observable contract clauses, outcome oracles may be absent, evaluations may inherit the same erroneous specification, and permissions or dependencies may change between validation and invocation. We argue that the appropriate unit of prospective trust is a Warranted Reuse Claim (WRC): a defeasible, claim-specific authorization tied to a versioned skill, target context, evidence, assumptions, and identified defeaters. The paper sharpens this position through Warrant-Preserving Evidence Transport (WPET), a proposed discipline for deciding which historical evidence remains admissible after context change. It distinguishes
s973b7c2f93.summary: SCAFFOLD proposes Warranted Reuse Claims as a way to authorize reuse of LLM-agent skills based on versioned evidence, assumptions, and defeaters rather than past test success.
s973b7c2f93.why: Agent skills that passed earlier tests may not be safe to reuse as dependencies and permissions change, so reuse needs explicit justification.

sb20a5243e1.title: Space-X: Self-Evolving Spatial Agents Weaving Clues into Evidence Chains
sb20a5243e1.description: arXiv:2611.24004v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spatial reasoning connects visual observations, geometric estimates, and linguistic decisions into a coherent derivation. Yet tool-augmented agents often acquire evidence without clear targets, combine outputs under inconsistent object or reference-frame semantics, and misjudge evidence sufficiency. Thus, more tools or calls do not reliably improve reasoning. We introduce Space-X, a spatial-reasoning framework that self-evolves toward complete, continuous evidence-chain construction. An Execution Agent acquires, associates, and judges evidence per problem using role-specific memory. A Control Agent diagnoses evidence-chain breaks from execution traces and jointly revises tools, interfaces, skills, memory organization, and decision rules. This
sb20a5243e1.summary: Space-X is a spatial reasoning framework where tool-augmented agents self-evolve to build complete, continuous evidence chains from visual and geometric clues.
sb20a5243e1.why: It targets the problem that more tool calls do not reliably improve agent reasoning, a common issue in tool-using agent design.

s50b5f18b55.title: Test-Time Symmetrization: Scaling Laws for Model-Agnostic Learning under Structure
s50b5f18b55.description: arXiv:2611.24032v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Test-time compute has emerged as a powerful way to improve the accuracy of language models at inference time, with scaling laws quantifying how accuracy improves with additional forward passes. Existing scaling laws, however, focus on repeated sampling from a fixed prompt, even though many tasks admit multiple equivalent representations of the same underlying problem. A graph does not depend on how its nodes are numbered, and a program does not depend on the names of its variables, yet language models can change their answers under such rewritings. In this paper, we study test-time symmetrization, which uses forward passes on rewritings of the input and aggregates the resulting answers over the group $G$ of rewritings. We prove that no amount
s50b5f18b55.summary: The paper studies test-time symmetrization, using scaling laws to show how averaging over equivalent rewritings of a problem, such as renumbered graphs or renamed variables, improves model answers.
s50b5f18b55.why: Models change answers under equivalent rewrites, so symmetrization offers a model-agnostic way to trade inference compute for consistency.

se2c1fd58d7.title: A Capability Framework for Evaluating Agentic AI Platforms in Regulated Enterprises
se2c1fd58d7.description: arXiv:2611.24039v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic AI platforms-systems in which LLM agents plan, invoke tools, retain memory and coordinate to change the state of enterprise systems-are being procured faster than they can be measured. Public agent benchmarks score models in fixed harnesses; enterprises buy integrated platforms whose orchestration, memory, governance and tooling layers dominate outcomes, and they buy them largely on the strength of vendor demonstrations. We report an industrial evaluation programme ("bakeoff") run by the innovation laboratory of a global bank in which ten platforms-spanning open-source frameworks, proprietary products and hyperscaler ecosystems-were assessed by a cross-functional panel on nine capability dimensions across three financial-services work
se2c1fd58d7.summary: Researchers report an industrial evaluation program, run by a global bank's innovation lab, for assessing agentic AI platforms that are being procured faster than measured.
se2c1fd58d7.why: Enterprises buying agent platforms largely on vendor demos need structured, capability-based evaluation methods before committing to integrated systems.

sc5fe7e0f67.title: Attention Is Not Relevance: Challenging the Causality of Attention in Autonomous Driving
sc5fe7e0f67.description: arXiv:2611.24051v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Attention has become one of the most widely adopted solutions for estimating the relevance of surrounding objects and interpreting an autonomous vehicle's driving decisions. However, its ability to capture the causal impact of individual input elements on an AI model's output has long been discussed in the literature, particularly in the Natural Language Processing (NLP) domain. This work brings this discussion into the autonomous driving domain by analyzing the accuracy of attention in estimating the impact of an input object on an autonomous vehicle's driving, i.e., its relevance. To this end, we compare different attention-based relevance estimation methods against a causal reference of object relevance obtained through counterfactual anal
sc5fe7e0f67.summary: The paper argues that attention weights are not reliable causal estimates of how much an input object affects an autonomous vehicle's driving decisions.
sc5fe7e0f67.why: Teams using attention maps as explanations for autonomous driving models may be misreading which inputs actually drive decisions.

s60921a219a.title: 3D GameDev Arena: Benchmarking Coding Agents That Plan, Build, and Playtest extreme Long-Horizon Browser Games
s60921a219a.description: arXiv:2611.24073v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coding agents now resolve repository issues and generate compact playable games, but whether they can build a large 3D game from scratch remains open. Such games tightly couple mechanics, scenes, assets, and interaction logic, and their quality rests on player enjoyment, which existing benchmarks rarely assess. Thus, we introduce 3D GameDev Arena, a first extreme long-horizon benchmark of 108 from-scratch game-development tasks across 14 genres. Given only a text specification and UI/UX reference images, a fully automated plan--implement--test--repair pipeline builds each task into a self-contained browser game. Runs average $\sim$1,000 LLM calls ; the longest uses 14,407 calls, 2.13B tokens, and 608 assets. Evaluation spans (1) objective cod
s60921a219a.summary: Researchers introduce 3D GameDev Arena, a benchmark of 108 long-horizon tasks testing whether coding agents can build large 3D browser games from scratch.
s60921a219a.why: It tests end-to-end agent capability on complex, multi-part software builds rather than isolated repository issues, useful for judging agent readiness.

sc64cb56963.title: Recurrent Domain Incremental Adaptation of Time-Series Foundation Models
sc64cb56963.description: arXiv:2611.24075v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pretrained Time-Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) provide strong representations for downstream classification tasks. Yet adapting a TSFM under changing operating conditions remains challenging. A model must improve on each newly observed condition without sacrificing conditions it has already learned, often from only a small labeled calibration set and without knowing the operating condition at inference time. We find that this difficulty has an important geometric structure. Under an operating-condition shift, the embedding space of a TSFM does not move uniformly: some local regions change substantially, while others remain nearly unchanged. Consequently, a global adaptation can unnecessarily move embeddings that were already correctly class
sc64cb56963.summary: The paper proposes a method for adapting pretrained time-series foundation models to changing operating conditions without forgetting earlier conditions, using small labeled calibration sets.
sc64cb56963.why: Industrial time-series deployments face shifting conditions, and this targets adaptation without catastrophic forgetting using limited labeled data.

s9f21873a24.title: Embodied Graph: A Relational World Model for Long-Horizon Tasks
s9f21873a24.description: arXiv:2611.24115v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-horizon tasks in embodied and web environments involve extended decision sequences and delayed feedback, making accurate planning crucial for success. World models tackle this by learning latent dynamics for imagination-based planning. However, existing approaches merely rely on dense pixel-level observations, which forces the model to absorb redundant information while overlooking relations among task-relevant entities. Consequently, small errors may accumulate over long imagined rollouts and gradually corrupt the predictions. In this paper, we explore world models that imagine over sparse state abstractions, which poses two key challenges: 1) how to remove redundant information and form a compact state abstraction; 2) how to incorporat
s9f21873a24.summary: The paper introduces Embodied Graph, a relational world model that plans over entities and their relations instead of dense pixel observations for long-horizon embodied and web tasks.

s27e8e8e0fa.title: Fast Bayesian Methods for Uncertainty Quantification in Sparse AI Evaluation
s27e8e8e0fa.description: arXiv:2611.24159v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Estimating how an AI system will perform on a new benchmark need not require another large model. We use public evaluation counts to choose a weak Beta prior, then update it exactly from at most 31 revealed outcomes. The predictor uses no item semantics, pretrained weights, or inference API. Its single online evaluation in the AIMS competition returned a team-reported Brier ALC of 0.188477, a 24.6% reduction from the constant-0.5 reference. The complete submission is 7,754 bytes; a server microbenchmark measures 12.71 microseconds per prediction with 31 matching labels. We describe how source evaluations are compressed into 301 prior means and show why a concentration of two lets new evidence rapidly determine the prediction. The resulting po
s27e8e8e0fa.summary: A team describes a lightweight Bayesian method that predicts AI benchmark performance from at most 31 revealed outcomes, reporting a 24.6% Brier reduction in the AIMS competition.
s27e8e8e0fa.why: It offers a cheap way to estimate model performance on new benchmarks without running another large model, though results are team-reported.

sa0c5487ee9.title: GALA: Gallery-Level Alignment for Real-Life Vision Decoding from EEG
sa0c5487ee9.description: arXiv:2611.24206v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural decoding of visual experience from electroencephalography (EEG) has achieved strong performance in intra-subject settings, but current methods fail to generalize across individuals: on the standard 200-way benchmark THINGS-EEG-2, top-1 accuracy drops from above 80% within subjects to about 32% for an unseen subject. Adapting a pre-trained encoder to new subjects and sessions typically requires labeled data, a bottleneck whose collection time severely limits practical device deployment. In a practical Brain-Computer Interface (BCI), however, the possible outcomes are known in advance and form a gallery of candidates, and the unlabeled EEG of the user accumulates as soon as the device is used. We propose a new setting, incremental transd
sa0c5487ee9.summary: The GALA paper proposes gallery-level alignment to decode visual experience from EEG across individuals, addressing a drop in accuracy for unseen subjects without labeled data.
sa0c5487ee9.why: Cross-subject generalization without labeled calibration data is a key barrier to practical brain-computer interface deployment.

sf92ae705fd.title: Learning to Coordinate: LLM-Guided Workflow Evolution for Token-Efficient Red Teaming
sf92ae705fd.description: arXiv:2611.24221v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated red teaming is essential for identifying safety failures in large language models (LLMs), but its practical scalability depends on the resources required to discover those failures. Multi-agent systems can combine complementary capabilities, yet repeated planning, redundant exchanges, and ineffective information routing can make their coordination expensive. Moreover, a target model's response indicates the outcome of a test without identifying which collaboration decision should change. We present Learning to Coordinate (L2C), an LLM-guided framework that evolves an executable multi-agent workflow for each red-teaming case. L2C represents agent responsibilities, execution dependencies, and input bindings in a versioned graph, and a
sf92ae705fd.summary: The paper presents Learning to Coordinate (L2C), an LLM-guided method that evolves multi-agent red-teaming workflows to find LLM safety failures with fewer tokens.
sf92ae705fd.why: Lowering the token cost of automated red teaming makes continuous safety testing of LLMs more practical to run at scale.

sc7022bc03a.title: From Points to Trajectories: Rethinking Multimodal Alignment for Physical Events
sc7022bc03a.description: arXiv:2611.24249v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Advancing physical artificial intelligence (Physical AI) requires moving beyond static object recognition to ground how real-world mechanics (e.g., impact, friction, and force transfer) unfold over time. While multimodal aligners seek to capture these interactions by matching multi-sensor streams, prevailing architectures compress each temporal sequence into a single pooled embedding. We show that this paradigm fails on twin events: distinct physical executions recorded under identical task conditions. Collapsing the temporal dimension averages out transient cross-modal dynamics, effectively reducing physical event alignment to static scene recognition. Formally, we prove that as sequence length increases, any temporally pooled representation
sc7022bc03a.summary: The paper argues that pooling multi-sensor sequences into single embeddings fails to distinguish physically distinct events, and proposes trajectory-level multimodal alignment instead.

s88eda9f8b8.title: FedE2E: One-Shot Federated Learning for End-to-End Autonomous Driving with Closed-Loop Evaluation
s88eda9f8b8.description: arXiv:2611.24254v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated learning enables collaborative model training without sharing datasets. However, existing federated learning methods for autonomous driving typically require multi-round communication and lack closed-loop evaluation, while one-shot methods mainly focus on perception tasks. To address these limitations, we propose \method, a one-shot federated learning method for end-to-end autonomous driving. It comprises multi-client calibration, anchor-based feature alignment, and token-wise consensus distillation to distill knowledge from heterogeneous models. Closed-loop evaluation on Bench2Drive demonstrates the effectiveness of \method in both one-shot and multi-round federated learning. In the one-shot setting, it achieves a Driving Score of
s88eda9f8b8.summary: FedE2E proposes one-shot federated learning for end-to-end autonomous driving, with multi-client calibration and closed-loop evaluation, avoiding multi-round communication.
s88eda9f8b8.why: One-shot federated training could reduce communication costs for training driving models across fleets without sharing raw data.

s8a8cf06198.title: Beyond Corpus-Driven Imitation: Evolving Musical Mindsets in the Agentic Orchestra via Quantum Reinforcement Learning
s8a8cf06198.description: arXiv:2611.24290v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a framework for computer-aided music composition and performance based on quantum reinforcement learning and multi-agent interaction. We introduce the agentic orchestra, where musical agents evolve distinct mindsets through trial-and-error engagement with a musical environment, rather than through training on large datasets. The agents are implemented as parameterised quantum circuits. They evolve distinct compositional behaviours, referred to as mindsets. This enables the exploration of musical decision spaces using quantum superposition and entanglement within a hybrid quantum-classical loop. We present two complementary agent architectures: atomistic agents, which process pitch and rhythm independently, and holistic age
s8a8cf06198.summary: The paper presents an agentic orchestra in which musical agents implemented as parameterised quantum circuits evolve compositional behaviours via quantum reinforcement learning.

sd3cf60ca9d.title: KnowledgeClaw: Towards Agentic Knowledge Engineering via Omnimodal Hypergraphs
sd3cf60ca9d.description: arXiv:2611.24294v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Knowledge engineering (KE) turns raw files into a reasoning-ready knowledge base, a task now within reach of LLM agents. KE has progressed from chunk and graph retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to memory agents, agentic KE and multimodal KE. However, a live knowledge base needs omnimodality, a closed-loop lifecycle and multi-granular application at once, yet existing systems meet at most two and no benchmark measures all three. We formalize Omnimodal Knowledge Engineering (OmniKE) and release OmniKE-Bench, six tasks with 1,829 model-free items over 3,960 real files in five modalities. We further propose KnowledgeClaw, an agentic system that builds an omnimodal typed hypergraph, keeps it current with a closed-loop lifecycle agent and routes
sd3cf60ca9d.summary: KnowledgeClaw introduces OmniKE, an omnimodal knowledge-engineering formulation, and OmniKE-Bench, a benchmark of six tasks with 1,829 items for agentic knowledge base construction.
sd3cf60ca9d.why: A benchmark covering multimodal inputs, closed-loop lifecycles and multi-granular use gives teams a way to compare knowledge-base agent systems.

s3cfea67a36.title: OpenKAGE: Open-Ended Lifelong Learning in the Open World via Knowledge-Sharing Agent-Group Evolution
s3cfea67a36.description: arXiv:2611.24302v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Building autonomous agents that continually explore open worlds and acquire new capabilities through experience is a long-standing aspiration in artificial intelligence. Existing research often pursues lifelong learning within predefined tasks, curricula, or objectives, with self-improvement largely confined to individual agents. We introduce OpenKAGE, an agent-group evolution framework for open-ended lifelong learning. Within this framework, agents autonomously explore open worlds and continually acquire new capabilities by accumulating and reusing knowledge from their own interactions and the experience of others. OpenKAGE builds on two key mechanisms: (1) a two-layer knowledge representation, with a memory layer for situated memories and a
s3cfea67a36.summary: OpenKAGE is an agent-group evolution framework in which agents explore open worlds and share accumulated knowledge to learn continually.

s29edeb1cb6.title: Benchmarking LLM abilities on postdoc-level natural science problems
s29edeb1cb6.description: arXiv:2611.24321v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scientific problems have no answer key, so evaluating an agent means deciding what counts as a better solution before any agent is run. Existing benchmarks either match a symbolic answer against a key or, where they require executable work, score it by unit tests, by a rubric, or by position on a competition leaderboard. None of these is the criterion by which a field decides that one published method beats another. STEMBench adopts that criterion directly. Each of its twelve research problems in high-energy physics, astrophysics and neuroscience is scored by its own field's figure of merit, and each comes with two measured anchors: a submission that uses no domain knowledge, and an expert reference reproducing a published method, both obtain
s29edeb1cb6.summary: STEMBench is a benchmark of twelve postdoc-level research problems in high-energy physics, astrophysics and neuroscience, scoring agents by field-accepted method comparisons rather than answer keys.
s29edeb1cb6.why: It evaluates scientific agents on the criteria researchers actually use to judge methods, not only on unit tests or fixed answers.

s1191b82a87.title: automodel: A Skill for Agentic Model Discovery
s1191b82a87.description: arXiv:2611.24347v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The search for better models, whether expressed as analytical equations or neural architectures, has increasingly shifted from manual design toward data-driven automation. While a multitude of algorithms exist, ranging from exhaustive search to AlphaEvolve, recent advances in general-purpose coding agents such as Claude Code and OpenAI Codex raise the question: could providing such systems with a "model discovery recipe" be enough to discover or improve models? We present automodel, an agent skill for general model discovery. With case studies in astrophysics, cardiovascular dynamics, precision agriculture, traffic flow, and vehicle tire dynamics, we show how commercial agents equipped with automodel can successfully identify novel and scient
s1191b82a87.summary: The paper presents automodel, an agent skill that directs general-purpose coding agents such as Claude Code and OpenAI Codex to discover analytical equations or neural architectures.
s1191b82a87.why: It tests whether off-the-shelf coding agents can automate model design when given a structured discovery recipe.

sf41c486401.title: When Figures Disagree with Text: Evaluating Autonomous Visual Evidence Verification in Scientific Papers
sf41c486401.description: arXiv:2611.24353v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scientific figures carry evidence for the claims that cite them, so reviewing a paper means checking that a figure agrees with the text, and not only describing what the figure shows. Benchmarks of figure-text verification typically hand the model the figure, the claim, or the knowledge that an inconsistency exists, which leaves untested whether a model can find the figure worth checking in a complete paper, relate a visual element to the claim it conflicts with, and recognize the conflict. We study this autonomous setting on 31 full manuscripts, each carrying a reviewer-documented figure-text inconsistency from PRISMM-Bench that is hidden from the model. Six multimodal models review each PDF under a neutral prompt, and we then add one input
sf41c486401.summary: Researchers evaluate whether autonomous systems can find, link and recognize figure-text conflicts across 31 full scientific manuscripts.
sf41c486401.why: It tests end-to-end paper review rather than pre-supplied inconsistencies, showing how far automated figure-claim checking is from practical use.

s7a63192098.title: Semantic Context Handoff with On-Demand Evidence for Long-Horizon Agents
s7a63192098.description: arXiv:2611.24357v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Traditional long-horizon LLM agents often hand off context through full-history prompting, retaining all previous action--observation interactions. As execution proceeds, this history keeps growing, increasing inference cost and potentially degrading accuracy. Existing methods control this growth by preserving compact conclusions while removing earlier observations, but doing so can discard evidence that later becomes relevant. We introduce Semantic Context Handoff (SCH), whose central abstraction is state--evidence separation: a compact semantic state carries the agent's current interpretation, while supporting action--observation evidence remains separately addressable and can re-enter context when later execution makes it relevant, without
s7a63192098.summary: Researchers propose Semantic Context Handoff, which keeps compact semantic state and retrieves earlier evidence on demand for long-horizon LLM agents.
s7a63192098.why: It targets rising inference cost and accuracy loss from full-history prompting, a practical problem for teams running long agent workflows.

s22fad911f7.title: MoE-Context: Show the Model Only What It Needs
s22fad911f7.description: arXiv:2611.24379v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents read their whole history at every step. People do not work like that: we keep what the moment needs and hold the rest as a rough note we can recall. MoE-Context applies this to language models. The context is split into blocks. Before each step a fast yes or no pass decides which blocks the step needs; the rest stay as one-line notes that can be brought back, and nothing is deleted. In the version we build, one model makes this decision and then answers, over a single key-value cache where hidden blocks are masked rather than removed. On a laptop with Qwen3-1.7B and a synthetic lookup task, showing only the needed block raises accuracy from 93 to 119 of 120, and a masked block is as hidden as a deleted one. The model's own picking i
s22fad911f7.summary: MoE-Context splits language model context into blocks, uses a quick yes-or-no pass to pick needed blocks, and masks the rest instead of deleting them.
s22fad911f7.why: Selective context masking could cut per-step context cost for agents without discarding history, relevant to anyone managing long agent contexts.

s9d29a80eef.title: CaDO: Formal Verification-Guided Multi-Agent Framework for Causal Dataset Repair and Generation
s9d29a80eef.description: arXiv:2611.24406v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-quality causal reasoning datasets are essential for developing models with reliable causal understanding, particularly in specialized domains. However, existing datasets frequently suffer from incorrect annotations and structural imbalances, which can lead to biased predictions and limited generalization. To address this issue, we propose CaDO (Causal-Engine-Guided Multi-Agent Data Optimization), a multi-agent framework for automated diagnosis and repair of causal reasoning datasets. Our framework consists of three key stages: formal causal reasoning, multi-level diagnosis, and automated data repair and generation. First, a Formalizer Agent translates natural language questions into formal causal queries to minimize semantic deviations a
s9d29a80eef.summary: CaDO is a multi-agent framework that uses formal causal verification to diagnose, repair and generate causal reasoning datasets.

sf68dd8c73c.title: Risk-Triggered Search: Behavior-Preserving Safe Control
sf68dd8c73c.description: arXiv:2611.24409v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pre-trained visual world models generate multi-step action plans from current and goal observations, yet terminal-proximity objectives fail to prevent forbidden-zone traversal or rigid-body collision sliding. Purely visual interfaces may lack analytical dynamics, structured states, or explicit collision geometry, requiring internal prediction of action-conditioned process risk. We propose Risk-Triggered Search (RTS) for frozen Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) world models. Rather than relying on static state features that cannot distinguish candidate plans sharing an observation, RTS unrolls action-conditioned future latent prefixes in the frozen world model and trains a lightweight risk head with process-violation supervision.
sf68dd8c73c.summary: Risk-Triggered Search adds action-conditioned risk prediction to frozen JEPA visual world models to avoid forbidden zones and collisions during planning.
sf68dd8c73c.why: Safer planning on top of frozen pretrained world models could matter to robotics teams, though the summary gives little detail on results.

s646ad3cf3c.title: Resolution as Attention for Efficient Agent Memory Perception
s646ad3cf3c.description: arXiv:2611.24422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM-based agents accumulate extensive interaction histories when solving complex, long-horizon tasks, making efficient memory management critical to their performance and scalability. While existing memory management methods primarily focus on what to retain or retrieve, they often overlook how much perceptual detail should be allocated to individual past interactions. We posit that effective agent memory depends not only on the information preserved, but also on the granularity at which each past interaction is perceived. Motivated by this insight, we propose Resolution as Attention (RAA), a memory perception mechanism that uses visual resolution as a means of attention allocation across interaction histories. RAA renders past interactions a
s646ad3cf3c.summary: Researchers propose allocating perceptual detail to past agent interactions based on resolution, treating resolution as a form of attention for agent memory.
s646ad3cf3c.why: Varying the granularity of stored memories offers a possible way to manage memory cost in long-horizon agents.

sa885ef85ff.title: From real to synthetic: PSG-GAN learns sleep apnea signal dynamics for AI training
sa885ef85ff.description: arXiv:2611.24436v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Synthetic polysomnography (PSG) data has great potential in healthcare applications, for example in substituting real data that is sensitive and challenging to collect. Previous research on synthetic PSG data has been largely focused on short segments of individual signals, overlooking the inter-signal dynamics related to sleep disorders. In this study, we developed a generative adversarial network (PSG-GAN) for co-synthesizing longer segments of multiple PSG signals with diverse and complex characteristics typical of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). The synthetic signals appeared realistic, and the electroencephalography and electrooculography band powers were similarly distributed across sleep stages. Moreover, the PSG-GAN learned to mirror s
sa885ef85ff.summary: PSG-GAN is a generative adversarial network that co-synthesizes longer multi-signal polysomnography segments showing obstructive sleep apnea characteristics.
sa885ef85ff.why: Synthetic multi-signal medical data could help teams train models where real patient data is sensitive or scarce.

sa6b3b1e011.title: Study and Improvement of Search Algorithms in Stochastic Perfect-Information
