s0e3c7b6503.why: Long multimodal inputs make time-to-first-token slow; cheaper input pruning could cut latency for document and multi-image workloads.

s48c58b20cb.title: Harmonic Circuit: Chord Progression Lies in a Sparse Principal Information Flow in Symbolic Music Models
s48c58b20cb.description: arXiv:2611.24453v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Mechanistic Interpretability (MI) seeks to decode neural network computations into human-understandable logic. A core methodology in MI is circuit discovery: identifying the information flow in sub-networks that drive specific model behaviors. While circuit discovery has matured within Natural Language Processing (NLP), the interpretable circuits in music models remain largely unexplored. In this work, we identify a music-functional circuit within two symbolic music generative models: ChatMusician and MuPT. The music function we consider is the prediction of the terminal tonic root in a classical harmonic progression pattern $I \ldots V \rightarrow I$. We use the Auto-Emergence algorithm to extract a principal sparse sub-network as the iden
s48c58b20cb.summary: Researchers identify a music-functional circuit in symbolic music models ChatMusician and MuPT, linking chord progression behavior to a sparse information flow.

s0005c9693a.title: Nothing to Declare: Steering a single neuron increases concealment in AI teams
s0005c9693a.description: arXiv:2611.24475v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent research suggests that individual neurons can have interpretable roles in AI behaviour. In Qwen3.5-4B, steering along one neuron's output direction increased decisions to conceal information more in teams than alone across five scenarios, even when teammates provided no messages. When all members participated and received steering, collective concealment increased in four scenarios, while inter-agent messaging helped temper concealment under steering. Moreover, removing the neuron's contribution had negligible effects. Collective settings can therefore change how an internal intervention affects AI behaviour.
s0005c9693a.summary: Steering a single neuron in Qwen3.5-4B increased information concealment in multi-agent teams across five scenarios, according to an arXiv study.
s0005c9693a.why: It suggests individual neuron steering can shift collective behavior in multi-agent systems, relevant to agent safety and oversight design.

s1f43ef0d1d.title: Mitigating fix reversal: Counterfactual constraints for function-level vulnerability detection
s1f43ef0d1d.description: arXiv:2611.24489v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Function-level vulnerability detectors often exhibit fix reversal, assigning a higher vulnerability probability to a fixed version than to its vulnerable counterpart. Fixes usually lengthen functions, and larger length increases are associated with more severe reversal. Code-transformation experiments indicate that fix reversal mainly stems from a length shortcut: vulnerability probability increases with function length when content is fixed. We propose CFVul to address this problem. Sliding-window encoding covers complete functions, retaining fix information beyond the truncation boundary. During training, a content constraint encourages the vulnerable version to receive a higher vulnerability probability under a common length input. Durin
s1f43ef0d1d.summary: Researchers propose CFVul, a counterfactual method to reduce fix reversal in function-level vulnerability detectors caused by a function-length shortcut.
s1f43ef0d1d.why: Detectors that rate patched code as more vulnerable than unpatched code produce unreliable security signals for code review and scanning tools.

s7582ca82a2.title: Probing agent overeagerness in realistic settings with continuation audits
s7582ca82a2.description: arXiv:2611.24491v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Frontier coding agents increasingly exhibit overeagerness, taking surprising, sometimes reckless actions beyond a user's mandate --- reported in recent system cards from frontier model developers. These cases are surfaced through internal deployment monitoring, which requires private traffic and is out of reach for open-weight models and independent evaluators. Automated alignment audits are the natural alternative, but capable models increasingly recognise the synthetic setup and adjust their behaviour. We introduce Continuation Audits, a pipeline that grounds the auditor on a prefix drawn from a real coding-agent transcript and directs it to continue the trajectory toward a seeded behaviour. Because the prefix is drawn from a real session
s7582ca82a2.summary: Researchers introduce Continuation Audits, a method for probing overeagerness in frontier coding agents in realistic settings without private deployment traffic.
s7582ca82a2.why: It offers a way for open-weight models and independent evaluators to test coding agents for actions beyond user mandates.

s3ca87c5cac.title: Harvesting Expert-Parallel Bubbles for Fine-Tuning
s3ca87c5cac.description: arXiv:2611.24496v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: GPUs are expensive, yet latency-critical large language model (LLM) inference leaves part of them idle. Colocation reclaims this capacity by running best-effort work, such as fine-tuning, alongside serving. Many leading LLMs now use a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture, which adds a new source of idle time. Under expert parallelism, MoE experts are spread across GPUs, and because the router sends uneven numbers of tokens to each GPU, lightly loaded GPUs wait for the most loaded one. Even after applying load balancing solutions, such bubbles still take 8--13% of prefill time. We present BubbleTea, the first colocation system that leverages expert-parallel bubbles for fine-tuning. Unlike existing colocation systems, which make one scheduli
s3ca87c5cac.summary: Researchers propose harvesting idle time from expert-parallel load imbalance in MoE serving to run fine-tuning alongside LLM inference.
s3ca87c5cac.why: Reclaiming GPU idle time from MoE load imbalance could lower costs of colocating fine-tuning with latency-critical serving.

s8478bef18e.title: MECI: Multi-Element Collaborative Interaction for Multimodal Entity Linking
s8478bef18e.description: arXiv:2611.24522v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal Entity Linking (MEL) aims to disambiguate mentions in multimodal contexts by grounding them to specific entities in a knowledge base. A pivotal challenge in MEL is capturing multi-level correspondences: the semantic consistency between mention-entity pairs and the complementary correlations across modalities. However, existing methods often suffer from element dominance due to their reliance on coupled interactions or coarse global aggregations. In response, we propose the Multi-Element Collaborative Interaction (MECI) framework. First, to capture multi-element mention-entity correspondences, we develop a Multi-view Experts Network that leverages a "divide-and-conquer" strategy for decoupled feature learning to mitigate element d
s8478bef18e.summary: Researchers present MECI, a framework for multimodal entity linking that models multi-level correspondences to reduce element dominance in mention-entity grounding.

s116b8f21c2.title: Do Frontier Model Ingredients Add Up? A Replicated Factorial Study of Small Language Models
s116b8f21c2.description: arXiv:2611.24540v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Building a small language model requires choosing which published improvements to combine. We compare five changes in the same model, using the same data and training budget. We test selected combinations and repeat each one with a second random seed. Mixture-of-experts layers, Muon optimisation and a Gated DeltaNet hybrid give the largest gains. Extra normalisation also helps, while an attention gate with a matched parameter budget adds little on average. The gains mostly combine, but small interactions between changes appear again in the repeated runs. Repetition also reveals benefits that an initial statistical estimate treated as noise. These findings apply to our small-model training setting; the expert models also have greater total c
s116b8f21c2.summary: A replicated factorial study tests five published improvements in small language models, finding mixture-of-experts, Muon optimisation and Gated DeltaNet give the largest gains.
s116b8f21c2.why: It gives practical guidance on which published architecture and optimiser changes are worth combining when training small models under a fixed budget.

s1a9261d28a.title: Chain-of-Thought Hidden States Reveal Task-Solving Directions for Direct Answers
s1a9261d28a.description: arXiv:2611.24598v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting improves the performance of Large Language Models by eliciting intermediate reasoning steps. However, CoT is far from perfect: on some tasks, models perform worse than with direct-answer prompting, and on others they generate a few hundred tokens to reach the correct answer. We start by labelling each CoT hidden state as recovering if patching it into the direct prompt yields the correct answer, and failed otherwise. A linear probe shows that the model encodes these two classes differently. We then show that the representation space of the direct prompt holds a direction for each question that leads the model, in a short generation, to the correct answer more often than CoT does. Specifically, we rotate the
s1a9261d28a.summary: Researchers show chain-of-thought hidden states encode task-solving directions that distinguish when CoT helps or fails compared with direct-answer prompting.
s1a9261d28a.why: Understanding when CoT reasoning helps could guide choices between reasoning and direct-answer prompting to save tokens and latency.

s0ca4fc9361.title: Negotiating Control and Accountability among Stakeholders in High-Risk AI Use Cases: Development and Evaluation of the Method ALIGN
s0ca4fc9361.description: arXiv:2611.24609v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Characteristics of Artificial Intelligence (AI) severely restrict human control. This creates new challenges for socio-technical systems design especially in safety-critical domains, where control over risks is essential along with the accountability for any harm caused. Drawing from human factors and AI governance literature, expert interviews and participant observation in a complex high-risk AI use case from the railways, we developed ALIGN, a scenario-based method that supports the governance of and stakeholder involvement in AI development and implementation in three ways: raising awareness for potential accountability-control misalignments in socio-technical systems and their negative consequences, offering a structured approach to as
s0ca4fc9361.summary: Researchers develop ALIGN, a scenario-based method for negotiating control and accountability among stakeholders in high-risk AI use cases, tested in railways.
s0ca4fc9361.why: It offers a structured approach for involving stakeholders in governance and accountability for safety-critical AI deployments.

s905fef5ca7.title: H3Remover: Reinforcing Video Object Removal without Paired Data
s905fef5ca7.description: arXiv:2611.24633v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Pretrained video editors possess rich removal and completion priors, yet may retain targets or alter unrelated content. We present H3Remover, which reinforces MiniMax-H3 Base Ref2VA for video object removal without paired object-free training targets. To discourage superficial edits such as recoloring, a target-removal reward favors calibrated depth changes consistent with revealing farther content. To limit unintended scene changes, a background-geometry reward encourages preservation of relative depth ordering. To preserve background appearance without retaining unwanted shadows or reflections, an appearance reward constrains RGB changes in source-derived protected regions while exempting targets and estimated effects. Frozen HPSv3 comple
s905fef5ca7.summary: H3Remover applies reinforcement learning with depth and background-geometry rewards to a pretrained video editor for object removal without paired training data.

s9f83ba81af.title: Clover-35B-A3B-Preview Technical Report
s9f83ba81af.description: arXiv:2611.24636v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce Clover-35B-A3B-Preview (Clover), a mixture-of-experts diffusion language model with 35 billion total parameters and 3 billion activated parameters, supporting thinking-mode generation. Clover adapts Gated Delta Networks to block diffusion by combining recurrent memory of previously generated context with bidirectional softmax attention inside the current block. Historical memory readout competes with current-block tokens in a shared softmax, with learnable block-size calibration and a separate, zero-initialized right-context convolution branch. Clover leads the seven evaluated agent metrics, including 73.6 on SWE-bench Verified and 51.7 on Terminal-Bench 2.1. On internal agent workloads, it reaches a reported generation speed o
s9f83ba81af.summary: Clover-35B-A3B-Preview is a mixture-of-experts diffusion language model with 35B total and 3B active parameters, adapting Gated Delta Networks to block diffusion.
s9f83ba81af.why: A large MoE diffusion language model with thinking-mode generation is a new architecture option for teams tracking non-autoregressive LLMs.

s8baa13cd46.title: Hypnos: A Dual-Phase End-to-End Platform for Scalable Continual Learning at the Edge
s8baa13cd46.description: arXiv:2611.24637v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Continual learning (CL) enables neural networks to adapt to non-stationary data streams by mitigating catastrophic forgetting, offering a path to robust, private, and adaptable edge devices. Yet, porting CL to real-world edge devices remains challenging for two reasons: (i) online operation, where sensor data arrives one sample at a time and the device must adapt on-the-fly, and (ii) the low footprint of edge devices, which makes traditional error backpropagation training prohibitive. Inspired by the brain's wake and sleep cycles, the former for rapid adaptation with minimal resources and the latter for long-term consolidation, we introduce Hypnos, an open-source dual-phase platform for efficient CL at the edge. In the wake phase (e.g., dai
s8baa13cd46.summary: Hypnos is an end-to-end platform for continual learning on edge devices, inspired by wake and sleep cycles to handle online, one-sample-at-a-time data streams.
s8baa13cd46.why: Edge deployments needing on-device adaptation without full backpropagation could benefit from this platform design.

s63a765c367.title: Choosing the Right Representations: Task-Aware Fusion for Multimodal Materials Language Models
s63a765c367.description: arXiv:2611.24641v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal language models for materials science rely on effective mechanisms for incorporating three-dimensional structural representations. MatterChat addresses this challenge using a large bridge module between a pretrained structural encoder and the LLM, together with a separate contrastive alignment stage. We instead ask whether this bridge can adaptively select and combine representations from multiple structural encoders according to the target property. We find that supervised and generative material encoders provide complementary information for property prediction. We found that, for Zatom-1, this information is not concentrated in the final layer. Instead, the most informative representations occur at different depths depending o
s63a765c367.summary: Researchers propose adaptively selecting and combining representations from multiple structural encoders for materials science multimodal language models.

s44c5959210.title: Piccolo: Co-Evolving Decision Models and Data through Recursive Self-Improvement
s44c5959210.description: arXiv:2611.24651v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present Piccolo, a family of multimodal decision models (0.8B to 27B) that coevolves model capabilities and training data via Agentic Data Engineering and recursive self-improvement (RSI). The models predict probabilities over candidate answers for general-purpose text and visual judgments, agent harnesses, data workflows, and interactive games. Piccolo-27B tops the Decision Index Vision Full leaderboard with a score of 75.59, while Piccolo-9B and Piccolo-4B achieve 68.35 and 67.46, respectively. All three rank first on the Private benchmark in their respective model-size categories. Research agents analyze model behavior, construct training data, conduct experiments, and use the results to refine subsequent proposals. Semantic slices an
s44c5959210.summary: Piccolo is a family of multimodal decision models from 0.8B to 27B parameters that co-evolve with training data via agentic data engineering and recursive self-improvement.
s44c5959210.why: Piccolo-27B reports top placement on the Decision Index Vision Full leaderboard, a benchmark claim engineers may want to verify.

sc93a1a5d5f.title: When Does Continual Pre-Training Help? A Controlled Study of Dialectal Adaptation for Qu\'ebec French
sc93a1a5d5f.description: arXiv:2611.24699v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Continual pre-training (CPT) is widely used to adapt pretrained language models to dialectal and non-standard language varieties, yet it remains unclear when this additional training is necessary, what drives its benefits, and whether aggregate evaluation scores adequately capture its effects. In this paper, we present a controlled study of CPT for Qu\'ebec French language understanding across nine LLMs spanning different families and scales. Using a budget-matched protocol of 30M tokens per experiment, our results show that the benefit of CPT depends strongly on the starting model's existing competence in the target variety. When CPT is beneficial, the improvements are driven more by corpus composition than by data volume, with literary te
sc93a1a5d5f.summary: A controlled study tests when continual pre-training helps LLMs understand Québec French, across nine models with a budget-matched 30M-token protocol.
sc93a1a5d5f.why: It offers evidence on when domain or dialect adaptation pays off versus when aggregate benchmark scores may hide its real effects.

sbe670c0815.title: Openhagen Worlds: Calibrated Environments for Measuring and Training Scientific Discovery Agents
sbe670c0815.description: arXiv:2611.24711v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agents that do science must choose informative experiments and reason from their results, but most discovery benchmarks cannot separate that skill from recall, unstated scoring rules or shortcut policies. We introduce Openhagen Worlds, a suite of 27 procedurally generated environments (some with finite truth spaces), from classic puzzles of experimental reasoning to simulator-grounded physics and chemistry, in which an agent runs experiments under a budget and commits an answer that a deterministic verifier checks against a hidden truth. Every observation states the complete scoring rule, and each of the 178 difficulty levels is calibrated: it is admitted only if, on 64 development instances, a scripted oracle succeeds on at least 0.75, the
sbe670c0815.summary: Researchers introduce Openhagen Worlds, 27 procedurally generated environments for testing whether AI agents can run budgeted experiments and reach verified scientific answers.
sbe670c0815.why: It gives teams a benchmark that separates experimental reasoning from recall and shortcut policies when evaluating discovery agents.

sd34b042324.title: How Generative Models Generate: A Concise Guide to the Generative AI Landscape
sd34b042324.description: arXiv:2611.24728v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The rapidly expanding generative AI landscape brings together methods that differ in architecture, learning objective, mathematical representation and sampling procedure. A concise, selectively organised technical guide can provide an accessible starting point for developing a coherent understanding of this increasingly complex landscape. This article takes a generation-centred approach, connecting how models produce new observations with the modelling and learning principles that make generation possible. We develop a two-level perspective: first, distinguishing three recurring generation routes-direct transformation or decoding, sequential conditional construction, and iterative updating or transport; and second, examining the modelling a
sd34b042324.summary: A concise technical guide organizes the generative AI landscape around how different models produce new observations and how they sample.
sd34b042324.why: It provides a structured overview of generative model families, useful for engineers building a coherent mental map of the field.

sb009456a3f.title: Elysium: Simulation-Free Unbalanced Schr\"odinger Bridges
sb009456a3f.description: arXiv:2611.24763v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reconstructing cellular dynamics from snapshots is challenging because the destructive nature of single-cell measurements makes tracking the same cells over time impossible. Cellular dynamics are inherently stochastic and involve changes in population size through proliferation and apoptosis. Growth-based methods represent population change as a rate on the density, which does not assign exits and entries to individual cells. Unbalanced Schr\"odinger bridges model individual events, but neural solvers for killed diffusion bridges simulate trajectories during training. We introduce Elysium, a simulation-free solver that jointly learns state transition and mass change. Using a killed Brownian reference and its time reversal, Elysium construct
sb009456a3f.summary: Elysium proposes a simulation-free neural solver for unbalanced Schrödinger bridges to model cellular dynamics with proliferation and apoptosis.

s353a4bf506.title: Horizontal Flow Matching for Single-Cell Spatiotemporal Dynamics
s353a4bf506.description: arXiv:2611.24764v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Learning the spatiotemporal dynamics of cells from spatial transcriptomics requires connecting snapshots of different cells acquired in different coordinate frames. A rotation or translation of a section can appear as cell movement and distort the inferred correspondence. We introduce horizontal flow matching, which learns changes in tissue organization, molecular state, and cell abundance up to shared rigid motion. The dynamics follow a continuity--reaction equation whose action assigns no cost to shared rigid motion, and the resulting horizontal projector removes this component from spatial prediction errors during learning and from predicted velocities during generation. An equivalent endpoint problem jointly estimates correspondence and
s353a4bf506.summary: Horizontal flow matching is introduced to learn single-cell spatiotemporal dynamics from spatial transcriptomics while ignoring shared rigid motion between tissue sections.

s4b6b3ba92a.title: LLM-Guided Cyber-Physical Attack Path Identification in Smart Grids
s4b6b3ba92a.description: arXiv:2611.24765v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Identifying high-impact attack paths in cyber-physical power systems is critical for improving grid resilience. Existing methods typically rely on either structural topology analysis or simulation-based cascading-failure models. Topology-based approaches capture connectivity but lack adversarial reasoning, while simulation-driven methods are primarily suited for offline analysis and are less effective for rapid evaluation of evolving attack scenarios. As a result, identifying realistic attack paths that jointly capture topology, threat semantics, and physical impact remains challenging. This paper presents a physics-grounded framework for identifying cyber-physical attack paths using large language models (LLMs), with cascading-failure-deri
s4b6b3ba92a.summary: Researchers propose using an LLM to identify high-impact cyber-physical attack paths in smart grids by combining topology, threat semantics and simulation.
s4b6b3ba92a.why: Grid operators and security teams may find LLM-guided attack path analysis useful for faster evaluation of evolving threat scenarios.

s536b59031a.title: Counterfactual World Models: JEPAs That Reason About "What If"
s536b59031a.description: arXiv:2611.24778v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: World models operate in a world they cannot fully observe. When a hidden disturbance, such as a current pushing a boat, changes the outcome of an action, a counterfactual question follows: what would have happened under a different action, subject to the same disturbance? Its answer separates bad decisions from bad luck. We prove that world models trained on factual transitions cannot answer it on their own, whatever their data or capacity. For many physical systems, the observed outcome and a simple property of the dynamics suffice: natura non facit saltus, nature makes no leaps. When actions and disturbances act as separate forces, their interaction is second-order in time, so the counterfactual outcome is, to first order, the observed ou
s536b59031a.summary: The paper proves that world models trained only on factual transitions cannot answer counterfactual 'what if' questions alone, and proposes JEPA-based counterfactual models.

sa21dfc2cb7.title: Learning Trajectories Leave Decodable Traces in Neural Network Weight Space and Internal Representations
sa21dfc2cb7.description: arXiv:2611.24782v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Neural networks trained on the same task develop related weight-space structures, yet remain distinguishable after learning. Do these differences merely reflect alternative solutions, or do they preserve information about individual learning histories? We tested whether final weights reveal initialization, task order, and earlier trajectory states. Training reorganized the ensemble: initial pairwise distances did not consistently predict final distances. Nevertheless, all 30 trained networks were correctly matched to their initial weights among ten candidates per dataset. Networks sharing an initialization also developed recognizable final hidden representations across different batch schedules, although direct comparisons with initial acti
sa21dfc2cb7.summary: Experiments show that neural networks trained on the same task retain decodable traces of their initialization, task order, and training trajectory in their final weights.
sa21dfc2cb7.why: Training history leaves recoverable traces in weights, which matters for reproducibility, auditing and model provenance questions.

s6b0d5e5519.title: Isabelle Pool Server: a pooled verification service for prover training and multi-agent proving
s6b0d5e5519.description: arXiv:2611.24788v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Isabelle Pool Server (IPS), a verification service with a pool of warm headless Isabelle sessions behind an HTTP API, with session leasing and reclamation, memory-aware admission control, and a time budget on every call. Its verification interface spans single-step execution, block-level proof checking and whole-theory builds, with checkpoints for cheap branching and backtracking, and a build from scratch as the final arbiter. The service runs as a single container with monitoring and is accessible via a Python client, two MCP servers and a raw HTTP API. In our measurements IPS is level with PIDE MCP, a PIDE frontend for agents, at one worker and ahead of it at eight, at its commit of October 2026 (the tool is now PIDE AI). Once its session
s6b0d5e5519.summary: Isabelle Pool Server is a verification service offering pooled warm Isabelle sessions behind an HTTP API, with Python client and MCP servers.
s6b0d5e5519.why: Teams training provers or running multi-agent proof systems get a deployable verification backend with leasing, admission control and time budgets.

sebf13212d4.title: Bias-Only Training Dynamics in ReLU Networks
sebf13212d4.description: arXiv:2611.24797v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Neural networks with randomly initialized, fixed weights and trainable biases are universal approximators, yet the dynamics of bias-only training remain largely unexplored. We study these dynamics in one-hidden-layer ReLU networks through activation codes, the binary patterns of active neurons that partition the input space into convex polyhedral regions. We show that the gradients with respect to the biases depend on each input only through its activation code, and hence the training dynamics can be characterized with these codes. In particular, as long as the activation codes remain fixed, training reduces to a linear least-squares problem with the codes as features. Training can then be understood as a sequence of least-squares problems,
sebf13212d4.summary: The paper analyzes training dynamics when only biases are trained in one-hidden-layer ReLU networks with fixed random weights, via activation codes.

s9ab52b2eed.title: Soft Mixture of Quantum Experts for Hybrid Quantum-Classical Learning
s9ab52b2eed.description: arXiv:2611.24798v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) has attracted increasing interest as a possible route to construct feature representations that are difficult to reproduce with classical models. However, near-term QML architectures based on trainable parametrized quantum circuits remain affected by limited hardware resources, noise, and severe optimization difficulties such as barren plateaus. In this work we propose Soft-MoQE, a Soft Mixture of Quantum Experts architecture that replaces variational quantum training with the input-dependent selection and combination of fixed quantum feature maps. The model is composed of a heterogeneous pool of non-trainable quantum circuits, each defining a distinct embedding, and a classical gating network that learns how
s9ab52b2eed.summary: Soft-MoQE proposes a soft mixture of quantum experts that replaces variational quantum training with input-dependent expert selection for hybrid quantum-classical learning.

s2e1c13d31b.title: LAaDT-DSS: decision support for non-experts on rooftop PV, incentive and grid simulations under Turkish tariff rules
s2e1c13d31b.description: arXiv:2611.24810v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rooftop photovoltaics raise three questions: should a household invest, which incentive costs the state least, and does the feeder stay within limits? Those who ask are rarely modellers. We present LAaDT-DSS, decision-support software that answers all three under Turkish tariff rules from one simulation core. Non-experts reach it by clicking a house on a 3D map or by asking in plain words; a language model is asked to call the simulation tools, not to compute. Each entry of its 125-entry parameter registry is marked as sourced or estimated. Case studies test the system. Its PV yield lies within $\pm$3.6% of two independent tools at equal losses. Across 2,048 draws of its estimated inputs, the answer for PV alone held in all but one; with a
s2e1c13d31b.summary: LAaDT-DSS is decision-support software that simulates rooftop PV investment, incentives and grid limits under Turkish tariff rules, with a language model calling simulation tools.
s2e1c13d31b.why: It shows a pattern for LLM-driven tools where the model routes requests to deterministic simulation rather than computing results itself.

se9b4f62a38.title: A Foundation Model to Measure and Predict Human Behaviour
se9b4f62a38.description: arXiv:2611.24830v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to infer psychological attributes, predict individual behaviour, and simulate human populations. However, despite generating plausible responses, they often misrepresent individuals and distort population statistics. Here we introduce Chiron, a foundation model to measure and predict human behaviour. We jointly fine-tune an LLM to represent psychological constructs, predict individual behaviour, and align population response distributions with human statistics. The training and evaluation data span 36 behavioural domains and 78 social science experiments, comprising 288,307 person records, 1,411,750 atomic behavioural decisions, and 99,953 psychometric assessments over 109 psychological con
se9b4f62a38.summary: Chiron is a foundation model fine-tuned to represent psychological constructs, predict individual behaviour, and align response distributions with human population statistics.

s1238ab8364.title: Does the Action Matter? Probing Action-Conditioned Semantic Forecasting as a World Model for Autonomous Driving
s1238ab8364.description: arXiv:2611.24840v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: World models are increasingly used in autonomous driving to predict how a scene evolves under the ego vehicle's actions, supporting counterfactual reasoning and model-based planning. However, existing evaluations focus on prediction fidelity and planning performance, and rarely verify that the predictions depend on the conditioning action. In this paper, we study action dependence in action-conditioned semantic forecasting, which predicts future semantic segmentation from past segmentations and the ego action. We compare a forecaster with feature-wise and input-level action conditioning against an identical model without action input, and measure action dependence with test-time action interventions scored by standard segmentation metrics.
s1238ab8364.summary: The paper probes whether action-conditioned semantic forecasting for autonomous driving actually depends on the ego vehicle's action, not just prediction fidelity.
s1238ab8364.why: World models used for driving planning may ignore the conditioning action, so teams should verify action dependence, not only forecast accuracy.

s2baf47cd69.title: Who are you? The Personal Imitation Game
s2baf47cd69.description: arXiv:2611.24888v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) now perform strongly on Alan Turing's 1950 Imitation Game, so we propose a harder challenge, the Personal Imitation Game, which asks whether a machine can replicate a specific individual in conversation rather than a generic human. Testing with 30 participants, we establish a human baseline and report the identity signals interrogators rely on: stylometric features, personality traits, and biographical facts. To demonstrate the framework, we design an LLM-based system that plays the game for one of the paper's authors, drawing on an autoethnographic dataset spanning ten years of personal digital communication. In a 20-person deception study, interrogators choose our system over the author's own friends in 7 of 1
s2baf47cd69.summary: The Personal Imitation Game proposes testing whether an LLM can replicate a specific individual in conversation, with a 30-participant human baseline.

sb034d9ec96.title: Agentic Harness Engineering Beta: Requirement-Centered Evolution of Agent Harnesses
sb034d9ec96.description: arXiv:2611.24924v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Real-world harness engineering is driven by explicit and implicit user requirements, which guide development and validation. However, existing harness evolution methods often overlook implicit requirements and interaction needs, while using a single evolution agent to modify the harness and benchmark scores to select changes. This process often produces narrow patches and leads to benchmark-specific local optima. We introduce Agentic Harness Engineering Beta (AHE-Beta), a requirement-centered loop that brings real-world engineering practices into harness evolution. The loop consists of three steps: (1) User-driven evaluation lets simulated users raise their requirements as issues while they work with the harness over multiple turns. (2) Tea
sb034d9ec96.summary: Researchers introduce AHE-Beta, a requirement-centered loop for evolving agent harnesses that targets implicit user requirements and interaction needs.
sb034d9ec96.why: It suggests harness improvements driven by requirements rather than benchmark scores alone, which may reduce narrow patches and benchmark-specific overfitting.

s6c63640809.title: Mapping the AI Supply Chain: Dependencies, Vulnerabilities, and Market Concentration in the AI Ecosystem
s6c63640809.description: arXiv:2611.24927v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI systems are built across many organizations that contribute models, data, compute, capital, talent, and other assets. While the layers of the AI stack are relatively well understood, the relationships between actors and components across layers remains sparsely documented. In this work, we focus on the organizations that make up the AI supply chain: the complex network of actors that contribute to the development and deployment of AI. We motivate the examination of the organizational AI supply chain---highlighting concerns about concentration, power, chokepoints, cascading failures, fragmented accountability, and risk---then describe our pipeline for mapping the AI supply chain. Our pipeline yields our main contribution: a multilayered,
s6c63640809.summary: A paper maps the organizational AI supply chain, examining dependencies, vulnerabilities, and market concentration across the actors that build and deploy AI.
s6c63640809.why: Understanding supplier dependencies and concentration risks helps leaders assess vendor lock-in and single points of failure in AI stacks.

s6b7ca1cf50.title: Human-AI Interactions and Societal Pitfalls
s6b7ca1cf50.description: arXiv:2309.10448v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: When working with generative artificial intelligence (AI), users may see productivity gains, but the AI-generated content may not match their preferences exactly. To study this effect, we introduce a Bayesian framework in which heterogeneous users choose how much information to share with the AI, facing a trade-off between output fidelity and communication cost. We show that the interplay between these individual-level decisions and AI training may lead to societal challenges. Outputs may become more homogenized, especially when the AI is trained on AI-generated content, potentially triggering a homogenization death spiral. And any AI bias may propagate to become societal bias. A solution to the homogenization and bias issues is to reduce
s6b7ca1cf50.summary: A Bayesian study models how users decide how much information to share with generative AI, finding individual choices and AI training can homogenize outputs.

sebf30649c3.title: Games played by Exponential Weights Algorithms
sebf30649c3.description: arXiv:2407.06676v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper studies the last-iterate convergence properties of the exponential weights algorithm with constant learning rates. We consider a repeated interaction in discrete time, where each player uses an exponential weights algorithm characterized by an initial mixed action and a fixed learning rate, so that the mixed action profile $p^t$ played at stage $t$ follows an homogeneous Markov chain. At first, we show that whenever a strict Nash equilibrium exists, the probability to play a strict Nash equilibrium at the next stage converges almost surely to 0 or 1. Secondly, we show that the limit of $p^t$, whenever it exists, belongs to the set of ``Nash Equilibria with Equalizing Payoffs''. Thirdly, we show that in strong coordination games
sebf30649c3.summary: A paper analyzes last-iterate convergence of exponential weights learning in repeated games, showing behavior near strict Nash equilibria.

s69b9207735.title: A Survey on Collaborative Mechanisms Between Large and Small Language Models
s69b9207735.description: arXiv:2505.07460v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) deliver powerful AI capabilities but face deployment challenges due to high resource costs and latency, whereas Small Language Models (SLMs) offer efficiency and deployability at the cost of reduced performance. Collaboration between LLMs and SLMs emerges as a crucial paradigm to synergistically balance these trade-offs, enabling advanced AI applications, especially on resource-constrained edge devices. This survey provides a comprehensive overview of LLM-SLM collaboration, detailing various interaction mechanisms (pipeline, routing, auxiliary, distillation, fusion), key enabling technologies, and diverse application scenarios driven by on-device needs like low latency, privacy, personalization, and offline op
s69b9207735.summary: A survey reviews collaboration mechanisms between large and small language models to balance cost, latency, and performance, especially on edge devices.
s69b9207735.why: Hybrid LLM-SLM architectures offer a way to cut serving cost and latency while keeping capability, relevant to deployment planning.

sb51f3d989d.title: MARBLE: An Agentic Benchmark for Spatial Reasoning and Visual Abstraction
sb51f3d989d.description: arXiv:2506.22992v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A central challenge for multimodal language models (MLLMs) in real-world tasks is to abstract visual observations into structured spatial states and reason over how those states change under actions over long horizons. Existing multimodal benchmarks often focus on static question answering, where answers can be directly extracted from images, or assume symbolic states are available and bypass the visual-to-spatial abstraction process. We present MARBLE, a diagnostic benchmark for spatially grounded multimodal reasoning and planning across three agent environments: CUBE, MAZE, and BLOX. MARBLE spans 2D and 3D spatial puzzles under geometric constraints, dynamic layouts, and spatial transformations, with difficulty systematically controlled
sb51f3d989d.summary: MARBLE is a diagnostic benchmark testing multimodal models on turning visual observations into spatial states and planning actions over long horizons.
sb51f3d989d.why: It exposes gaps in visual-to-spatial reasoning for agentic multimodal systems, useful when evaluating models for planning tasks.

s01f33b8cec.title: CXReasonAgent: Evidence-Grounded Diagnostic Reasoning Agent for Chest X-rays
s01f33b8cec.description: arXiv:2602.23276v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Chest X-ray plays a central role in thoracic diagnosis, and its interpretation inherently requires multi-step, evidence-grounded reasoning. However, large vision-language models (LVLMs) often generate plausible responses that are not faithfully grounded in diagnostic evidence and provide limited visual evidence for verification, while also requiring costly retraining to support new diagnostic tasks, limiting their reliability and adaptability in clinical settings. To address these limitations, we present CXReasonAgent, a diagnostic agent that integrates a large language model (LLM) with clinically grounded diagnostic tools to perform evidence-grounded diagnostic reasoning using image-derived diagnostic and visual evidence. To evaluate the
s01f33b8cec.summary: CXReasonAgent is a diagnostic agent for chest X-rays that grounds reasoning in visual evidence and supports new tasks without retraining.
s01f33b8cec.why: Evidence-grounded agents that adapt without retraining offer a design pattern for high-stakes domains where verifiability matters.

se5e037ab84.title: Prior Knowledge or Search? A Study of LLM Agents in Hardware-Aware Code Optimization
se5e037ab84.description: arXiv:2605.19782v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: LLM discovery and optimization systems are increasingly applied across domains, implementing a common propose-evaluate-revise loop. Such optimization or discovery progresses via context conditioning on received feedback from an environment. However, as modern LLM agents are increasingly complex in their structure, it is difficult to evaluate which components contribute the most, and when and how this exploration may fail. We answer these questions through three controlled experiments. Our findings: (1) In pure black-box optimization, LLMs act as greedy optimizers. (2) In zero-shot kernel generation, providing explicit input-size information has no measurable effect, models converge to the same kernel parameters regardless of size or tempe
se5e037ab84.summary: A study of LLM agents in hardware-aware code optimization examines when agents rely on prior knowledge versus search in propose-evaluate-revise loops.
se5e037ab84.why: Findings on when agent loops fail help engineers decide how much to invest in search versus prompting for code optimization.

sa282a94074.title: CaMBRAIN: Real-time, Continuous EEG Inference with Causal State Space Models
sa282a94074.description: arXiv:2605.28792v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is a critical, non-invasive method to monitor electrical brain activity. EEGs can span anywhere from a couple seconds to multiple hours, posing a major hurdle for existing deep learning methods due to two major factors: (1) existing EEG models are predominantly built upon the attention mechanism, incurring quadratic scaling as the sequence length increases, and (2) raw EEG signals must be processed in a sliding-window fashion due to fixed-length input requirements, preventing global understanding of the entire signal. To this extent, we propose CaMBRAIN - the first Causal, Mamba-based state space model (SSM) capable of real-time inference of EEG signals, arguing that bidirectional approaches are needlessly exp
sa282a94074.summary: CaMBRAIN uses causal state space models for real-time, continuous EEG inference, avoiding attention's quadratic scaling and sliding-window processing.

s9cd2892acc.title: Arbor: How Search Policy Shapes Agent Behavior in System Optimization
s9cd2892acc.description: arXiv:2606.12563v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Achieving peak performance on modern accelerators requires coordinated optimization across kernels, operator fusion, KV-cache management, quantization, scheduling, and communication overlap, a process that demands weeks of expert effort per model and hardware platform. We present Arbor, a system that gives autonomous agents an explicit optimization tree to reason over, backtrack through, and deepen with experience, with pluggable search policies, scored bandit traversal, parallel agent swarms, and depth-first sweep, sharing a common harness of containerized isolation, automatic rollback, and end-to-end validation. Arbor generalizes across domains: +40% to +193% on six production inference models across two GPU generations, +42.8% on LLM t
s9cd2892acc.summary: Arbor gives autonomous agents an optimization tree and pluggable search policies to tune kernels, fusion, KV-cache, quantization, and scheduling on accelerators.
s9cd2892acc.why: Agent-driven system tuning could cut weeks of expert effort per model and hardware platform, relevant to inference performance work.

sa5927d8049.title: GA-VINO: A Geometry-Aware Variational Physics-informed Neural Operator for Mindlin-Reissner Plates
sa5927d8049.description: arXiv:2606.16624v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Plate and shell structures are widely used in engineering fields. Rapid response prediction for such structures under complex geometries, heterogeneous materials, and varying loads is important for engineering design, but conventional numerical methods usually require repeated modeling and solution when the physical configuration changes. To address this issue, this study proposes a geometry-aware variational physics-informed neural operator (GA-VINO) for Mindlin-Reissner plates. GA-VINO represents the plate geometry using boundary point clouds and incorporates a material encoder, a load encoder, and a scalar-parameter branch to handle spatially random material fields, spatially varying pressure loads, and sample-level uniform parameters.
sa5927d8049.summary: GA-VINO is a geometry-aware physics-informed neural operator that predicts responses of Mindlin-Reissner plates across geometries, materials, and loads.

sb4a828e21b.title: When Does Learning to Stop Help? Configuring Risk-Controlled Early Exit for Reasoning-Model Services
sb4a828e21b.description: arXiv:2606.30852v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Early exit lowers the cost of serving a reasoning model by stopping its reasoning once a provisional answer looks final. An operator must choose between a learned stopping rule and one static token budget, and savings against full reasoning do not settle the choice. We present a procedure that decides on calibration data from the workload. It certifies both families with Learn-then-Test to one bound on the fraction of all questions that full reasoning answers correctly but early exit does not, prices provisional answers as the serving stack does, and deploys the cheapest certified candidate. Across four models and five benchmarks neither family is better throughout. At a 5% risk target the learned rule saves 10.4-17.0 percentage points mo
sb4a828e21b.summary: A procedure uses calibration data and Learn-then-Test to decide between learned stopping rules and static token budgets for early exit in reasoning-model serving.
sb4a828e21b.why: Operators serving reasoning models can use it to pick early-exit settings while bounding accuracy loss versus full reasoning.

sb0aee9977a.title: ElephantAgent: Contextual State Continuity in Agentic Systems
sb0aee9977a.description: arXiv:2607.01919v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Agentic systems enhance their capabilities by invoking external tools and maintaining persistent memory. However, recent tool and memory poisoning attacks can covertly bias agent behavior. We observe that such attacks mounted out of band share a single enabler: each succeeds only by presenting the agent with a contextual state (e.g., tool state and memory) that is not the latest faithfully evolved one. This observation suggests that a continuity check over the contextual state covers this family of attacks. We present ElephantAgent, a protocol that enforces Contextual State Continuity over the bounded, security-critical subset of the agent's context. Before each planning-and-execution cycle, ElephantAgent recomputes the digest of the loca
sb0aee9977a.summary: ElephantAgent proposes a continuity check over agent contextual state, such as tool state and memory, to detect tool and memory poisoning attacks.
sb0aee9977a.why: Agents with persistent memory and tools face covert poisoning risks, and state continuity checks offer a defense to evaluate.

s47be521c05.title: AgentAbstain: Do LLM Agents Know When Not to Act?
s47be521c05.description: arXiv:2607.10059v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Agent systems based on large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed for autonomous tasks, yet existing evaluations mostly focus on task success rather than whether agents know when to abstain. This gap poses real risks: under ambiguity, conflicting constraints, or tool failures, agents may execute unintended and irreversible actions. To close this gap, we present the first systematic evaluation framework for agentic abstention: the calibrated ability of tool-using LLM agents to recognize when not to act. At its core, AgentAbstain is a paired-task benchmark built on an agent-native taxonomy of 8 abstention scenarios across pre-execution reasoning and runtime discovery. It contains 263 paired tasks across 42 executable sandbox env
s47be521c05.summary: AgentAbstain introduces an evaluation framework measuring whether tool-using LLM agents can recognize when not to act under ambiguity or tool failures.
s47be521c05.why: Irreversible actions by agents under uncertainty are a deployment risk, and abstention metrics add a check beyond task success.

s2c6f16586e.title: Bringing Back Rule Induction to Fluid Intelligence Research? An Initial Validation of the ARC-AGI Benchmark in Humans
s2c6f16586e.description: arXiv:2607.11263v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Two competing perspectives on fluid intelligence (gf) measures propose that performance is primarily constrained either by working memory capacity or by the ability to induce novel relations. The first perspective is currently dominant in measurement, as evident from the use of a limited set of recurring rules, whereas the second perspective is reflected in many definitions but rarely present in measurement. The ARC-AGI benchmark predominantly requires rule induction and was proposed as a measure of gf for both humans and artificial systems. However, its psychometric properties have not yet been examined in human samples. We therefore investigated the psychometric characteristics and nomological network of ARC-AGI in a first study with 10
s2c6f16586e.summary: A human validation study examines whether the ARC-AGI benchmark measures rule induction as a fluid intelligence construct, versus working memory capacity.

sb9b4050c5d.title: Disagreement-Guided Agentic Data Curation for Multimodal Safety
sb9b4050c5d.description: arXiv:2607.14256v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Written safety policies in multimodal settings define categories whose visual boundaries span many contexts. We study disagreement as a signal for identifying useful synthetic boundary cases. Our pipeline generates policy-conditioned images, selects cases with target--rater or inter-rater disagreement, conditionally escalates unresolved cases, and retrieves the resulting rater-labeled examples as in-context demonstrations. On a failure-enriched multimodal safety benchmark, policy grounding reduces false negative rate (FNR) from 0.875 to 0.413 and raises F1 from 0.220 to 0.731; retrieval from 50 disagreement-selected examples further reduces FNR to 0.245, compared with 0.297 from a 350-example Regular pool. The selected memory also improve
sb9b4050c5d.summary: Researchers propose an agentic pipeline that uses rater disagreement to curate synthetic multimodal safety examples, cutting false negative rate from 0.875 to 0.413 on a benchmark.
sb9b4050c5d.why: Shows disagreement-driven synthetic data curation can substantially improve multimodal safety classifiers, a practical approach for teams building content moderation.

s5efff43e03.title: Making Mathematical Knowledge Explainable, Accessible and Interoperable Through Large Language Model Integration
s5efff43e03.description: arXiv:2607.24512v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Mathematical models are central to formalizing research problems, yet their documentation often falls short of FAIR principles. Knowledge bases such as the Mathematical Model Database (MathModDB) address this gap by providing curated, semantically rich representations of mathematical models. Built on Wikibase, the same open-source infrastructure underlying Wikidata, MathModDB utilizes Semantic Web technologies to support Linked Open Data, collaborative editing, and the storage of semantically enriched metadata, making it a domain-specific knowledge graph within the broader Wikidata ecosystem. However, access to MathModDB currently requires either navigating a complex web interface or proficiency in SPARQL and Wikibase APIs, posing signifi
s5efff43e03.summary: A paper describes integrating large language models with MathModDB, a Wikibase-based knowledge base, to make mathematical models more FAIR, explainable and interoperable.

s1b0a6850e4.title: CoNav-UAV: Cooperative Dual-Altitude Aerial Navigation via Stackelberg Learning
s1b0a6850e4.description: arXiv:2608.01802v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Aerial search missions often require an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) to locate a target from only a brief description of its appearance and surroundings, a task known as target-oriented aerial vision-and-language navigation (VLN). The task demands city-scale exploration and grounding as well as collision-free close-range approach, two interleaved processes that are difficult to reconcile within a single agent. Most existing methods adapt the ground VLN paradigm to a single UAV and rely on external assistance to compensate for its inefficiency. A recent attempt deploys two UAVs at complementary altitudes but still depends on privileged sensing and trains the two agents independently, precluding any mutual adaptation. We propose CoNav-UAV,
s1b0a6850e4.summary: CoNav-UAV proposes a Stackelberg learning approach using two cooperating UAVs at different altitudes for target-oriented aerial vision-and-language navigation.
s1b0a6850e4.why: Offers a multi-agent design pattern for splitting city-scale search and close-range approach across cooperating agents.

s44fadcd629.title: JUDOR: CTDE-Based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for the Co-Optimization of Joint UAV Motion and Decentralized Opportunistic Routing in Delay-Tolerant Network
s44fadcd629.description: arXiv:2608.04590v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The growing deployment of delay-tolerant networks (DTNs) has made store-carry-forward (SCF) communication indispensable for operating under sparse intermittent connectivity. However, intermittent contact opportunities, finite node buffers, and limited message time-to-live (TTL) degrade message delivery performance and induce network congestion. Yet unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), with extended radio coverage and controllable trajectories, can bridge ground-node pairs that would otherwise suffer poor connectivity. Nevertheless, conventional routing schemes decouple UAV motion control from message replication, and consequently fail to leverage UAV mobility to proactively create future contact opportunities. This paper presents JUDOR (Joint
s44fadcd629.summary: JUDOR applies CTDE-based multi-agent reinforcement learning to jointly optimize UAV motion and opportunistic routing in delay-tolerant networks.

s092b1aae65.title: Beyond Routing Weights: Faithful Response-Level Interpretation of Mixture-of-Experts Reward Models via Contribution Contrast
s092b1aae65.description: arXiv:2608.06400v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Reward models are central to learning from human preferences, yet identifying what drives their predictions remains challenging. Recent sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) reward models seek to improve interpretability by routing prompts to specialized experts and characterizing experts through examples with high routing weights. However, routing weights only reveal which prompts an expert $\textit{receives}$, not how it $\textit{judges}$ responses, providing only a partial account of expert behavior. We therefore propose $\textbf{Co}$ntribution-$\textbf{Co}$ntrast ($\textbf{CoCo}$) response-level interpretation, which faithfully characterizes experts' roles using chosen-rejected response pairs with the largest contribution contrasts, jointly
s092b1aae65.summary: A paper proposes Contribution-Contrast, a method to interpret how mixture-of-experts reward models judge responses, going beyond routing weights.
s092b1aae65.why: Better interpretability of reward models can help teams audit what drives preference-tuned model behavior.

sb53464610b.title: Linearized 2-Simplicial Attention
sb53464610b.description: arXiv:2608.09307v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a linearized form of 2-simplicial attention by rewriting the trilinear score as an inner product between a composite query and a key, so that the sum over keys takes the same form as ordinary softmax attention. We then approximate this sum with positive random features and store all previous keys in a fixed-size state, while the sum over second keys stays exact over all previous tokens. This reduces the cost from cubic to quadratic in sequence length, and both keys range over all previous tokens, which windowed 2-simplicial attention does not allow. We implement it with custom Triton kernels and combine it with Kimi Delta Attention to build a model with no softmax attention at all. With 15B equal training tokens on FineWeb-Edu,
sb53464610b.summary: Researchers present a linearized form of 2-simplicial attention that uses positive random features to reduce cost from cubic to quadratic in sequence length.
sb53464610b.why: Reducing attention cost from cubic to quadratic could make more expressive attention variants practical for long-sequence models.

s893706b691.title: Meta$^n$: Recursive Self-Improvement through Emergent Depth
s893706b691.description: arXiv:2608.24735v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Self-improving LLM agents refine answers, not the process that produces those answers. Systems that add a meta-level hold that level fixed, and those that edit themselves must leave part of their own editing machinery untouched to stay stable, capping the meta-depth they realize at roughly two. We present Meta$^n$, which keeps the meta-operation fixed and recurses on its input instead. That operation, $\Omega$, is applied repeatedly to its own products, reading the traces of the solver stack below together with the code that produced them, then writing the next layer as a strategic pre-process and a library of callable helpers. Because $\Omega$ never changes, it cannot destabilize the system, and because its input strictly grows, each lay
s893706b691.summary: Meta^n proposes a recursive self-improvement framework where a fixed meta-operation is applied repeatedly to its own outputs, rather than capping meta-depth at about two.

s0660ab1e9c.title: MAP: A Benchmark on Multimodal Accessibility Planning for Real World Places
s0660ab1e9c.description: arXiv:2608.28384v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce MAP, the first benchmark to evaluate multimodal AI systems as assistants for users with accessibility requirements when planning visits to places in the real world. In our evaluation, systems are presented with requests to verify or recommend a point of interest meeting an accessibility requirement. MAP contains two novel assessments: Claim verification for accessibility planning assesses if information on places and stated accessibility features is supported and identifies places that satisfy requested accessibility features. Visual evidence retrieval for accessibility planning checks if a multimodal AI system can select visual evidence for the requested place and accessibility feature. Our methodology supports comparison of
s0660ab1e9c.summary: MAP is a benchmark testing multimodal AI assistants on planning real-world place visits that meet users' accessibility requirements.
s0660ab1e9c.why: Highlights gaps in how well multimodal assistants verify accessibility claims, relevant to teams building location or travel assistants.

s57ceb4866e.title: Bad Genius: Counterfactual-Guided Harness Evolution Beyond Task-Specific Shortcuts
s57ceb4866e.description: arXiv:2609.18366v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An optimized agent harness can improve on held-out tasks by relying on formatting conventions that those tasks share with the rest of the benchmark. We introduce Counterfactual Harness Search and Evolution (CHASE) to test whether harness improvements survive changes to the evaluation protocol. A Proposer edits the harness around a fixed foundation model. A Challenger then searches for a protocol change that preserves the tasks but reduces the updated harness's gain over the initial harness. Executable checks test whether the transformation preserves task semantics. If the gain loss is confirmed on held-out tasks, CHASE adds the transformation to an archive that constrains subsequent harness updates. We give conditions under which this fin
s57ceb4866e.summary: CHASE proposes counterfactual search over evaluation protocols to test whether agent harness gains survive changes to the benchmark, rather than relying on shared formatting shortcuts.
s57ceb4866e.why: Suggests agent benchmark gains may reflect formatting shortcuts, so teams should stress-test harness improvements under protocol changes.

sd42233a24b.title: RiskWorld: Risk-Aware World Modeling with Flow-Guided Occupancy Evolution for Selective Trajectory Planning in Automated Driving
sd42233a24b.description: arXiv:2609.18442v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Safe motion planning in automated driving requires anticipating evolving traffic risks and deciding when to revise the current planned trajectory. We introduce RiskWorld, a risk-aware world modeling framework for shared occupancy forecasting and selective trajectory replacement. Spatial risk fields and temporal actor context are fused with visual bird's-eye-view features. Flow-guided evolution transports occupancy and scene features, while signed residuals correct occupancy after transport. One forecast is generated per planning step and reused across candidates. Each candidate is compared with a current-state persistence reference, yielding a nonnegative collision-score correction. The trajectory selected by current-world evaluation serv
sd42233a24b.summary: RiskWorld is a risk-aware world-modeling framework that forecasts shared occupancy and selectively replaces planned trajectories for automated driving.

s1e3f192daf.title: WorkWorlds: Evaluating Agents in a Company Built Before the Task
s1e3f192daf.description: arXiv:2609.23806v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Many knowledge work benchmarks are built around single tasks, where the context and files for each task are selected concurrently or after task definition. Research has argued that this construction method does not reflect real workplace work, yet the impact has never been measured under controlled conditions. To compare the two constructions under controlled conditions, we introduce WorkWorlds, an infrastructure that modularizes company components into revision, date, and employee seat to be separately adjusted. Using historical data donated by a real company, we reconstructed a pharmaceutical company, PharmaCo. Two experts with over ten years of industry experience each wrote eight tasks based on real events that occurred at the company
s1e3f192daf.summary: WorkWorlds is an evaluation infrastructure that builds company contexts before tasks, and it compares this against single-task benchmark construction for knowledge-work agents.
s1e3f192daf.why: Indicates single-task agent benchmarks may not reflect real workplace conditions, which matters when evaluating enterprise agents.

s3268b93121.title: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy response prediction using pretreatment diffusion and contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging with clinical variables
s3268b93121.description: arXiv:2609.26105v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Prediction of pathological complete response before neoadjuvant chemotherapy may facilitate more tailored therapeutic planning for breast cancer patients. This work proposes a deep-learning model for pretreatment data only, combining apparent diffusion coefficient maps, dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging, and clinical variables. The study uses the public ACRIN 6698/I-SPY2 multicenter dataset. The architecture employs EfficientNet-B0 pretrained encoders for image feature extraction and late fusion with clinical information. Multiple clinical variables were evaluated, including age, race, histological type, HR/HER2 subtype, SBR grade, and maximum diameter. Only HR/HER2 subtype improved the average area under the receiver o
s3268b93121.summary: Researchers propose a deep-learning model combining pretreatment diffusion and contrast-enhanced MRI with clinical variables to predict pathological complete response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy in breast cancer.

s88b3e0f24f.title: Cost-Efficient LLM Evaluation: A Framework for Narrow Confidence Intervals Under Fixed Budgets
s88b3e0f24f.description: arXiv:2609.29140v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) play an increasingly important role in both academic research and industry. Reliable evaluation helps researchers understand model capabilities and assess progress during model development. However, evaluation can be costly, and researchers often need to assess performance within a fixed budget. Because model outputs can vary across runs, this budget must be allocated between testing different tasks and repeating selected tasks. A confidence interval quantifies the uncertainty in the resulting performance estimate. Obtaining narrower intervals at the same confidence level and evaluation cost provides a more precise assessment of model performance, helping researchers draw clearer conclusions from limited obser
s88b3e0f24f.summary: A paper presents a framework for allocating a fixed evaluation budget between tasks and repeated runs to produce narrow confidence intervals for LLM performance.
s88b3e0f24f.why: Gives practical guidance for budgeting LLM evaluations, helping teams get reliable scores without excess compute spend.

s883b6b3236.title: What Does a Harness Buy? Tokens, Mostly
s883b6b3236.description: arXiv:2610.04433v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A coding agent is a language model inside a harness: the system prompt, the tools, and the context management that let a chat model work in a repository. Most of the engineering on these agents goes into the harness, and vendors and leaderboards credit it with score gains. Earlier studies have fixed the model and swapped the harness, but have not measured whether the swap changes the pass rate more than running the same harness again. We run seven models through three production harnesses, Claude Code, mini-SWE-agent, and OpenCode, on SWE-bench Verified and two benchmarks of other kinds, and rerun them unchanged. No harness leads consistently across models. Where the data can bound the difference between two harnesses, the bound is 2 to 5
s883b6b3236.summary: A study runs seven models through three production coding-agent harnesses on SWE-bench and measures how much harness choice versus repeated runs changes pass rates.
s883b6b3236.why: Suggests harness engineering may matter less than vendors claim, so teams should check whether score gains exceed run-to-run variance.

s47508245c8.title: CADFather: Autonomous CAD Reconstruction through Coordinated Tool Use
s47508245c8.description: arXiv:2610.09127v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Reconstructing an editable CAD model from a 3D shape remains a challenging engineering task. Existing methods can propose CAD operations, but no single source of proposals works equally well across different part geometries and stages of reconstruction. We introduce CADFather, an autonomous agentic system that coordinates complementary tools to recover parametric CAD programs from 3D meshes. A vision-language assistant inspects renders of the target and intermediate reconstructions, then decides which candidate CAD programs to extend, which tools to invoke, how many proposals to generate, and when to finish. Learned and algorithmic tools propose CAD operations, while numerical optimization refines the parameters of existing programs. Prop
s47508245c8.summary: CADFather is an agentic system that coordinates multiple tools and a vision-language assistant to reconstruct editable parametric CAD programs from 3D meshes.

s21b8c16a7b.title: MemeLogos: Knowledge-Driven Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning for Harmful Meme Detection
s21b8c16a7b.description: arXiv:2610.15463v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: With the rapid proliferation of social media, harmful memes have become a growing threat to online ecosystems. Their harmfulness is often implicitly conveyed through complex interactions among visual, textual, and contextual cues, making accurate detection challenging. Recent studies have introduced Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and external knowledge into harmful meme detection. However, existing methods mainly retrieve similar instances or auxiliary information, limiting their ability to capture reusable harmfulness knowledge and underlying reasoning mechanisms, and thus constraining both detection performance and interpretability. To address these challenges, we propose MemeLogos, a knowledge-driven retrieval-augmented reasoning
s21b8c16a7b.summary: MemeLogos, a knowledge-driven retrieval-augmented reasoning method, is proposed for detecting harmful memes by capturing reusable harmfulness knowledge.
s21b8c16a7b.why: Shows how retrieval of reusable domain knowledge, not just similar instances, may improve multimodal content moderation systems.

s7f56ab6256.title: Toward Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Enterprise Retail Workflows over Heterogeneous Data Sources
s7f56ab6256.description: arXiv:2610.25096v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Enterprise retail workflows require agents to chain evidence across heterogeneous sources, from structured product and order records to unstructured inquiries and reviews, yet existing agentic RAG benchmarks rarely capture this challenge. To enable controlled evaluation of such workflows, we introduce RetailBridge, a compositional retail benchmark built from persona-driven simulations. Its questions are constructed by linking entities and intermediate answers across heterogeneous sources, requiring agents to identify the relevant sources, carry evidence between them, and produce a grounded answer. To systematically evaluate LLMs on these retail workflows, we develop RetailRAG, a retail-aware framework equipped with auto-schema briefing, s
s7f56ab6256.summary: RetailBridge, a compositional benchmark built from persona-driven simulations, is introduced to evaluate agentic RAG across heterogeneous enterprise retail data sources.
s7f56ab6256.why: Gives teams a controlled way to test whether agents can chain evidence across structured and unstructured enterprise retail data.

sf8a9ca9868.title: ProteinGeoBench: Frontier Structural-Biology Agents Are Fluent at Lookup but Lost in Geometry
sf8a9ca9868.description: arXiv:2610.26829v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: ProteinGeoBench is a set of 131 tasks that give an agent protein structure files and ask it to look up recorded facts, check sequences, calculate geometry from atom coordinates or reason about structures. We ran four frontier models on every task several times (4,249 runs) and 26 models on a subset. A single overall score hides two different skills. Three of the four frontier models are best at looking up facts and worst at calculating from coordinates: Claude Opus 5 scores 0.907 on lookup and 0.716 on calculation. Gemini 3.1 Pro is the exception. Geometry is overrepresented among the hardest tasks. Half of the twelve tasks that all four models fail are calculations, although calculations are a fifth of the suite, and eight of the twelve
sf8a9ca9868.summary: ProteinGeoBench, a 131-task benchmark, finds frontier models strong at looking up protein structure facts but weaker at calculating geometry from atom coordinates.
sf8a9ca9868.why: Highlights that agent benchmark scores can hide large gaps between skills, so teams should evaluate tasks separately.

s0e9d0f602a.title: DataPraxis: Scaling Analytics Tasks via Verified Workspace Evolution
s0e9d0f602a.description: arXiv:2610.26924v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: General-purpose agents are increasingly expected to perform professional analytics work, which requires sustained reasoning, iterative investigation, and reliable evidence. Training these capabilities requires diverse and challenging tasks. However, generating tasks directly from raw data often overlooks deeper questions that emerge through analysis and provides limited evidence for verification. To address these limitations, we introduce DataPraxis, an analytics task synthesis framework based on verified workspace evolution. The framework progressively enriches workspaces with validated findings and artifacts, then inherits and combines these workspaces to uncover deeper questions. It constructs tasks from accumulated findings and their
s0e9d0f602a.summary: DataPraxis, a framework based on verified workspace evolution, is introduced to synthesize verified analytics tasks for training general-purpose agents.
s0e9d0f602a.why: Offers a method for generating verifiable training tasks for analytics agents, which could matter for teams building data-analysis agents.

sff33c277a2.title: DuoCook: An Overcooked-Inspired Benchmark for Visual Planning and Coordination
sff33c277a2.description: arXiv:2610.31511v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Coordinating two players in a cooking task requires a vision-language agent to track changing scene states, sequence recipe steps, and allocate shared resources under a time budget. We introduce an Overcooked-inspired benchmark for evaluating these capabilities in Unreal Engine environments constructed using coding agents. A single vision-language model controls both players from top-down visual observations \rev{through separate per-player decision calls}, selecting high-level actions \rev{and image-labeled target cells} while the engine executes navigation. The benchmark contains 20 maps in five categories. These categories support evaluation of \rev{two-player} coordination under equipment contention, changing terrain, and handoff depe
sff33c277a2.summary: DuoCook, an Overcooked-inspired benchmark in Unreal Engine, evaluates whether a single vision-language model can coordinate two players in visual planning tasks.
sff33c277a2.why: Provides a testbed for multi-agent coordination from visual observations, relevant to teams building embodied or game-like agents.

s7e3b4fba42.title: Query-Driven Learning for Lifted Reasoning
s7e3b4fba42.description: arXiv:2610.34747v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Learning and reasoning are both essential to intelligent agents, but have traditionally been treated as two separate stages: first learning a knowledge base from data (or taking one as given), and then verifying queries as if the knowledge base were complete. This separation has been shown to be inefficient when the downstream goal is to verify only a small set of queries. Moreover, it neglects the possibility that data and a knowledge base contain partial yet complementary information, requiring an agent to combine both sources to justify or refute a query. Motivated by the need to integrate learning and reasoning more tightly, we study the problem of query-driven learning for reasoning. More specifically, we extend prior work to the fir
s7e3b4fba42.summary: A query-driven approach to lifted reasoning is proposed that combines learning and verification instead of treating them as separate stages.

sef9dac0c4f.title: Glyph: An Interpretability Engine for AI-Driven Scientific Discovery from Clinical Data
sef9dac0c4f.description: arXiv:2611.08922v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Automated scientific discovery has the potential to advance understanding of disease mechanisms and accelerate identification of early disease markers. Manual data annotation is infeasible at population scale, motivating methods that automatically extract pre-defined phenotypes from multimodal and unstructured clinical data. Such pre-defined feature sets determine and limit which associations these approaches can discover. This limitation extends to agentic AI systems that use these tools to query population-scale data. In contrast, foundation models (FMs) trained on large volumes of clinical data can perform tasks beyond their training objectives. This suggests their latent embeddings may represent novel or unexplored features that could
sef9dac0c4f.summary: Glyph, an interpretability engine, is presented for AI-driven scientific discovery from clinical data using foundation models rather than predefined phenotypes.
sef9dac0c4f.why: Suggests an approach to discovering clinical associations beyond fixed feature sets, relevant to teams building health data analytics.

sfcbc80e1e9.title: Learning When to Think: Dual-Reference Offline Optimization for Adaptive VLM Reasoning
sfcbc80e1e9.description: arXiv:2611.09154v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Reasoning traces improve vision-language models on complex multimodal tasks, but forcing every input to follow a long reasoning process leads to overthinking and unnecessary inference cost.
